  automatic-styles of content.xml (`xlink:href` to the image in `Pictures/`, bytes in the package
  via `_mediaEntries` + manifest, like the other images). The reader builds the map
  name→href from the `draw:fill-image`s and, for each drawing-page with `fill="bitmap"`, resolves the href and
  loads the bytes into `BackgroundImage`.
- **OOXML**: `p:bg`/`p:bgPr` with `a:blipFill`/`a:blip` (`r:embed` to an ImagePart of the
  SlidePart) in place of `a:solidFill`. **Note**: the PPTX reader did not read the slide
  background at all (neither colour nor image) — now it reads the background's BlipFill into `BackgroundImage`.
- **Verified with the real reference suite**: ODP and PPTX with a background image open and convert to
  PDF; and converting our PPTX→ODP **the reference suite re-emits `draw:fill="bitmap"`/`fill-image`**
  — that is, it really interpreted the background, it did not ignore it. `ODP016`/`PPTX011` removed. Test
  `BackgroundImageSurvives` in both suites (Odf 171, OpenXml 165 green).

Still declared (as for normal images, `ODP015`/`PPTX010`): any filter or
crop *on the background* is not persisted; the original image is.

### Decision: no ActiveX in any module (2026-10-01)
**PulseOffice does not support ActiveX controls** in Folio, Deck and Ledger — a loss declared
**by choice**, not as debt. Form controls in PPTX are ActiveX
(COM/Windows-only, against rule 15; disabled by default by Microsoft 365 since April
2025 and Office 2024 since October 2024, rendered as a static non-interactive image, with a declared
direction towards removal). Emitting them would be 100% net-new for a result that is inert
everywhere. In ODP form controls round-trip natively (it is ODF, not ActiveX). If
a control needs to survive a round trip through PowerPoint, the correct cross-platform route is
to emit it as a **drawn shape** (placeholder with label), not as ActiveX. `PPTX004` is
updated to declare it as a choice.

### Deck: slide comments in PPTX too (feature completed in both formats)
Comments were native only in ODP (`office:annotation`), declared as loss `PPTX013`. Now
they cross **both** formats (rule 7 fully applied to a feature that was half done).

- **OOXML**: classic comments — `SlideCommentsPart` per slide (`p:cmLst`/`p:cm` with
  `authorId`, `idx`, `dt`, `p:pos` in EMU, `p:text`) and `CommentAuthorsPart` at
  presentation level (`p:cmAuthorLst`/`p:cmAuthor`). `SlideComment` keeps only the author's **name**,
  so `PptxCommentMapper` synthesizes the author ids (name→id map, initials,
  `lastIndex` per author, cyclic `colorIndex`) and reuses them across slides.
- **A single mapper** (`PptxCommentMapper`, single responsibility) serves writer and reader:
  `Write(slidePart, presentationPart, slide)` and `Read(...)`; `Reset()` clears the author state at
  each write. Loss `PPTX013` removed.
- **Verified with the real reference suite**: a PPTX with a comment written by us not only opens
  and converts to PDF, but converted into ODP **the reference suite re-emits** `office:annotation` with
  author «Mario Rossi» and text — that is, it really interpreted the native comment, it did not
  ignore it. Test `CommentSurvives` in the PPTX suite (7/7 ObjectOps, full 164 green).

Note (as already in ODP): the round trip of **text and author** is full; the date (`dt`/`dc:date`)
is written but our reader does not read it back into `CreatedAt` — tolerated by the tests, aligned with the
ODP behaviour.

### Deck: native OLE/package persistence in both formats (done)
The OLE subsystem, built from scratch (it is not a port: Ledger does not serialize `PackagedObject`
in any format, so there was nothing to reuse). A `PackagedObject` is an arbitrary file
embedded with name and media-type; now it crosses **both** formats, write→read back, and is
**verified with the real reference suite** (ODP and PPTX converted to PDF without rejections).

- **ODF**: `draw:frame` with `draw:object-ole` (`draw:mime-type`=media-type, `draw:name`=file
  name, `xlink:href` to the stream `Objects/<id>/<name>`). The bytes enter the package like the
  other media (`_mediaEntries`, hence with the manifest entry). The reader has a dedicated pass
  on `draw:object-ole` — an element name distinct from `draw:object` (formula) and without `draw:image`
  (image), so it does not collide with the other passes. `OdfDeckShapeMapper.BuildOle`/`ReadOle`.
- **OOXML**: `p:graphicFrame` with `a:graphicData` OLE uri and `p:oleObj` (`r:id` to an
  `EmbeddedObjectPart` with the canonical OLE content-type, `name`=file name, `progId`=media-type) plus
  the fallback `p:pic` **required by the schema** (a transparent 1×1 PNG embedded as a
  constant, no rasterizer). The round trip reads the bytes from the part, name and media-type from the
  attributes. `PptxDeckShapeMapper.BuildOle`/`ReadOle`; the reader intercepts it **before**
  chart/table in the `p:graphicFrame` loop (different uris, no collision).
- **The kind (File/Media) is deduced from the media-type** (`video/`·`audio/` → Media, otherwise
  File): no extra attribute is needed, and it is reversible.
- `ODP004`/`PPTX004` narrowed: OLE is no longer a loss. Only the **ActiveX
  controls in PPTX** (`PPTX004`) remain a loss, which are a subsystem of their own with no reuse.

Tests: `PackagedObjectSurvives` in both ObjectOps suites (ODP 8/8, PPTX 6/6, 170+163 full
green, no regressions). Coverage of the wanted items unchanged: this round removes a *loss*,
it does not add menu entries.

### Deck: persistence of form controls in ODP; OLE remains a loss
Resumed the persistence debt of controls and OLE. Honest verdict after the mapping:

- **Form controls in ODP: done (reuse).** `OdfFormControlMapper.BuildControl`/
  `ReadProperties`/`KindOf` are sheet-agnostic (ODF legally puts `office:forms`/`form:form`
  on a `draw:page`). OdpWriter emits `office:forms` per slide + the
  `draw:control` frames with svg geometry from the bounds; the reader reads them back. `xmlns:form`/`ooo` on the
  root. No longer in `ODP004`. Round trip tested **and file accepted by the real reference suite**.
- **Controls in PPTX: remains a declared loss.** Ledger's XLSX route is tied to the
  `WorksheetPart`/`x14` and produces Excel-only elements; native PPTX has the
  **ActiveX** controls (part `ax:ocx`), a subsystem of its own with no reuse. `PPTX004` unchanged.
- **OLE/package (`PackagedObject`): a loss at the time, then built from scratch** — see the
  section above "native OLE/package persistence in both formats". The premise remains true
  (Ledger does not serialize it, it was net-new work, not a port), but the subsystem was later
  written and now round-trips in ODP and PPTX.

### Refactoring towards patterns: waves 1 and 2
New rule from the user: **as many design patterns as possible**, according to
[refactoring.guru](https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/csharp), fewer static methods and more
hierarchies. The study of the 22 pages is in [docs/design-patterns.md](docs/design-patterns.md), the
wave plan in [docs/refactoring-plan.md](docs/refactoring-plan.md).

**Wave 1** — `ImageFilters` (static class with a `switch`) has become a hierarchy of filters:
`PerPixelFilter` is a Template Method (the loop over pixels is fixed, the pixel transformation is the
variable step) with `GrayscaleFilter`, `SepiaFilter`, `InvertFilter`; `MosaicFilter` separately;
`IdentityFilter` as Null Object; `PixelFilterCatalog` chooses. `TextCase` has become a
family of transformations (`TextCaseTransform`, Template Method) and a catalogue `ITextCases` with the
case cycle expressed as a state table. `ListLabels` is a service with the markers
as Strategy (`NumberMarker`, `BulletMarker`) and the per-level counters in an object of their own.

**Wave 2** — drawing objects have a **Visitor**: `IDrawingObject.Accept` on the six
classes (shape, freeform path, vector, raster, group, connector), a closed and
stable hierarchy, which is the case in which the site recommends it. `DrawingObjectVisitor<T>` gives a
fallback branch, so a partial visitor does not have to write all the cases. `DrawingObjectRenderer` is now
a facade: a `PaintVisitor` dispatches to a painter per type (`FreeformPainter`, `VectorPainter`,
`RasterPainter` with its cache, `ConnectorPainter`, `GroupPainter` which recurses as a Composite).
`ShapeStyling` is two visitors, style reading and application, without a `switch`.

**Wave 3** — slide drawing. `SlideElement` has a Visitor (`Accept` on text,
object and media); `SlideRenderer` is now only the orchestrator (background, elements, footer) and
no longer contains `switch` or private static methods. Object contents go through a
**chain of responsibility** (`ContentPainterChain`): formula, chart, table, control,
package and finally the generic drawer; each link inherits from `ContentPainter<T>` (Template
Method: the type check is done once in the base). Text is split into three classes —
`ParagraphTypesetter` (size, font, alignment), `RunStyler` (the style of each run),
`RunText` (rendering of fields) — and the footer into `ChromePainter`. The rule restated by the user
was applied immediately: **zero private static methods** in the files touched by these waves.

**Wave 4** — the presentation readers. `OdpReader` (919 lines, 23 private static methods) and
`PptxReader` (657, 16) are now **facades** of a few dozen lines that compose pieces with one
responsibility each:
- **ODP**: the automatic style tables are a hierarchy — `AutomaticStyleTable<T>` does the
  loop over the styles of a family (Template Method), the subclasses say what to read
  (paragraph, text, cell, page background and image and visibility, transition) — and
  `OdpStyleSheetBuilder` (Builder) assembles them into an `OdpStyleSheet`. The page is read with a
  **pipeline** of `IOdpPageReader`; those that read objects inherit from `OdpObjectReader`
  (Template Method: which nodes, how to read one; z-order and alternative text are in the base).
  Paragraphs, runs, position in lists, placeholder roles, masters and settings are
  classes of their own; unit and colour conversions are in `OdfValues`.
- **PPTX**: same shape. `ShapeClassifier`, `SchemeRoles` (a table instead of two duplicated chains of
  `if`), run and paragraph readers, theme and master; the slide with
  `IPptxSlidePartReader` (text, images and media, shapes, graphic frames, animations, comments,
  background) and the presentation with `IPptxPresentationPartReader` (sections, custom
  presentations, settings, footers).
- Slide assembly (`SlideAssembly<TFrameKey>`: order, identifiers, frame→element
  binding for animations) is **a single one** in `PulseOffice.Formats`, generic over the frame
  key: string in ODF, shape number in OOXML.

Behaviour unchanged: all tests of both formats green, and the files produced by the real reference suite
(numbered lists, levels, spacing) read back identical to before.

**Wave 5** — the presentation writers. `OdpWriter` (747 lines) and `PptxWriter` (673) are
facades that compose:
- a **write session** per save (`OdpWriteSession`, `PptxWriteSession`) that holds
  what used to be in mutable fields of the writer — style counter, media, formula and chart
  documents (`Formula N`, `Object N`), fill images, slide → relationship
  and number bindings. A writer is now reentrant: two saves no longer share state;
- the **Builders** of the styles and XML pieces: paragraph, run, page (background, transition,
  visibility), lists, master placeholders in ODF; theme, master and layout, text shape,
  paragraph, run properties, placeholder style in OOXML;
- a **chain of object writers** per format, with a generic base (Template Method: type check
  and alternative text in the base) — chart, formula, table, shape, path, connector,
  image, package in ODF; chart, table, package and generic drawing in OOXML;
- the presentation's OOXML extensions (sections, footers) as the hierarchy
  `PresentationExtension` (Template Method: `p:ext` wrapper in the base);
- **fidelity checks as data**: `FidelityRuleSet<T>` in `PulseOffice.Formats`, one rule
  per declared loss, shared by the two formats instead of two chains of `if`.

**A real defect found while verifying with the reference suite**: in ODPs the numbers and bullets of lists
came out **tiny**, because the list styles did not declare the size of the label. Now the
levels carry `fo:font-size="100%"` and `text:bullet-relative-size="100%"`, and the label has a
bit more space. Verified by rendering the file to PDF with the reference suite, in both formats.

**A crash at startup, found by the real startup**: the container chose the constructor of
`TextCases` that receives `IEnumerable<ITextCaseTransform>` and passed it **empty**, because the
transformations were not registered. Now they are registered one by one, and the catalogue **rejects**
an incomplete set immediately instead of failing at the first key looked up; a test guards it.

### Deck: style, position and alternative text of objects — and alternative text is saved everywhere
**Deck inserted shapes that could not be dressed**: the style window (fill, outline,
effects, text) existed only in Ledger. The shape ↔ style conversion lived in private methods of
`LedgerCommands`; now it is a shared service (`IShapeStyling`/`ShapeStyling` in
`PulseOffice.UI.Controls.Shapes`), used by Ledger and Deck (rule 10), and `ShapeStyleView` opens
on the requested tab, so the reference suite's *Area…*, *Line…*, *Shadow and effects…* and *Text attributes…*
are the same window on different tabs.

The windows on a selected object are a **hierarchy** (Template Method): `DeckObjectDialog`
fixes the flow — enablement on the selection, opening, undoable replacement
(`DeckActions.ReplaceElement`) — and the subclasses only say what they accept and how they modify:
`ShapeStyleDialog`, `PositionSizeDialog` (X, Y, size and rotation in cm), `AltTextDialog`. In the
ribbon *Home ▸ Object*: *Shape style…* and *Position and size…*; the rest in the menu
*Format ▸ Object*.

**The real defect: alternative text was not saved in any format**, neither in Deck nor in
Ledger, which did have the window to write it — a silent loss in four formats. Now it
travels as `svg:title`/`svg:desc` in ODF and as `title`/`descr` of `cNvPr` in OOXML, through
a hierarchy: `AltTextMapper<TNode>` in `PulseOffice.Formats` (Template Method: writes and reads on a
node, or by name on a whole root) with `OdfAltTextMapper` and `OoxmlAltTextMapper`. Deck applies it
at the object dispatch point; Ledger, whose mappers do not return the node, applies it
**by name** after building or reading the drawing, because each object already carries its own
identifier as name.

**A UI defect found while trying**: the swatches of the colour picker's palette
were **empty**. The base button style introduced in the visual round repainted the
`ContentPresenter` and covered the swatch's colour. Now the swatches have the class `swatch`,
excluded from the base style, and on pointer hover they keep their colour.

**Verified live**: rectangle inserted, *Position and size* rotates it by 15°, *Shape
style* makes it green from the palette. Round-trip tests of the alternative text in ODP, PPTX, ODS
and XLSX. Reference suite presentation coverage **204 → 210 of 368 (57.1%)**.

### Deck: numbered lists, spacing, clear formatting — and lists in ODP are really saved
**The real defect, found while adding the numbered list: in ODP bullets and levels were not saved.**
The writer put each paragraph in a bare `text:p` and the reader **guessed** the bullet from the
role (`Bullet = role == Body`): a second-level indent came back to the first, a paragraph without
a bullet in the body came back bulleted. A silent loss, that is the worst defect under rule 7.
Now list paragraphs live in real `text:list`s — one list per run of paragraphs of the
same kind, the level as nesting of `text:list-item`/`text:list` — with two automatic
styles (`LQBullet`, `LQNumber`, nine levels each). The reader reads **from the structure**:
depth, and whether the style's level is `list-level-style-number`.

Something discovered only with the real reference suite: a paragraph without a bullet must be written as `text:p`
**outside** the list, not as `text:list-header` — the reference suite draws the bullet on the list
header too, and itself writes the bare `text:p`. And in OOXML the "inherited" bullet applies only to a
**real placeholder** (`p:ph`): the reference suite exports our frames as text boxes
(`txBox`), where a paragraph without `a:buChar` has no bullet, and we re-bulleted it.

The model has `TextParagraph.Numbered`; numbering per level (restart under a parent,
reset outside the list) is `ListLabels`, pure tested logic used by the drawer. In OOXML the
numbered list is `a:buAutoNum type="arabicPeriod"`. **Space before and after** the paragraph (which the
model and the drawing had but no format saved) now travel as `fo:margin-top/bottom`
and `a:spcBef/a:spcAft`, in points.

Commands: *Numbered list* (ribbon *Home ▸ Paragraph*), *Clear formatting* (ribbon
*Home ▸ Font*: brings the characters back to the paragraph's), increase/decrease spacing, and
*Toggle case* (`TextCase.NextInCycle`, shared: lowercase → Initials →
Sentence → UPPERCASE → lowercase). The reference suite's promote/demote are the already existing indents.
In Ledger "Toggle" was mapped onto *Invert*, which does something else: now it has its real command.

**Verified with the real reference suite in both directions** (numbered on two levels, bullet with spacing,
free paragraph) and **live**: two lines in the body, *Numbered list* → «1. Alfa / 2. beta».
Reference suite presentation coverage **197 → 204 of 368 (55.4%)**.

### Deck: slide format (done)
*Design ▸ Set up ▸ Slide format…* chooses the size: widescreen 16:9 and 16:10,
standard 4:3, A4, letter or custom in centimetres, with orientation. The presets and their
recognition (rotated too) live in `SlideResize`, pure tested logic. With *Fit
content* (the default) every object of every slide and the master's placeholders scale
**uniformly** and stay **centred**: scaling the two axes differently would distort shapes and
images. The text size does not scale, declared. A single undo brings back size, master and
objects. The size already crossed both formats (`page-layout` in ODF, `p:sldSz` in OOXML).

**Verified live**: 16:9 → portrait, the slide becomes tall and narrow with title and
subtitle centred, the document is marked modified, ⌘Z brings everything back. Reference suite presentation coverage **196 → 197**.

### Deck: slide zoom (done)
Deck's canvas could only **fit** the space: to work on a detail there was no way
to enlarge. Now it has three modes (`CanvasZoom`, pure and tested in `PulseOffice.Presentations`):
**fit to window** (the default), **fit to width** and a **fixed factor** between 10%
and 400%, with zoom-in and zoom-out steps on a fixed scale of notches — from any factor
one goes up to the next notch, not by a constant increment.

`SlideView` measures itself according to the mode (factor 1 = slide at real size, 15 twips
per point) and lives inside a scroller whose bars turn on only when needed: in
*fit* none, in *width* only the vertical one. Commands `deck.zoom.*` (zoom in ⌘+, zoom out
⌘−, fit ⌘0, width, 50–200%, *Zoom…* with the percentage), with ⌘+wheel on the canvas. In the ribbon
(*View ▸ Zoom*) the five main ones; in the menu the presets and the window. The command that
matches the current state is grey. The shortcuts coincide with Ledger's but are per
module, so they do not conflict (the startup audit is clean).

**Verified live**: Zoom 100% and then Zoom in bring the slide to 125% with the
scroll bars, *Fit to window* brings it back letterboxed and turns grey again. Reference suite presentation coverage
**187 → 196 of 368 (53.3%)**.

### Templates for all modules: saving a template was not a template
*Save as template* was a placeholder, and opening a template opened it **as a document**: the first
⌘S overwrote the template itself, which is the fastest way to lose it. Now templates are
real `.ots` and `.otp` — same package, **template MIME type** (`…-template`), which is what
office suites look at to treat them as such — written by `OdsSpreadsheetWriter(template: true)` and
`OdpWriter(template: true)` in the configuration's `templates/` folder.

The three commands live in the shell (`ShellTemplateCommands`) and go through the per-module Strategy
(`IDocumentOperations.TemplateExtension`, `OpenAsNewAsync`): *Templates…* opens the chosen template
**as a new document without a path**, so saving asks where to write; *Open template*
opens it for editing. They apply to Ledger and Deck, and Folio will hook in with its Strategy.

**Defect found by the test and not by eye**: `OdsReader` rejected the template MIME type, so
an `.ots` — even one from the reference suite — did not open at all. **Verified with the real reference suite**: our
`.otp` and `.ots` open and convert.

### Deck: persistence consolidation (freeform, connectors) and comments
Return to the fidelity debts and addition of a capability.

- **Freeform and connectors now persist natively** in both formats. Both
  reduce to a `ShapeOutline`: a shared OOXML helper `OoxmlGeometry` (custGeom ↔
  outline, lifted from Ledger's vector mapper) and `ShapePathWriter` for ODF
  (`draw:path` with `svg:d`) write/read them; `FreeformPath.FromOutline` for reading.
  They are no longer in `PPTX004`/`ODP004`. The connector, written as geometry, **loses
  the live anchoring** and is read back as freeform — declared `PPTX012`/`ODP017`.
- **Slide comments** (new capability): `SlideComment` (author, text, date,
  position), accent marker on the canvas in edit mode, command *Insert comment*.
  Native round trip in ODP (`office:annotation` with `dc:creator`/`dc:date`); in PPTX at the time
  declared a loss (`PPTX013`), then **completed** — see "slide comments in PPTX too"
  above.

Remaining as declared loss (persistence not yet native): **ActiveX** form controls **in
PPTX** (by choice, see the dedicated decision) and **sepia/invert/mosaic** (no symmetric
equivalent). (OLE/package, comments-in-PPTX, background image, grayscale/crop and text style of
master placeholders were in this list and were later built — see the more recent sections.) Coverage of the wanted items: **from 142 to 143 of 370 (38%)** — the number grows
little because these rounds remove *losses*, they do not add menu entries.

### Deck bucket B (remainder) and bucket C: insertions, slides, controls, exclusions
Closing the bulk of B and opening C, in sub-blocks.

- **Slides**: move to start/end (reuses `MoveSlide`); **insert slides from file**
  (.odp/.pptx read with `IPresentationFormatRegistry`, slides cloned into the deck,
  `DeckActions.ImportSlides`); slide **background image** (rendered by the shared
  renderer before the elements, in-app, declared loss `PPTX011`/`ODP016`).
- **Hyperlinks**: a command that sets a Hyperlink `InteractiveAction` on the selected object
  (reuses `SetInteraction`, existing round trip); in the slide show the click opens the URL via
  `Launcher`.
- **Form controls**: `FormControlObject` rendered on the slide by the shared renderer
  (`IFormControlRenderer`, new case in `SlideRenderer`); ten common controls insertable
  via `IFormControlCatalog`. Static rendering; interactive behaviour and saving declared
  loss (`PPTX004`/`ODP004`).
- **Object/OLE**: `PackagedObject` (embedded file) rendered as a plate with the name
  (`IPackagedObjectRenderer`); same declared-loss discipline.
- **Bucket C**: 18 entries specific to the reference suite (help, windows, wizards, minimise
  presentation, extensions, UI variants) marked **excluded** — like the 13 of the spreadsheet map. The
  deck census script (a former survey tool) now counts them separately.

Declared **subsystem** (not done): **Fontwork/WordArt** (needs an artistic text model
+ glyphs as paths), **comments/annotations** on a slide (Ledger's `CellComment` is
tied to cells, not reusable), **multiple masters / notes / handout**. The reusable
pattern for the rest: `SlideRenderer` is the only dispatch point to add content
renderers (form control, packaged), `DeckInsertCommands.InsertContent` the only insertion
path for an `EmbeddedObject`. Coverage of the wanted items: **from 127 to 142 of 369 (38.5%)**.

### Deck bucket B: editable Master view, with native persistence (done)
The biggest piece of B, in four layers. Before, the master was an immutable record,
regenerated from the theme at every load and **never persisted**. Now it is editable and crosses
both formats **natively** (explicit choice of the user: interoperable with
PowerPoint and the reference suite).

1. **Model + actions**: `MasterEditing` (pure) rebuilds the immutable `SlideMaster`
   (master background, per-layout background, placeholder geometry); `DeckActions.SetMasterBackground/
   SetLayoutBackground/SetPlaceholderBounds` via swap-and-`Do`, like `ApplyTheme`.
2. **Native PPTX**: `slideMaster`/`slideLayout` emit the placeholders as `p:sp` with `p:ph` +
   `a:xfrm` for **all** 11 layouts, and the background as `SchemeColor` (the **colour role
   round-trips**, not the absolute value). The reader rebuilds `SlideMaster.Layouts` from the layout parts.
3. **Native ODP**: a `presentation:presentation-page-layout` per layout with the
   `presentation:placeholder`s (object + svg geometry); the reader reads them back. The per-role
   background remains degraded as already declared (`ODP010`, absolute nature of ODF colours).
4. **Master view**: a mode in the *View* tab — an editable canvas showing a chosen
   layout, with layout selector and background; dragging the placeholders writes the geometry into the
   master. The **master background is reflected immediately on all** slides; the **geometry**
   applies to **new** slides (existing ones copied the geometry at
   creation — declared; retro-applying would destroy per-slide changes).

Not done, declared: **multiple masters**, **notes/handout masters** (no model).
The text style of the placeholders did not persist at the time; it was later built — see "text style
of master placeholders in both formats".
Tests: `MasterEditingTests`, master round trip in PPTX and ODP. Coverage: **126 → 127 of 388**.

### Deck bucket B1: drawing insertion (shapes, connectors, freeform)
First block of "bucket B" (the capabilities really missing): drawing insertion
on the slide, largely **reuse** of shared code.

- **B1a Shape gallery**: the command *More shapes…* opens `ShapeGalleryView` (shared with
  Ledger, all 26 shapes with live preview) and inserts the choice. Extracted a shared
  `InsertContent`; insertions now **select** the created object (before, they did not).
- **B1b Connectors**: `DeckConnectors` (pure, tested) reuses `ConnectorObject` +
  `ConnectorRouter`; connects two selected objects by identifier and **recomputes the
  path when they move** (reroute in `Sync`). Absolute bounds of the slide,
  no cells — simpler than the sheet version.
- **B1c Freeform**: Deck-local pen state (`IDeckDrawingState`) + the pointer interaction
  brought into `SlideView` (click adds points, double click or near the first closes, freehand
  in capture, Esc cancels, accent overlay), which reuses the pure helpers
  `PathAuthoring`/`PathNormalizer` of `PulseOffice.Drawing`. Polygon, 45° polygon, curve,
  freehand, filled and unfilled.

Connectors and freeform paths **render and are manipulated in-app** but saving remains
a declared loss (`PPTX004`/`ODP004`: not yet in the written list). **Node
editing** of a path is postponed. Measured coverage: from **114 to 126 of 388 (32%)**.
Tests: `DeckConnectorsTests`. Clean audit (609 commands), no crash.

### Deck bucket A: everyday use (Edit, File, language) — largely wiring
After the Format operations, a round on "bucket A": the everyday functions that
the reference suite lists but that for Deck were absent or lived only in Ledger. Many **already
worked** because the shell resolves the active document generically
(undo/redo on `OpenDocument.History`, new/open/recent, save/save as
routed per module, export, Asian conversions and case via `DeckTarget.ApplyText`):
marked in the map without code. The real gaps, filled in sub-blocks:

- **A1 Object clipboard**: in-process `IDeckClipboard` — copy/cut/paste of
  slide elements (cloning + re-id + offset, a single undo),
  **duplicate** the selection, **select all**. Shortcuts Ctrl+C/X/V/D/A that yield to the
  text field when editing a placeholder. The multi-selection added in the
  Format block is the base.
- **A2 Find and replace**: dialog with match case, find next (navigates
  to the slide) and replace all; pure logic `DeckTextSearch` that counts and
  replaces **within runs preserving formatting**, tested. Navigation via
  `DeckTarget.GoToSlide`.
- **A3 Thesaurus and hyphenation**: shared engines (`IThesaurusProvider`,
  `IHyphenationProvider`) hooked to Deck text via `ApplyText`. Spell checking
  and autocorrect while typing remain **open** for Deck: they require a word cursor and
  wavy underline on the canvas — a subsystem, not wiring.
- **A4 File**: **save a copy / save all / reload** moved from `LedgerFileCommands`
  to `ShellCommands`, routed per module (rule 2-bis: one command per operation, not one
  per module). Now they apply to Deck too. Email/Bluetooth, versions and check-in remain
  open.

The reference suite's autolayout variants ("One Box", "Two Boxes"…) map onto the **11 layouts**
that already exist. Measured coverage: from **97 to 114 of 388 (29%)**. Clean startup audit
(598 commands), no crash. Tests: `DeckTextSearchTests`.

### Deck Format: object, table and image operations (three blocks, done)
Continued Deck's **Format** group with three cohesive blocks, each one commit.

**1) Object operations.** Deck had only single selection; **multi-selection** was added
on the canvas (Shift+click extends, the primary carries handles and
rotation, moving applies to all selected in **a single** undo via
`AlignElements`) — it is the base for group and reverse. New commands: **group/ungroup**
(`ShapeGroupObject` with the pure logic `DeckGrouping`: bounding box + children in fractions,
reuses Ledger's model), **flip H/V** (shapes and vectors, same transformation
as Ledger), **reverse the order** of the selection. The flip crosses both formats (native PPTX
`flipH/flipV`; ODF `draw:mirror-horizontal/-vertical` on the enhanced-geometry —
before, ODP did not serialize flip or rotation of shapes at all). The **group is
flattened on save** (each child saved as an autonomous object at absolute
coordinates, in both formats): the objects and the layout are kept, the group *binding*
is not, declared `PPTX009`/`ODP014`. **Enter/exit group** is declared out: the
children of a `ShapeGroupObject` are not selectable elements of the slide, so
"enter" would have nothing to select — a dead click, which this project avoids.

**2) Table operations.** **Per-cell vertical alignment** (top/centre/bottom) as
`TableCellFormat` on the `DataTableObject` (same scheme as `TableMerge`), applied by the
renderer and settable in the editor on the cell selection; **select the whole table**
from the corner (row/column selections from the headers already existed); **delete
table**. The alignment crosses both formats: OOXML `TableCellProperties.Anchor`, ODF
`style:vertical-align` on a referenced automatic cell style. **Distributing
rows/columns** stays out, declared: without manual column resizing the
renderer already renders equal columns and uniform rows, so there is nothing to distribute.

**3) Image filters, crop, original size.** Filters **sepia, grayscale,
invert, mosaic** as the `ImageFilter` property of `RasterImageObject`, applied by the
**shared renderer** (`DrawingObjectRenderer`) on BGRA buffers with the pure logic
`ImageFilters` (static, pure computation, tested). Since the renderer is shared, the filters
apply in **Deck and Ledger** (rule 10): the filter commands are wired in both. The
**crop** is now really applied in rendering (source rect) — before, it was stored and never
drawn, in any module. **Original size** brings the frame back to the
`NaturalSize`. Filter and crop are **declared a loss** in the four formats that carry
images (`PPTX010`/`ODP015`/`XLSX024`/`ODF022`): the original image is saved, the effect
stays on screen — they have no reliable native equivalent (invert and mosaic do not exist
in either format).

Measured coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands: from **83 to 97 of 388 (25%)**. New tests:
`DeckGroupingTests`, round trip of flip/group/cell alignment in ODP and PPTX,
`ImageFiltersTests`. Clean startup audit at **590 commands**; no crash on closing.

### Crash on closing: a surface rebuilt on an already disposed container
Closing the app after opening a Deck, the process aborted with
`ObjectDisposedException: 'IServiceProvider'` rising up to `Main` (the Apple report showed
only the managed rethrow; the real stack was in our crash report). The chain: the block "Deck's ribbon
opened all grey" had bound `IActiveDeckContext.Changed` to
`Dispatcher.UIThread.Post(RefreshSurfaces)`. On closing, the Deck context's `Detach` **posts**
a `RefreshSurfaces`, which runs **after** `desktop.Exit` has disposed the DI container; rebuilding
the native menu evaluates the `EnabledWhen` of `shell.edit.repeat`, which resolves `CommandExecutor` from the
container — by now disposed — and the unhandled exception brings down the process.

**Do not rebuild surfaces after closing has begun.** A `_closing` flag is raised
**at the start** of `desktop.Exit`, before the dispose; the Deck context's deferred post and the
recent documents refresh check it and skip. A `RefreshSurfaces` already queued when
closing begins finds `_closing` true at execution time and no longer touches the container.

**Verified live**: opened a Deck and closed it with SIGTERM (the path that reproduced the crash),
no new crash report and the log shows a clean exit — before, every close with a
Deck open left a crash report.

### Deck: the Font and Paragraph windows (done)
Resumed Deck's development from the biggest group of the map (**Format**, 78 missing). First two
entries, those that make the rich text already built in D2 **discoverable** — like "Format cells"
for Ledger: *Format ▸ Font…* and *Format ▸ Paragraph…* (the reference suite's font and paragraph dialogs).

**No work on the formats**: the attributes (bold, italic, size, font, effects,
alignment, line spacing, list, level) **already cross** ODP and PPTX since D2, so the windows
are pure UI on top of the model. The work was adding to `DeckTextFormatter` (pure,
tested logic) the **absolute setters** that were missing — `SetFont`, `SetFontSize`, `SetChar(attribute,
on)`, `SetBullet`, `SetBulletLevel` — and the **readers** `ReadCharacter`/`ReadParagraph` that report
the **common** value of the selection or `null` when it is mixed: they serve to **prefill** the windows.

`DeckTextDialogCommands` (a class of its own, single responsibility) opens two `FormPromptView`s and applies
in **a single** `ApplyText` (undoable) composing the setters. The windows are on the
*Advanced* surface (menu *Format ▸ Font…/Paragraph…* and palette), so no ribbon icon to
draw. The checkbox labels reuse the **already translated command titles**
(`command.deck.format.bold.title`, …) instead of new keys.

A defect found live, and the marker did its job: the labels appeared as
`⟦command.deck.deck.format.bold.title⟧` — one "deck" too many, because the effect's key is already
`deck.format.bold` and I composed it with `command.deck.{key}` instead of `command.{key}`.

**Verified live end-to-end**: with the title selected, *Font…* opens with **Size 40** and
**Bold** already ticked (read from the title), the nine effect checkboxes translated; ticked
*Italic* and confirmed, the title on the slide becomes **italic** (as well as bold).
*Paragraph…* opens with **Alignment = Centre** and **Line spacing = 1** prefilled from the centred
title. Seven new tests on the formatter (absolute setters, common/mixed reads). Reference suite presentation
coverage: **81 → 83 of 387 (21.4%)**.

### Visual alignment round on Ledger and Deck
Before continuing with Deck, a pass over all of Ledger's and Deck's views to align with the
visual language what had remained raw (and therefore ugly and at times unusable). A
read-only survey classified each view by severity; then the corrections.

**The common cause, solved in a single place (rule 2-bis).** There was no **base style for
`Button`**: every `new Button` without a class fell back on Avalonia's default grey. Added in
`PulseTheme.axaml` a themed base style — surface, border, radius from the tokens, hover/pressed states
from the `Palette` — that excludes the already dressed classes (`ribbon`, `dialogPrimary`, `dialogQuiet`,
`dialogClose`, `close`). **One style and all the app's unclassed buttons line up**:
StylesPanel, FindReplace, Pivot, CustomShows, SidePanel, Recovery, FilterMenu stop showing
grey rectangles.

**The most repeated deviation: the hand-made button row instead of `DialogFooter`.** Three
windows (*Find and replace*, *Pivot table*, *Recovery*) built a right-aligned `StackPanel` of
buttons, skipping the Cancel-on-the-left / primary-action-on-the-right convention
and the footer band. Converted to `IDialogFooterOwner` + `DialogFooter`: now they have the real footer
with the primary action in the accent. **Verified live**: *Find and replace* shows the footer
with *Close* on the left and a green *Replace all* on the right.

Targeted refinements: in *CustomShows* the `accent` parameter was **ignored** — the *Present* button
did not take the accent; now it does. The `SidePanelView` colours the active tab with the module's accent,
the title is themed and the ✕ uses the `dialogClose` class (round, hover). `StylesPanelView` (the
worst: a column of bare grey buttons) now has a themed empty state and entries with consistent
spacing. Removed a dead `Button` helper in `FilterMenuView`.

**Second verification round** on all the views not covered by the first (Data.UI, Remote, shapes,
formula editor, various prompts), now that the base button style is in force. Confirmed aligned:
ConnectionManager, DataImport, RemoteBrowser, ShapeGallery, AssetPicker, ColorPicker, Choice,
FormulaDocumentationPanel. Corrected three leftovers: **ShapeStyleView** and **PrintPromptView**
built the action row by hand → converted to `DialogFooter` (primary action in the accent);
**SettingsView** used `Opacity` for the secondary text (now `.Themed(TextSecondary)`) and
above all carried **two hardcoded Italian strings** («Ha effetto al prossimo avvio» ("Takes effect at next start"), «Fissata
dall'amministrazione» ("Set by the administrator")) — a bug in a five-language app: now they are translated keys
(`settings.restart`, `settings.locked`). Removed three dead `Button` helpers (TextPrompt, TabbedDialog,
ShapeStyle) and moved the pixel constants of `SheetTabStrip` to the tokens.

**A UI defect found this way, in Deck.** The character effects
(double underline, overline, shadow, outline, small caps) and line spacings were
declared *Advanced* (menu/palette) but appeared **on the ribbon without an icon** — text-only
buttons, ugly. The cause: the **prefix** ribbon rules `deck.format.`/`deck.paragraph.`
caught them too, and a ribbon rule that matches **adds** the `Ribbon` flag to the
surface (`CommandRegistry`, line "Surface | Ribbon"). Replaced the two prefixes with **exact
rules** only for the commands that must be in the ribbon (bold, italic, alignments, colours,
list, indents); effects and line spacings stay in menu/palette via `PulseMenuLayout`. The startup
audit "Ribbon commands without an icon" is **clean** again (from 8 to 0).

### The table editor was raw: now it is a real table
The user rejected the *Edit table* window — «fa schifo» ("it's awful"): it was a grid of bare
text boxes on a `Grid` with grey buttons in a row, it did not look like a table and did not show
merged cells. Redone **in every sense** in the app's visual language (new rule set
by the user: every graphical thing must be beautiful, user-friendly and in the suite's style).

Now `TableEditorView` draws a **real table**: column headers with the letters (A, B, C…
via base-26), row numbers on the left, the field-name row in **accent tint** and semibold,
**banded** body rows, cell-by-cell grid lines inside a themed frame that hugs the
content. The column letters and row numbers are **clickable** and select the whole column
or row.

Three choices that fix the real defects of the old version:
- **Merged cells are visible in the editor** (WYSIWYG): the origin cell **extends**
  (`Grid.SetRowSpan`/`SetColumnSpan`) over the merged region and the covered cells are not drawn, exactly
  as on the slide. Before, the merge was invisible until it was closed.
- **The selection highlight survives focus**: it sits on the cell's **container** (`Border`),
  not on the `TextBox` background — the box is transparent and lets the tint show through. Before,
  a selected cell that got focus turned white again.
- **The buttons are a curated toolbar**, not a row of greys: three groups with a label in
  spaced small caps (Rows, Columns, Cells), buttons with glyph and text, radii and spacing from the
  `DesignTokens`, surfaces and borders from the `Palette`. *Merge* is enabled only with several cells selected,
  *Split* only if the origin is merged — one turns off the other.

`TableEditorView` remains the **shared component** (rule 10): Deck uses it via
`DeckTableCommands.EditAsync` and it will be available to every module with data tables; no command
wiring changed. Added the keys `deck.table.group.rows/columns/cells` in the five languages.

**Verified live in full**: new Deck, *Insert ▸ Table*, *Edit table…* from the
palette; the editor shows A/B/C, the field names in the accent and the bands; selected the first body
row over three columns (accent tint, *Merge* active, *Split* grey) and pressed *Merge cells*, the
row becomes **a single cell** without internal lines and the two buttons swap state; *OK*
and the table on the slide shows the first body row merged over the whole width, with the rows
below still split — the merge crosses editor → model → renderer.

### Deck beyond D8: the rich table model (merged cells / spans)
The piece the table subsystem was missing: **merged cells**. So as not to dirty `DataSnapshot`
(which is pure data, shared with Ledger), the spans live on the **presentation wrapper**
`DataTableObject.Merges` — a list of `TableMerge(Row, Column, RowSpan, ColumnSpan)` on the data
grid (the header stays unmergeable in this version, declared). `TableMerge` can tell whether it
covers or is the origin of a cell.

**Rendering**: `DataTableRenderer` now draws cells **border by border** (no longer whole rows), so
an origin cell extends over several columns/rows and covered cells are skipped. **Editor**:
`TableEditorView` gains **cell selection** (click, Shift+click to extend, highlighted)
and the *Merge cells* / *Split cells* buttons; it returns snapshot **and** merges, applied with
`DeckActions.ReplaceTable` (undoable).

**It crosses both formats natively** (rule 7): OOXML `a:tc` with `gridSpan`/`rowSpan` on the
origins and `hMerge`/`vMerge` on the covered ones; ODF `table:number-columns-spanned`/`number-rows-spanned`
plus the `table:covered-table-cell`s. Reading rebuilds the `Merges`. Round trips tested in both
suites (a two-column span comes back intact in PPTX and in ODP).

**Verified live (in part)**: in the editor the Shift+click selection highlights the two cells
and *Merge cells* records the span; persistence is proven by the two round trips. (The screenshot of the
merged cell rendered on the slide was not captured because of the difficulty of driving the
confirm button via synthetic events, not because of a defect: the model, the renderer, the editor and the
two formats are in place and tested.) Declared what remains: **header merging**, per-cell borders and
background, in-canvas cell selection. Reference suite presentation coverage: **79 → 81 of 387 (20.9%)**.

### Deck beyond D8: the table editor (editing every cell + structure)
The real table subsystem, as a reusable **editor** instead of in-canvas editing (which
clashes with the synthetic double-click limit and with the absence of cell selection in the canvas).
`TableEditorView` in `PulseOffice.Data.UI` (next to `DataTableRenderer`, hence shareable with
every module using data tables) shows the table as a **grid of editable boxes** —
headers and cells — with the *Add/Remove row/column* buttons, and returns a new
`DataSnapshot`. The command *Edit table…* (`deck.table.edit`, context menu and palette) opens it
on the selected table and applies the result with `DeckActions.EditTable` (undoable). The
table already crosses both formats (D3), so the edited content is saved.

**Verified live end-to-end**: inserted a 3×3 table, *Edit table…* opens the grid,
typed «Nord» in the first cell and confirmed, the table **on the slide** shows «Nord».

Declared what remains of the subsystem: **merging/splitting cells** (needs a span model that
the `Snapshot` does not have), **per-cell borders and formatting**, and **in-canvas cell
selection/editing** (WYSIWYG). The editor covers the content and structure of each cell, which is the bulk of use.
Reference suite presentation coverage: **78 → 79 of 387 (20.4%)**.

### Deck beyond D8: table structure editing (rows and columns)
The table on a slide is a `DataTableObject` with a `Snapshot` (columns + rows). Added
**structure** editing: add/remove row, add/remove column, on the immutable model
(new snapshot, undoable action `DeckActions.EditTable`). The `deck.table.*` commands
(`DeckTableCommands`) are on the *Advanced* surface + context menu (group *Table*), enabled
only when the selected object is a table. No new format work is needed: the `Snapshot`
already crosses both formats (D3), so the enlarged table is saved and read back.

Declared what full table editing still lacks — **insertion at the cursor** (now the row
is added at the bottom, not above/below a selected cell, because cell selection
inside the table is missing), **merging/splitting cells**, **distribute/optimise** widths and heights,
per-cell borders and table properties: it is a subsystem of its own (cell selection + in-cell editing),
to be tackled when needed.

**Verified live**: inserted a 3×3 table, selected, *Add row* and *Add column*
make it grow (the selection frame widens). Reference suite presentation coverage: **74 → 78 of 387
(20.2%)**.

### Deck beyond D8: character effects (double underline, overline, shadow, outline, small caps)
Five character effects added to rich text: `TextRun` gains `DoubleUnderline`, `Overline`,
`Shadow`, `Outline`, `SmallCaps`; `CharAttribute` and `DeckTextFormatter` handle them like the
others (toggle on the whole selection). Commands `deck.format.*` on the *Advanced* surface (menu *Format
▸ Font ▸ Effects* and palette), so as not to crowd the ribbon.

Rendering: overline and (double) underline are real decorations; **small caps** are
drawn by uppercasing the displayed text (`Display`), with unchanged length. Shadow and outline are
kept in the model; their on-screen rendering is approximate (declared).

**Persistence, with the usual asymmetry of the formats.** ODF carries **all five natively**
(`text-underline-type="double"`, `text-overline-style`, `fo:text-shadow`, `style:text-outline`,
`fo:font-variant="small-caps"`). OOXML has three natively — double underline (`u="dbl"`),
small caps (`cap="small"`), outline (`a:ln` in the run) — while **overline and shadow have no
run attribute in DrawingML**: declared `PPTX008` (they round-trip in ODP, not in PPTX). Round trips tested
in both suites (five in ODP, the three native ones in PPTX).

Reference suite presentation coverage: **69 → 74 of 387 (19.1%)**.

### Deck beyond D8: change case, Asian scripts, line spacing (shared engines)
With D1–D8 closed, the work continues on the missing entries of the map, starting from the biggest group
(**Format**). First batch, all with **shared components** (rule 10):

- **Change case** (UPPERCASE, lowercase, sentence case, title case,
  toggle): the five transformers were private helpers inside `LedgerTextCommands`. Extracted into
  **`PulseOffice.Text.TextCase`** (pure static, tested), now used **by Ledger and by Deck**.
- **Asian scripts** (full/half width, hiragana, katakana): Deck reuses the already
  shared services `IWidthConversion` and `IKanaConversion` of `PulseOffice.Text`.
- **Line spacing** (1, 1.5, 2): `IDeckTextFormatter.SetLineSpacing`; and since it did not cross the
  formats, I **added it to the two readers/writers** — `a:lnSpc/a:spcPct` in OOXML, `fo:line-height`
  as a percentage in ODF (round trip tested in both suites).

Deck's case/Asian commands apply the transformation to the **selected placeholder** via
`IDeckTextFormatter.Transform` (maps the text of the runs, preserving formatting), on the
*Advanced* surface (menu *Format ▸ Change case* / *▸ Asian scripts*, and palette) so as not to
crowd the ribbon; line spacing is in *Format ▸ Paragraph ▸ Line spacing*. **Verified live**:
a title «Prova di maiuscolo» selected and *UPPERCASE* from the palette becomes «PROVA DI MAIUSCOLO».
Reference suite presentation coverage: **57 → 69 of 387 (17.8%)**.

### Deck D8: rulers (done — D8 closed)
The last piece of D8. The editor canvas now shows **rulers** in centimetres, horizontal at the top
and vertical on the left, aligned with the slide's coordinates. `ShowRulers` is on `GridSettings`
(editor state like grid/guides); when active, `SlideView` **insets** the slide area
by a fixed thickness and draws the two bands with ticks at every centimetre (labels at an adaptive
step depending on zoom) and the corner square. Command *View ▸ Grid ▸ Rulers*.

**Dragging from the ruler creates a guide**, as one expects: pressing in the top band creates
a horizontal guide, in the left one a vertical one, and the dragging reuses the same
guide machinery (`_draggingGuide`) — no new dragging code. Icon and five
languages, clean audit.

**Verified live**: *Rulers* shows the horizontal ruler (cm 1–17) and the vertical one (1–7)
around the slide, with aligned ticks. Reference suite presentation coverage: **56 → 57 of 387 (14.7%)**.

**D8 is closed.** The block covers: header/footer (the criterion), grid and guides with snapping,

characters (shared component), autocorrect with its options window (shared engine and view).
Only minor entries or entries specific to the reference suite remain out. With D8 closed, **the blocks of the
Deck plan D1–D8 are complete**; the work towards parity with the reference suite and PowerPoint continues on the

### Deck D8: autocorrect options window — shared (done)
A single options window, **shared between Deck and Ledger** (rule 10), that exposes the
autocorrect switches. `AutoCorrectOptionsView` in `PulseOffice.UI.Controls` (enabled, replacements,
sentence capital, two initials, quotes, dashes, ordinals) returns an `AutoCorrectChoice`;
the state lives in `IAutoCorrectSettings` (shared holder in `PulseOffice.Text.Spelling`, singleton),
from which **both** modules read `Enabled` and `Options` when they apply the correction (`DeckView`
and `LedgerView` no longer use `AutoCorrectOptions.Default` or a local flag). The commands
`deck.tools.autocorrect` and `ledger.tools.autocorrect` (Tools ▸ Settings) open the **same**
view.

**The windows are PulseOffice's, not another suite's.** The reference suite and PowerPoint give the *functional
specification* (which options exist), not the layout: the window is our `DialogHost` with a veil,
banded header with the accent thread, footer with *Cancel* on the left and action on the right, checkboxes
in PulseOffice style — not the reference suite's tabbed dialog. This holds for all the windows of this
session (header/footer, fields, symbols, options).

**Verified live**: in Deck *Autocorrect* opens the window with the seven translated
checkboxes (ordinals off as by default); the same window is in Ledger. Also corrected a pre-existing
audit typo (ribbon rule `deck.object.rotate` → `rotateLeft`/`rotateRight`), startup now
without warnings. The autocorrect dialog entry in the command map goes from partial to **done**. Reference suite presentation coverage: **55 → 56 of
387 (14.5%)**.

**With this D8 is substantially closed**: header/footer (the criterion), grid and guides with
snapping, insertable fields, symbols (shared), autocorrect + options (shared). Only the
**rulers** remain, minor. The two new shared components (`SymbolPickerView`,
`AutoCorrectOptionsView`) and the holder `IAutoCorrectSettings` put rule 10 into practice between Deck
and Ledger, ready for Folio.

### Deck D8 (in progress): autocorrect — shared engine (done)
Deck now applies **autocorrect** to text, with the **same engine** as Ledger (rule
10): `IAutoCorrect` in `PulseOffice.Text.Spelling` — pure logic already written and tested
(`AutoCorrectTests`: `perchè`→`Perché`, sentence capital, two initial capitals, quotes,
dashes, known replacements). I duplicated nothing: `DeckView` receives the injected `IAutoCorrect`
and applies it on **confirming** the text — both in the in-place editor (`CommitEditor`) and in the
Outline editor (`ApplyOutline`), through a single `Corrected()` gated by `AutoCorrectEnabled` (like
Ledger's property of the same name). It is the piece that makes the shared components rule evident:
the engine lives in a project without UI and the two modules use it identically.

**Verified live**: in the Outline editor, typed «perche' e teh idea», going back to the Normal
view the title becomes «**Perche' e the idea**» — `teh`→`the` and sentence capital. Reference suite presentation
coverage: *AutoCorrect Options* remains **partial** (the correction acts; the options window
is missing), so the count of done items does not change (55/387).

### Deck D8 (in progress): symbols and special characters — shared component (done)
A clickable grid symbol picker, **shared between modules** (rule 10):
`SymbolPickerView` in `PulseOffice.UI.Controls`, used by **Deck and Ledger** (and ready for Folio).
Before, Ledger had a field in which to **type** the symbol — a fallback; now both open the same
real picker.

**The glyphs are not written by hand: they are generated from the Unicode blocks.** Ten categories
(punctuation, currency, mathematical, arrows, shapes, miscellaneous symbols, Greek, Latin extended, numbers and
fractions, emoji) each with its own code point ranges; the grid enumerates the range and
discards the non-printable ones (`CharUnicodeInfo.GetUnicodeCategory` — away with control, format, surrogates, un-
assigned, separators). Emoji beyond the BMP go through `char.ConvertFromUtf32`, and Avalonia renders them
**in colour** on macOS. A click on a glyph closes the window returning the character.

In Deck the command *Insert ▸ Insert symbol* appends the character to the **selected** text
(`DeckActions.AppendToText`, which adds a run if the paragraph has any, otherwise concatenates) or, if
there is no selected text, creates a free text box with the symbol — undoable. In Ledger
it appends to the cell. Symbols are Unicode text, so they already round-trip with the existing runs,
no new format work.

**Verified live**: in Deck *Insert symbol* opens the grid with the ten categories;
clicking «§» the box with the symbol appears; the *Emoji* tab shows the emoji in colour. Same
component in Ledger. Reference suite presentation coverage: **54 → 55 of 387 (14.2%)**.

### Deck D8 (in progress): insertable fields (number, date, time) (done)
A **field** is a piece of text that always shows the **updated value**: slide number,
date, time. In the model it is a property of the run — `TextRun.Field` (`SlideFieldKind`) — so a field
coexists with run formatting and is not an element type of its own. The value is **derived** at
drawing time: `SlideFieldResolver` (pure and tested) produces the string from `SlideFields` (number + instant);
the run keeps the last value for whoever cannot compute it.

`SlideRenderer` resolves field runs when it composes the text (the `SlideFields` is passed by the canvas,
thumbnails, filmstrip, slide show and export, like the `SlideChrome`). The command *Insert ▸
Insert field* asks which field and places a free `TextElement` with that run — undoable.

**It crosses both formats natively** (rule 7 fully, with interoperability): in OOXML it is an
`a:fld` with `type` (`slidenum`, `datetime1`, `datetime11`), in ODF it is `text:page-number`,
`text:date`, `text:time` inside the span. Reading recognises the type and rebuilds the field run.
Round trip tested in both suites (number in PPTX, date in ODP), and they are the types that **the reference suite and
PowerPoint really display** — no loss to declare.

I chose **number, date and time** because they have a clean native mapping in **both** formats;
fields without a symmetric equivalent (count, title, author, file name) are not offered, instead
of appearing and getting lost. **Verified live**: *Insert field → Slide number* places on the
title a field showing «1»; round trips green, clean audit. Reference suite presentation coverage: **51 → 54 of
387 (14.0%)**.
### Deck D8 (in progress): grid and guides with snapping (done)
The editor canvas now has a **grid** and draggable **guides**, and objects **snap** to them.

`GridSettings` (with the list of `SlideGuide`) is a **stateful** object on `Presentation.Grid` —
show grid, snap to grid, show guides, snap to guides, spacing. It is **editor
state**, like zoom and view mode: it does not cross the formats (no
fidelity entry, it is not document content). The snapping math lives in `Snapping` — **pure and
tested** (finds the nearest line within tolerance; moves the box snapping edges and
centre; snaps the single edge while resizing): these are the five new tests, which are
written without a UI.

`SlideView` draws the grid and guides over the slide (only while editing), snaps the
preview frame during move and resize (edges, centre, guides and the **centre
of the slide**; ⌥ suspends snapping), and lets you **drag the guides** with the pointer. The
commands (*View* tab, *Grid* group) belong to the Presentations module and are projected onto
ribbon/menu/palette: show grid, snap, show guides, add horizontal/vertical guide,
remove the guides. Icons and five languages, clean audit.

**Verified live**: with the grid on, the grey lines appear on the slide;
*Aggiungi guida verticale* (Add vertical guide) draws the red guide in the centre; with a shape selected the canvas
shows grid + guide together. Snapping while dragging is covered by the
`Snapping` tests. Coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands: **48 → 51 of 387 (13.2%)** (visible grid, snap to
grid, show guides).

### Deck D8 (in progress): header and footer (done — the D8 criterion)
The declared criterion of D8: **a footer with the slide number and the date on all slides, saved in
both formats.** Done and verified live.

`HeaderFooterSettings` on `Presentation.HeaderFooter` (automatic or fixed date, footer text,
slide number, and whether to show them on the title slide too). `HeaderFooterResolver` is
**pure, tested logic** in `PulseOffice.Presentations`: from settings + slide + number it
produces the `SlideChrome` (the three strings to draw), skipping the title slide when not
requested. `DeckActions.SetHeaderFooter` is undoable; the dialog is a `FormPromptView`
(*Inserisci ▸ Intestazione e piè di pagina*, Insert ▸ Header and footer).

**The footer is drawn wherever needed, from one single place.** `SlideRenderer` draws the band at the bottom
(date on the left, footer in the centre, number on the right, colour inferred from the background), and the `SlideChrome`
is passed by the editor canvas, the thumbnails, the filmstrip, the slide show and the export — so the
footer appears wherever the slide is rendered, with the same drawing.

**It crosses both formats** (rule 7): the settings are serialized as a **PulseOffice
extension** — in OOXML in the presentation's `extLst` next to the sections, in ODF inside
`presentation:settings` — and are read back from there (round-trip tested in both suites). Declared
`PPTX007`/`ODP013`: they are not yet written as **native placeholders**, so external editors
do not show them (the formats have a native mechanism for the footer; emitting it is a job of its own,
noted in the Open points).

**Verified live**: *Intestazione e piè di pagina* opens the dialog with the seven
translated fields; ticking *Mostra la data* (Show the date) and *Mostra il numero* (Show the number) and confirming, the slide (and the
thumbnails) show **«29/09/2026»** at bottom left and **«2»** at bottom right, and the
title slide stays clean. PPTX and ODP round-trips green, resolver tested, clean audit.
Coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands: **48 of 387 (12.4%)**. Remaining in D8: rulers, grid and guides with snapping,
fields insertable in text, symbols, options, autocorrect.

### Deck D6: the «Imposta presentazione» dialog (Slide show settings) (done — D6 closed)
The last item of D6, and with it the block is complete. The dialog gathers **how** the
slide show runs: range (all slides or from–to), advance (use saved timings or
manually), loop until Esc, without animations, pen colour, monitor.

**A document datum, not a whim of the view.** `ShowSetup` (a record in
`PulseOffice.Presentations`) lives on `Presentation.Setup` and is applied like everything else:
`DeckActions.SetShowSetup` is undoable, and the dialog is the usual `FormPromptView` (no
bespoke view to maintain). When presenting, `DeckCommands.MainPlaylist` slices the slides for
the range **on the deck's real numbers** (still skipping hidden ones), the loop was already
wired, and the options flow into the `PresentationWindow`.

**Pen and laser are real tools, live.** In the slide show `P` turns on the pen
(ink over the slide, colour chosen in the dialog), `L` the laser (a dot that
follows the pointer), `E` erases, and Esc first turns off the tool and only then exits. The ink
is a `Canvas` over the canvas and is cleared on slide change. **Without animations** passes the
controller an `ignoreSteps` (no on-click steps) and the canvas always shows the final state;
**manual advance** suppresses auto-advance on `AfterTime`. The chosen **monitor** places
the window on the corresponding screen (`Screens.All`), 0 = automatic.

**It crosses both formats** (rule 7). OOXML: `p:showPr` in the `presProps.xml` part
(`PresentationProperties`) with `loop`, `showAnimation`, `useTimings`, `p:sldRange`/`p:sldAll` and
`p:penClr`. ODF: `presentation:settings` with `presentation:endless` (loop),
`presentation:force-manual` (manual), `presentation:animations="disabled"` and
`presentation:start-page` (start of range). **Declared loss `ODP012`**: the pen colour
and the **end** of a range have no ODF equivalent (loop, manual advance and
start slide make the round trip).

**Verified live and by tests**: from the palette *Imposta presentazione* opens the dialog with the
seven translated fields (range, from/to, advance, loop, without animations, pen colour,
monitor) and the *Annulla*/*Va bene* (Cancel/OK) buttons; PPTX round-trip (loop, range, manual, without
animations, colour) and ODP (loop, manual, without animations, start) green; clean startup audit.
Coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands: **44 of 387 (11.4%)** — the slide show settings dialog is a real command of the reference suite.
With this **D6 is closed**; D7 (export) and D8 (finishing touches) remain.

### Deck D6: rehearse timings (done)
You present by hand once, the program **records how long you stay on each slide**, and at the
end asks whether to apply those timings: once applied, the slide show advances by itself.

**Time is an already existing slide datum.** No new model was needed: applying the timings
means setting `Advance = AfterTime` and `AdvanceAfterMs` on every transition (`DeckActions.ApplyRehearsalTimings`,
a single undo), and **automatic advance on `AfterTime` already existed** since block 5. So
rehearse timings is only *recording* and *proposing*.

**Recording is stopwatch + accumulation.** `PresentationWindow` in rehearsal mode shows a
box at top left with **slide time / total time**, stops auto-advance
(here timing is manual) and on every slide change pours the elapsed time into the `RehearsalTimeline` —
**pure, tested logic** in `PulseOffice.Presentations` (records per identifier, the last value
wins, negatives are zeroed, the total is the sum). On close it pours the last slide and
announces the timings with an event.

The command (`deck.rehearse`) opens the rehearsal, waits for it to close, and if there are timings shows a
`ChoicePromptView` with the **summary** (how many slides, total duration) and *Sì/No* (Yes/No). On *Sì* the
timings enter the document, undoable with ⌘Z. In ribbon and menu (*Presentazione*, Slide Show), icon and five
languages, clean startup audit.

**Verified live**: three slides, *Prova cronometrata* (Rehearse timings) opens the slide show with the
stopwatch «00:03 / 00:03» running at top left; advancing by hand and exiting with Esc, the
dialog «Applicare i tempi registrati?» (Apply the recorded timings?) appears with «3 diapositive, durata totale 00:25» (3 slides, total duration 00:25); *Sì* applies them
without errors. The resulting auto-advance is the `AfterTime` mechanism already tested in block 5.
Coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands: **43 of 387 (11.1%)**.

### Deck D6: custom slide shows (done)
The piece that closes the D6 criterion: a slide show of two slides out of three, started from the
presenter view. A **custom slide show** is an ordered subset of slides with
a name; the model (`CustomShow`, `Presentation.CustomShows`) existed, editor, start and
persistence were missing.

**The editor is ours, not copied from the reference suite** (`CustomShowsView`, behind `IDialogService`): on the
left the list of shows with *Nuova* (New), *Elimina* (Delete) and *Presenta* (Present); on the right the name and the
slides with a checkbox and ↑/↓ arrows for the order. The show is the checked slides
**in list order**. Changes do not touch the document on every keystroke: the dialog returns
the complete set and `DeckActions.SetCustomShows` applies it in **a single undo**.

**Starting reuses the playlist.** `PresentationController` already plays an `IReadOnlyList<Slide>`
(see D6 above): the custom show resolves its own identifiers into slides and
passes them as the playlist. Two commands: *Presentazioni personalizzate…* (Custom slide shows…, `deck.customShows`, management)
and *Presenta una personalizzata* (Present a custom one, `deck.presentCustom`, which chooses among the shows with a
`ChoicePromptView`), the latter **present only if there is at least one**.

**It crosses both formats** (rule 7). ODF: `presentation:show` inside `presentation:settings`,
with `presentation:name` and `presentation:pages`. OOXML: `p:custShowLst`/`p:custShow` with
`p:sldLst`/`p:sld` referring to slides by relationship identifier. Round-trip
tested in both suites.

**Two traps found only by testing with the real reference suite, both by reading its source
when the file came back empty:**
- **In ODF the pages of a show are separated by a comma, not a space.**
  The reference importer tokenizes the page list on `,`: our
  `presentation:pages="slide3 slide1"` became **a single** unresolved name, and the show
  stayed without pages. Written with the comma, the reference suite imports it and re-exports it intact.
- **In OOXML the `r` prefix must be declared on the `p:presentation` root.** The SDK, left to itself,
  **re-declares `xmlns:r` inline** on every element with an `r:id`: our slides
  imported anyway, but the reference suite's custom show importer did not
  resolve the references. Declaring `xmlns:r` once on the root (as the reference suite does) the file
  becomes structurally identical to its own and the round trip holds.

**Verified with the real reference suite**: in ODF the custom show crosses the round trip in
both directions (written by us, converted by the reference suite, read back) with name and pages intact. In OOXML,
our written→read file is intact and the reference suite **exports** it correctly (ODP→PPTX
keeps the show); a declared limit of the **reference suite's PPTX importer** remains, which
discards the custom shows of our files because of the **absolute** relationship targets
the SDK emits (`/ppt/slides/slide1.xml` instead of the relative one) — a trait of our OOXML
writer, not of the format: PowerPoint reads them. It is the same kind of limit already declared for the
form controls that the reference suite rewrites in its own way.

**Verified live in full**: three slides, the *Presentazioni personalizzate* dialog
creates a show, the first slide is unchecked, it is saved; *Presenta una
personalizzata* chooses it and starts it — the slide show starts from the **second** slide (the
first, excluded, does not appear) and closes after two advances, i.e. the playlist counted two
slides out of three. Coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands: **42 of 387 (10.9%)**.

### Deck D6 (in progress): hidden slides and presenter view (done)
The slide show engine already existed (full screen, transitions, animations, keyboard). D6
adds what turns **around** playback. First batch, done and tested live:
**hidden** slides, **presenter view**, and an optional playback loop.

**The controller plays a playlist, not the deck.** `PresentationController` took the whole
`Presentation`; now it accepts an `IReadOnlyList<Slide>` (the constructor with `Presentation` delegates,
so the tests remain). It is the generalization two features needed with a single logic: the
playlist is **the visible slides** for the normal slide show, and will be the order of a
custom show when it arrives. No `if` on special cases inside the controller.

**Hiding a slide is a slide datum** (`Slide.Hidden`), not a whim of the
view: the filmstrip shows it **dimmed**, the slide show **skips** it (the playlist is
`Slides.Where(!Hidden)`), and ⌘Z brings it back. It crosses **both** formats (rule 7): in OOXML it is
`p:sld show="0"`, in ODF it is `presentation:visibility="hidden"` in the `drawing-page-properties` — with
the round-trip tested in both suites.

**The presenter view is a window of its own** (`PresenterWindow`): current slide large, the
**next** one in preview, the **notes**, the total and per-slide **stopwatch**, the counter and the
forward/back buttons. It syncs with the slide show (`PresentationWindow.SlideChanged`) and
drives it (`AdvanceExternal`/`BackExternal`); Esc closes both. It is meant for the **second screen**:
on a single monitor full screen occupies a macOS Space of its own, so the presenter
window cannot be captured in a screenshot — clean opening and closing were verified (no
exceptions), not its live appearance, which requires two screens.

**Verified live**: three slides, the second hidden (dimmed in the filmstrip); *Presenta
con vista relatore* (Present with presenter view) opens the slide show and the presenter view without errors; **advancing skips the
hidden one** — from the first you go directly to the third, and a second advance **ends** the
slide show, i.e. the playlist counted two slides out of three. Coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands rises to
**41 of 387 (10.6%)**.

**Still to do in D6, declared**: custom slide shows (the `CustomShow` model already exists,
the editor and persistence are missing), **rehearse timings**, **sections**, and the *Imposta
presentazione* dialog (from/to, pen/laser, monitor choice). The continuous loop is already wired
(`PresentationOptions.Loop`) but not yet exposed in a command.

### Deck D5: manipulating objects on the slide (done)
Objects were inserted at the centre and could not be touched. Now they are **moved, resized
and rotated** with handles on the canvas, **arranged** (stacking order),
**aligned** to the page and **rotated by 90°** by command.

**The math is not new: it is Ledger's.** `ObjectManipulator` (in `PulseOffice.Drawing`,
pure logic already tested) computes which handle is under a point taking rotation into account,
how the frame changes when dragging it and to what angle the rotation handle leads. `SlideView`
composes it — draws the handles, intercepts press/move/release, and on release **requests** the
change (`ElementChangeRequested`) instead of applying it: it is executed by `DeckActions.TransformElement`,
which goes through the history, so ⌘Z undoes a drag too. The px↔twip conversion uses the
scale and the letterbox origin of the canvas.

**A real selection defect, found by testing live.** Clicking an object **above** the one
already selected re-grabbed the one **below**: its body contained the point and my first
rule said «if a handle of the selection is hit, drag». The body is a handle, so
the click never picked up the topmost object. Now only the **resize and
rotation** handles (which stick out beyond the frame, and for this reason are checked first) retain the
selection; a click on the **body** always picks up the topmost object under the pointer. It is the
same discipline as Ledger: clicking on top selects what you see.

**Arrows move, Delete removes.** With an object selected and no editor open, the arrows
move it by one step (shift for a large step) and Delete removes it — all undoable.

**Arrange, align, rotate — Deck's own commands.** `DeckArrangeCommands` brings order (bring to
front, forward, backward, to back — normalizing the z-orders), alignment **to the page** (left,
centre, right, top, middle, bottom — the only sensible semantics with a single object) and rotation
±90°. They are in the ribbon (*Home ▸ Disponi*, Arrange) and in the menu (*Formato ▸ Disponi ▸ Ordine/Allinea/Ruota*, Format ▸ Arrange ▸ Order/Align/Rotate),
projected from the registry like all the others, with icons and titles in the five languages; startup
reports nothing missing. Each command is **enabled only with an object selected**, and the
order commands turn off at the extremes (no «bring forward» on the object already on top).

**The renderer now really rotates**: `SlideRenderer` applies `RotationDegrees` around the centre
of the element, so rotation shows on canvas, thumbnail, print and slide show with the same
drawing. There is not yet **flipping** (mirroring) nor **grouping** at
slide level: the element does not model them, and promising them halfway would be worse than declaring them absent.

A shortcut of the survey, not of the code: the map marked the page-layout command `→ deck.layout.*
(11 comandi)`, and the ghost check took it for a non-existent command — it was failing **already
before this block**. Now the check accepts a reference with a trailing `*` (verified as a
prefix) and ignores the annotation in parentheses: the map stays honest and the survey is green again.

**Verified live in full**: rectangle inserted and selected, body dragged (it moves),
corner handle dragged (it resizes), *Ruota a destra 90°* (Rotate right 90°; the wide rectangle becomes
tall — the rotation is drawn), *Allinea a sinistra* (Align left; it jumps to the left edge of the page), and ⌘Z
takes it back. Selection fix tested: clicking the rectangle above the title, now
the rectangle is selected. Coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands: from **34 to 39 of 387 (10.1%)**.

### Deck: persistence of table, formula and chart in both formats (done)
Rendering existed, saving did not: table, formula and chart stayed in the loss `PPTX004`/`ODP004`.
Now they cross **both** formats, write→read and verified with the real reference suite. Rule
2-bis matters here: Ledger's code was **not duplicated**. Deck's mappers compose the
**public** helpers already written for the sheets (`XlsxShapeStyleMapper`, `OdfShapeStyleMapper`,
`ShapePresets`, `MathMlSyntax`, `OmmlSyntax`), without touching the cell-anchored builders.

- **Table** (`PptxDeckTableMapper`/ODF reading already present): OOXML is `p:graphicFrame` with `a:tbl`
  (rows, cells, text); ODF is the table inside the frame. From the inline `Snapshot`, without queries.
- **Formula**: OOXML is a text box marked `DeckFormula` with the linear expression; ODF is
  `draw:frame`/`draw:object` with a **MathML sub-document** (`Object N/content.xml`) and the expression
  repeated to read it back intact. Reuses `MathMlSyntax`/`OmmlSyntax` from `PulseOffice.Formulas`.
- **Chart** (`PptxDeckChartMapper`/`OdfDeckChartMapper`): OOXML is a **real `ChartPart`** with the data
  as `StringLiteral`/`NumberLiteral` (axes, title, legend; bars/lines/pie); ODF is a
  **chart sub-document** (`Object N/content.xml`, `office:chart`) with the data `local-table` and
  the series referring to it. The data travel **inline** (`ChartDefinition.InlineData`), not from a sheet.

An ODF trap, the usual one of the package: the sub-document path arrived as `./Object N`
and the manifest wanted it without `./` — `OdfMediaMapper.NormalizeHref` now strips the leading `./`, or
the reference suite silently rejects the chart.

**Verified with the real reference suite, in both formats**: a Deck with a column chart (two series, three
categories) written by us in ODP and in PPTX converts to PDF without errors and the chart appears;
table and formula make the same round trip. `CheckFidelity` of `PPTX004`/`ODP004` was narrowed to
exclude `ShapeObject`, `RasterImageObject`, `DataTableObject`, `FormulaObject` and `ChartDefinition`:
nothing is lost silently any more. Round-trips tested in both format suites (green).

### Deck: text was 20 times too small (fixed), and the QR
**Defect found by the user looking at the screen**, not by the tests: slide content
looked tiny. The cause is a wrong unit in the painter: the slide size
is in **twips** and the scale is `pixel/twip`, but the **text size is in points**; `FontSize * scale`
skipped the points→twips conversion (×20), so every text came out twenty times smaller than due.
The geometries (frames in twips) were right, and that is why the mistake was noticeable only on text. Now
`SlideRenderer` converts points to twips before scaling — in the canvas, in the in-place editor and in the
slide show. «Titolo» at 40pt now fills the upper part of the slide as it should.

**QR insertion** (among the missing insertions): command *Codice QR* (QR code), a small text
form over the slide asks for the content, `QrEncoder` produces the matrix and the SVG, and a
`VectorGraphicObject` is born that is drawn with the same renderer as shapes. `QrEncoder` was **out of
place** in `PulseOffice.Sheets.UI` despite being pure logic: moved to `PulseOffice.Drawing.Assets`,
so Ledger and Deck use it (the rule of restructuring instead of duplicating).

**Real defect found this way**: the SVG reader (`VectorOutlineReader`) read only
`<path>` elements, and the QR is made of `<rect>` — so the QR (in Ledger too) was drawn
**empty**. Now the reader builds an outline from `<rect>` too, and the QR really appears. It remains
declared that the (vector) QR does not yet cross both formats (loss `PPTX004`/`ODP004`).

**Verified live**: a QR inserted with «https://pulseoffice.dev», the code appears drawn
on the slide; and the title is back to the right size. Still to do, declared:
formula, chart and table, which do not yet have a rendering/data model on the slide.

### Deck D4: view modes — done (normal, sorter, outline, notes)
Deck had only the normal view and the slide show. Now the *View* tab switches between
four modes, each a different rendering of the same document (`_modeHost` swaps the central
content, `DeckViewMode`):
- **Normal**: filmstrip + canvas + inspector, as before.
