- **Slide sorter**: grid of large thumbnails, with **reordering by drag**.
  The trap solved: Avalonia **captures the pointer** on the pressed element, so the release
  goes back to the starting thumbnail, not to the target one — the target is found by **hit-testing**
  the release position on the panel, not with the event of the thumbnail under the pointer. And
  the view is not rebuilt on press, otherwise the drag is interrupted halfway.
- **Outline**: a text editor showing the titles (and the indented bodies); on
  confirmation it rewrites titles and bodies of the existing slides (`ApplyOutline` → `SetSlideText`).
- **Notes**: the slide above, the speaker notes area below (`Slide.Notes`, undoable
  via `SetNotes`).

The commands belong to the Presentations module and are projected onto the ribbon and menus like all others;
**the command of the active mode is disabled** (`ViewMode() != this`) — the rule of
context sensitivity. A name collision fixed: the *Progettazione* (Design) tab and the
*Struttura* (Outline) view were both «Struttura» in Italian.

**Master postponed**: the master view (editable slide/notes/handout) is the biggest
and least used piece; the master model already exists, its editing view is a block of its own.

**Verified live**: with three slides, *Ordine diapositive* (Slide sorter) shows them in a grid and
dragging the third to the top really reorders them; *Note* shows the slide and the notes area;
*Struttura* opens the text editor. 508 commands, clean startup audit.

Measured coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands: from **26 to 30 of 387 (7.8 %)**.

### Deck D3: object insertion — done (shapes and images)
Cross-app objects now land on slides, with the same idea as the rest of the project:
they are `EmbeddedObject`, so the same object lives in Ledger and in Deck without new code. D3
**inserts, draws, selects and saves them in both formats** — shapes and images in full; charts,
tables, formulas and vector objects stay declared as a loss until their
model arrives (they have no native equivalent on a slide: the chart wants sheet+range, the
table a query).

**Insertion** (`DeckInsertCommands`, our Insert tab): eleven shapes (rectangle, ellipse,
triangle, diamond, hexagon, star, arrow, chevron, callout, line, rounded rectangle),
text box, image from file (`RasterImageObject` via StorageProvider). `DeckActions.InsertObject/
DeleteObject` are undoable; the `ObjectElement` is drawn with Ledger's `DrawingObjectRenderer`,
already wired. **Selection** generalized to any element (dashed outline); *delete
object* is enabled only with an object selected — the rule of context sensitivity.

**Persistence in both formats, without touching Ledger's mappers**: the public, reusable
pieces are composed — `XlsxShapeStyleMapper`/`OdfShapeStyleMapper` (fill, outline, effects,
text), `ShapePresets` (preset name in both directions) — inside **slide-native** wrappers
(`p:sp`/`p:pic` for OOXML, `draw:custom-shape`/`draw:frame` for ODF) instead of the sheet's cell
anchors. Shapes carry geometric preset, style and text; images the bytes (image part in
OOXML, `Pictures/` in ODF). Losses narrowed to `PPTX004`/`ODP004`: charts, tables, formulas and
vectors.

**The trap solved, and instructive**: the reference suite, converting ODP→PPTX, **removes all the
`p:ph`** from placeholders — so the reader, which told inserted shapes and placeholders apart by the presence
of `p:ph`, took title and subtitle for shapes. The classification now has three steps: a
**marker** on the shapes we write (`Name="DeckShape"`), then the **geometry** (a non-rectangular
preset is a shape), finally the text (a rectangle with text and without a marker is a
placeholder). So our round trip is exact for every type, and the reference suite's files are read back without
mixing up placeholders and shapes.

**Verified live and with the real reference suite, in both directions.** Live: from the Insert tab a
rectangle appears blue on the slide, a click selects it, *Elimina oggetto* (Delete object) removes it. With
the reference suite: a red ellipse with the text «Ciao», written by us in ODP and converted to PPTX, comes back
ellipse/Ciao/#C0392B; and the same from PPTX to ODP comes back identical. Our round-trip (write→read)
intact for shape (type, text, colour) and image (bytes) in both formats; four tests.

Measured coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands: from **24 to 26 of 387 (6.7 %)** — the number grows little
because in the reference suite shapes are not menu items (they are in a toolbar), but the **capability** is large.

### Deck D2: rich text formatting — done
Slide text now carries **run formatting**, no longer only per paragraph. The
model has `TextRun` (character, size, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, superscript/subscript,
colour, font) inside `TextParagraph`, which stays backward compatible: without runs, the paragraph
is a single run with its default values. `IDeckTextFormatter` is **pure, tested logic**:
it applies an attribute to the **selection** (splitting runs at the boundaries) or to the whole placeholder,
with Ledger's toggle semantics (if all covered runs are already bold, it turns off).

**Commands** (twenty, Home tab): *Carattere* (Character) — bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, superscript,
subscript, grow, shrink, five colours; *Paragrafo* (Paragraph) — align left/centre/right,
justify, bulleted list, increase/decrease indent. The selection of a placeholder (single click,
dashed outline) is the target; while editing text, the range selected
in the box becomes the target (previous runs are lost when the text is confirmed — a
declared limit of D2, because the text→run diff is not yet written).

**Rendering draws the runs**: `SlideRenderer` builds a `FormattedText` per paragraph and applies
weight, style, font, size, colour and decorations per run range; superscript and subscript
shrink (the vertical offset is approximated, declared).

**Persistence in both formats** (rule 7): ODP writes a `text:span` per run with a style of
family *text* (bold, italic, underline `text-underline-style`, strikethrough
`text-line-through-style`, superscript/subscript `text-position`), OOXML an `a:r` with `a:rPr` per run
(`b`, `i`, `u`, `strike`, `baseline`) plus bullets (`a:buChar`/`a:buNone`). Symmetric
reading in both. Round-trip tests of the runs in both formats.

**Verified live, with the strongest test — the file saved by the app.** In Deck: typed
«Titolo D2» in the title, selected the placeholder (dashed outline), pressed **Bold**
in the ribbon (`deck.format.bold` in the registry) and **Grow** several times. Saved as ODP
**by the app**, the `content.xml` contains the span with `font-weight="bold"`; converted by the reference suite
to PPTX, the shape comes back with `b="1"` and `sz="7080"` — bold and enlarged size survive the
round trip. Five tests on the formatter, two run round-trip tests.

Measured coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands: from **9 to 24 of 387 (6.2 %)**.

### Deck D1: the command surface (ribbon, menus, palette) — done
The block that fixes the rejected UX. Deck now has **its own command surface**, designed
by us with Ledger's infrastructure (`CommandRegistry`, `ICommandLayout`), **not copied from
the reference suite**: 33 commands of the Presentations module projected onto ribbon, menus, palette and
shortcuts without code dedicated to each surface.

**Deck's ribbon** (our tabs and our names): **Home** (Slides group: new,
duplicate, delete, move up/down), **Struttura** (Design; Layout: the eleven; Themes: Chiaro/Ardesia/Sabbia — Light/Slate/Sand),
**Transizioni** (Transitions; the eleven types), **Animazioni** (Animations; add, play), **Inserisci** (Insert; Media),
**Presentazione** (Slide Show; start, from current). The menus: *Diapositiva* (Slide; Manage, Order, Layout, Theme,
Transition, Animation), *Inserisci ▸ Media*, *Visualizza ▸ Presentazione* (View ▸ Slide Show).

**How, without copying the reference suite:** the inspector's scattered buttons become `CommandDefinition`
with `Module = Presentations`; an `IActiveDeckContext` (like Ledger's `IActiveSheetContext`) holds
the active deck and the current slide — the `DeckView` announces itself in `OnAttachedToVisualTree` and
the commands act on it. The layout rules are in `PulseRibbonLayout`/
`PulseMenuLayout` (ours, not the reference suite's menus); the icons in `DeckIcons`, one per command
identifier; the titles are derived keys `command.deck.<id>.title` in the five languages.
**Enabling** is real: «Sposta giù» (Move down) is grey on the last slide, a theme is grey if it is
the active one, «Elimina» (Delete) is grey with a single slide.

**Verified live**: opening a Deck the ribbon fills with Deck's seven tabs, the
palette finds «Duplica diapositiva» (Duplicate slide) under *Diapositiva › Gestisci*, and both from the ribbon
(`deck.slide.add`) and from the palette (`deck.slide.duplicate`) the commands run and the filmstrip
shows the new slide; startup reports no command without title, icon or rule (clean
audit), 469 commands registered.

Measured coverage of the reference suite's presentation commands: from **2 to 9 of 387 (2.3 %)** — D1 is above all
the infrastructure and a first set; the real jumps are D2 (rich text) and D3 (object insertion).

### Deck: honest assessment and the real plan (survey of the reference suite)
The user rejected Deck's UX, rightly: **its own ribbon and menus are missing**, and with them
almost all features. The survey redone on the **reference suite's real presentation menu**
(its menu bar definition plus its command lists) gives
**387 commands**, of which today **2 done** (0.5 %). The reference suite is the functional specification; **the
layout of Deck's menus and ribbon is ours**, as for Ledger — neither the structure nor the
code of the reference suite or PowerPoint is copied. The area-by-area study was in
a former survey document, the ordered plan is in
[docs/deck-plan.md](docs/deck-plan.md), and the measurable map was in a former survey map with
its survey script.

**The three gaps that each weigh more than a hundred items:** Deck's **command surface** does not exist
(two commands, F5 and ⇧F5, no ribbon or menu — it is the foundation of everything else); **rich
text formatting** does not exist (character, paragraph, lists, line spacing, colour);
**object insertion** on the slide does not exist (image, table, chart, shape, text
box, fontwork, formula, QR, comment — almost all already present in the project as `EmbeddedObject`,
but without the way to place them on a slide).

**Plan in eight blocks** (detail in [docs/deck-plan.md](docs/deck-plan.md)), in order of what
unlocks the rest: **D1** command surface (ribbon+menus+palette, ours) — it is the block that
fixes the rejected UX; **D2** rich text; **D3** object insertion; **D4** view modes (sorter,
outline, notes, master); **D5** object manipulation (arrange, align, group, rotate); **D6**
complete slide show and presenter view; **D7** export (PDF/images/video); **D8** finishing touches (fields,
headers/footers, grid/guides, options). Rule 7 as always: every feature crosses ODP **and**
PPTX or the loss is declared. Coverage is **measured, not promised**.

### Deck, block 6: media, sounds and events (done)
The last declared block. Three things, all with rule 7 as the gate: either they cross
both formats, or the loss is declared with its code.

**Events (on-click actions).** A shape can carry an interaction — go to next
slide, previous, first, last; stop the slide show; link; run macro;
play sound; go to a slide. ODF writes them as `office:event-listeners` with
`presentation:event-listener` inside the frame; OOXML as `a:hlinkClick` with the
`ppaction://…` actions and links as an external relationship. One mapper per format, used by
writer and reader. **In the slide show the click follows the action** (the navigations and stop),
otherwise it advances. In the editor the inspector has an *Interazioni* (Interactions) section: one drop-down per shape.
Declared losses: none in ODF; in OOXML `go to slide` and `play sound` degrade
(PPTX003), the other actions make the full round trip.

**Media (audio and video).** A `MediaElement` carries the bytes **inside** the document. ODF writes it
as `draw:frame`/`draw:plugin` with the file in `Media/` and the manifest entry; OOXML as
`p:pic` with `a:videoFile`/`a:audioFile`, the embedded media part, the relationship and a
fallback poster. The renderer draws it as a plate with the play triangle
(video) or the note (audio), with the same canvas for editor and slide show; the editor inserts it
from file (the bytes enter the document). Round-trip in both formats.

**Sounds.** The transition sound: ODF writes it as `presentation:sound` and reads it back; in
OOXML it is declared a loss (PPTX006, an embedded audio part would be needed: our model
holds a reference, not the sound's bytes). The sound of a *play sound* interaction makes the
round trip in ODF as `presentation:sound` inside the listener.

**Verified with the real reference suite, in both directions.** The interaction and the media survive the
PPTX→ODP round trip; the media in **both** directions with bytes intact; the transition sound in ODP.
A limit **of the reference suite, not ours**: converting ODP→PPTX, it **discards** the
on-click action (in the PPTX it produces only the film's `ppaction://media` remains) — our
write→read round-trip instead keeps it in both formats. Tests: interactions (eight ODP, seven
PPTX), media (one ODP, two PPTX), transition sound (ODP), plus the model tests on
`SetInteraction`/`RemoveInteraction` and on the clone that re-identifies the media and keeps its
interaction.

**With this the six blocks *of my initial plan* are closed — but it is not parity with
PowerPoint.** It was a mistake to imply that Deck was finished: those six blocks built
the **invisible foundations** (document, two formats, playback), not the surface
the user uses. The honest assessment and the real plan are below, in «Deck: honest assessment».

### Deck, block 5: slide show mode (done)
The full-screen slide show. A **pure, tested controller** (`PresentationController`) holds
the slide and the **step** within the slide (the on-click groups of the animations): advancing
reveals the next group, and only when the slide is fully revealed does it move to the next one;
going back does the opposite. The `PresentationWindow` is a full-screen window on a black
background that draws the slide letterboxed with the **same renderer** as the editor: slide show
mode is not a second rendering, it is the same one.

**Animations play step by step**: revealing a group, the canvas animates from its start
to its end with the scheduler already written, then stops; elements of later groups stay
hidden until their turn. **Transitions play** when changing slide —
fade for all, with directional sliding for push and cover — animating the
incoming slide over the outgoing one. **Automatic advance** starts when the transition
asks for it (`AfterTime`).

Keyboard as expected: space/arrow/Enter/PageDown advance, back arrow/PageUp go back,
Home and End go to the first and last, Esc exits. F5 presents from the start, ⇧F5 from the current
slide — commands of the Presentations module, so in menu and ribbon (*View* tab,
*Slide Show* group) without dedicated code. Eleven tests between controller and scheduler.

**Verified live**: F5 opens the full-screen slide show with the slide on a black background,
space moves to the next slide, Esc returns to the editor — without errors.

### Deck, block 4: transitions and animations (done)
**Transitions: complete.** Editor in the inspector (translated type, direction active only where it
makes sense), playback, and **serialization in both formats tested with the real reference suite**.
ODF uses the **SMIL** attributes in the `drawing-page` style — and here the lesson to remember: the
SMIL names must be the **real** ones (`pushWipe`, not `push`; `slideWipe`, `barWipe`), otherwise the reference suite
imports the transition but on export **discards the type keeping only the subtype**, and the
transition is lost halfway through the round trip. OOXML uses `p:transition` (fade/push/wipe/cover/pull/split/
dissolve/cut/zoom). A single mapper per format, used by writer and reader so they do not diverge.
**Verified**: an ODP with Push upwards, re-saved by the reference suite and read back, comes back Push/Up;
nine round-trip tests on both formats; losses `ODP001`/`PPTX001` removed.

**Animations: complete.** The panel lists the slide's animations and adds/removes them
(undoable commands), a **pure, tested scheduling engine** (`AnimationScheduler`) computes
the order from the triggers (on click / with previous / after previous), the duration and the **visual per
element over time** (opacity, offset, scale), and the *Riproduci* (Play) button runs it on the canvas
with a timer while the renderer applies the visual. Seven tests on the scheduler.

**Animations too are serialized in both formats, tested with the real reference suite.** OOXML
uses the timing tree `p:timing` (main sequence, on-click groups, `p:par` per effect
with `presetClass`/`presetID`/`nodeType`, visibility `p:set` and `p:animEffect`); ODF uses
`anim:par`/`anim:seq` with `anim:set` and `presentation:preset-class`/`preset-id`. The target is bound
to the shape by identifier — the `spid` in OOXML, the frame's `xml:id` in ODF — and on reading
the element is found from the identifier, so the binding holds even after a round trip through the reference suite,
which rewrites the ids. One mapper per format, used by writer and reader. Losses
`ODP002`/`PPTX002` removed. **Verified**: a slide with two entrance animations (fade on click,
fly-in after previous) written in both formats, **re-saved by the reference suite and read back, comes back with
both animations intact** — category, preset and trigger — in ODP as in PPTX. Five
round-trip tests on both formats.

It remains declared that the exact rendering of effects across different applications is approximated (our
model covers entrance/emphasis/exit/path with a set of presets; what does not fit
degrades to fade), but the animation information **crosses the formats without being lost**.

### Deck, block 3: ODP and OOXML formats (done)
Both formats read and write, **tested in both directions with the real reference suite** and with a
parity test, and a Deck now **is saved and reopened from the app**. Rule 7 applies as for sheets: either a
feature crosses both formats, or the loss is declared in `CheckFidelity` with its
code.

**The ODF wrapper is shared, not duplicated.** The package logic (uncompressed mimetype at the
head, `content/styles/meta`, manifest) was **extracted into `PulseOffice.Formats.Package`**
(`OdfPackage`, namespace `PulseOffice.Formats.Packaging`), and both sheets (ODS) and
presentations (ODP) use it. The structure follows the **format families**, not the modules: `Formats.Odf`
hosts ODS **and** ODP, `Formats.OpenXml` hosts XLSX **and** PPTX, and `PulseOffice.Formats` carries the two
abstractions (sheets and presentations) with the same `FidelityReport`.

**ODP** (`OdpWriter`/`OdpReader`): slides as `draw:page`, placeholders as `draw:frame`
+ `draw:text-box`, formatting in automatic styles, size from the master's `page-layout`,
per-page background, notes. Two round-trip pitfalls **found only with the real reference suite** (the same
lesson as for sheets, «reading back only what we write is not enough»):
- the reference suite **removes `presentation:class`** from slide frames (it keeps it only on
  notes): the placeholder's role is now inferred by **order and geometry** when the class is missing;
- the reference suite writes **several `page-layout`s** (slide and A4 notes): the size is resolved from the
  `page-layout` cited by the master, not from the first one found.
Declared losses (`ODP001..010`): transitions, animations, interactions, embedded objects, and
the **theme colour roles degrade to absolute** (ODP does not keep the theme object).

**PPTX** (`PptxWriter`/`PptxReader`, with the Microsoft SDK): presentation, one master, one layout, and
a **real `theme1.xml`** (colour scheme aligned to `dk1/lt1/dk2/lt2/accent1..6/hlink`, major/minor
font scheme). Background written **per slide** (`p:cSld/p:bg`) and text colours
resolved to absolute, because without a master background the reference suite showed white on black. PPTX,
unlike ODP, **keeps the theme** (name and colours) across the round trip. Declared losses
(`PPTX001..004`): transitions, animations, interactions, embedded objects.

**Verified with the real reference suite, in both directions and for both formats**: one of our ODPs and one of
our PPTXs open in the reference suite and render as they do for us (Slate background, light bold title,
secondary subtitle); re-saved by the reference suite and read back, they come back with titles, multi-paragraph
body, layout, size and background — and the PPTX also with the theme name.

**Saving and opening in the app** (`IPresentationFormatRegistry`, `DeckDocumentService`,
`DeckDocumentSaver`): the shell routes by module (⌘S/⇧⌘S on a Deck save as .odp/.pptx with
the choice of format), and opening goes through an **`IDocumentOpenRouter`** — each module is an
`IWorkspaceOpener` and the router chooses by extension, so ⌘O offers sheets and presentations together
and Folio will hook in without touching the shell. **Verified live**: new Deck saved to disk,
and `sample.odp` opened from disk appears in a new tab with the two slides, the texts, the
theme background and the bulleted body, rendered in the canvas and in the thumbnails.

Tests: 8 ODP round-trips, 7 PPTX, 3 parity tests between the two formats (text, structure, size,
formatting, theme), besides `CheckFidelity`. Full suite green.

### Deck, block 2: masters and themes (done)
The structural layer on which the two formats will rest. A **theme** is colours and fonts
(`Theme`: `ColorScheme` with background, text, two secondaries and six accents plus the two for links,
aligned to the OOXML roles — `dk1/lt1/dk2/lt2/accent1..6/hlink`; `FontScheme` with major
and minor font). A **master** (`SlideMaster`) carries the theme, the background and the **layout
templates** (`SlideLayoutTemplate`), and each layout declares its own **placeholders** (`PlaceholderTemplate`:
role, frame, style). It is the shape of ODF presentations (`style:master-page` + `presentation-page-layout`) and
of PowerPoint (`slideMaster` + `slideLayout`), so the model matches what the formats
save instead of having to be translated on the fly.

**Placeholder geometry has left the factory and entered the master.** Before, `SlideFactory`
hard-coded frames and sizes in the code; now the **`MasterFactory`** (a service, not statics)
builds the standard master from a theme, and `ISlideFactory.Create(id, master, layout)` copies the
placeholders from the layout template. So the master is **the single source** of layout and
style, and it is what a loaded file will bring with it.

**Colours and fonts are no longer absolute in slides: they are references to the theme.** A
placeholder paragraph declares a `ColorRole` (and whether it uses the major font), not a fixed
colour; the renderer resolves colour and font from the theme at drawing time. **Changing the theme
recolours everything without touching the slides** — it is the same rule already chosen for the
interface palette and for conditional formatting (the rendering changes, not the content), and it is
the behaviour the formats expect (a placeholder inherits from layout → master → theme). An
explicit slide background wins over the layout, the layout over the master, the master over the theme.

`IThemeCatalog` (Catalog/Strategy) carries three predefined themes — Chiaro (Light), Ardesia (Slate, dark), Sabbia
(Sand, warm, with Georgia as major font) — and the Deck bar has the selector for the **theme** and the
**layout** of the current slide, both undoable commands (`DeckActions.ApplyTheme`,
`SetLayout`).

**Verified live**: new presentation in the Chiaro theme; choosing **Ardesia** from the selector, the
slide and the thumbnail switch to the dark background with light text instantly; ⌘Z brings back
Chiaro and the selector realigns; choosing the **Intestazione di sezione** (Section header) layout, the placeholders
reposition at bottom left and the layout background appears (Background2). Ten tests on the
core (placeholder geometry from the master, resolution of colour roles, per-layout background,
major font for titles), all green.

### Refactoring wave 7: form controls, one class per type (done)
Three places decided with a `switch` on the control type — how it is drawn, how it responds to a
click, how it writes and reads the linked cell — and one of them had fifteen static methods. Now they are
three families:
- **drawing**: `ControlPainter` with one painter per type (label, check box, option, buttons,
  frame, list, combo box, spinner, scroll bar, image, table, navigation, file
  selection, field); check box and option share `ChoicePainter` (Template Method: the mark changes,
  the label next to it does not). The common primitives — field, button, truncated text — are in
  `ControlCanvas`;
- **interaction**: `ControlBehaviour` for check box (with the third state), option, buttons, list,
  spinner and scroll bar; a control «responds» if it has a behaviour, so the question and the
  answer can no longer diverge;
- **cell link**: `ControlLink` for choice (TRUE/FALSE), list (one-based position), number
  (clamped to the range) and text as fallback.

### Refactoring: sheet readers and writers (ODS and XLSX) as pipelines (done)
The last giants of the formats — `OdsReader` (20 static methods), `OdsWriter`, `XlsxReader`,
`XlsxWriter` — are now facades, like the presentation writers and readers of waves 4–5:
- **ODS reading**: a context (`OdsReadContext`) and a chain of readers per part of the sheet
  (`IOdsSheetPartReader`: rules, images, shapes, charts, formulas, controls, alternative text,
  comments, merges, sparklines, print ranges, measures); cells are read by `OdsTableReader` with
  `OdsCellReader`. Rows are walked by a single iterator, `TableRows`, on top of which sits `TableCells`;
- **ODS writing**: cell, annotation, defined names, styles document, nesting of
  groups and anchored frames are classes of their own; frames come from a list of sources
  (`AnchoredFrameSet`) instead of four nested `Merge`s;
- **XLSX**: the writer is a list of **sections in schema order** (`WorksheetSection`), the
  reader a chain of readers per part; string table, cell codec and outline
  levels are classes shared by both directions.

**Three real defects found doing it:**
- **rows inside `table:header-rows` were not read**: in a file from the reference suite with rows to
  repeat when printing, the data of those rows vanished on opening;
- **rows to repeat when printing were not saved in ODS**, while XLSX wrote them
  (`Print_Titles`): a silent loss, against rule 7. Now they are `table:header-rows`, and
  **the reference suite really recognizes them**: one of our ODS files converted to XLSX comes out with the two rows as
  print titles;
- **cell hyperlinks were not saved in XLSX**: ODS wrote them, OOXML lost them
  silently. Now they are `hyperlinks` with the external relationship, and they come back from the round trip through the reference suite too.
And a schema error: in XLSX `scenarios` was written after the validations, while the schema
wants it before the merges; the reference suite tolerated it, Excel would have «repaired» the file. The sections
now follow the schema order by construction.

### Refactoring wave 9: sheet formulas have a Visitor (done)
Four places dispatched by hand on the ten expression node types — evaluator, dependency
collection, rewriting for paste and structure, writing in the user's language — and two
printers each had their own table of symbols and precedences. Now `FormulaNode` has
`Accept` and `IFormulaNodeVisitor<T>`:
- `FormulaRewriter` **is** a visitor that rebuilds the tree: the descent into unary, binary,
  function and matrix nodes is in the base, and `OffsetRewriter` and `StructureRewriter` only say what
  to do with a reference and a range (Template Method);
- printing is a hierarchy, `FormulaPrinter` with `CanonicalFormulaPrinter` (parentheses only where
  needed) and `LocalizedFormulaPrinter` (function names, separator and numbers in the language); the
  table of symbols and precedences is a single one (`BinaryOperators`);
- evaluation and dependency collection are `NodeEvaluation` and `DependencyCollector`.
The static class `FormulaText` no longer exists, and the evaluator no longer has private static methods.

### Refactoring wave 8: math formulas have a Visitor (done)
Five classes — measuring (`FormulaLayout`), drawing (`FormulaRenderer`), MathML, OMML and node
children (`MathNodes`) — did the same `switch` on the fifteen node types: adding a node
meant remembering five places. Now `MathNode` has `Accept` and there is `IMathNodeVisitor<T>` with
the base `MathNodeVisitor<T>` (fallback for cases not handled): measuring is `MeasureVisitor`,
drawing is `NodePainter` over a `FormulaPainter` that carries context, ink and the map of hit
points, MathML and OMML writing are `MathMlWriter` and `OmmlWriter`, the children `ChildrenVisitor`.
A new node is now one more method in the interface, and the compiler points out all the visitors
that must handle it. `MathNodes` is no longer static.

### Refactoring wave 6f: the rest of the mapper family (done — wave 6 closed)
Twenty-eight mappers with 135 static methods. In the family of Odf* and Xlsx*/Pptx* mappers **not
a single static method remains**: only the namespace constants remain.

The real work was not removing the word `static`, but finding what was **written several times**:
- **the same tables in two directions**: every `switch` from value to token had its twin from
  token to value. Now they are `TokenMap<T>` (text tokens, in `PulseOffice.Formats`) and
  `OoxmlValueMap<TModel, TSdk>` (SDK enumerated values): pivots, sparklines, animations,
  interactions, validations, transition directions;
- **the cell scan** existed six times, and almost all skipped the row groups. Now there is
  `TableCells`, the single iterator that walks groups, header rows and covered cells, and
  on top of it `AnchoredFrames`; images, formulas, validations and scenarios use it;
- **the OOXML geometry** was copied in full in the vector mapper: now it is a single service
  (`OoxmlGeometry`, with the flattener injected);
- the **on-click groups** of animations (`AnimationClickGroups`), the **media types**
  (`MediaTypes`), the **image types**, the **qualified ranges** (`Foglio.A1:Foglio.B2`), the
  **cell values** of scenarios and the **normalization of references** to the package
  (`OdfHrefs`) were duplicated across two or three files;
- the **PPTX transitions** and the **on-click actions** have become hierarchies: one effect per
  transition type (simple, sliding, letter-based), one action per click type (jump, macro,
  link), each able to write and recognize itself.

**Three real defects closed along the way:**
- in ODS the **validation alert type** was not read back: a *Warning* came back as *Stop*, i.e.
  a validation that let the user decide became one that forbade. A test guards it;
- **validations, images, formulas and scenarios** in grouped rows were not read;
- **transitions of PPTX files written by the reference suite and by PowerPoint were lost**: both
  wrap them in `mc:AlternateContent` (a `p14` choice and a standard fallback), and the reader
  looked only for the direct `p:transition`. Now it reads the fallback. Found by testing with the real
  reference suite — an ODP with *Spinta verso l'alto* (Push up), converted to PPTX by the reference suite, came back without a
  transition; now it comes back *Spinta, Su* (Push, Up). A test builds the wrapped file the way they write it.

**Verified with the real reference suite**: transitions and animations in both directions (PPTX→ODP and ODP→PPTX),
with the two entrance animations and their triggers intact.

### Refactoring wave 6e: shapes in the four formats (done)
The four shape mappers — sheet and slide, ODF and OOXML — relied on `switch` on the
object type and on counters passed by `ref`. Now:

**Writing by Visitor.** On the sheet, in both ODF and OOXML, the shape to write is chosen with
the drawing-object visitor born in wave 2 (`SheetShapeElementVisitor`,
`SheetDrawingVisitor`): shape, path, group and connector are four methods, and a group
writes its children **by visiting them** with a frame derived from its own (`ShapeSlot`, `DrawingBox`).
The OOXML identifiers, which before travelled as `ref uint` between static methods, are an object
(`DrawingIdentifiers`) that assigns them and finds them by name, which is what connectors need.

**Reading by chain.** Each element knows who reads it: shape, framed shape, path
(`draw:path`, `draw:polygon`, `draw:polyline`), connector, group in ODF; shape, group and
connector in OOXML. Frames in cells are found by the single iterator of 6d, which now accepts several
names, so shapes inside **grouped rows** no longer vanish on reading either.

**Slide: one codec per object.** `OdfDeckShapeMapper` and `PptxDeckShapeMapper` were two
containers of six different objects; now they are facades over separate codecs (path, shape, image,
formula, OLE, table), with a common base for frame and measures. Image types are tables
(`OdfImageTypes`, `OoxmlImageTypes`) instead of two static `switch`es called from outside.

**A real defect closed along the way: in PPTX the shape style was lost halfway.** The writer
wrote everything — gradients, patterns, dashes, shadow, glow, bevel, text — but Deck's
reader read back only the solid colour and the line colour and width: a shape with a
gradient came back solid, without shadow, with the text in the default style. The complete
reader already existed, inside Ledger's shape mapper and in static form: it became
`DrawingStyleReader`, a chain of readers per style part **shared** between sheet and
slide, and placed next to the writer in `XlsxShapeStyleMapper`. Writing and reading now use the
same vocabulary (`DrawingVocabulary`: dashes, caps, arrowheads, bevels, patterns, anchors,
alignments, connectors), so they can no longer diverge. A new test guards it.

The bidirectional token dictionary moved up into the common project (`TokenMap<T>` in
`PulseOffice.Formats`), because both format families now use it.

**Verified with the real reference suite**: a sheet with a gradient ellipse with shadow and text and a group
of two shapes, written by us in ODS and in XLSX, rewritten by the reference suite and read back, comes back with the
gradient, the shadow, the text and the group of two children in both formats; the reference suite's PDF
shows the gradient and the shadow.

### Refactoring wave 6d: form controls in both formats (done)
`OdfFormControlMapper` had twenty-two static methods and thirty-five `form:properties` properties
written once in one method and read back in another, hundreds of lines away: adding one
meant remembering to touch two places. Now each property is a **symmetric descriptor**
(`FormSetting`): `TextSetting`, `NumberSetting` and `FlagSetting` are configured with name, fallback
value and the two directions, and the special cases — password character, range of the scroll bar or
spinner, control type — are subclasses of their own. The list (`FormSettings`) is the single
grammar, read by the writer and by the reader. The `form:properties` bag (`FormPropertyBag`)
hides the XML form of text, number and flag.

The three tables on the control type — the reference suite's service, element name, recognition — were three
`switch`es and a dictionary built separately; now they are **a list of rows** (`OdfControlKinds`).
Events and check box states go through `OdfTokenMap`, which gained `Find` for tokens that
may be missing.

The cell scan to find anchored frames existed **twice** — once for charts,
once for controls — and the chart one did not walk row groups: a chart anchored
in a grouped row vanished on reading, the same defect already fixed at the time for data.
Now there is a single iterator (`AnchoredFrames`, with the frame name as a parameter) that descends
into groups and header rows, and both use it.

In OOXML the encoded control name and the `x14` properties are two separate codecs
(`ControlNameCodec`, `X14ControlPropertiesCodec`), with the object types in a table.

**Verified with the real reference suite**: a check box with label, linked cell and state, a list with its
items and a scroll bar, written by us, rewritten by the reference suite and read back, come back whole.

### Refactoring wave 6c: cell styles and conditional formatting (done)
Four mappers, fifty-nine static methods, and the same disease: every property written
twice, once per direction, with a `switch` in each.

**Cell styles.** In ODF each property is now a class that knows how to **write and read itself back**
(`OdfCellProperty` for background, borders, wrap, vertical alignment; `OdfTextProperty` for language,
superscript and subscript, colour, font, size), and the nine font toggles — bold,
italic, underline, strikethrough, double underline, overline, shadow, outline — are **a
single class configured nine times** (`FontToggleProperty`), instead of nine `if`s in writing and nine
expressions in reading. The builder (`OdfCellStyleBuilder`) and the reader (`OdfCellStyleReader`)
walk the same lists, so a new property is added in one place. The decoding of the reference suite's
names (`_5f_`) and the recognition of marked names are in `OdfStyleNames`.

In OOXML the three lists of fonts, fills and borders were three copies of the same code
(dictionary, index, add, counter): now they are **one generic type**, `StyleTable<T>`, which
deduplicates by key. Font, fill, border and alignment are codecs in both directions, and the
SDK enumerated values go through `OoxmlValueMap<TModel, TSdk>`, a bidirectional table like
`OdfTokenMap`. Reading is `XlsxStyleReader`, no longer static.

**Conditional formatting.** The three renderings — data bar, colour scale, condition — are a
hierarchy of codecs in both formats, chosen per element on reading and per rule on writing.
In ODF the condition syntax is a family of **forms** (formula, function with its arity,
keyword, comparison), each able to write and recognize itself: the ordered list
of forms is the only place where the grammar lives. In OOXML the operators are a single table
(operator ↔ rule type ↔ SDK operator) read in both directions, and the differential formats
are in `DifferentialFormatTable`. The rules that carry a style share a base
(**Template Method**: style, priority and «stop if true» once only, the condition in the
subclass).

**Verified with the real reference suite**: an XLSX with data bar, condition «> 25» in bold on
pink and three-colour scale, converted by the reference suite to ODS, comes back from our ODF reader with the three
rules intact, style included.

### Refactoring wave 6b: shape style in both formats (done)
`OdfShapeStyleMapper` had twenty-three static methods, almost all `switch`es between a model value and
an ODF token written **twice**, once per direction. Now the vocabularies are **data**: `OdfTokenMap<T>`
is a bidirectional table (value ↔ token, with fallback), and `OdfShapeVocabulary` gathers
eight of them — fills, gradients, dashes, joins, caps, alignments. A token lives in one
place only, so writing and reading cannot diverge.

The rest is split by style part, in both directions: a chain of writers
(`GraphicPropertyWriter`: fill, line, shadow, glow, soft edges, bevel, text
area) working on a common context, and a chain of readers (`GraphicPropertyReader`) that
**enrich** the style one piece at a time. Line arrowheads are a hierarchy
(`ArrowMarker`: arrow, open arrow, circle, diamond), each with its own path.
`OdfShapeStyleReader` is no longer static; the reading side of `OdfShapeMapper` moved to instance
to use it.

In OOXML (`XlsxShapeStyleMapper`) fills are a family of builders — none, solid,
linear gradient, path gradient (Template Method on the list of stops), pattern — and
effects another one (glow, shadow, soft edges); the colour with its alpha is a component
(`DrawingColours`). No change in the files produced: the shape round-trip tests are
green without touch-ups.

### Refactoring wave 6a: charts in the four formats (done)
The chart mappers were four files of static methods, each with its own `switch` on the chart
type, and the two pairs (sheet and slide) had drifted apart: Deck's chart in PPTX
knew only columns, bars, lines and pies, and wrote **every** series as a bar series.

**ODF** (`Formats.Odf/Charts`): a vocabulary (`OdfChartVocabulary`, class and options of the area ↔
type), a sub-document builder as **Template Method** (`OdfChartDocumentBuilder`, with the
subclasses for cell references and for local table) and a reader with the same shape. Anchored
frames are walked with an iterator (`AnchoredFrames`). Deck's chart thus inherits the complete
vocabulary, the area style and the legend.

**OOXML** (`Formats.OpenXml/Charts`): a **hierarchy of families** (`ChartFamily`: bars, lines,
areas, pie, doughnut) that knows how to build the chart, the series, its own finishing touches and to read itself back; a
single `ChartSpaceBuilder` that receives the series source as a **Strategy** (`ISeriesSource`:
sheet references with caches, or literals for the slide); a shared
`ChartSpaceReader`. `XlsxChartMapper` and `PptxDeckChartMapper` are now thin instances, and `ReadCharts` is no
longer static.

**Two real defects found by looking at the reference suite's PDF**, invisible to the tests:
- **series had no colour**: without `c:spPr` the reference suite draws transparent bars and slices, and
  the chart was reduced to axes and legend. Now `ChartPalette` gives a fill to every series and, for
  pie and doughnut, to every slice (`c:dPt`);
- the doughnut lacked `firstSliceAng` and `holeSize`, which the schema requires.

**Verified with the real reference suite**: a doughnut in PPTX and a column chart in XLSX render with their
colours; four new tests on the Deck chart types in PPTX (doughnut, stacked areas,
smoothed line, percentage bars).

### Refactoring wave 10: sheet operations (done)
The operations of `PulseOffice.Sheets.Engine/Operations` were static classes or services full of
private static methods. Now **none remains**:
- **Fill** (`ISheetFill`): the four directions are axes (`FillAxis`: source cells,
  steps, destination, origin of the formula to translate) and the rules are a chain —
  formula, progression, numbered text, repetition — the first that answers wins.
- **Clipboard** (`ISheetClipboard`): the arithmetic operations of paste special are a
  hierarchy (`PasteArithmetic`), tab-separated text is a codec of its own.
- **Search** (`ISheetSearch`): matching is a family (`TextMatcher`: whole cell,
  contained, regular expression, none), and **find and replace use the same object**,
  so they can no longer diverge: before, the regex was built twice with two different
  error handlings.
- **Filter**: the static twin class of `SheetFilterService` has disappeared into it.
- **Chart data** (`IChartDataExtractor`): series by columns and by rows are two
  arrangements of the same Template Method; the near-identical copies of the code are gone.
- **Sheet structure**: inserting and deleting rows and columns is a pipeline of parts
  (cells, formulas, measures, objects, rules, comments, print ranges, merges, groups), and the
  shift rule — where a position, an address, a range, a
  span ends up — lives **in a single object** (`StructureShift`) instead of being rewritten in each method.
- **Conditional formatting**: the three renderings (style, bar, scale) are strategies, and each
  operator is a test (`StateTest`, `TextTest`, `ComparisonTest`, `BetweenTest`).
- **Statistics**: the shared computations are three classes — moments, distribution tails,
  table layout.
- `FormulaTranslator` is a service. The other operation files have lost their
  private static methods.

Behaviour unchanged: 400 engine tests green, the app starts with the new composition
(`ISheetFill` registered and passed to the view).

Known limit, pre-existing and not tied to this wave: `PdfSignerTests.ManometterePagineDopoLaFirmaLaRompe`
fails **sometimes** (about one time in three); to be investigated in the infrastructure wave,
which touches precisely PDF signing.

### Refactoring waves 11–14: Deck, infrastructure, grid, commands (done)
**Number formats and Deck text.** `NumberFormatParser` is no longer static: sections, bracketed
tags (`ColorTag`, `ConditionTag`, Template Method on recognition), body classifier
as a table of rules, placeholder syntax as a strategy per value type, body measures
in a class of their own. `DeckTextFormatter` is split into three collaborators: the **character
attributes** as a table of objects that know how to read and write themselves on a portion (instead of two
twin `switch`es), the **range walk** (portions touched, paragraphs touched, cutting
portions at the edges) and the **merging** of equal portions; the three `UniVal`/`UniStr`/`UniNum`
are a single `CommonValue`.

**Wave 11 — Deck.** Framing a connector (routing, margin, normalization of the
path in the frame) was **copied identically** in `SheetConnectors` and `DeckConnectors`: now it is a
single service, `ConnectorFramer` in `PulseOffice.Drawing`, and the two modules only say how an
object is measured and how it is repositioned. `HeaderFooterXml` is a list of symmetric fields (like the
form control descriptors), and the attribute string for OOXML is derived from the element
instead of being written a second time by hand. `SlideResize` is a service with the formats as a
table and uniform fitting as an object.

**Wave 14 — infrastructure.**
- **A real defect in PDF signing**, found by the test that failed one time in three: to
  read the signature the **trailing zeros** were stripped from the hexadecimal padding, and when the real PKCS#7
  ended with null bytes the trimming ate a piece of it — the signature appeared absent. Now the
  length is read **from the DER header** (`DerEnvelope`). The signer is split into file
  tail, catalog, incremental update (which groups the contiguous identifiers of the
  table by itself), signature space and detached signature. Verified with PDFKit that the signed file opens.
- **CPython**: the candidate sources are a chain per system (PATH, Windows, macOS, Linux),
  the library locator a strategy per system, probe and reader separated. Verified
  live: it finds the same three interpreters and chooses 3.14.7.
- **mp4**: the container is a **Composite** of boxes (`LeafBox`, `ContainerBox`) with a
  field builder; the output is **byte-identical** to the previous one, compared on the same
  input. VideoToolbox keeps only the P/Invoke declarations static; a video encoded live
  reads back with AVFoundation.
- **WebDAV**: paths, DAV properties and error messages are classes of their own.

**Wave 12 — Ledger's grid.** The pointer gestures — drag selection, column and row
resizing, fill handle — were six loose fields (`_isDragging`,
`_resizingColumn`, `_fillSource`, …) checked in cascade; now they are **states** (`GridGesture` and its
four subclasses), only one active at a time, which know how to move and conclude. The grid no
longer has private static methods. **Verified live**: 1 and 2 in A1:A2, drag selection,
handle down to A6 (1…6), column B widened by dragging its border.

**Wave 13 — the commands.** Seventy command groups each built their own
`CommandDefinition` from scratch. Now they inherit from `LedgerCommandSet` or `DeckCommandSet`, which carry the
active context and a **prototype** (`Prototype(id)`: identifier and module) from which every command is born
with `with`. The prototype carries **only** what all commands really have: putting in it also the required
state or the enabling would have silently changed the commands that did not declare them. 175 of them go
through the prototype; five groups that do not receive the active context stay out (global Deck
commands, export, paste special, signature line, Ledger collections), where the base has nothing
to give. **Verified**: startup registers the
same 661 commands, without any report.

A trap of mine, discovered here: the startup check of the previous waves looked for «Main window
opened» in the log, but the executable is called `PulseOffice` and not `PulseOffice.Desktop.dll`; the command
failed and the line found was **old**. The right check reads only the lines written **after**
startup. Redone that way: the application starts with all the waves.

### Refactoring waves 15–21: second pass on patterns (done)
**Wave 15 — path segments have a Visitor.** Sixteen files did the same `switch` on
move, line, cubic, arc and close. Now `ShapeSegment` has `Accept`, and on top there are two pieces:
- shared visitors in `PulseOffice.Drawing`: `SegmentPoints` (all points, to measure),
  `SegmentEnds` (only the end points, for arrowheads), `SegmentMapper` (transforms points and
  radii: scale, normalization in the frame, offset);
- a **path writer** (`PathSink`, Builder) that receives MoveTo/LineTo/CubicTo/ArcTo/Close with the
  current point already computed by `PathReplay`. Every output is a writer: SVG, ODF path
  (`EnhancedPathSink`), OOXML `custGeom`, PDF, arc flattening, freeform path nodes, and
  Avalonia's geometry.

The screen and the print preview had **two** almost identical Avalonia geometry builders, and
the preview one ignored arcs: now there is only one (`OutlineGeometry`). **Verified live**:
an ellipse draws correctly in the grid and in the print preview.

**Wave 16 — formula syntaxes are dialects.** ODF and OOXML had two static classes with the
same skeleton (strip the prefix, convert only outside quotes). Now `FormulaDialect`
in `PulseOffice.Formats` is the Template Method and each dialect only says how it converts a piece.
**A real defect, found by testing with the reference suite**: the reference suite writes references to a sheet
as **absolute and quoted** — `[$'Foglio con spazi'.A1]` — and we read `'$Foglio con spazi'`, i.e. a
sheet that does not exist: every cross-sheet formula of a file from the reference suite opened broken. Now the `$`
(absolute sheet, which our model does not distinguish) is stripped and the quotes are resolved. Two tests
guard it, and the real round trip XLSX → reference suite → ODS → us comes back with the formulas intact.

**Wave 17 — Deck's canvas.** Like Ledger's grid: the dragged guide and the transformation of
an object (move, resize, rotation, with snapping) are **states**
(`GuideGesture`, `TransformGesture`) instead of six loose fields that the drawing also read.
**Verified live**: rectangle moved, resized from the corner and rotated from the handle, with
the thumbnail following and ⌘Z taking it back.

**Wave 18 — parser and evaluation values.** The formula parser is a service
(`FormulaParser`) with an internal session for each parse. The evaluation values (scalar,
range, matrix, lambda, missing) have a **Visitor with the context as a parameter**, so the
visitors are stateless and the hot path of computation allocates nothing extra; `ValueCoercion`
is no longer static and reaches the functions through `ArgumentReader` (`Values`, `TryNumbersOf`).

**Wave 19 — series.** Progressions (linear, geometric, dates) and date steps (day,
weekday, month, year) are strategies.

**Wave 20 — command registry.** It is a facade over placement per surface (menu, ribbon),
search score as a table of rules, shortcut checking, collection of structure
keys and a **tree builder** with ordering as a strategy (by map or fixed).
Same 661 commands at startup, no report.

**Wave 21 — charts.** The only helper truly duplicated among the painters (`Polar`) moved up into the
base; the other helpers are no longer static.

**Two defects seen along the way, and fixed right after.**
- **The order of top-level menus was not a decision, it was a side effect.** Each menu
  took the rank of its first rule in the map, so a single misplaced rule was enough — the
  Chinese and Hangul conversions, written in the format block but directed to *Strumenti* (Tools) — for
  *Strumenti* to end up before *Foglio* (Sheet) in Ledger; in Deck *Modifica* (Edit) ended up after *Inserisci* (Insert). The order of
  top-level menus is now **declared** in the map (`CommandLayout` with the list of roots),
  while rank continues to decide what goes inside. A test guards it. **Verified on the
  real menu bar**: Ledger File, Modifica, Visualizza, Inserisci, Formato, Foglio, Dati, Strumenti,
  Aiuto; Deck File, Modifica, Visualizza, Inserisci, Formato, Diapositiva, Strumenti, Aiuto.
- **In Deck's thumbnails charts had full-size text.** It was not only the text: the whole
  chart structure (margins, title height, legend width, sizes) is in fixed
  measures. Now below a reference size (360×220) the chart is drawn at that size and
  **scaled uniformly**, as the slide is; above it nothing changes. **Verified live**: the
  thumbnail shows the chart shrunk with the right proportions, and the chart on the canvas and the one
  in Ledger stay identical to before.

### Refactoring waves 22–27: third pass on patterns (done)
- **22 — autocorrect as a chain of rules**: replacements, two initial capitals, sentence
  capitalization, dashes and quotes are five `AutoCorrectRule`s, each with its own option; the
  correction applies them in a row instead of a ladder of `if`s.
- **23 — animation effects as strategies**: fade, fly (with its direction), zoom,
  grow, pulse and path are `EffectMotion`s in a table looked up by category and preset,
  with fallback to the category's effect; smooth easing lives in the base (Template Method).
- **24 — Deck's logic is no longer static**: sections, fields, footer, master editing,
  snapping and text search are services.
- **25 — freeform paths**: the node type (corner, smooth, symmetric) is a strategy that knows how
  it reacts to dragging a handle and how to adopt the type; the two sides of the handle are
  objects (`HandleSide`), so «move the handle before» and «after» are no longer two mirror copies.
- **26 — pivot**: the value display modes (percentages of total, of column, of
  row, running totals, rank) are strategies with a per-column pass that computes total and
  values **before** rewriting, as before.
- **27 — macros**: the nine facades exposed to scripts inherit from `ScriptFacade`, which receives the
  dispatcher to the UI thread (`IScriptDispatcher`) from the container instead of
  calling a static class. **Verified live**: the macro editor's example writes A1 and
  A2 and prints 42.

### Refactoring wave 28: pivot aggregations (done) — and the point at which to stop
The fifteen pivot aggregations were a `switch` plus a row of `if`s: now they are strategies —
on cells (count, distinct count, first, last) and on numbers (sum, average, minimum,
maximum, product, median, variance and standard deviation in both modes). **Median and variance were a second
copy** of the sheet function computations: now the pivot uses `SpreadsheetMath`, so a pivot and
the `MEDIANA` (MEDIAN) function on the same data cannot give different numbers. Seven new tests with known
values.

A fourth search pass (the `switch`es with more branches, the remaining type checks, the largest files)
found **only this** real case. The others were left on purpose, because there a pattern
would worsen readability: key handling in the slide show and in the grid (a `switch` on the
key is the clearest form of a key→action map), the lexers of formulas and of SVG paths,
the PDF font metrics, the theme colours, the cell value type, the eight handles of
`ObjectManipulator` and the table of 26 shapes. From here on, further sweeping passes would yield
little: it is better to apply the rule **while writing new code**, which is where patterns help.

### Deck: new fields and special characters (done)
Resumed Deck's development from the missing items of *Inserisci* (Insert). **Fields**: besides number, date and
time, there are now **number of slides**, **slide title**, **author** and **file
name**, plus **fixed** date and time (plain text, not fields). Values are derived at drawing
time by `SlideFieldsFactory` (document + slide → `SlideFields`), used by canvas,
slide show and export: this is why the field updates by itself. The file name is set by
`DeckDocumentService` on opening and saving (`Presentation.FileName`).

**Special characters** (eight: non-breaking and narrow space, non-breaking and optional hyphen,
zero-width space, word joiner, LRM and RLM) are inserted **at the cursor** if you are typing,
otherwise at the end of the selected text. Inserting text is now a single service
(`IDeckTextInsertion`), used by fields, symbols and characters: cursor → selected text → new
box. The optional hyphen has no shortcut: ⌘− is zoom.

**Formats.** In ODF all fields are native (`text:page-count`, `loext:page-name`,
`text:author-name`, `text:file-name` with `text:display="name-and-extension"`, otherwise
the reference suite shows the whole path); a single table (`OdfFieldElements`) serves writer and
reader. In OOXML PowerPoint has no field type for count, title, author and file name:
they are written as `a:fld` with a `pulseoffice.*` type that our reader recognizes, and PowerPoint
shows the stored text. The loss is declared (`PPTX015`).

**Verified with the real reference suite**: in our ODP, with the stored text falsified, the reference suite
recalculates count (3), file name and title («Conclusioni»); the author stays the inserted one,
as in the reference suite's own presentation editor. **Live**: *Inserisci ▸ Testo ▸ Campi* (Insert ▸ Text ▸ Fields) and *▸ Caratteri speciali* (Special characters) translated, and
«Numero di diapositive» (Number of slides) on three slides shows 3. Reference presentation coverage **210 → 224 of 368 (60.9%)**.

### Deck: table column widths and row heights (done)
The table had no measures of its own: columns were decided by the painter from the content, rows
were all the same height, and no format saved them — PPTX wrote equal columns and rows one sixth
of the frame high, ODP one repeated column. Now `DataTableObject.Layout` (`TableLayout`)
carries the **width fractions** of the columns (empty = automatic) and the **row heights in
points** on the shown rows, header included.

The reference suite's six commands — optimal and minimal row height, optimal and minimal column
width, distribute rows and columns — are **strategies** (`ITableSizing` in
`PulseOffice.Document/Embedding`, pure, tested logic): *optimal* follows the longest text,
*minimal* the longest word, *distribute* evens out. Injected as a set, they become one command
each with no per-command code. Changing the rows, the frame takes the total height, so the
table does not stay in a frame taller than itself (which was the case for every freshly inserted table).
They are in the *Formato ▸ Tabella ▸ Dimensioni* (Format ▸ Table ▸ Size) menu and in the context menu.

**Formats**: in OOXML `a:gridCol/@w` and `a:tr/@h`; in ODF a `table-column` style with
`style:column-width` per column and a `table-row` style with `style:row-height` per row. An automatic
table is written with the optimal widths, close to what is seen.

**Verified with the real reference suite, in both directions**: columns 20/80 and rows 40/20/30 pt come back intact
from our PPTX converted to ODP; from our ODP converted to PPTX the columns come back intact and the
rows **grow** (40→46.6) — the reference suite treats the height as a minimum and widens it to its own text
size, which is its normal behaviour. **Live**: table inserted, *Altezza minima delle
righe* (Minimal row height) lowers it and the frame shrinks onto the rows. *Seleziona riga/colonna* (Select row/column) is still missing: it needs
cell selection on the canvas, which is a subsystem of its own. Reference presentation coverage **224 → 230 of 368 (62.5%)**.

### Images: eight new filters, replace, save and compress — shared between Deck and Ledger (done)
**Filters**: charcoal (Sobel), pop art, posterize, emboss, remove noise (3×3 median),
sharpen, soften and solarize, in `PulseOffice.Drawing/Assets/Filters`. The per-pixel ones
inherit from `PerPixelFilter`; those that look at neighbours from `NeighbourhoodFilter` (Template
Method: reads from a **copy** of the image, otherwise each pixel would see neighbours already filtered),
with `KernelFilter` for convolutions. The commands are born **from the enum** in both modules, so
a new filter is one row in the catalog. In the formats they stay screen-rendered and declared
(`ODP015`/`PPTX010`, now «all filters except greyscale»), like sepia and mosaic.

**Replace, save, compress** are a single service (`IRasterImageFiles` in
`PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Objects`), used by Ledger and Deck; it also absorbed the two readers of the
pixel size and of the MIME type that `DeckView` and `SheetImageInsertion` each had on their
own. *Comprimi* (Compress) reduces to the chosen longest side and re-encodes — **JPEG with the requested quality if
the original is a photo, PNG otherwise**, so as not to lose transparency — with Avalonia 12's
encoders (`JpegBitmapEncoderOptions`, verified by reflection). If the result is not
smaller the image stays as it was, and the status bar says so. Deck also has *Salva l'immagine di
sfondo* (Save background image).

**A defect found by a real startup, which crashed the app**: Ledger already had a
`ledger.image.compress` in another command group, and registering a second one makes the
registry fail at startup. The old one was a **placeholder**: it asked for the quality and always answered
«unchanged» without touching the image, while the reference spreadsheet command map counted it as done. Removed; the
real command remains. **Verified live**: the app starts with 704 commands and no report, and
*Formato ▸ Immagine ▸ Filtri* (Format ▸ Image ▸ Filters) in Ledger lists the thirteen translated filters. Reference presentation coverage **230 → 242 of 368
(65.8%)**.

### Deck: redaction and Chinese and Hangul conversion — and the capital letter that broke addresses (done)
Four *Strumenti* (Tools) items, none written from scratch: Ledger's pieces were tied to cells only
on the surface, and now they are shared.

- **The redaction engine** (`ITextRedactor` in `PulseOffice.Text/Redaction`: patterns, mask,
  replacement) came out of `SheetRedaction`, which now uses it. The mask comes from the engine, so the
  `mask` parameter that Ledger's methods received — and that would have been ignored — is gone.
- **The dialogs** are shared in `PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Prompts`: `IRedactionPrompt` (confirmation,
  choice of patterns) and `ITextConversionPrompt` (conversion direction, table check).
  They return the choice, they do not apply it: the caller brings its own phrases, because in Deck
  «cells» and «sheet» were wrong words.
- **In Deck redaction works on the whole paragraph text**, not portion by portion
  (`DeckTextRedaction`): an address with half its characters in bold is two portions, and
  redacting them one by one would let it through. Automatic redaction also touches **the speaker
  notes**, which are document text like any other. A redacted field stops being a field,
  otherwise it would be recalculated and the data would come back.
- **A single undo for an operation over the whole document**: `DeckActions.RewriteTexts`. It is also used
  by *Sostituisci tutto* (Replace all), which until yesterday recorded one undo for every box touched.

**A defect of autocorrect, shared between modules**: sentence capitalization fired
after **any** full stop, even without a space, so «ada@esempio.org» became «esempio.Org», and the
same for `www.sito.it` or `3.5kg`. Now a sentence starts only after a full stop followed by a space;
three tests guard it.

**Verified live**: «Scrivere a ada@esempio.org» in the title, *Oscuramento automatico* (Automatic redaction) →
«Scrivere a ■■■■», ⌘Z brings it back in one go; the dialog says «in tutta la presentazione, note del
relatore comprese» (in the whole presentation, speaker notes included); with the address retyped, it stays lowercase. Reference presentation coverage **242 → 246 of 368 (66.8%)**.

### Deck: macros, and the scripting framework becomes the suite's (done)
Deck now has its own macros with the same IDE as Ledger. To get there the scripting framework left
Ledger, where it was born, and moved into `PulseOffice.Scripting.Editor`:

- **dispatcher, facade base and `app`** (`Facades/ScriptFacades.cs`). `app` was written for the
  sheet — the module was always «Ledger» and the clipboard was the cells' one. Now it receives
  the module host as a strategy (`IScriptHost`: module name and clipboard), implemented by
  `LedgerScriptHost` and `DeckScriptHost`;
- **the API catalog is composed of sections** (`IScriptApiSection`): `app` is a section of the
  shell, visible in every module; Ledger brings its eight roots, Deck brings `deck`. Before, `app`
  was registered as an entry *of the sheet*, and Deck would not have seen it;
- **the editor launcher** (`IMacroEditorLauncher`) builds the window with texts, engines,
  output and library: each module passes only the script objects, the library, the history and the
  key of its own example. The thirty editor text keys were written inside Ledger.

**The `deck` object** (fourteen members, translated in the five languages): number and current
slide, go to, add and delete, title, body and notes for reading and writing, hide. Slides
are counted from 1, every write goes through `DeckActions` — so it respects read-only
and is undone with ⌘Z — and `app`'s clipboard goes through the same commands as the user
(`IDeckClipboardActions`, extracted from `DeckClipboardCommands`). In ODP the macros go in
`Scripts/pulseoffice/` with the same mapper as the sheets; in PPTX the loss is declared
(`PPTX016`: OOXML accepts only VBA, and only in `.pptm`).

**Three real defects, two of which already existed for Ledger:**
- **saving or deleting a macro did not mark the document as modified**: nobody listened to the
  library, so on closing the work vanished without the «Save?» question. Now a **Decorator**
  (`RecordedMacroLibrary`) puts every save and deletion in the document's history:
  the document appears modified and the macro can be undone. An identical save does not count;
- **the editor output lost lines**: they were collected with an asynchronous `Post` to the
  UI thread and the text was composed as soon as the script finished, before they arrived.
  It depended on timing; in Deck it was always lost. Now they are appended immediately, under a lock;
- **the documentation showed the entries of the wrong module**: the list was filled in the constructor,
  before the module was set, so it was always the default one (sheets). Now
  setting the module reloads the list.

**Verified with the real reference suite**: an ODP with macros opens and converts, with the entries declared
in the manifest. **Live**: in Deck the editor opens with the presentation example and the
documentation of `deck`; *Esegui* (Run) adds the slide «Riepilogo» (Summary) with the body «Diapositive: 2» (Slides: 2)
and the output prints «Riepilogo». Reference presentation coverage **246 → 250 of 368 (67.9%)**.

### Form controls in Deck — and the text shortcuts that the macOS menu stole (done)
**Control properties, activation order and navigator** are now shared dialogs
(`IFormControlDialogs` in `PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Forms`), extracted from Ledger: they work on the
control's properties and receive from the module only the list of macros for the events. Ledger and
Deck each say how to replace the object. The activation order is now applied in **a single
undo** in both modules: in Ledger it created one for each control
(`DeckActions.ReplaceElements` in Deck). **Design mode** stays out in Deck, declared:
it would make sense only with controls that respond in the slide show, which today are only drawn.

**The real defect, of the whole application, found by testing the dialog.** With focus in a text
field, ⌘A, ⌘C, ⌘X, ⌘V and ⌘Z **did not act on the text** but on the document: the items of the native macOS
menu carry their shortcut as a *key equivalent*, and macOS executes it before the key reaches
the window. In Deck ⌘A selected the slide's objects while typing a label,
and pasting into a field pasted objects. The existing check (`IsEditingText`) looked only at the
window's path, not the menu's.

Now `ITextEditingRouter` (in `PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Text`) decides in one place only: if focus is in
a text field and the gesture is a text operation, the operation goes to the field. Both the
native menu and the window dispatcher ask it. The code editors (macros and formulas, AvaloniaEdit) are not
`TextBox`es: they declare themselves text targets with `ITextEditingTarget`. Before, even in the
window's path ⌘A in the macro editor selected the slide.

**Verified live**: check box inserted in Deck, *Proprietà del controllo* (Control properties) with its four
tabs; ⌘A in the label field selects the text (before it did not) and «Accetto le condizioni» (I accept the terms) appears
on the slide. Reference presentation coverage **250 → 253 of 368 (68.8%)**.

### Image map: it was lost silently, it was written in a mini-language — now a visual editor for all modules (done)
**The worst defect the project knows, in Ledger since the map has existed**: the image
map was not saved **in any format**, and no `CheckFidelity` declared it. A
document with clickable areas was saved, reopened, and the areas were gone.

Now **ODF writes it natively** (`draw:image-map` in the image frame, with `draw:area-rectangle`,
`draw:area-circle`, `draw:area-polygon`, link and description), with a single codec
(`OdfImageMapCodec`) used by ODS and ODP, in both directions. **OOXML has no image maps**: loss
declared in XLSX (`XLSX025`) and PPTX (`PPTX017`).

**The trap, found only with the real reference suite**: in polygons the reference suite reads `draw:points` as
**hundredths of a millimetre from the image corner** and ignores the `viewBox`. Our first codec
wrote the points on a 0–10000 `viewBox`, and after a round trip through the reference suite the polygon ended up outside
the image, while rectangles and circles came back right. Now the points are in hundredths of a
millimetre and the `viewBox` coincides with the frame in that unit, so the two readings coincide.
**Verified**: rectangle, circle and polygon, written by us in ODS and ODP, rewritten by the reference suite and
read back, come back with the same coordinates, links and description.

**The editor**: in Ledger the map was written in **a text field with a mini-language**
(`Rectangle 0,0 0.5,0.5 https://…`). Now `ImageMapEditorView` (in `PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Objects`,
shared) shows the fitted image with the areas semi-transparent in the accent colour; the tools
— select, rectangle, circle, polygon — are **states**, like the gestures of the grid and the canvas;
next to it are the list of areas, the address and the description of the chosen one. Rectangle and
circle are dragged, the polygon is traced by clicks and closed with a double click or Enter. The
mini-language reader (`ImageMapParser`) no longer served anyone and was removed.

**In the slide show the map works**: a click on an area opens its address, and an address that
starts with `#` leads to the slide with that name; the click on the area takes precedence
over the object's action.

**Verified live in Deck**: image inserted from the macOS panel, *Mappa immagine* (Image map) opens
the editor, a dragged rectangle with its address and a circle appear on the image and
in the list. The click in the slide show, which would open the browser, was not tested. Reference presentation coverage **253 → 254 of
368 (69.0%)**.

### Colour replacement, and two image defects that already existed (done)
**Replace colours** (the reference suite's colour replacer tool), in Deck and in Ledger with the same
dialog (`ColorReplacerView`, shared): up to four rules «source colour, tolerance →
new colour or transparent», with the live preview beside it and the **eyedropper**, a click on the image
that picks the colour for the highlighted rule. The computation is pure and tested
(`ColorReplacementFilter` in `PulseOffice.Drawing/Assets/Filters`): the first matching rule
wins, tolerance applies per channel, an already transparent pixel is not touched, and the comparison
happens on the colour's **true values** and not on those premultiplied by alpha, otherwise a red
at 50% would be 128 and would not be recognized. Unlike the filters it **really changes the pixels**
(`IRasterRecolor` re-encodes to PNG to keep transparency): the new image is saved as
it is in all four formats, with no losses to declare.

The «image → BGRA pixels → image» step was inside the image painter; now it is a
common service (`IBitmapPixels`) used by filters, colour replacement and picking. Moving it brought
out **two real defects**:
- **red and blue swapped in the filters**: the bytes were copied as they arrived and declared
  BGRA, but a decoded PNG arrives in **RGBA** (and sometimes with non-premultiplied alpha). With
  greyscale it did not show; with sepia, pop art, solarize and with the replacement preview
  it did. Now the service converts format and alpha according to what the image declares;
- **the image cache looked at the identifier and not the content**: after *Sostituisci
  l'immagine* (Replace image), *Comprimi* or *Sostituisci i colori* (Replace colours) the slide kept showing the old
  image, because the identifier stayed the same. Now the key is the content itself (the byte
  array, in a weak-reference table, so an image no longer used frees its copy).

**Verified live in Deck**: gradient image inserted, the eyedropper at the centre picks `#86AA8D`
(before the fix it picked `#8DAA86`, with red and blue swapped), the preview shows the area
turned white and the slide shows it after *Va bene* (OK; before it did not), «Pixel sostituiti: 18088» (Pixels replaced: 18088), and
⌘Z brings back the original. Reference presentation coverage **254 → 255 of 368 (69.3%)**.

### Deck: summary slide and expand slide (done)
*Diapositiva riassuntiva* (Summary slide) creates after the current one a slide «Riepilogo» (Summary) with one bullet for
each title of the visible slides; *Espandi diapositiva* (Expand slide) turns each top-level bullet
of the body into a new slide with that title, and the sub-bullets become its body, one level
up — as in the reference suite. The logic is pure and tested (`ISlideOutlining` in
`PulseOffice.Presentations`: empty titles and hidden slides excluded, empty paragraphs skipped);
`DeckActions.InsertOutlineSlides` builds the slides from the master with the placeholder style and
inserts them in **a single undo**. The commands are in *Diapositiva ▸ Gestisci* (Slide ▸ Manage) and in the thumbnail's
context menu, off when there is nothing to summarize or expand. No work
on the formats: they are ordinary slides. **Verified live**: title «Introduzione»,
*Diapositiva riassuntiva* → «Riepilogo • Introduzione», *Espandi* on that one → slide
«Introduzione», ⌘Z removes it. Reference presentation coverage **255 → 257 of 368 (69.8%)**.

### Deck: spelling on slides, with the same engine as Ledger (done)
*Ortografia…* (Spelling…, F7) walks the slides starting from the current one, goes to each unknown
word (slide and box selected) and offers ignore, add to dictionary or the
suggestions; *Correzione ortografica automatica* (Automatic spell checking) draws the **red waves** under misspelled words
on the canvas. The engine is Ledger's (`ISpellChecker`, Hunspell dictionaries, user dictionary), and
the automatic toggle is now **a shared setting** (`IAutoSpellSettings` in
`PulseOffice.Text.Spelling`): `SheetSpelling.Enabled` delegates to it, so turning it on in one module
turns it on in the other too.

`IDeckSpelling` (pure logic, tested with a fake checker) finds errors paragraph by
paragraph skipping fields, and **replaces inside portions keeping the formatting**: a
word straddling two portions becomes one, with the style of the first. After a replacement the
subsequent errors of the same paragraph shift by the length difference, otherwise the
wrong word would be corrected. The waves are drawn by `SpellingWaves` with
`FormattedText.BuildHighlightGeometry`, so they sit under the right word with any font and
alignment; they go only through the editor palette (`SlidePalette.Proofing`), so they do not appear
in the slide show, in thumbnails or in exports. Results are kept in a small per-text
cache, emptied when the user dictionary changes.

**Verified live**: «Questo e un testoo sbagliaato» in the title; with automatic checking on,
the waves appear under the two invented words and not under the others; F7 finds «testoo», offers
«testo», the replacement happens and the search moves on to «sbagliaato» in the right position. Reference presentation coverage
**257 → 259 of 368 (70.4%)**.

### Deck: language of all text, and the document language in both formats (done)
*Strumenti ▸ Lingua ▸ Lingua di tutto il testo…* (Tools ▸ Language ▸ Language of all text…) chooses, among the installed dictionaries, the language with
which to check the presentation (prefilled with the current one). It is a document property
(`DocumentProperties.Language`), set with an undoable action; spelling and the waves on the
canvas use it, with the system language as fallback, and the waves cache has the language in its
key, so changing it redraws immediately.

**It crosses both formats natively**, and applies to all modules because it goes through the common
property mappers: `dc:language` in `meta.xml` (`OdfMetaMapper`) and the `language` property of the
OOXML package (`OoxmlCorePropertiesMapper`). **Verified with the real reference suite**: «de-DE» written by
us in ODP and in PPTX, converted by the reference suite to the other format and read back, comes back «de-DE» in
both directions. **Live**: the dialog opens with it-IT, confirming marks the document and the
status bar says «Lingua della presentazione: it-IT» (Presentation language: it-IT), ⌘Z brings it back unmodified. Reference presentation coverage
**259 → 260 of 368 (70.7%)**.

### Macro signing for all modules — and in ODS it was not saved (done)
**The defect**: in Ledger the macro signature was applied, but **no format wrote it** — neither ODS
nor (declared) XLSX — and it did not go through the history. Saving and reopening it vanished, without any
report: a silent loss against rule 7.

Now signing is a shell command, `shell.tools.macroSignature` (*Strumenti ▸ Macro*, Tools ▸ Macros), valid
for Ledger and Deck. Documents carrying signable macros implement `IMacroSignatureHolder` (in
`PulseOffice.Security`: the signature and the name/source list to sign), and the per-module Strategy
exposes it (`IDocumentOperations.MacroSigning`, with a default implementation on the model). The
dialog states **the status of the current signature** — verified on the content, so «the document has
changed after signing» if a macro has been modified — and offers to sign with a certificate or to
remove the signature; the operation enters the history, marks the document and can be undone.

**In ODF** the signature travels in the macro index (`Scripts/pulseoffice/index.xml`, element
`qs:signature` in a namespace of ours: signer, issuer, fingerprint, expiry, moment, value and
