certificate), for ODS and ODP with the same `OdfMacroMapper`. It is our own part of the package, already
declared in the manifest: the reference suite ignores it and opens the file. **In PPTX** it stays lost with the
macros (`PPTX016`, which now names it), as in XLSX.

**Verified**: signature written and read back in ODP and in ODS, and after the round trip verification answers
«untrusted certificate» (i.e. the signature holds, with a self-signed certificate generated by the test)
and «broken» as soon as a macro is changed; the reference suite converts our signed ODP. Signing was **not tested
live**: the dialog lists the keychain's certificates, which must not be touched; startup is
clean. Reference presentation coverage **260 → 261 of 368 (70.9%)**; reference spreadsheet coverage stays 412/413.

### Deck: all twenty-one controls, live controls, design mode and form settings for all modules (done)
Deck now inserts **all** the control types of the catalog (image button, formatted, date,
time, numeric, currency and pattern fields, image control, file selection, table control, navigation
bar): the commands are born from the enum, so a new type comes in by itself.

**Controls respond**: outside design mode a click on a check box, an option, a list, a
spinner or a scroll bar acts on the control, on the canvas and **in the slide show**, with the same
`IFormControlInteraction` as Ledger (now registered in the container) and one undo per change;
⌥+click selects anyway. **Design mode** is a shared state
(`IFormDesignMode`, moved to `PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Forms`) and the command belongs to the shell
(`shell.form.designMode`), as do **Automatic focus** and **Open in design mode**
(`shell.form.automaticFocus`, `shell.form.openInDesignMode`): these two are **document
settings** (`FormDocumentSettings` on `IFormDocument`, implemented by `Workbook` and `Presentation`),
undoable. Before, Ledger's automatic focus was an in-memory toggle that no format
saved, and *Apri in modo struttura* (Open in design mode) was missing (reference spreadsheet coverage back to 413/413). Opening a document with the flag
design mode turns on; with automatic focus Deck selects the first control in
activation order.

**Formats**: in ODF they are the `form:apply-design-mode` and `form:automatic-focus` attributes of
`office:forms`, which we always wrote as `false` — now they carry the value, in ODS and ODP. XLSX loses them,
declared (`XLSX026`); in PPTX controls are already a declared loss (`PPTX004`).

**Verified live**: check box inserted, the click ticks it; with design mode on, the
same click selects it without changing it. Reference presentation coverage **261 → 276 of 368 (75.0%)**.

### Deck: snapping, grid, panes, display quality and zoom tools (done)
Eighteen *Visualizza* (View) items. **Snapping and guides** (`GridSettings`, editor state like the
grid): grid and guides in front of or behind objects — behind they are drawn with an `Underlay` of the
palette, called by the renderer after the background and before the elements —, dashed helper lines at the
object's edges while moving, and snapping to guides, to the edges and centres of other objects and
to the slide margins, which enter the lines of `SnapLines`. **Panes and view**
(`DeckViewOptions`, one per view and reached by commands through `DeckTarget`): slides
pane, notes pane below the canvas (notes are saved when leaving the field or changing
slide), comments shown or hidden, and **quality** in colour, greyscale or black and
white: the slide is rendered into a bitmap and goes through the shared filters (`GrayscaleFilter` and the
new `ThresholdFilter`). **Zoom**: forward and back history (`ZoomHistory`, pure and
tested logic), zoom on the selected objects with scrolling that centres them, and two pointer
tools — the hand that pans the view and the zoom that magnifies on click (⌥ reduces) around the
pressed point. **Verified live**: notes pane and greyscale. Reference presentation coverage **276 → 294 of 368
(79.9%)**.

### Deck: the reference suite's nine automatic layouts (done)
Centred text, three panes (1+2 and 2+1), two panes one above the other, three panes (2 above, 1
below), four and six panes, vertical title with text and chart, title with two vertical texts:
in the enum, in the master with their placeholders, in the layout commands, with icon and five languages. In
OOXML each has its native type (`objOnly`, `objAndTwoObj`, `twoObjAndObj`, `objOverTx`,
`twoObjOverTx`, `fourObj`, `vertTitleAndTxOverChart`, `twoColTx`); the six panes has no type and
is written `cust`, recognized by the layout **name** (`cSld/@name`, which is the enum name): the
registry now has `FromOoxml(type, name)`, so someone else's custom layout does not by mistake become
a six panes. The twenty round-trip tests per format also cover the nine new ones.

**Correction of a verification written here in the past**: testing with the real reference suite, the layouts of
slides **from the second onwards do not survive** the round trip either from ODP to PPTX or the reverse —
not even the eleven from before, which the log gave as verified. The reference suite derives the automatic
layout from the list of placeholders of the `presentation-page-layout` and applies it
to the first page only. Our round trip is exact; interoperability with the reference suite on layouts is an
**open point**, entrusted to a separate task. Reference presentation coverage **294 → 303 of 368 (82.3%)**.

### Deck: paste special and unformatted, fields, embedded objects, external tool, scanner for all modules (done)
**Paste unformatted text** (⌥⇧⌘V) takes the text from the system clipboard and puts it at the cursor
if you are typing, otherwise in the selected text or in a new box; **Paste special**
(⇧⌘V) asks for the form among those really available (Deck objects, unformatted text). The
system clipboard text goes through a shared service (`ISystemClipboardText` in
`PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Services`), instead of a second function that fishes for the window. **Edit
field** changes the type of the fields of the selected box recalculating their value. **Open the embedded
object** writes the file into a temporary folder of its own and opens it with the system application;
**Edit with external tool** does the same with an image and reloads it when the file changes, with
Ledger's watcher made shared (`IExternalEditWatcher` in `UI.Controls/Objects`). The reference suite's
search bar corresponds to our *Trova e sostituisci* (Find and replace) dialog.

**The scanner belongs to the shell** (`shell.scan.selectSource`, `shell.scan.request`): it was Ledger's, and now it
inserts the acquired image into the active module through the Strategy
(`IDocumentOperations.InsertImage`, implemented by Ledger with its anchored insertion and by Deck at the
centre of the slide). SANE and WIA remain the two paths, so nothing exclusive to Windows.

Fixed along the way: in the inspector free text boxes appeared as «Free», the
enum name, and captions and images likewise. Unformatted paste **verified live**.
Reference presentation coverage **303 → 310 of 368 (84.2%)**.

### Deck: paragraphs, lists, named objects and interaction, distribution, image colour (done)
Align to paragraph start and end (in Deck text is left to right, so they
coincide with left and right), **move paragraph** up and down (`MoveParagraphs`: the block of
touched paragraphs swaps places with its neighbour), **Elenchi puntati e numerati** (Bullets and numbering) dialog (type and level,
`SetList`). **Distribution** with the new pure logic `BoxDistribution` in `PulseOffice.Drawing/Layout`
(extremes fixed, equal spaces); **in front of or behind a chosen object** (with two selected, the
primary one goes right above or below the other); **Interazione…** (Interaction…), the dialog for the on-click action.

**Object names** are a datum of `EmbeddedObject` (`Name`, distinct from the alternative text) and
cross both formats: `draw:name` in ODP, and in PPTX an extension of ours inside `cNvPr`
(`a:extLst/a:ext` with `qo:name`), because the `name` of `cNvPr` is already the marker by which we recognize
shapes. **Image colour** (brightness, contrast, red, green, blue, gamma) is a per-pixel filter
(`ColorAdjustmentFilter`) behind a shared dialog (`IRasterColorAdjust`), in Deck and in Ledger;
like colour replacement it really changes the pixels, so it has no losses in the formats. **Resolution
check** lists the images below 150 dots per inch at the size at which they are shown.
Reference presentation coverage **310 → 322 of 368 (87.5%)**.

### Deck: shape conversions, 3D extrusion in both formats (done)
*Formato ▸ Converti* (Format ▸ Convert): **to curve** and **to polygon** (`ShapeConversion` in `PulseOffice.Drawing/Freeform`,
pure, tested logic: arcs are flattened into cubics and cubics are sampled into segments),
**to contour** (the path without fill, with the fill colour on the line if there was no
line), **to metafile** (a vector with the SVG of the outline and its paint), **to bitmap** (the
shared painter into a `RenderTargetBitmap`, at two pixels per point).

**To 3D** and **To 3D rotation object** are a new datum of the shared shape style
(`ShapeExtrusion`: type and depth), so they apply in Ledger too: the shared painter draws the
shaded depth planes behind the shape, and the rotation object with a cylindrical light. **Native
formats**: in ODF `draw:extrusion` and `draw:extrusion-depth` on `draw:enhanced-geometry` — and the reference suite
**really draws** our extruded shape in 3D, verified in its PDF —, in OOXML `a:sp3d` with
`extrusionH` and an `a:scene3d` with an isometric camera, and the reference suite brings it back from one of our PPTXs into ODP
extruded. The rotation object has no equivalent on shapes and is saved extruded, declared
(`ODP018`, `PPTX018`).

**A silent loss closed along the way**: in Deck's PPTX the shapes' **bevel** was not
written at all (only Ledger wrote it); now `Scene` and `Bevel` receive the whole style and Deck
writes them. One round-trip test per format covers extrusion, bevel and name. **Verified
live**: rectangle inserted, *In 3D* (To 3D) extrudes it on the canvas. Reference presentation coverage **322 → 329 of 368 (89.4%)**.
### Real flowchart and symbol shapes, for every module (done)
Ledger's "flowchart shapes" and "symbol shapes" were generic shapes
(rectangle, diamond, hexagon) gathered under another name. Now the shared catalogue has **42 new
shapes**: the 28 flowchart shapes of PowerPoint and the reference suite (process, decision, data, document, multiple documents,
terminator, preparation, connectors, punched tape, sort, merge, delay, magnetic
disk, …) and 14 symbols (smiley face, sun, moon, lightning bolt, cloud, "no" symbol, donut, block arc, folded
corner, bevel, frame, plaque, square and curly brackets). The geometry is written with a
**Builder** (`OutlineBuilder`) inside a table (`ExtendedShapes`), the families live in
`ShapeFamilies` and serve both the Deck gallery and the Ledger gallery. Each shape has its own
**native OOXML preset** (`flowChartDecision`, `smileyFace`, …) and the reference suite's name on reading.

**A real defect closed along the way**: Deck's ODP writer declared only the type
`ooxml-<preset>` and not the path, and the reference suite **did not draw** shapes it does not recognise by itself;
Ledger's writer also wrote `draw:enhanced-path`. Now Deck writes it too. **Verified with the
real reference suite**: decision, document, sun and smiley face come back as such in both directions (ODP→PPTX and
PPTX→ODP) and are drawn in its PNG. Presentation coverage **329 → 331 of 368 (89.9%)**.

### Deck: multiple masters, master elements, master background and objects (done)
A presentation now has **several masters** (`Presentation.Masters`; `Master` remains the main one) and each
slide can point to one (`Slide.MasterId`, null for the main one). Rendering asks for the master and
theme **of the slide** (`MasterOf`, `ThemeOf`): `SlideView` receives the presentation and derives them by
itself, so canvas, thumbnails, slide show, presenter view and export follow without code for
each. Commands: **New master** (from a catalogue theme), **Delete master** (the slides that
use it go back to the main one, undoable), **Change the slide's master** (for the current one or for
all), **Master elements** (date, footer, number: `MasterElements`, which the footer resolver
respects). New slides inherit the master of the slide after which they are created. Per slide,
**Master background** and **Master objects** (`ShowMasterBackground`, `ShowMasterObjects`).

**Formats, native**: in ODF one `style:master-page` per master (with its background style, the
`date-time`/`footer`/`page-number` frames for the elements and the theme name in an attribute of ours) and
`draw:master-page-name` on the pages; `presentation:background-visible` and
`background-objects-visible` on the page. In OOXML one `slideMaster` per master, each with its own
`theme` and its layouts, the `dt`/`ftr`/`sldNum` placeholders for the elements and `showMasterSp` on the
slide; a hidden master background becomes an explicit white background (`PPTX019`).

**A real defect found along the way**: the PPTX layouts **had no relationship to their
`slideMaster`**, which the schema requires — a strict PowerPoint would have had to repair the file. Now it is there.

**The reference suite**: from our ODP it keeps the two masters (renaming them with the visible name); when importing a
PPTX it instead creates one master per layout, and when exporting to PPTX it merges them into one — that is its model, not
a defect of ours. Our round trip is exact and tested in both formats. **Verified live**: new
master with the Ardesia (Slate) theme, *Change the master* moves the slide onto the dark background. Presentation coverage **333 → 337
of 368 (91.6%)**.

### Deck: gallery, photo album, coordinate guides, theme, navigator, developer tools, colour bar (done)
**Gallery** opens the icon and sticker collections (the same `AssetPickerView` as Ledger) and inserts the
chosen vector. **Photo album**: several photos are chosen (the file service can now open
more than one, `OpenFilesAsync`), one, two or four per slide, with the title from the name; the
arrangement is pure logic (`PhotoAlbum`) and the insertion a single undo. **Snap guide**
at coordinates in centimetres (horizontal, vertical or point). **Theme…** chooses the theme and the fonts
for titles and body text. **Navigator** (⌃⇧F5): slides and named objects, and takes us there.
**Developer tools**: the state of the model — presentation, masters, current slide with every
element (type, position, size, rotation), selection, history. **Colour bar** below the
canvas: a click colours the fill of the selected shapes, right click the line.

**Verified live**: rectangle inserted, colour bar switched on, a click on red colours it.
Presentation coverage **337 → 344 of 368 (93.5%)**.

### Deck: graphic styles (done)
A **graphic style** is a named appearance (`GraphicStyle` in the `Presentation.GraphicStyles` catalogue)
and shapes and paths remember which one they are bound to (`StyleName`). **New style from selection**
creates it from the selected object; **Update style** redefines it from the object and **all the
bound objects change together**, in a single undo (`DeckActions.ChangeGraphicStyles`, which
re-binds the objects with a function); **Edit style…** opens the shared shape-style dialog
on the style; **Style management** (F11) applies it to the selection or deletes it (the objects
keep their appearance); the **styles panel** in the sidebar lists them and a click applies them.

**Native ODF**: the styles are `style:style` of family `graphic` in `styles.xml` (with `display-name`),
and the shape's automatic style inherits from them with `style:parent-style-name`. **Verified with the real
reference suite**: rewritten by it, the "Avviso" (Warning) style and the shape's binding come back intact (together with
the reference suite's default graphic styles, which are document styles and are read as such). OOXML
has no graphic styles: the objects keep their appearance and lose the binding, declared (`PPTX020`).
Presentation coverage **344 → 349 of 368 (94.8%)**.

### Deck: enter and exit group, table cells on the canvas (done)
**Enter group** (F3) opens the selected group into single objects and remembers which they are; **Exit
group** (⌃F3) joins them back into a new group. Each is a step in the history.

**Tables now have a cell selection on the canvas**: with the table selected, a click chooses
the cell and ⇧+click extends the range; the range is drawn translucently. **Select row** and **Select
column** widen it, and **add/delete row and column** work on the selection — they insert
after and remove the selected rows or columns — instead of always at the end. The geometry
(`TableGeometry`, `TableCellRange` in `PulseOffice.Document/Embedding`) uses the same measurements as the
renderer. **Verified live**: click on a cell of the second row, *Select row*, the whole row
is highlighted. Presentation coverage **349 → 353 of 368 (95.9%)**.

### Deck: complete transition and animation dialogs (done)
The two items were "partial": type and direction were chosen in the inspector, the rest was not. **Transition…**
sets effect, direction (translated), duration, advance on click or after a time, sound and sound
looping, and applies to the slide or to all of them in a single undo (`SetTransitions`).
**Animation…** chooses an animation of the slide and sets its effect (the presets of its
category, which the registry can now list), start (on click, with previous, after previous),
delay, duration, repetitions and order (earlier, later, delete), also undoable (`ReplaceAnimations`).
All these fields already crossed both formats.

**Found by a real start-up**: `IAnimationPresetRegistry` was not in the container and the application crashed
at start-up; now it is registered. **Verified live**: the transition dialog opens with the values
of the slide. Presentation coverage **353 → 355 of 368 (96.5%)**.

### Deck: Fontwork (done)
`FontworkObject` (in `PulseOffice.Drawing/Fontwork`) carries text and warp — plain, arch up/down,
circle, wave, slant up/down, triangle — and `FontworkRenderer` draws it glyph by glyph along the
path (`FontworkPath`), so it works on canvas, thumbnail, print and export. The warp table
is a single one (`FontworkWarps`, `fontwork-*` tokens in ODF and `text*` in OOXML) and both codecs
read it. In OOXML it is `a:prstTxWarp` and **the reference suite renders it as arched WordArt**; in ODF it is
a `custom-shape` with `draw:text-path`, which we read back intact but which the reference suite still shows
as plain text — open limit, queued among the defects. Fixed along the way: the master placeholders
in ODP appeared in the reference suite as light-blue boxes; now they have a style with no fill and no
outline, the `backgroundobjects` layer and `presentation:placeholder`.

### Deck: the last eleven items — presentation coverage is 367 of 367 (100%)
Each item closed with a real feature, and each one brought up something to fix.

**Edit points** (`deck.draw.editPoints`): the nodes of the freeform path are visible and can be
dragged on the canvas, with insertion, deletion, node type and path closing. At the
end the object's box **refits** to the path (`FreeformRefit`, pure and tested logic):
without it, a node pulled out of the box stayed outside the handles and the snap points.

**Glue points** (`deck.draw.gluePoints`): a mode in which every object shows its four
connection points, and a click on two points of different objects creates a connector fixed exactly to those
sides (`IDeckConnectors.Connect` now accepts the sides).

**Macro recorder** (`shell.tools.recordMacro`, part of the shell, hence for Ledger and Deck): it records
the executed commands and, at the end, saves a JavaScript macro that replays them with **`app.Run`**, a new
member of the API (`IScriptCommands`). The macro enters the document library going through the
history. Ledger's existing command was a toggle that recorded nothing.

**Add field** (`deck.form.addField`): it chooses a source with the already shared data import
dialog and adds, for every chosen column, a label and a box **bound** to the
column with the value of the first row. The binding is native in ODF (`form:data-field` on the
control, `form:datasource` and `form:command` on the form) and **the reference suite keeps it**; in XLSX it is
declared (`XLSX026`).

**Notes and handout master** (`deck.view.notesMaster`, `deck.view.handoutMaster`): two views
with the A4 page, draggable slide and notes boxes, header, footer, page
number, notes body and slides per page (`HandoutLayout`, pure logic). Print and
export use them. In ODF they are `presentation:notes` inside every `style:master-page` and
`style:handout-master`; in OOXML they are real `notesMaster` and `handoutMaster`, and the slides per
page — which PowerPoint does not save — travel in an extension of ours (`PPTX021`).
**Two silent losses found along the way**: in PPTX the **speaker notes were neither saved nor
read**, and in ODP they were written as a direct `draw:text-box`, which the reference suite discarded. Now they are
real notes pages in both formats, and the round trip through the reference suite keeps them.

**External links** (`deck.edit.links`, `deck.insert.imageLink`): an image can show an
external file instead of containing it (`RasterImageObject.LinkPath`). Native in both formats —
external `xlink:href` in ODF, `r:link` in OOXML — and the relative paths written by the reference suite are
resolved against the document on opening. The dialog (`ExternalLinksView` with `IImageLinks`,
shared) updates, changes source or unlinks. In spreadsheets the link is lost, declared
(`ODF023`, `XLSX027`).

**Media player** (Deck and Ledger, `IMediaPlayer`): it lists the document's media, plays them
with the system player, opens a file and inserts it. **In the slide show** too a click on
a media item now plays it: before, media were only drawn. Writing to a temporary file
and opening it, which were copied in Ledger and in Deck, are now a single service (`IEmbeddedFileLauncher`).
Declared: playback happens in the system player, not inside the slide.

**Animated image** (`deck.insert.animatedImage`): the selected objects become the frames of
an **animated GIF** that takes their place. We write the GIF codec ourselves (`GifCodec` in
`PulseOffice.Drawing/Assets/Gif`: fixed palette, LZW, loop extension, decoding with
interlacing and frame disposal), tested on a round trip and read by macOS. The
shared image renderer **animates GIFs** on the canvas, in the thumbnails and in the slide show.

**Remote control** (`deck.slideshow.remote`): instead of the reference suite's Bluetooth app, a small
local web server (`RemoteServer`, in the core, with no UI) with a four-digit PIN and a
QR code: the phone opens the page, moves forward, back and reads the notes. Without the PIN nothing
can be controlled — a test guards it. **Not tried on screen**: on this Mac the firewall is active
and opening the port would have brought up the system warning.

**Fontwork** closes the previous round: eight warps in both formats; in ODP the reference suite still
shows it as plain text (queued among the defects).

### Layouts survive the round trip through the reference suite (done)
The defect of layouts lost from the second slide on was **ours**: we wrote
`presentation:presentation-page-layout`, while the element is `style:presentation-page-layout`, and
the reference suite ignored it. Now it is written correctly and both forms are read. The reference suite renames the
layouts `AL<n>T<id>`, where `id` is its autolayout: the registry
recognises them, and accepts the OOXML aliases the reference suite uses when exporting (`tx`, `txAndTwoObj`, …).
**Verified with the real reference suite**: twenty layouts written in ODP, rewritten by it in ODP,
all come back except those it does not have (they degrade to the nearest one).

### Fontwork looks like Fontwork in the reference suite too (done)
In our ODP and ODS files the reference suite showed Fontwork as straight text. The geometry was right:
found by bisection on a file produced by the reference suite itself, **it does not bend the text along the
path if the font size is small**, and the shape style carried the default 11 pt. Now the style
of a Fontwork (`OdfFontworkGeometry.Lettering`, shared by Deck and Ledger) declares a size
proportional to the frame height and no wrapping. **Verified with the real reference suite**: "Benvenuti" (Welcome)
in an arch in its PNG.

### Saving over a signed document asks for confirmation (done)
Saving rewrites the package, so the digital signatures, which cover the content, are no longer valid and
disappear. Before, this happened silently. Now `ISignedSaveGuard` (in the shell, hence for Ledger and Deck)
checks whether the file about to be written carries `META-INF/documentsignatures.xml` and, if so, asks:
*Save and remove the signatures* or *Cancel*, which is the default choice. It applies to *Save* and to *Save
as* over the same file. **Verified live**: an ODP signed with a certificate generated on the
spot, edited in Deck, ⌘S shows the question, and on cancelling the signature stays in the file.

### Native header and footer in both formats (done)
Before, they travelled only as an extension of ours, which the reference suite and PowerPoint ignore: our files
opened without date, footer and number. The extension stays, because it reads back our
settings exactly; next to it there is now the native form.
- **ODF** (`OdfHeaderFooter`): `presentation:footer-decl` and `date-time-decl` at the top of the
  presentation, `use-footer-name` and `use-date-time-name` on the pages, `display-footer`,
  `display-page-number` and `display-date-time` in the style of each page, and the master frames with
  the fields `presentation:footer`, `presentation:date-time` and `text:page-number`.
- **OOXML** (`PptxHeaderFooter`): on the slides where they must be shown, the `dt`, `ftr` and
  `sldNum` placeholders with the text and the `datetime1` and `slidenum` fields.
On reading, without the extension, the settings are derived from the native form; and the date, footer and number frames
and placeholders no longer become text boxes. Removed `ODP013` and `PPTX007`.
**Verified with the real reference suite**: from our ODP and our PPTX its PDF shows "1 ottobre
2026 · Riservato · 2" (1 October 2026 · Confidential · 2) on the second slide and nothing on the title slide; the round trip ODP →
reference suite → PPTX comes back with texts and switches. In the direction PPTX → reference suite → ODP it is the reference suite that
loses the date and footer texts: the switches come back, not the words.

### Bug audit, first round: Ledger engine and spreadsheet formats (done)
Before Folio, a systematic audit: four parallel searches (spreadsheet formats, presentation
formats, engine, Deck UI and shell), then verification of each report in the code,
fix, test and — for the formats — round trip through the real reference suite.

**Engine.** A cell cited both directly and in a range (`=A1+SUM(A1:A3)`) came out as
circular. **Paste, sort, replace and their undos did not recalculate**: they wrote into the
sheet without going through the engine. Now it is the sheet that notifies (`Worksheet.ContentChanged`, re-raised
by `Workbook.CellContentChanged`) and the engine resynchronises formula and dependencies of any cell
changed from outside, so no caller can forget it any more; the engine's own writes
are excluded by a counter. Others: moving cells did not rewrite the formulas (now
`StructureChange` has a "band" of rows or columns); writing into a cell filled by a spill
lost it on recalculation (now the spill goes to `#SPILL!` and the data stays); readers of spilled cells
stayed stale; backward fill and numbered text with several source cells; numbers in
pasted and replaced text read according to the locale (`1.5` became 15); *Replace* turned
formulas into constants; blanks at the top in descending sort; pivot with several row fields and percentage
of row; the snapshot for undoing structural operations did not save formulas of other
sheets, comments, print ranges and groups; transposed paste; volatile functions and defined names that
did not recalculate. **Not fixed, by choice**: `=VERO()=1` (`=TRUE()=1`) stays TRUE, because in the reference suite — the
specification — booleans are numbers; the report reasoned like Excel.

**Spreadsheet formats.** The worst defect: **in XLSX cell comments did not exist**, neither on
writing nor on reading, and no `CheckFidelity` said so — the log above claimed the
opposite. Now `XlsxCommentMapper` writes the comments part and the VML drawing Excel uses to
show them. Then: **the ODF formula dialect did not quote sheets with spaces or apostrophes** and did not
read back ranges with the sheet on both ends (the reference suite's form), so
any formula across sheets with such names broke; in XLSX inline strings lost and text
formulas misread, user-defined names never written nor read, hidden empty rows and closed
column groups lost, string spaces not preserved; in ODS hidden rows and columns never
written nor read, nested row groups by position in the list instead of by row number,
comments and validations on empty cells lost, times read as empty, multi-line text and multiple
spaces (now `OdfParagraphText`, shared by cells and comments), sheet-local names that
hid the global ones, print ranges on sheets with spaces. The ODF package is saved without
indentation and read preserving spaces.

**Verified with the real reference suite, in both directions**: a sheet "Dati 2024" (Data 2024) with text with spaces and line breaks,
comment on an empty cell, hidden row and column, group after empty rows, print range, defined
name, formula from another sheet and time, written in ODS and in XLSX, rewritten by the reference suite
in the other format and read back, comes back intact. **Live**: pasting 5 in A1 updates `=SUM(A1:A2)`
and ⌘Z takes it back.

**Presentation formats.** ODP coordinates in inches, millimetres or points were read as
zero: there were **seven** different measurement parsers, each with its gaps, now reduced to one
(`OdfLength`). **The stacking order among different types was lost** in both formats,
on writing (first all texts, then media, then objects) and on reading (the order of the readers,
not that of the document): now a single pass in stacking order and the position of the node on
reading. Respecting the order uncovered a hidden defect: without placeholder markers (the files
the reference suite rewrites) **the title was "the first text in the list"**, and with the right order it
no longer is; now it is the topmost text of the slide. Then: animations on non-text objects
never written in PPTX; slide background colour never read back in PPTX and always read back as
its own in ODP (now `SlideBackgroundNormalizer` removes what the master would give anyway); ODP master
backgrounds never read back; fill definitions in the automatic styles instead of in
`styles.xml`; duplicate style names for layouts with two bodies; duplicate page names; spaces and
line breaks in text, comments, shapes and tables; date of ODP comments; the reference suite's
comments (`officeooo:annotation`) ignored; theme hyperlink colours and system colours
in PPTX; order of the children of `draw:page`; readers that left the stream moved or crashed on
malformed files (ODS too, which caught none of them); state that grew from one save
to the next; every PPTX run marked as Italian. **Verified with the real reference suite in both
directions**: shape under the title, animation on the shape, own and inherited background, double spaces in the
title and two-line comment come back intact from ODP → PPTX and from PPTX → ODP.

**Deck UI and shell.** Two crashes: **autosave ran on a background
thread** (`System.Threading.Timer`) reading lists and models that the UI modifies, and
caught only I/O errors, so any other error brought the application down
(now `DispatcherTimer`, with no overlapping runs); **an unreadable recovery snapshot brought
the app down at every start-up**, and after a partial recovery the snapshots not recovered were
deleted. **Text being typed was lost**: title, notes and Outline entered the
document only on leaving the field, so ⌘S saved without it and ⌘Q closed without asking; now the views
with pending edits implement `IPendingEditsOwner` and the document commits them before
saving and closing. **Saving emptied the file before writing it**: now it is written in
memory and then the file is replaced atomically (`AtomicFile`), in Ledger and in Deck.
Autosave **did not cover presentations** (`DeckSnapshotProvider` was missing). Changing
layout erased animations, interactions, comments, name and background image, and the undo
put back a clone instead of the slide; `NextId` gave a new slide the identifier
of one already read from file; `SetSlideText` recorded changes even for unchanged text (leaving the
Outline marked the document and erased its formatting). Then: closed tab that stayed
visible and re-activatable, memory leaks (`SlideView` and `StartView` hooked to shared
services), previous slide's footer after a transition, laser pointer stuck,
outline mode switched back on at every tab change, Ledger save messages written in
Italian in the code. **Verified live**: title typed in Deck without leaving the field, ⌘Q
shows "Deck1 ha modifiche non salvate" (Deck1 has unsaved changes), and the exit is clean.

### Bug audit, second round: PDF, Ledger, macros, external data (done)
Four parallel searches — charts, PDF and printing; Ledger UI and commands; macros and
scripting; external data and remote storage — then verification of each report in the code.

**PDF and printing.** An **emoji** in a cell, in a title or in the author **brought down the
export**: half of a surrogate pair ended up in `Normalize`, which throws. Now it becomes `?`, only
once, and the exporter also catches argument errors. Strings escape control
characters (`\r`, `\t`, octal), in a single place (`PdfEncoding.Literal`) instead of two copies; NaN and
infinities no longer enter the stream; the paginator does not produce blank pages when a slice starts
with hidden rows. In charts, scales with infinite values and OOXML points with non-contiguous `idx`
(Excel and the reference suite skip the gaps) ended up in the wrong category.

**Ledger.** The most serious: **editing a cell containing 1,5 turned it into 15** — the editor showed the
number in English form ("1.5") and the write read it back in Italian, where the dot separates thousands.
Now the cell is shown and read back in the same locale, and numbers are read without thousands, currency or
parentheses. Then: switching tab during editing wrote the text **into the other sheet** (the edit
now remembers the sheet too); undoing the insertion of a sheet brought down the view; **pivots,
revisions, autofilter and named styles** changed the document without history, hence without
undo and without the "Save?" question. For pivots and revisions there is now a **workbook
restore point** (`IWorkbookCheckpoints`: sheets, snapshots, pivots), shared by the command
base (`LedgerCommandSet.Checkpointed`); the autofilter has a memento (`AutoFilterMemento`).
Fill, controls and objects ignored read-only mode and protection. The view hooked itself forever
to global services (signatures, outline mode, tools): now only while it is loaded. The numeric
settings rejected a `long` where they expected an `int`, and out-of-range values read from file
were used as they were.

**Macros.** **IronPython cannot be isolated**: the facade objects are CLR objects, and from there
reflection reaches everywhere. Python macros **no longer start from the document macro sandbox**
(control events); they run only from the editor, where the user starts them
(`ScriptPermissions.AllowsUnsandboxedEngines`). And now **they stop at the time limit**: a trace
function checks the token, and a safety deadline answers anyway. JavaScript catches
exceptions from the facades (before, they made the task fail without being observed); an approval that
fails **denies**; `app.Run` does not execute commands that touch files, mail, printing, network, signatures or other
macros; `page.ExportPdf` writes only a new `.pdf`, never over an existing file. **Macro writes
did not enter the history**: now every cell write is undoable and operations on
ranges go through a snapshot; a range over a million cells is rejected instead of
freezing the UI. In ODF two macros with names that reduce to the same file ("Totale 1" and
"Totale-1") overwrote each other; now the files are unique. **The macro signature also covers the
language** and uses length prefixes, and the signer's identity is derived from the certificate, not
from the file attributes, which anyone can write.

**External data and remote storage.** On macOS **the password was passed as an argument** to `security`,
visible to anyone with `ps`: now it goes on the standard input of `security -i`, in hexadecimal, and
reading recognises the hexadecimal answer for non-ASCII passwords. **Not tried live**: it requires the
real keychain, which is not to be touched. On Linux trailing newlines of the password are no longer stripped. WebDAV
encodes paths (a file `report#1.ods` was truncated at the `#`) and does not send basic authentication over
`http` outside the local machine; timeouts and odd JSON responses no longer bring down WebDAV and cloud;
Google Drive follows pages beyond 200 items; token refresh happens one at a time; the OAuth
sign-in ignores unrelated requests (the icon requested by the browser closed the sign-in) and frees the port if
the browser does not open. Import quotes the table name with the provider. In
CSV a quote in the middle of a field (`Tubo 3/4"`) **swallowed the rest of the file**, and saving
moved to A1 data that started further down. HTML writes only valid colours in styles,
mail addresses cannot add parameters to `mailto:`, and the iCloud folder no longer brings
anything down on a rejected path or an access denied by the system.

### Bug audit, third round: shell, signatures, Deck, drawing (done)
Four parallel searches — shell and undo; signatures, protection and security; Deck editing
commands and remote control; shared drawing — plus the minor points left open by the second round.

**Shell and history.** An exception inside a transaction left it open forever: from then on every
change ended up in the dead transaction, hence no undo and no "Save?" question. The
defect was born in the second round (named styles and revisions): now transactions are `using`.
`UndoStack` no longer loses the action if undoing it fails, refuses undo and redo during a
transaction, and after `Clear` no longer makes a modified document look saved. Shortcuts and the native
menu **acted behind an open dialog** (⌘Z inside a form undid the document underneath): now they
stop while there is a modal (`CommandSurfaceFactory.Blocked`). The same tab no longer opens two
close questions; remote hand-off does not upload an unsaved file and does not release the lock;
*Save* in the close question no longer closes a document nobody knows how to save. Versions
open as a new document (before, from a temporary folder, where ⌘S saved) and temporary
folders are deleted.

**Signatures.** The PDF signature **could be bypassed**: by adding an update after the signature, the signed
range still covered the original file and verification said *valid*. Now the range must start
from zero, the gap must be exactly the signature, and if the range does not reach the end of the file the
signature is *broken*. The signature is read **from the gap in the range**, not from the first `/Contents` in the file;
the certificate is the signer's (`SignerInfos[0]`), not the first in the chain; signing a PDF
that was already signed looked for the placeholders from the start and **corrupted the previous signature**; trailer and catalogue
are taken from the last update; writing is atomic. In ODF the signature date is read only
from the signed and referenced property (before, any `dc:date` before it was enough), package
entries that differ only in case break the signature, and a damaged package no longer brings
down opening.

**Sheet and structure protection was not saved in any format**, without declaring it. Now in
ODF it is `table:protected` and `table:structure-protected` with `table:protection-key` in SHA-256, which is
exactly our hash: **the reference suite recognises and keeps it, password included**. In XLSX the
protection is written but the password is not (Excel uses a salted, iterated hash that cannot be derived from ours):
declared loss (`XLSX028`). A password in a format we cannot verify blocks instead of
letting through. Structure protection now goes through the history.

**Deck.** When merging text runs five effects and the fields were ignored: the shadow on a letter
in the middle disappeared at once. Now two runs merge only if they are identical in everything and neither is a field.
**The remote control** had a four-digit PIN with no attempt limit, listened on all
interfaces and read lines without limit: now it listens on the address it shows, locks after ten
wrong PINs, compares in constant time, limits lines, headers, time and connections. Adding
or removing rows and columns **ruined merges, formats and measurements** of the table: now the structure is a
pure and tested service (`ITableStructure` in `PulseOffice.Document/Embedding`) that moves everything together.
Deleting a slide also removes it from custom shows and from the slide show
range, and if it opened a section the mark passes to the next one. Search finds words split
across runs and replace keeps the formatting of the first; pasted objects have
content with its own identifier; summary, expand and album use the master of the neighbouring
slide.

**Drawing.** A malformed GIF brought down rendering (minimum LZW code size, huge
dimensions, frames outside the canvas): now there is a cap on pixels and memory. The filters worked on
**premultiplied** pixels as if they were not, and *Invert* turned transparent areas
white: now alpha is removed and put back. **The arc flattener ignored the radii**: a
semicircle became a straight line in ODF, OOXML and PDF. Now it is the real endpoint-to-centre conversion,
split into segments of at most 90°, and the arc also carries `LargeArc` and rotation, which the SVG reader
read and threw away; compact flags (`a1 1 0 01 5 5`) are read one by one. The SVG reader derives the
scale from `width`/`height` when `viewBox` is missing, reads circles, ellipses, lines, polylines and polygons,
ignores what lies in `defs` and similar, and forbids DTDs. The QR code **rejects** a text that is too long
instead of truncating it, and an unknown licence of a collection is no longer declared MIT but treated as
share-alike. Left out, declared: SVG transformations (`transform`).

**Verified.** With the reference suite: protection in both directions (sheets always, structure in ODF; in XLSX
the reference suite itself loses it); rounded rectangle and ellipse drawn correctly after the new
arc conversion. Live in Deck: table inserted, column added and row removed with the
headers in their place; clean exit.

### The areas left open after the three audits (done)
Sixteen points left open, all closed; the seventeenth (printing on Windows) stays in the Open
points, to be tried on a real Windows.

**ODF signatures interoperable with the reference suite.** The biggest point, and a clear result: before, the reference suite's
signatures always came out *broken* for us, and the reference suite judged ours *not valid*. Verification
is now an implementation of XML-DSig of our own (`XmlDsigAlgorithms`): it respects the declared digest
and signature algorithms (SHA-1/256/384/512, RSA and ECDSA), the C14N transform, encoded
URIs and internal references canonicalised in their context, XAdES ones included. .NET's `SignedXml`
could not be used: it rejects external references on principle, and an ODF signature is made
of nothing else (the resolver is not even called). The signature we write follows the reference suite's
form: it also signs `mimetype` and `META-INF/manifest.xml`, applies C14N to the streams the manifest
declares `text/xml`, carries `X509IssuerSerial`. **Two defects found along the way**: the signatures file
was written *indented*, and the added whitespace invalidated what had just been signed; and the
canonical form of the date property depended on where the serializer put the namespace
declarations. Like the reference suite, a signature with several certificate blocks or with an `X509IssuerSerial`
that does not match the verifying certificate does not indicate a trustworthy signer.
**Verified with the real reference suite**, querying its signature service (`DocumentDigitalSignatures`)
from a macro run inside the reference suite with a temporary profile: our signature is *valid* for
the reference suite; the signatures of its test documents (`good.odt`, `good-xades.odt`, certificate
chain) are valid for us and `bad.odt` is broken; a document signed by the reference suite and then by us
carries two signatures valid for both. The certificate is judged at the signing date and with its key
usage (`CertificateJudge`, shared by ODF and PDF).

**The others.** SVG transformations (`SvgTransform`, affine matrices composed from the ancestors).
Huge images decoded downscaled by reading the size from the header (`ImageHeader`), filtered
variants in a bounded cache. Icon collections with duplicate identifiers. Empty chart values:
they stay empty in ODF and OOXML in both directions (verified with the reference suite) and the lines break; along
the way, charts in PPTX files converted by the reference suite were lost in ODP because the frame has
a fallback image. Temporary files in a session folder (`ITemporaryFiles`) deleted
on exit. Redaction of IBANs with spaces and cards with 13 to 19 digits, and a pattern that times out redacts
everything instead of leaving the data. Lock files in the reference suite's format. Save guard that
sees the reference suite's macro signature. Macros that wrote into a read-only document: the
dispatcher is decorated (`ReadOnlyGuardedDispatcher`) and functions that modify go through `Write`.
Cursor position in completion, computed in one place only (`SourcePositions`). Pagination of
OneDrive and Dropbox, with the Dropbox path escaped in the JSON. Local name of remote files. Paragraph
positions in Deck measured in one way only. Without animations, going back to the previous slide
required two presses.

Still to verify live: writing the password into the macOS keychain (the real
keychain is not touched) and video export on Windows.

### Bug audit, fourth round: functions, number formats, analysis, presentations, video (done)
Four parallel searches on the areas not touched by the previous rounds, about ninety reports,
verified and fixed.

**Sheet functions.** Rounding with binary error (`ROUNDUP(1.1;1)` gave 1.2): now the value is
scaled to fifteen significant digits before rounding, like the reference suite's `approxFloor`. `ERF`/`ERFC`
with Cody's approximations (`ERFC(5)` = 1.537·10⁻¹²). Wildcards `? * ~` shared
(`WildcardPattern`) by criteria, `SEARCH` and `MATCH`; `""`, `"="` and `"<>"` in criteria count
empty and non-empty cells. `INDEX` with row or column 0, `LOOKUP` on a range from the last column,
`ADDRESS` in R1C1 and with sheets in quotes, `SUMIF` with the sum range enlarged, `SUBTOTAL` 3
as a count of values, `AGGREGATE` 14–19 with separate k, `DAYS360` with end of February, `CHAR`
1–255, `UNICHAR` without crash. **Locale-aware number reading**: `ISpreadsheetLocale`
(`PulseOffice.Sheets/Formatting`) and `NumericText` serve `VALUE`, `DATEVALUE`, `TIMEVALUE`, `FIXED`,
criteria, filter and text to columns: in Italian `VALUE("1,5")` is 1.5, never the thousands
separators. The engine tests use the invariant locale, so they do not depend on the machine.

**Number formats**, rewritten: a tokenizer separates literals, labels and codes, the type is
decided on the body without the literals (`0.00" EUR"` is no longer scientific), and dates and times are
drawn by us with a token table instead of passing the code to .NET — no more labels
or quoted texts printed, upper-case `YYYY`/`DD`, `m` as minutes after `h` or before `s`,
`AM/PM`, elapsed `[h]`, literal `/` and `:`. Negative section in absolute value, optional decimals
`#`/`?`, scientific digits from the code, fractions that round to the integer and
fixed denominators, logical values in the locale (`IBooleanNames`), one-section text format.

**Analysis and pivots.** Percentage of row computed on the original values, percentage of grand
total distinct from percentage of column, rank only over items, numeric ranges without error
at the edges and sorted by value, pivot that would cover its own data rejected (translated messages).
Regression with constant X without crash, no NaN in cells, one-tailed F test, correlation on
columns of different length, goal seek that restarts. Consolidation with
variances and deviations and without dropping a column; `SubtotalFunction` aligned with the codes of
`SUBTOTAL`. **Scenarios keep formulas** (`Scenario.Formulas`, `IScenarioManager.Restore`);
in ODS they are `table:formula` and **the reference suite keeps them**, in XLSX declared loss (`XLSX029`).
Custom validations relative to the cell, descending sort with a list, text to columns
that does not turn 1.5 into 15 and respects quotes, duplicates that distinguish 1 from "1".

**Form controls.** Option buttons of the same group are mutually exclusive (`IOptionGroups`, one
transaction, FALSE in the linked cells) in Ledger and Deck; clicking on the list box uses the same
row height as the drawing (`ListBoxLayout`); stepped scroll bar, horizontal spin button.

**Text, formulas, printing.** Chinese and Hanja tables that map every candidate and characters outside
the basic plane; case cycling that does not get stuck; autocorrect with word boundaries
and outside addresses, quotes according to context, capital after an opening
quote; hyphenation in the dictionary's language and with libhyphen headers; combining
accents in words. Math formulas: unmatched brackets and leading superscripts, surrogate pairs,
MathML without `semantics`, OMML with several arguments and the default values of `nary` and `acc`. Rows to
repeat in print as an explicit range, no longer "the first rows of the area".

**Presentations and drawing.** Slide show with no visible slides rejected; exit
animations that do not show the element before the entrance; motion path that starts from the
position; the first automatic group animates on entering the slide; jumping to a
slide restarts the animations; presenting from a hidden slide starts from the next one.
Distribution measured up to the last edge, elbow connectors that leave from the side, curve
bounding box on the real extremes, flat paths refitted, automatic names rejected.

**Video, window, settings.** ffmpeg reads the error stream in parallel (it no longer hangs), closes
on cancellation deleting the half-written file; odd sizes reduced to even (`VideoFrameFitter`);
VideoToolbox counts times on the produced samples (`SampleTiming`); mp4 over 2 GB rejected. The
window opens even with a minimum size larger than the screen; unreadable settings and recents
do not bring down start-up, and on Linux the recent paths are case-sensitive.

**Verified**: whole suite green; a scenario with a formula written by us in ODS, rewritten by
the reference suite and read back, comes back with the formula. **Live**: `=VALUE("1,5")*2` gives 3,
`=DAYS360(DATE(2023;2;28);DATE(2023;3;31))` gives 30 and `=ROUNDUP(1.1;1)` gives 1.1. Video was not
tried live (no ffmpeg started).

### Font picker and fonts embedded in the document (done)
Wherever a font was chosen there was a text box (or, in *Format cells*, seven names
written by hand). Now there is a **shared picker** everywhere: Deck's *Font* and *Theme*,
Ledger's *Format cells*, the *Text* tab of the shape style, form control
properties, Fontwork (which before did not ask for the font at all). In field-based forms it is a
`FontField`, so every future dialog gets it without code.

**Three layers, as for macros and spelling.**
- `PulseOffice.Typography` (pure logic, no Avalonia; the name is not `PulseOffice.Fonts` because a
  `PulseOffice.Fonts` namespace hides the OpenXml SDK's `Fonts` type in all `PulseOffice.*`,
  the same trap already seen with `PulseOffice.Math`): OpenType/TrueType reader written by us
  (`OpenTypeReader`, `.ttc` too; `name` tables 0/1/2/4/5/6/9/13/14/16/17, `OS/2` with `fsType`,
  panose, class, Unicode ranges, `head`, `post`), extractor of one face from a collection,
  **Embedded OpenType** codec (the XOR is deciphered, and **MicroType Express** compressed EOTs are decompressed with our decoder, see below),
  model of the licence (`FontLicense`, free / restricted / unknown, classified by SPDX,
  description and URL) and of the embedding permission (`EmbeddingPermission.FromFsType`).
- **Sources as Strategy** (`IFontSource`): system (`SystemFontSource`, folders from
  `ISystemFontDirectories` in `PulseOffice.Platform` plus the names from Avalonia's `FontManager`), document
  (`DocumentFontSource`, embedded and used fonts), **Google Fonts without a key** (public metadata
  `fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts` and complete TTF files from the `google/fonts` repository on GitHub, with
  `METADATA.pb` for file names and licence) and **Fontsource** (`api.fontsource.org/v1`, free and
  keyless; TTFs are per subset, the default subset is downloaded). A **Decorator**
  (`CachedFontSource`) keeps lists and files in `fonts/` in the configuration folder, seven
  days for the list and forever for the files, and works offline; a **Composite** (`CompositeFontCatalog`)
  joins the sources, with the system ahead of online and the "in the document" mark. Addresses and
  activation of the services are changed in `fonts.json` (HTTPS only). Asynchronous download with
  progress and cancellation, injected `HttpClient`, tested against a fake server.
- `PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Fonts`: `FontPicker` (button with the name written in its own font,
  drop-down with search, recents, document fonts and — when searching — online ones) and
  `FontBrowserView`, the full dialog: pill filters by source and category, script, "free
  licences only", live preview with editable text and size, details (styles, scripts, licence
  with its green or amber **badge**, embedding permission, origin, author). Downloaded
  fonts are **registered in Avalonia without installing them**: a custom `FontCollectionBase` plus a
  mapping table passed to `FontManagerOptions.FontFamilyMappings` at start-up, so every
  `new FontFamily("Pacifico")` already scattered in the renderers finds the font. Verified headless
  before adopting it, even after the same family had been looked up unsuccessfully.

**Embedding.** On saving `IDocumentFontEmbedder` collects the used fonts
(`IUsedFontCollector` per module: cell styles, text runs, themes, shapes, Fontwork,
controls) and **always** embeds the downloaded ones and, if the document asks for it
(*File ▸ Embed system fonts in the document*, undoable), the system ones as well.
`fsType` decides: a "restricted" or bitmap-only font is not embedded and the status bar says so.
On reopening the document fonts register themselves.

| Format | How | Verified with the real reference suite |
|---|---|---|
| ODS, ODP (and ready for ODT) | `Fonts/*.ttf` with manifest entry `application/x-font-ttf`, `style:font-face` with `svg:font-face-src`/`svg:font-face-uri` and `loext:font-style`/`font-weight`, `settings.xml` with `EmbedFonts` | yes: the reference suite's PDF uses **Pacifico** (not installed) only thanks to the embedded file; without it, it falls back to Arial Unicode |
| PPTX | `p:embeddedFontLst` with `.fntdata` parts (`application/x-fontdata`) in **uncompressed EOT**, as the reference suite writes them, and `embedTrueTypeFonts`; on reading also PowerPoint's **MTX-compressed** EOTs | yes, in both directions: the PDF uses Pacifico, and PPTX files written by the reference suite and by PowerPoint are read back |
| XLSX | Excel does not embed fonts | declared loss `XLSX036` |

Two silent losses closed along the way: in **ODP and in PPTX the font chosen for a text run
was not saved** (the theme font was always written), and in PPTX a run that differed only
in font was merged into the paragraph. Now runs without a font of their own write
`+mn-lt`/`+mj-lt`, like PowerPoint. ODP finally declares `office:font-face-decls`.

Declared limits: the "embed system fonts" preference in PPTX is `embedTrueTypeFonts`, which
is switched on even when there are only downloaded fonts; with `EmbedFonts` on, the reference suite, when re-saving,
also embeds its own system fonts;
previewing an online font requires downloading it; macOS hidden fonts (name starting with `.`) do not appear.

### MicroType Express: PowerPoint's compressed fonts are read (done)
PowerPoint often embeds fonts as **MicroType Express compressed** EOTs, and until yesterday we
discarded them. The decoder is ours, in pure C# and without packages, in
`PulseOffice.Typography/MicroType`, written from the W3C specifications (MTX and EOT of 2008) and with libeot as a
reference for behaviour, not for code. The pieces, each with one responsibility:
- **bit readers** (`BitReader`, Template Method on the order: most significant first for LZCOMP,
  least significant first for the magnitude coding of `hdmx` and `VDMX`);
- **LZCOMP** (`LzcompDecoder`): three **adaptive Huffman** trees (`AdaptiveHuffmanTree`: symbols,
  lengths, distances), preloaded window, distance copies, `DUP2/4/6`, and the output as a Strategy
  (`PlainByteSink`, `RunLengthByteSink` for the run-length coded block);
- **CTF** (`CtfFont`, `CtfCursor` with the `255USHORT`/`255SHORT` types): one translator per table
  (`CtfTableTranslator`, chosen as the first that answers): `glyf` rebuilt glyph by glyph — simple ones
  with coordinate **triplets** (`TripletTable`, generated and not transcribed), composites, `PUSH`
  data with the **hop codes** and instructions from blocks 2 and 3 (`GlyphProgramDecoder`) — plus the `loca`
  rebuilt (long if the short one is not enough, and `head` updated), `cvt ` as differences, `hdmx` and `VDMX`
  from prediction plus surprise (Template Method `PredictedMetricsTranslator`, which also recognises
  tables left uncompressed, version `0xFFFF - v`); the others are copied;
- **reassembly** (`SfntAssembler`): tables in order, aligned to four bytes, per-table checksum
  and `checkSumAdjustment`; the original signature is kept (`OTTO` for CFF).

**Other people's data, hence caps** (`MtxLimits`): input, output of each block, rebuilt font,
tables, glyphs, points and components per glyph; lengths and distances of copies checked. Any
damaged input becomes an `InvalidDataException` with a readable message, and the PPTX reader discards
the font as before. `hdmx` and `VDMX`, which are optional, are dropped if unreadable without bringing
down the font. `fsType` changes nothing: a "preview and print only" font is used to
display the document.

**Verified**: six real `.fntdata` files from the external test corpus (Boldonse TrueType, Labil Grotesk CFF,
variable Figtree in the four styles) give **tables identical byte for byte** to libeot's,
compiled on purpose as a reference; our `OpenTypeReader` reads their names, CoreText loads them with
the glyph outlines, and Avalonia (headless with Skia, through `RuntimeFonts`) registers them and measures
text with them. The corpus PPTX a corpus file opens with the four Figtree styles. Tests on truncated
data, corrupted bits and noise: no exception other than `InvalidDataException`.

Limits: compressed `hdmx` and `VDMX` are tested only on tables built by hand from the specification (no
real test file contains them); in the absence of real files, nobody guarantees their interoperability.

**A package with a reference to a missing part opens anyway.** The corpus file `BoldonseFontEmbedded.pptx`
refers to a thumbnail that is not there, and the OpenXml SDK rejected the whole file, while
PowerPoint and the reference suite open it. Now `OoxmlPackageRepair` copies the package into memory (with a
cap) and removes from the `.rels` the internal relationships to non-existent parts before opening it; it applies to
PPTX and XLSX. Tested with that file: it opens, and Boldonse loads and is the font of the runs.

### Bug audit, fifth round: formats in depth, Ledger, Deck, shell and charts (done)
Four parallel searches, about eighty-five reports, verified and fixed.

**Formats: the biggest silent losses since the start.** **In ODS number formats were not
saved at all**: dates, percentages and currencies came back as bare numbers, and a date from the reference suite was
read as 45000. Now `number:*-style` with `style:data-style-name` and `office:value-type`, in both
directions (`CellStyles/NumberStyles.cs`); in XLSX Excel's custom formats enter the catalogue.
In both formats the following are now saved as well: text rotation and **unlocked** cells (which came back
locked on protected sheets), hidden sheets and tab colour, right-to-left direction in ODS,
indent and left alignment distinct from "general", **complete page styles** (paper,
orientation, margins, headers with fields, scale) with manual breaks
(`Spreadsheet/PageStyles.cs`, `XlsxPageSetupCodec`), rows **and columns** to repeat, auto
filter and database ranges (in XLSX the ranges are declared, `XLSX031`), **classic array
formulas**, hyperlinks on non-text cells and internal links translated between `#Foglio.A1` and
`Foglio!A1`, editing cycles as `revision`, typed custom properties, label ranges
and sheet events in ODS, revisions with their password in ODS (`TrackedChanges`; in XLSX
`XLSX032`). Underline `none` and the reference suite's numeric weights are read correctly. The pivot in XLSX is not
written: declared loss (`XLSX030`) and the declared capability removed. Tables on slides:
header row and bands in both formats, repeated rows and columns and header groups from
the reference suite, columns counted from `a:tblGrid`, cells with several paragraphs.

**Ledger.** **Protection could be bypassed**: unprotecting a sheet now asks for the password, and
structure protection really stops insertion, deletion, renaming, moving and visibility
of sheets, from macros too. **Delete** goes through the history, respects read-only mode and locked cells and
no longer freezes the UI on a whole column; resizing rows and columns can be undone.
Arrows that skip hidden rows and merged cells, Shift+Tab and Shift+Enter backwards, frozen panes
that do not hide the active cell, editor and frame over the whole merged cell. Validation that cannot be
bypassed with a formula and also applies to fill and controls. **Duplicating a sheet** copies it
entirely with new objects (`ISheetDuplicator`); **renaming it** rewrites formulas, names and page
style (`ISheetRenaming`), and sheet names with spaces now go in quotes in formulas. "Format
cells" on several cells changes only what was touched (`CellStyleDelta`), "Page setup" has four
margins and history, the function wizard keeps empty arguments, name management
no longer redefines a name with another's reference. Compare, merge and revisions go
through the history.

**Deck.** When copying slides or shapes the connectors follow the copies (`ElementIdRemap`); "Replace
all" disabled in read-only mode; find next over all occurrences and in the notes; custom show
name that does not lose focus; presenter view with the right timer and the
footer (`ShowSlideSetup`, shared with the slide show); synonyms only on the selection;
hyphenation that does not double the hyphens (`SlideTextHyphenation`); formatting that does not shift after
autocorrect (`TextOffsetMap`); "enter group" bound to the slide; slide
size on all masters; image export without the hidden slides and with confirmation before
overwriting; Delete in a text field does not delete the object.

**Shell and charts.** **A dialog opened from another one crashed on closing**: now every
entry of the stack keeps its own frame. Menu clicks, native ones too, respect the dialog
block. In charts the axis labels use the drawing scale, horizontal bars have the right
axes, negative values stay within the plot area, a one-slice pie is a circle, missing
values do not break pie, radar, scatter, hierarchies and gauges, an unreadable colour falls back
on the palette, and "Nessun dato" (No data) is translated (`chart.empty`). Bitmaps replaced in the cache are
freed, filters apply to animated GIFs and the canvas is redrawn continuously only for truly
animated GIFs.

**Verified**: whole suite green. With the real reference suite, in both directions: page style, headers,
breaks, print titles, array formula, labels, events, revisions with password,
typed properties and a date from the reference suite come back intact (in XLSX what is declared is lost); an
ODS with a rotated cell, an unlocked one and a hidden sheet with a red tab comes back intact from the round trip through
XLSX. **Live**: 42 in A1, Delete removes it and ⌘Z puts it back.

### Bug audit, sixth round: sheet extensions, animations, exchange and printing, shared dialogs (done)
Four parallel searches, then each one resumed until the area was covered.

**Sheets in the formats.** **Sparklines in ODS were written with invented attributes**: the reference suite lost ours and we lost its. Now `calcext:sparklines` in the reference suite's form (`data-range`, `color-series`, `color-negative`, markers, axes, width in pt), also reading the old form; in XLSX the group stays a group and colours, markers and high/low/first/last points are saved. **Expression names in ODF used `of:expression`** instead of `table:expression` (the reference suite gave `#NAME?`), decimal constants became ranges and local names were written as global. **ODF pivots** lost totals, layout, subtotals, sorting, exclusions, groupings, display modes and the median; the remaining losses are declared (`ODF024`, `ODF025`). **Validations** lost the time type, lists from a range, titles, help and drop-down, and text length and custom formula were in forms unknown to the reference suite; in XLSX the formulas were not converted and `showErrorMessage` was false (`XLSX034` for items containing a comma). Always-visible comments in both formats and VML with per-sheet ids (`XLSX035`: the date). Qualified references (`QualifiedRanges`) quote sheets with spaces and read several areas: this applied to data ranges, pivots, scenarios, conditional rules (A1:A5 plus C1:C5 became A1:C5) and charts, which now also have `chart:categories`.

**Animations and transitions.** The scheduler started an on-click group before the end of the previous one, ignored repetitions and hid an element that exits and re-enters. **Repetition, motion path and the real duration did not cross the formats**: from the reference suite the duration came back as 1 ms, from PPTX the fly-in came back as 500 ms, and a 0.7 s transition became 2 s in the reference suite. Now they are written in the reference suite's form (duration on the filter, delay on the `par`, page transition node) and in PPTX with the exact duration; the animation sound in PPTX is declared (`PPTX022`). **Seventeen presets had wrong identifiers** compared with the reference suite's table: converting changed the effect. Click actions on shapes, images and media were not saved (only on text boxes); the notes in the reference suite's PPTX files were lost. ODP and PPTX readers no longer crash on out-of-range numbers, tested by altering every attribute and element.

**Exchange, printing, text.** CSV: "1,5" in invariant became 15, "3/4" a date, times numbers, and dates were rewritten with day and month swapped; now a single parser (`ICsvNumberParser`) with thousands in groups of three and explicit formats. HTML with correct colspan on hidden rows. Printing: merged cells with the first row hidden disappeared and overflow crossed merges and hidden columns. Dictionaries declared ISO8859 read with their encoding, typographic apostrophe in spelling, repeated thesaurus entries, invalid regex in redaction, conversion tables with spaces and BOM.

**Shared dialogs.** Numeric fields with NaN, zero step or out of range (`NumericBounds`), colours written by name, language listeners never detached in dialogs and in the status bar, `Ctrl++` and multi-key shortcuts, table editor that erased merges and alignments when adding a row, image map zones with duplicate identifiers, empty blocks in menus, internal keys in Italian in the control properties.

**Verified**: whole suite green; with the real reference suite, in both directions, sparklines, pivots, seven validations, names, comments, rules and charts on sheets with spaces, animations with path and repetition, 0.7 s transition, notes and CSV with dates and times. **Live**: `=2*21` gives 42, ⌘+ takes the zoom to 110%, ⌘Q asks to save and "Non salvare" (Don't save) closes cleanly. Still open: the notes written in ODP that the reference suite imports as a plain box, and two identical local names on different sheets (a model limit).

### Bug audit, seventh round: the parts left out of the sixth (done)
Three parallel searches on the points the sixth round had left uncovered or open.

**Sheets.** **Identical local names on different sheets now coexist**: the document keeps names by scope-name pair (`DefinedNameKey`), the engine resolves first the name of the cell's sheet and then the global one, renaming and name management take this into account, and when a sheet is deleted its local names go with it and come back on undo. **Conditional formatting on several areas** is a single rule with all the areas and an anchor (`ConditionalRule.Ranges`, `Anchor`): XLSX read only the first area of `sqref`, ODS made separate rules of them, and relative formulas are now re-anchored to the first area also when inserting and deleting rows. **In the grid, formula rules were never applied**: the view did not pass the calculation context. **In XLSX almost all images from Excel and the reference suite disappeared**, because only those anchored to a cell were read: a common service (`XlsxAnchorLayout`) now handles the three anchor types for images, shapes, vectors and charts, with correct sizes, offsets and rotations; other applications' form controls are also read inside `mc:AlternateContent`. **In ODS the reference suite's rotated shapes ended up elsewhere** (the `translate` was ignored): rotation is written and read as the reference suite writes it, vectors and paths keep rotation and mirroring, objects anchored to the page are no longer lost, and controls also write `form:linked-cell` and `form:source-cell-range`, without which the reference suite did not link them to the cell.

**Presentations.** **Notes written in ODP became a text box in the reference suite**: found by bisection, it creates the notes placeholder only if the frame carries `presentation:style-name`; and the body of the notes master goes in the `<master>-notes` style, which is where it looks for it. **The main theme of an ODP was never read back** (it always came back as "Chiaro" (Light)): now it is found by attribute, master name or background colour. **The reference suite discarded our ODP media**: it wants them with the type `application/vnd.sun.star.media`, and the real type is now derived from the name or the first bytes; in PPTX an audio saved by the reference suite came back as video. The reference suite's placeholder texts in the notes master, visible object names, masters with duplicate identifiers rejected.

**Commands, shell, formulas, scripts.** The math formula parser was a stateful singleton (two parses in parallel got mixed up) and crashed with a stack overflow on deep nesting; shortcuts were compared as raw text, so `Ctrl+Shift+Z` and `Shift+Ctrl+Z` coexisted (`GestureKey`); the workspace did not detach the handlers of closed documents and opened the same file twice; **an autosave in progress during saving left a snapshot that on restart offered a non-existent recovery**. Macro completion, written twice, opened inside strings and comments and after numbers (`CompletionSites`, single), ⌃Space in the middle of a word produced `shsheet`, *Run* could start twice and an exception brought the app down; nested output captures switched each other off.

**Verified**: whole suite green; with the real reference suite, in both directions and chained, a sheet with a rotated shape, rotated vector, image, linked check box, rule on two areas, merged cell and three "Locale" (Local) names comes back exact; a presentation with two masters and themes, graphic style, extrusion, Fontwork, audio, comment, footer, notes and notes master comes back intact from ODP→ODP, with the residual losses all due to the reference suite's exports. **Live**: `=SUM(5;7)` gives 12 and exiting with "Non salvare" (Don't save) is clean. Remaining: our controls in XLSX invisible to Excel (`XLSX020`), rotated raster images read straight (the model does not rotate them).

### Deck: the slide context menu, context-dependent (done)
Reported by the user: in Deck the right click worked only on the thumbnails, never on the slide being edited. Now the canvas has its own menu, projected from the registry as in Ledger, and different according to where it is pressed (`ICanvasContextChooser`, pure and tested logic): on an **object** (selected first if it was not) clipboard, text with the *Font* and *Paragraph* submenus, arrange, format, interaction and the groups of the type — image with filters, table with dimensions, path with point editing; **inside the text being edited** clipboard, format, insert, review; on an **empty area** paste, insert, slide and layout, appearance, grid and guides; in point editing the nodes menu. With pen, glue points, hand and zoom the menu does not open.

**The layout of the context menus is now a map in a single place** (`ContextLayout` in `PulseOffice.UI.Commands`, Deck's map in `PulseContextLayout`), like those of menus and ribbon: a command can be in several menus, and start-up reports the rules that catch nothing. The old paths `slide/object`, `slide/image`… put the object items into the thumbnails menu, which now has only management, order and sections. Opening at the pointer is shared (`IContextMenuFactory.Open`), used by Ledger, thumbnails and canvas.

Two defects seen only live: **opening the menu inside the text closed the editor** — the menu takes the focus and losing the focus committed the text; now while the menu is open the editor stays, and on closing the focus goes back into the text. And the menu **inherited centred alignment and bold from the title**: now it sets them itself. To see it, `uiprobe/windowshot` has the `--popup` option, which captures the open popup of the same process.

**Verified live**: right click on an empty area, on the title and inside the title being edited show the three menus, and an item chosen inside the editor acts while leaving it open.

**Verified live in Deck**: *Font…* shows the drop-down with the names written in their own font and the orange dot on restricted fonts; searching for "Pacifico" it appears among the online ones, once chosen it is downloaded and the title and the thumbnail show it. **A defect found this way**: a font chosen on a still-empty placeholder was lost when typing the text — zero-length runs did not receive the formatting, and committing the text always reset the runs. Now formatting on the whole placeholder also applies to empty runs, and if the runs have a uniform format the new text keeps it (`SlideText.WithPlainText`).

### PPTX: placeholders inherit from layout and master (done)
A slide placeholder with an empty `<p:spPr/>` — the normal form in PowerPoint files —
came out **with zero size**, and the text was not visible: the title of a file just created in PowerPoint
turned out as an empty slide. The reader took only what the shape declared.

Now there is ECMA-376 inheritance (`Presentation/Reading/PlaceholderInheritance.cs`):
- **matching** slide → layout → master with a chain of rules (`IPlaceholderMatchRule`):
  exact type and index, then index, then type, then **family** (`ctrTitle`↔`title`; `subTitle`,
  `obj`, `body` and index without type are body); towards the master type and family count;
- **geometry**: the first `xfrm` along the chain. It also applies to layouts read as the master's
  template, which often have no geometry of their own;
- **text**: the layers (`ITextStyleLayer`, composed by `CompositeTextStyle`) are the `lstStyle` of the
  shape, of the layout, of the master and then `p:txStyles` (`titleStyle`, `bodyStyle`, `otherStyle`); the
  boxes that are not placeholders fall back on the presentation's `defaultTextStyle`. Per level,
  size, bold, italic, colour (also `schemeClr`, which stays a theme role),
  alignment, font (`+mj-lt`/`+mn-lt`), bullets and numbering, line spacing and space before and after
  are inherited; the slide's `pPr` and `rPr` prevail.

Our files already write everything explicitly, so their round trip does not change. The
theme name was fixed too: an empty name no longer passes, and it falls back on the colour scheme's name.

**Verified** on twelve PowerPoint PPTX files taken from the external test corpus (in
`tests/.../Fixtures/PowerPoint`): no placeholder with text comes out with zero size, and positions, sizes and
colours match the reference suite's PNG (a corpus file: dark blue title and red subtitle in the
same position; `placeholder-priority`: "aaa" 14 pt orange and "bbb" 24 pt green matched by
index). **Limits**: `bodyPr` (vertical anchoring, insets, autofit) and level indents are not
inherited because the model does not carry them; the master's `clrMap` is not applied to the roles.

### Deck: text frame, master colour map, document theme (done)
**The text frame is model data** (`TextFrame` on `SlideText.Frame` and on
`PlaceholderTemplate.Frame`): vertical anchoring (top, middle, bottom, justified), internal
margins in points, autofit (none, shrink text, resize shape) with PowerPoint's
shrink factor. Every paragraph has its own indents (`MarginLeft`, `Indent`, in points; null = the
historical indent of 18 pt per level). The defaults are PowerPoint's — margins 7.2 and
3.6 pt, top anchoring — and the standard master anchors titles like PowerPoint
(`TextFrameDefaults`: at the bottom in the title slide and in the section header, in the middle
elsewhere). A new slide copies the frame from the placeholder, and when changing layout takes that
of the new layout.

**Rendering.** `TextElementPainter` now rests on three pieces: `TextFrameGeometry` (the inner area minus the
margins), `TextBlockTypesetter` (composed paragraphs, with the list label drawn **hanging**
when the indent is negative, as in PowerPoint and the reference suite) and `TextFramePlacement` (the vertical
position according to anchoring). With *shrink text* the size is reduced by bisection until the text
fits, as PowerPoint and the reference suite do; the factor saved by PowerPoint is not used for drawing.
The same drawing serves canvas, thumbnails, slide show and exports; the inline editor takes the
same margins as `Padding` and the same anchoring.

**PPTX.** `a:bodyPr` (`anchor`, `lIns/tIns/rIns/bIns`, `noAutofit`/`normAutofit fontScale
lnSpcReduction`/`spAutoFit`) is **inherited** along the resolver chain (`PlaceholderInheritance`:
