shape, layout, master) with `BodyFrameReader`; `marL` and `indent` enter `LevelStyle` and thus
come from `pPr`, `lstStyle`, `txStyles` and `defaultTextStyle`. They are written on shapes, on layout
placeholders and in the `lstStyle` of the seeds. The partial frame layer (`TextFrameLayer`) lives in
`PulseOffice.Formats` because both formats use it.

**ODP.** `draw:textarea-vertical-align`, `fo:padding-*`, `draw:auto-grow-height` with `fo:min-height`,
`draw:fit-to-size="shrink-to-fit"` and `style:shrink-to-fit` in the frame's graphic style and in the
styles of the master's seeds; `fo:margin-left` and `fo:text-indent` in the paragraph. On reading the frame
follows the style chain (`draw:style-name` and `presentation:style-name`, with the parents in
`styles.xml`: so a slide from the reference suite takes its anchoring from `Default-title`), and the
placeholders of someone else's master take it from the frames of the `style:master-page`. For list
items the reference suite puts the indent in the **list style** (`text:space-before` +
`text:min-label-width`, or `style:list-level-label-alignment`): it is read from there when the paragraph does not
declare one. The reference suite does not save the shrink factor: declared loss `ODP019`.

**Verified with the real reference suite**: in `boldonse-mtx.pptx` the `ctrTitle` title inherits `anchor="b"`
from the layout and `normAutofit` from the master, and the reference suite draws it at the bottom of the box as we do;
a deck of ours (title in the middle, body at the bottom with 20 pt margins and a hanging indent of 27 pt)
converted by the reference suite to ODP and to PPTX comes back with anchoring, margins and indents intact, and its PNG
draws it that way in both formats.

**`p:clrMap` and `p:clrMapOvr`.** Our roles are logical (`bg1`, `tx1`, …): the master's map
decides which physical theme colour (`dk1`, `lt1`, …) is behind them. On reading the theme is translated
with the master's map (`ColorMapCodec.Logical`), and `SchemeRoles` resolves references within a
**scope** — master, layout, slide — opened by the reader: `tx1` of a slide with an inverted
`clrMapOvr` becomes the master role that points to the same physical colour. On writing a
dark theme goes out with the inverted map (`bg1=dk1`, `tx1=lt1`) and the consistent physical theme, like
PowerPoint's dark masters; the reference suite draws it dark.

**Theme drop-down.** A document with a theme that is not in the catalogue (PowerPoint's "Office Theme")
left the drop-down empty. `IThemeChoices` lists first the theme **of the document**
("Nel documento" (In the document) section) and then those of the catalogue, with the colour preview next to the name
(`ThemePicker`); when choosing a catalogue theme the original design is remembered
(`Presentation.DocumentDesign`, in memory only) and one can go back to the document theme with its
master. The *Theme…* dialog uses the same list. Texts in the five languages.

### Deck: text frame commands, real "resize shape", first-line indent (done)
**Commands.** *Align text top / middle / bottom* (`deck.paragraph.anchor*`) sit in the
*Home ▸ Paragraph* ribbon with their icons, in *Format ▸ Paragraph ▸ Vertical alignment* and in the
"object" and "text" context menus; the one already active is greyed. *Text format…* (`deck.format.textFrame`)
is a field-based dialog with anchoring, autofit (none, shrink text, resize shape), *word wrap*,
the four internal margins in centimetres and the paragraph indents (before text, first line),
pre-filled from the selection. Everything goes through `ApplyText` → `DeckActions.EditText`, so it can be undone and
is disabled in read-only mode. The formatter has `SetIndents`, `SetAnchor`, `SetFrame`, and
`ReadParagraph` also reads the effective indents.

**Word wrap** is now frame data (`TextFrame.WordWrap`): `wrap="none|square"` in `a:bodyPr`,
`fo:wrap-option` in the ODF graphic style, inherited with `TextFrameLayer`. Without wrapping the paragraph is
composed at its natural width and aligned by hand in the frame.

**Resize shape.** There is a single measurement: `TextFrameMeasure` uses the same `TextBlockTypesetter` as the
renderer (in twips, scale 1) and returns the height of the text plus the margins; `TextFrameFitting`
applies it to elements with `ResizeShape`, and `TextFrameResize` (pure, tested logic) decides on which side
it grows according to anchoring — at the top the upper edge stays fixed, at the bottom the lower one, in the middle
both by half. `DeckActions` passes every "after" state of an element through `Fitted` (typing,
formatting, replacements, transformations, insertions), so the new measurement enters **the same
action** as the change that caused it and is undone with it; the model carries the right height and both
formats write it.

**First-line indent.** A positive indent now moves only the first line: the first line is
laid out separately, at the reduced width, and the rest of the paragraph restarts from the margin. The
break point is found by `FirstLineBreaker` (pure, tested logic: last word that fits, line break,
word too long) by measuring prefixes with the same styled composer (`StyledParagraph`), so
formatted runs, alignments and sizes remain those of the paragraph. `TypesetLine` is now made of
segments, and the spelling squiggles follow the segment in which the word falls. It applies to canvas, thumbnails,
slide show and exports, which all use the same renderer. The hanging indent of lists
does not change.

**Verified with the real reference suite**: a box with a 48 pt first-line indent and a
"resize shape" box anchored at the bottom, written by us in ODP and in PPTX, are drawn by the reference suite as
by us (same indent, same shape grown upwards with the lower edge fixed); from the PPTX
converted to ODP indent and autofit come back; the ODP → PPTX direction is dealt with in the following section.

### Deck: inline editor that draws like the slide, real justification, indent towards PowerPoint via the reference suite (done)
**The inline editor is no longer a visible `TextBox`.** An Avalonia `TextBox` cannot indent only the
first line — tested: `TextParagraphProperties.Indent` exists but `TextLayout` ignores it — so
it showed the text in a layout different from the real one. Now the `TextBox` stays as the **input
engine** (keyboard, IME, clipboard, text ⌘Z, selection, context menu, `_editorMenuOpen`,
commit and cancel unchanged) but it is transparent and does not receive the pointer; the text is shown **drawn
by the slide itself**: `SlideView.LiveText` replaces the element with the one being typed
(`SlidePalette.Live`, which also switches off the prompt text), so colours, fonts, runs, indents,
lists and anchoring are those of the renderer. `InlineTextEditor` (a `Decorator` above the canvas)
draws the blinking caret and selection and translates click, drag, double and triple click into text
positions with the same composition. Composition is now a service (`TextFrameComposer`, with
text shrinking inside) used by the renderer and the editor; `TextCaretGeometry` derives caret,
selection and hit point from it; `PlainTextPositions` (pure, tested logic) converts between the
`TextBox` index and paragraph/position, with `\n` and `\r\n`. **With "resize shape" the frame grows while
typing**, from the anchoring side: every change goes through `DeckActions.FitPreview`, that is through the same
shared measurement as the commit. Limits: up and down arrows and the IME window follow the layout
of the hidden `TextBox` (same margins and size, but not the first-line indent); the IME composition
text appears only when the character is committed.

**Justification.** Avalonia 12 **does not justify** a multi-line `FormattedText` (tested in a
headless program: positions and pixels identical to left alignment; it justifies only a single
truncated line). Justification is therefore done by us: `ParagraphLineBreaker` breaks the paragraph line
by line (first line at its width, the others full) and `LineJustifier` distributes the space among the
words, one run per word; the last line and the one before a line break stay left-aligned. Both
pure and tested logic. So the indented first line reaches the margin like the others.

**The dialogs read the right box.** `DeckTarget.TextTarget` is the box being typed in (with the
text not yet committed) or the text target even if not selected, and `TextRange` the
editor's selection: *Text format…*, anchoring (greyed state included), *Font…*,
*Paragraph…* and *Lists* use them instead of the object selection alone.

**Reference suite ODP → PPTX: why the indent was lost, and the form that keeps it.** Bisection: even
an ODP **rewritten by the reference suite itself** (with `fo:text-indent` in its `P2` style) comes out in PPTX with
an empty `<a:pPr/>`, and the same file with `fo:margin-left="0.001cm"` comes out with `marL="360" indent="609480"`.
It is its exporter: it writes the first-line indent only if the left paragraph margin is
non-zero, otherwise it uses the numbering indents. So we write, when the margin is zero and there is an indent, a margin of one twip
(`ParagraphMargins.Hairline`, 0.05 pt), and on reading — ODF and OOXML — such a small margin comes back as zero.
**Verified with the real reference suite**: our converted ODP comes out with `marL="720" indent="609480"`.
**Height of the resized shape**: with the font embedded in the document (Boldonse, not installed,
registered as in the app) our measurement gives 4.051 cm and the reference suite rewrites 4.052 cm in ODP and in PPTX:
the difference seen before came from the substituted font, not from the measurement.

**Inline editor verified live**: the text looks while typing exactly as after committing; double click on a word selects it and typing replaces it; Esc cancels; the context menu inside the text works. **A defect found this way**: after a click inside the editor, the typed characters arrived wrong (with the test tool, "della" became "aaaaa"). The drawn editor was focusable: the click gave it the focus and only afterwards passed it back to the hidden field, and in that handover macOS text input stayed badly hooked, so the character was derived from the key code instead of from the text. With a non-US keyboard, accents and IME would have gone wrong. Now the editor never takes the focus: the click moves the caret and the focus stays in the field.

### Deck: the inline editor navigates the drawn lines, talks to the IME and corrects while typing (done, to be tried live)
The hidden TextBox knows only its own layout, which is not the drawn one (first-line
indent, justification, lists): the up and down arrows, Home, End, PgUp and PgDn — and ⌘← ⌘→ on macOS —
ended up on the wrong line. Now `InlineTextEditor` intercepts them in the tunnel phase and moves over the **composer's
lines**: `ITextCaretGeometry.Rows` derives the visual lines from the composed box (segments
at the same height in the same paragraph) with the X of every position, and `ICaretRowNavigation`
(`PulseOffice.Presentations/CaretRows.cs`, pure and tested logic) chooses the position keeping the
**preferred column** across successive moves; Shift extends the selection. An index at the boundary of
a wrapped line belongs to the following line, as the caret draws it.

**IME.** `InlineImeClient` is a Proxy of the TextBox's client (hooked on
`TextInputMethodClientRequested`): it forwards surrounding text, selection and actions, but declares the
decorator as surface and the **drawn caret** as `CursorRectangle`, and announces it at every
movement — the candidate window appears under the real caret. The composition text arrives
from `SetPreeditText` and is shown **on the slide** underlined, with the composition caret:
`IPreeditComposer` (`PulseOffice.Text/Input`, pure and tested) splices it in place of the selection in the
live text, without entering the document until it is committed.

**Autocorrect while typing.** `IWordBoundaryCorrection` (in `PulseOffice.Text.Spelling`,
pure and tested) corrects only the word just ended by a space, a punctuation mark or a line break,
with the same `IAutoCorrect`: it compares the correction of the text up to the caret with that of the text
before the word, and keeps only the difference — previous words are not touched. The shared
component `ITypingAutoCorrection` (`PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Text`) applies it to a TextBox
through `SelectedText`, which takes an undo snapshot before replacing: ⌘Z right afterwards
removes only the correction and leaves what was typed. It respects the switch and the options of
`IAutoCorrectSettings`. On commit the whole text is no longer re-corrected (it would have redone a
correction just undone): only the last word is corrected, if it is not closed by a boundary.
Ledger keeps the choice already declared — correction on cell commit, because in the grid
correcting under the user's fingers is intrusive — but the component is ready for Folio.

Limits: PgUp and PgDn go to the first and last line of the box; the replacement and its
snapshot go through the internal history of Avalonia's TextBox, to be verified live.

**Verified live**: "Prova teh " becomes "Prova the " at the space, with the caret after the space; ⌘Z brings back "teh " and leaves the rest; ⌘← takes the caret to the start of the line; committing with Enter does not re-correct the word just restored. IME composition and the position of the candidate window are not tested live (a Japanese or Chinese keyboard would need to be active).

### The ribbon becomes "smart": rich controls, live state, step-by-step reduction (done)
The ribbon was made only of buttons that run a command: bold did not say whether it was
on, font colour did not exist, cell background was three fixed-colour buttons
and borders three items (none, all, bottom). Now a command can declare a
**rich presentation** and the ribbon draws it, without code in the module views.

**The model (pure logic, `PulseOffice.UI.Commands/Ribbon`).** `CommandDefinition` gains
`CheckedWhen` (on state, read from the active context) and `RibbonControl`, a hierarchy of
specifications: `ColorSplitSpec` (split button with the current colour), `FontFamilySpec`,
`NumberBoxSpec` (size and zoom, with preset values), `ChoiceSpec` (drop-down with preview or
**gallery**), `BorderGallerySpec`. The specifications carry functions, not values: the state is read
when drawing, and Folio will use them without new code. **The action always goes through the registry
command**: the control invokes the same command with an argument (`CommandContext.Argument`:
`RibbonColor`, `RibbonBorder`, a string, a number). Without an argument — from the palette, from the menu,
from "More colours…", "More borders…", "More formats…" — the same command opens the **dialog**. So
undo, read-only mode, `EnabledWhen` and the macro recorder apply identically, and the dialogs
remain reachable from every surface.

The appearance of each command in the ribbon is a **layout decision**, not the command's: the
`DisplayRules` table next to `PulseRibbonLayout` (`IRibbonDisplayMap`) says which is a compact
icon (bold, alignments, decimals), which is large (Paste, New slide) and which is a
**gallery tile** (layouts, themes, transitions, chart types).

**Rendering (`PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Ribbon`, shared).** Each element is a `RibbonSlot` created
by a chain of factories (`IRibbonSlotFactory`, Strategy, registered in the container): command
button (large, small, icon, tile), split colour with the palette (`ColorPaletteView`:
automatic/none, ten theme columns with five tints, ten standard, "More colours…"),
font box (the shared `FontPicker`), numeric box with a + list, drop-down/gallery,
border gallery with line style and colour. Compact icons and controls are arranged in
**strips** over two or three balanced rows (`RibbonStripLayout`), like the rows of Office's Font
group.

**Live state (Observer).** If the ribbon's structure does not change, `RibbonView.Update` does not
rebuild anything: it refreshes the existing slots (`RibbonSlot.Refresh`), so boxes and popovers
do not lose focus. The ribbon updates on context change, on every document change
(`ActiveUpdated`) and on cell change in Ledger (`IRibbonStateNotifier`, which the shell listens to):
before, the context, identical from cell to cell, said nothing.

**Space (`RibbonReductionPlanner`, pure and tested).** Groups are reduced **step by step**, from
the right: full → medium (large ones become small) → compact (icons only, narrow boxes,
drop-down galleries) → partial (the first commands plus a "more" button) → collapsed into a button
with a popover. In the popover the controls **change shape**: icons go into wide rows, the border
gallery becomes an open grid with line and colour, galleries show all the tiles. Each
level is built once and stays in cache.

**Ledger.** *Home ▸ Font*: family and size, grow/shrink, bold, italic,
underline, strikethrough, superscript, subscript (on according to the cell), **borders**, **background colour**,
**font colour**. *Alignment*: vertical, wrap, horizontal and indents as icons with
state, merges. *Numbers*: format drop-down (general, number, currency, accounting, short and
long date, time, percentage, fraction, scientific, text) with **the preview of the active cell's
value**, plus currency, percentage, thousands and decimals. *Styles*: **cell style gallery**
with their appearance. *View ▸ Zoom*: percentage box. There are sixteen borders
(`BorderPreset`/`IBorderPresets` in `PulseOffice.Sheets`, pure and tested logic: none, all,
outside, thick outside, inside, inside horizontal and vertical, four sides, top and
bottom, double and thick bottom, two **diagonals**), with one command each in the
*Format ▸ Cells ▸ Borders* menu and "More borders…" that opens *Format cells* on the Borders tab
(`ICellFormatDialog`, `FormatCellsTab`). Red/yellow/green background remain in the menu, not in the ribbon.

**Diagonals are new in the model** (`CellBorders.DiagonalUp/DiagonalDown`) and cross both
formats: `style:diagonal-bl-tr`/`diagonal-tl-br` in ODF, `diagonal` with `diagonalUp`/`Down` in
OOXML, where a single line serves both — declared loss `XLSX037` if they differ. They are
drawn in the grid and in print; the double border in the grid is now two lines.

**Deck.** *Home ▸ Font*: family and size of the selection, toggles on according to the text, text
colour with the **slide's theme colours**. *Paragraph*: alignments on, list,
**line spacing drop-down**, vertical anchoring as an exclusive group (before, the active anchoring
switched off, now it stays on). *Object*: **shape quick styles** (solid, light, outline for
the six theme accents), **fill** and **outline** as split colour (`IShapeStyling.Restyle`,
shared with Ledger), full style. *Design* and *Transitions*: layouts, themes and transitions
as tile galleries. *View ▸ Zoom*: percentage box.

**Declared limits** (later resolved, see the following section): text highlighting in Deck, selection colour in the split button, colour memory across sessions, button state on caret movement.

**Verified live**: in Ledger font and size, icon buttons, split colours and number format sit in the ribbon; applied bold lights up on the button; in Deck, with the title selected, font, size, bold, centred and bottom anchoring show as on. Three defects found this way: **the app did not start** (`INumberFormatParser` was not registered in the container: the tests do not compose it, start-up does); in the border gallery the named items overflowed the popover and the third column was cut — now they are icon tiles on eight columns with the name in the tooltip, as in Office; and in the palette a colour present several times (black) showed as selected in all its swatches — now only in the first.

### Ribbon: highlighting in Deck, selection colour, memory, state at the caret (done)
**Text highlighting in Deck.** `TextRun.Highlight` (ARGB) in the model, `SetHighlight` in the
formatter, `ReadCharacter` reports it. It is drawn as a rectangle behind the runs, with the
geometry of the composed text (`TextElementPainter.PaintHighlights`), so on canvas, thumbnails,
slide show and exports. Command `deck.format.highlight` in *Home ▸ Font* as a split
button with the ten highlighter colours, in the *Format ▸ Text ▸ Colour* menu and in the
context menus. **Native in both formats**: `fo:background-color` in the text properties in ODF,
`a:highlight` in OOXML. **Verified with the real reference suite**, in both directions: its PNG shows the
word in yellow and the ODP↔PPTX conversion keeps the colour, which we read back.

**The split button marks the selection's colour.** The button stays "last colour applied"
(that is what the click does, as in Office), but the palette marks the swatch of the colour the
selection really has (`ColorSplitSpec.Selected`): font and cell background in Ledger,
text, highlight, fill and outline in Deck.

**Last colour and last border are remembered** from one session to the next: `IRibbonMemory`
(`UI.Controls/Services`) in `ribbon.json` in the configuration folder, a separate file like
`window.json` and `recent.json`; an unreadable file restarts from the factory values.

**The state follows the caret.** Caret movements in the inline editor (position and
selection of the `TextBox`) notify the ribbon with a 120 ms delay (`IRibbonStateNotifier`,
the same as Ledger's); the ribbon readers use `DeckTarget.ReadRange()`, which with only the
caret reads the run **before** the caret (`TextRangeWalker.RunAt`).

**Three real defects found while testing live:**
- **typing in a box with mixed formatting flattened it**: while typing and on
  commit the text went through `WithPlainText`, which keeps the runs only if they are all identical.
  Bold on one word disappeared as soon as another word was corrected, and the same from the Outline
  view and from macros. Now `ITextEditSplice` (`PulseOffice.Presentations`, pure and tested)
  compares the old text with the new one: common prefix and suffix keep their runs, the
  new text takes the style of the character before, a new line break copies the paragraph, a field
  stays a field until it is touched;
- **a click on the ribbon closed the editor** and the formatting ended up on the whole box; now the
  ribbon and the popups are "companions" of the editor (`ITextEditingCompanion`, `ITextEditingFocus`) and do not
  commit it, and after formatting the editor reopens with the same selection;
- **with only the caret the formatting took the whole box**: now, as in PowerPoint,
  it takes the word under the caret (`ICaretWord`) and paragraph commands the current paragraph.
  And in Deck **⌘B, ⌘I and ⌘U did not exist**: now they do.

**Verified live**: "tre" (three) selected and highlighted on its own, the text typed afterwards keeps
the highlight and the italic of "Uno" (One); italic lights up with the caret inside "Uno" and
switches off at the end of the line; ⌘I with the caret in "Uno" makes it italic; the green chosen is remembered on
restart; from the arrow, with the editor open, red goes only on "due" (two) and typing continues.
Limit: with the caret outside a word a character command changes nothing (PowerPoint
prepares the style for the text that will be typed next).

**Cell styles in the ribbon: a drop-down, not a row of tiles.** The row of four tiles
took too much space. Now a gallery can declare itself without inline tiles (`InlineTiles = 0`):
in the ribbon it is a drop-down as wide as a field that shows the **current style in its appearance**
("Buono" (Good) in green on light green), and opens the same tile popover as before. **Verified
live** in Ledger: "Buono" chosen from the popover, the drop-down shows it.

**Groups with too many icons: buttons with menus.** Reduced to icons, Ledger's *Cells* group was
a grid of seventeen mute symbols. Now a **subgroup in the ribbon map**
(`home/cells/insert`) becomes a button with name, icon and arrow that opens a menu of its
commands with icon and title (`RibbonItem.Menu`, `MenuSlot`; the title is the translated structure
key, `ribbon.home.cells.insert`), as in Office. *Cells* is now **Insert ▾ · Delete ▾ ·
Format ▾**, and Deck's *Arrange* **Order ▾ · Align ▾ · Rotate ▾**. Deck's shape quick styles
also moved to the compact drop-down, because their tiles had truncated
labels. **Verified live**: the *Insert* menu lists the five commands and *Insert rows
above* runs.

### Delete removes the selected objects, in Ledger and in Deck (done)
**Ledger**: with objects selected, Delete (and ⌫) emptied the **cells** under the selection instead of
deleting the objects. Now the grid, if there are selected objects, asks to delete them
(`ObjectsDeleteRequested`) and the view removes them all in a single undo, respecting read-only
mode; the *Delete object* command too now removes all the selected ones and is disabled in read-only mode.
**Deck**: the key handler was there, but the key did not arrive: a click on the canvas did not give it
keyboard focus (it was not focusable). Now the canvas is focusable, without a focus frame, and
takes it at every click outside the text editor. **Verified live** in both: rectangle in
Ledger deleted with ⌫ and brought back with ⌘Z, Deck title deleted with ⌫.
When a dialog closed (palette included), the focus went back to the previous element even when it
no longer existed — for example the start page tab — and the keyboard was left without a recipient:
the first ⌫ after an insertion from the palette did nothing. Now `DialogHost` restores the previous
focus only if it is still in the window, otherwise gives it to the active document
(`IDocumentFocusTarget`, implemented by `LedgerView` and `DeckView`). **Verified live**:
rectangle inserted from the palette and deleted immediately with ⌫.

### Deck: the text box can be typed in (done)
*Insert ▸ Text box* created a **rectangle with no fill or outline with a space
inside**: a shape, not a text, so double click did not open the editor and there was no way to
type in it. Now it creates a free `TextElement` (`PlaceholderRole.Free`, size 18, *resize shape*),
selects it and opens the editor immediately (`DeckTarget.EditText`), as in PowerPoint and the reference suite. In the formats it is
the native text box (`draw:text-box`, `txBox`). **Verified live**: inserted from the palette,
"Ciao mondo" (Hello world) typed at once, committed, reopened with double click and completed.
The selection frame **did not follow the growth**: while typing with *resize shape* the text
went out of the dashed box, which stayed at the previous size until the box was
reselected. `SlideView` now draws the selection on the live text when it is the same element, and on
commit the selection passes to the updated element. **Verified live** with three lines.

### Deck: twenty-one themes with their graphics, in both formats (done)
There were three themes — Chiaro, Ardesia, Sabbia (Light, Slate, Sand) — made only of colours: a white slide with a
title. What makes the themes of PowerPoint and the reference suite beautiful is not the palette but the **master
graphics**: bands, stripes, corners, arcs, gradients. Now the catalogue has **twenty-one original themes**
(no name, colour or design taken from Microsoft), light and dark, each with twelve colours, a
pair of fonts available everywhere (Inter bundled with the app, Georgia, Arial, Verdana, Trebuchet
MS, Courier New) and a decoration: Light, Slate, Sand, Meridian, Aurora, Horizon, Prism, Atelier,
Nordic, Ember, Lagoon, Citrus, Midnight, Terracotta, Orchid, Graphite, Botanical, Coral, Blueprint,
Mosaic, Quartz.

**Theme names end up in the files, so they are English.** "Chiaro", "Ardesia" and "Sabbia" have
become Light, Slate and Sand; the old names remain **aliases** in `ThemeCatalog.Find`, so
documents saved before reopen with their theme. In the UI the name is translated
(`deck.theme.<name>` in the five languages, `IThemeNames`).

**The decoration is data, not a separate drawing.** `SlideMaster.Objects` carries the master's
background objects, `SlideLayoutTemplate.Objects` those of the layout and `HideMasterObjects` says whether the
layout hides the master's (the title slide and the section header thus have an
appearance of their own). The theme declares its own family (`Theme.Decoration`) and the families are
**strategies** (`ThemeDecoration`, Template Method on master, title and section): side band,
top bar, bottom stripes, corners, arcs, gradient, frame, mosaic, circles, oblique cuts.
They draw with a builder (`DecorationCanvas`) preset shapes that take their colours from the theme,
so **changing theme regenerates the graphics** going through `MasterFactory.CreateStandard`, as already
happened for the placeholders. The shapes stay outside the placeholder areas: a test checks that
no solid shape covers the title of content slides, and that the text of the twenty-one themes
has WCAG contrast ≥ 4.5 on both backgrounds.

`SlideRenderer` draws the graphics after the background and before the elements, only if the slide
shows the master objects: this applies to canvas, thumbnails, slide show, print and exports.
`SlideResize` scales them with the slide size.

**Formats, native.** In PPTX the master graphics are non-placeholder shapes in the `spTree` of the
`slideMaster`, the layout's in the `slideLayout`, with `showMasterSp="0"` when the layout
hides the master; the reader reads them back (before, non-placeholder shapes of other applications' masters and layouts
were ignored) and a theme read from file that matches one in the catalogue comes back as that theme. In ODP the
master graphics are `draw:custom-shape` in the `style:master-page`, on the
`backgroundobjects` layer. **ODP has no per-layout shapes**: the honest solution is a **master page for
each decorated layout** (`Default-TitleSlide`, with attributes `qm:master`, `qm:layout`,
`qm:hide-master-objects`), to which the slides of that layout refer; on reading these pages
come back as layout graphics and not as extra masters. What is not a preset shape is not written:
declared loss `ODP020` and `PPTX023`.

**The trap found with the real reference suite**: when rewriting our ODP, it **removes our
attributes** from the master pages and **renames** them with the visible name
(`Meridian_20_TitleSlide`). The layout pages came back as extra masters. Now they are also recognised
by the visible name ("Meridian TitleSlide" next to the "Meridian" page), and if the attribute is missing the
"hide master" is inferred from whether the page repeats the master's graphics or not. A test
removes the attributes from the file and checks that the round trip stays exact.

**Verified with the real reference suite**: the twenty-one themes written by us in ODP and in PPTX, converted to
PDF, show the master, title and section graphics as ours do; an ODP rewritten by the reference suite
comes back with a single master and the layout graphics; ODP→PPTX and PPTX→ODP through the reference suite keep the
graphics visibly (when importing a PPTX the reference suite creates, as always, one master per layout).

**UI**: the *Design* tab has the **Themes** gallery (`deck.design.themes`): four
inline previews and all of them in the pop-up menu, each a **title slide drawn by the
same renderer** (`ThemePreviews`, painted in the ribbon by `IRibbonThumbnailPainter`, a new, shared
extension point). Without an argument the gallery opens *Theme…*
(`deck.design.themeDialog`, now in `DeckThemeCommands` together with the gallery). The theme drop-down
in Deck's bar shows preview, translated name and the six accents. The three commands
`deck.theme.light/slate/sand` were removed: they were one command per theme, and with twenty-one themes the
gallery is the right form. *New master* lists the themes with the translated name.

Limits: the graphics are built for the 16:9 format and scaled in the others; a full-page
gradient also covers a slide's own background, as in PowerPoint (it is switched off with *Master
objects*); the Trebuchet MS, Verdana and Georgia fonts may be missing on Linux and fall back on the
system font.
**Two defects found while testing live, after the work on themes.** In the app **no theme showed
its graphics**: `ThemeDecorations` had two constructors, and the container chose the one that receives
the list of graphics, passing it **empty**, because they were not registered — the same trap already
seen with `TextCases`. Now the ten graphics are registered one by one and an incomplete list makes
start-up fail immediately. And in the *Design* tab the twenty layouts as tiles squashed the
theme gallery into an icon: the layouts are now a **Layout ▾** button with the menu (subgroup
`design/layout/choose`), as in PowerPoint, and the gallery shows seven themes inline. Tiles with
a preview show only the 16:9 preview, with the name in the tooltip: with the name underneath, the
thumbnail came out truncated. **Verified live**: Aurora chosen from the gallery draws the gradient,
the arc and the accent lines on the slide and in the thumbnail.

### Deck: full-height theme gallery, no bar above the slide, a real "Theme…" dialog (done)
**The ribbon's theme gallery** was strips of 76×43 points. Now it is a **reusable ribbon
form**, `RibbonChoiceLook.Band` (`ChoiceSpec.Band`: visible rows, columns, aspect ratio, size of the
tiles in the popover), like PowerPoint's theme gallery: a box as tall **as the ribbon
body**, tiles with the slide's aspect ratio, and on the right three buttons — row up, row down and
"more", which opens the full grid. The size is not hard-coded: the gallery enters the "large" lane
of the `RibbonItemFactory`, which already has the row height (`rows × ControlHeight`), and `RibbonBandPanel`
derives the tiles from it with `RibbonBandLayout` (pure and tested logic: size, scrolling within the rows,
row that shows the current choice). The wheel scrolls the rows, the current theme has the accent
border, so does the hovered one, and the translated name is in the tooltip. In the popover
(`ChoiceGrid`, also shared with the drop-down) the tiles are large, with the name underneath, divided by
section (`RibbonChoice.Section`: "Nel documento" (In the document), "Temi" (Themes)) and with "More…" towards the dialog. With little
space the group goes through the planner's steps: in the compact form the gallery becomes a
drop-down (`ChoiceSlot`), in the collapsed group the grid. New icons `ui.chevronUp` and `ui.galleryMore`.

**Removed the bar above the slide** (Theme, Layout, Play): controls do not belong in the editing
space. Everything remains reachable from the ribbon and the menus — theme gallery and dialog, the
*Layout* menu and the `deck.layout.*` commands, *Play animation* (`deck.anim.play`). `ThemePicker` was no longer
needed by anyone and was removed, along with the parameters `DeckView` received only for it.

**The "Theme…" dialog** is no longer a field-based form: `ThemeDialogView` shows on the left the grid of
themes with real previews (same renderer as the slides) and the sections, on the right the name,
the preview of a title slide and of a content slide (`ThemeSample`, new in `IThemePreviews`),
the ten colours with their names and the two fonts with the shared `FontPicker` and a sample in the
chosen font. The previews follow the font choice live; when choosing a theme the fonts
go back to its own. Footer with *Cancel* on the left and *Apply theme* in accent; it is applied with the same
undoable action as before (main master). Texts in the five languages.

Fixed along the way a test that had fallen behind: `UnTemaSenzaDecorazioneNonAggiungeNulla` built the
decorations with none registered (now the class rejects that) and used Prism, which now has a decoration.
**Testing live**, three defects of the band gallery, invisible to the tests: the tiles came out
**zero wide** (the panel was measured with infinite height, so the aspect ratio gave zero
width — now the height is that of the three ribbon rows); the previews received a non-numeric
size and stayed dots; and the tiles out of view, laid out in an empty rectangle but with a size
of their own, were drawn over the first one — now they are hidden. The popover showed two columns instead of
four: the stock `FlyoutPresenter` has a maximum width, which for `plain` popovers is now
wider. The gallery shows six themes per row. **Verified live**: bar above the slide gone,
full-height gallery with arrows that scroll the rows, four-column popover, *Theme…* dialog
that updates the preview when choosing Brace and applies it.

### Theme on a single slide, and two distinct "Theme…" items (done)
The *Theme…* dialog applied the theme only to the main master. Now it has **"Apply to"**: *all
slides* (as before) or *current slide only*. In the second case the multiple-masters mechanism
is used: if a master with that theme already exists it is reused, otherwise one is created
(`MasterFactory.CreateStandard`, with the translated theme name), and the slide is bound to it — all
in **one transaction**, so a single ⌘Z. It is saved like any multiple master, in both formats.
The choice sits at the top of the dialog's right column, under the theme name.

In the palette there were **two "Theme…" items**: the presentation's and the interface's
(light/dark). The second is now **"Interface appearance…"** in the five languages, and the
dialog's footer note no longer talks about the "main master".

**Verified live**: two slides, *Current slide only* with Brace on the second — the
second becomes dark with the graphics, the first stays light; ⌘Z undoes everything in one go.

### Bug audit, eighth round: ribbon, Deck editor, presentation formats, fonts and Ledger (done)
Four parallel searches on the parts born after the seventh round, each resumed until the area was covered.

**Ribbon and shared controls.** Esc in the numeric boxes (size, zoom) did not cancel, an out-of-range
value stayed written as it was and "NaN" was accepted; the theme gallery redrew the twenty-one
previews at every caret movement; zoom from the palette without an argument did nothing in Deck and
reset to 100% in Ledger — now it opens a shared dialog (`IZoomPrompt`); a command repeated in a
group brought down the ribbon; "None" did not show as selected in the palette; *Apply style* crashed
on a `long` index and showed the internal names; the *Theme…* dialog crashed with an empty list.

**Column and row styles.** Formatting a whole column or row ran through a million cells. Now
the default column and row style is sheet data (`SheetLayout`), with the precedence of ODF and
the reference suite — cell, then row, then column — and cells written afterwards inherit it; formatting touches only
the used area (`ISelectionWorkArea`, pure logic). It travels in both formats: `default-cell-style-name` on
ODS columns (on rows the reference suite misinterprets it, so rows are written the way it writes them),
`<col style>` and `<row s customFormat>` in XLSX. **Verified with the real reference suite** in both directions and **live**:
column B in bold on an empty sheet, the text typed afterwards is bold and column C is not.

**Explicit plain cells and insertion with the neighbour's format.** A cell reset to the default
style inside a formatted column or row could not be told apart from "inherits", and took back the
column's style. Now the cell has a style **of its own** even when it is the default one (`Cell.ExplicitStyle`,
`Worksheet.OwnStyleAt`/`SetOwnStyle`, where `null` means "inherits"); the flag drops by itself where the row and the
column have no style, so it does not bloat the sheet. Formatting, *Clear formatting* (it now goes through the
formatting service and the used area, and on whole columns removes the column style) and undos
restore the previous state, inherited included; copy and paste carry the effective style. In the formats: in ODS
`table:style-name="Default"` on the cell, which wins over the column's `default-cell-style-name`; in XLSX every
`<c>` is explicit by definition (without `s` style 0 applies, not the column's). **Inserting rows or
columns copies the format of the row above or of the column to the left**, as the reference suite does:
row or column style and the cells' own styles (`NeighbourFormatPart`), with
the snapshot undo, which now restores the layout before the cells. **Verified with the real reference
suite** in both directions: plain B4 inside bold column B and plain E7 in bold row 7
stay plain after ODS→XLSX and XLSX→ODS, and the reference suite's HTML draws them without bold.

**Deck editor.** The text of boxes joined paragraphs with the system newline: on Windows the
formatting shifted by one character per paragraph and every commit marked the document. An isolated "\r"
stayed in the text; words with decomposed accents, characters outside the basic plane and "dell'anno" were
split by the caret and by double click (a single word logic, `ICaretWord.Enclosing`); the
caret could fall in the middle of an emoji and split it; a word longer than the line went back past a line
break; slide search did not look at the notes.

**Presentation formats.** **A single malformed attribute made a whole PPTX be rejected** (and an XLSX):
now `OoxmlAttributeSanitizer` removes invalid typed attributes on opening and converts OOXML Strict
percentages, and references to missing parts are skipped. The theme of a master rewritten by
the reference suite was lost: now `loext:theme` is read and written too. "No wrap" with "resize shape"
is written the way the reference suite exports it to PPTX (it grows in width and in height). Verified with the real reference suite
in both directions.

**Fonts and Ledger.** Fonts with duplicate tables or huge sizes brought down opening; an error
page from the online services ended up in cache as a font; concurrent downloads and families with similar
names trod on each other; a face that failed to register was not retried; the online list had no cap. Sample
tests on the real `.fntdata` files: the MicroType decompressor holds. In Ledger objects could be deleted
and moved on a protected sheet.

### "No wrap" towards PowerPoint via the reference suite (done, with a limit of the reference suite)
The reference suite exports the wrap option (`TextWordWrap` → `wrap="none"`) **only for custom
shapes**; for text frames it writes it only if the frame grows in width and in height
(bug tdf#134400). **Free text boxes** without wrap, with "shrink
text" or without autofit, are now written in ODP as a rectangular `draw:custom-shape` with the text inside and
a type of ours (`pulseoffice-text-box`, `OdfFreeTextShape`) which the reference suite draws, keeps and exports as
`prstGeom rect` with `wrap="none"`; our reader recognises them by the type and reads them back as text boxes
(runs, frame, identifier and animations, order). **Verified with the real reference suite**: ODP → PPTX with
`wrap="none"`, drawn on one line, ODP → ODP round trip intact. A limit of the reference suite, not of our file: the
**placeholders** without wrap remain frames with `presentation:class`, and the reference suite does not export their wrap.
**Verified live in Ledger**: column B in bold, B4 reset to normal stays normal and B5 written
afterwards is bold; with a column inserted before C, the value typed in the new C is bold.

### Bug audit, ninth round: shell, Ledger beyond the engine, Deck beyond text, drawing and macros (done)
Four parallel searches, each resumed until the area was covered.

**Shell.** With the "unsaved changes" question open, a second ⌘Q or ✕ opened another one
(`QuitGate`); a recovered document lost its original path — now ⌘S writes to the original file,
as in the reference suite; *Release* of sharing never worked and the redaction confirmation
always answered "no" (the choice dialog returns the value, not the choice); properties could be
edited in read-only mode; Deck's print, mail, template and version ignored uncommitted text;
the content of a nested dialog closed the one on top; the window's normal size was lost
if closed maximised; abandoned temporary files; recents gone from disk still opened.

**Ledger.** Merge and centre, Find by format, CSV and HTML ignored column and row styles;
pasting a block with empty cells the destination kept the old values (now it empties them, as the reference suite does);
comments did not follow sorting; charts showed hidden rows and columns; a new pivot
silently overwrote a sheet with data (`PVT005`); *Remove conditional formatting* looked
only at the first area and the undo changed the priority; the page style took the sheet's name,
so a sheet named "Default" changed all of them (`PageStyleCatalog.OwnNameFor`, verified with the reference suite). The
**advanced filter** now has "Copy results to…" with shifted formulas and protection, and criteria on another
sheet. "Serie N" is translated in the UI and canonical ("Series N") in the files.

**Deck.** Masters were always born 16:9 even in 4:3 or custom presentations, and so were the theme
previews; the main master took the fixed id "master1"; hidden slides ended up in the PDF and in
print; moving the first slide of a section took the section away with it.

**Drawing and macros.** **The rotation of Deck objects was not saved in any format**, and the grouped
shapes of files from the reference suite and PowerPoint **disappeared on opening**: now rotation travels in ODP
(`draw:transform`) and PPTX, and other applications' groups are dissolved into objects in their place; rotation of group
children is saved in ODS and XLSX; grouping and ungrouping in Deck lost rotation and order; linked
controls did not follow moved rows, columns and cells; object distribution now follows
the reference suite's rule; the macro recorder recorded its own toggle and forbidden commands;
macro error messages are translated; SVG with non-finite sizes and the colour adjustment.
**Verified with the real reference suite** (rotations in both directions, page styles) and **live** (pasting a
block with empty cells empties the destination).

### Bug audit, tenth round: engine and grid, spreadsheet formats, PDF and data, texts and languages (done)
Four parallel searches, each resumed until the area was covered.

**Engine and grid.** A number turned into text (`="x"&0,5`, `CONCAT`) used the dot and seventeen
digits: now fifteen significant digits and the locale's separator through the calculation context,
with integers up to sixteen digits as in the reference suite. `VERO()`/`FALSO()` (`TRUE()`/`FALSE()`), the `|` row separator in
arrays, `ATAN2(0;0)` and `TROVA`/`RICERCA` (`FIND`/`SEARCH`) with empty text behave as in the reference suite. Conditional
formatting evaluates with the container's engine (hence `LET` and `LAMBDA` too); the name box
resolves names and ranges with a single resolver. F4 in the editor also cycles on ranges and skips
function names; Enter and Tab move within the selection; Shift+arrows extend keeping the active
cell fixed; fill skips hidden rows and repeats merges (`FillMergePlan`).

**Spreadsheet formats.** ODS structure with header rows, scenario order, error constants,
hyperlinks on numeric cells, `loext:table-protection`, default widths and heights; in XLSX
column widths (`XlsxColumnMetrics`) and internal links in quotes; single-column charts,
object replacements not read as images, anchors in hidden rows; dates and percentages in CSV.
New declared losses: `ODF026`, `ODF027`, `XLSX038` (portability of sheet names).

**PDF, data and security.** Shapes with gradient only, combining accents, Info strings in UTF-16;
print scale, fit to pages and centring (`ScaledPageCanvas`), repeated titles taller than one
page, notes that wrap, merged cell straddling pages drawn once and clipped as in
the reference suite (`ClippedPageCanvas`); double PDF signature. SQL table names in quotes, invalid WebDAV
address, and **passwords written inside a connection string go to the keychain**
(`ConnectionSecretSplitter`).

**Texts and languages.** Title bar tooltips and many strings written in the code moved to keys or
to canonical English; settings keywords in the five languages; form event globals
in English (`sheet`, `control`, `event`); spelling replacements that do not shift;
undoable document language; ordinals, phone numbers in redaction, kana iteration marks.

**Verified**: whole suite green. **Live**: with B2 active, Shift+down and Shift+right
select B2:C3 with the active cell fixed on B2; `=CONCAT(1/2;1/3)` gives "0,50,333333333333333".

Still open: Ledger commands that just show a message (external links, streams, XML
source, data provider, theme, pivot calculated field), the QR correction level ignored,
*Fill sheets* that copies only values, "Campo1" (Field1) written in the code, format diagnostic messages
still in Italian in the code.

### Ledger: external data, streams, XML source, providers, sheet themes, pivot calculated fields (done)
Six commands that answered with a message now do their job. **External data**: the model is
`Workbook.ExternalData` (`AreaLink`, `DataStreamSource`, `DataMapping`), it enters the workbook restore
point (database ranges too) and can be undone. Reading is `IExternalDataFetcher` (file or http/https, cap of
16 MB), interpreting is a family of strategies in `PulseOffice.Formats.Interchange` (`ITabularSources`: CSV with
the separator guessed, HTML tables `HTML_n`/`HTML_all` named as the reference suite names them, repeated XML records with children and
attributes as columns), writing is `IExternalDataWriter` (clears the previous area, respects the million cells,
leading zeros stay text). *Link to external data*, *Data stream* (most recent rows at the bottom or at
the top), *XML source* (import) and *Data provider* (fills and links a database range);
*Refresh external data* re-reads everything in a single undo. **Native ODS as the reference suite writes it**:
`table:cell-range-source` in the anchor cell, `calcext:data-stream-source`, `calcext:data-mappings`;
**verified with the real reference suite**, which keeps links and providers (it writes the stream only in
experimental mode). XLSX: declared losses `XLSX042`–`XLSX044`. A relative href (the reference suite rewrites them that way) is
resolved from the document's folder; XML with namespaces is read by local name; paths have "Browse…"
(`PathField` of the shared field-based form). **Sheet themes** (`ISheetThemes`, `ISheetThemeApplier`): six themes
redefine the named cell styles and restyle the cells that carry them (`Cell.StyleName`), a single
undo. **Pivot calculated field**: `PivotField.Formula`, evaluated with the engine's parser on the
**totals** of the cited fields (as Excel does), names with spaces in quotes; in ODS it does not exist, declared `ODF028`.

### Diagnostic messages speak the user's language; QR with the four levels; "Fill sheets" like the reference suite (done)
**Diagnostics.** The messages of formats, platform, cloud, fonts and data were
written in Italian in the code. Now `Diagnostic` carries a code, an **English** message (for the
log) and its arguments (`With`); the translation key is derived from the code
(`diagnostic.<code>`) and `IDiagnosticTexts` resolves it, with the English message as fallback. The
views and commands that showed `.Message` use the translator. A test checks that **every code
used in the source has the key in the five languages**; codes that carried two different messages
were split. The old remote storage translator is absorbed.

**Sheet names.** In files and readers the default name is canonical (`Sheet1`); the UI
names the first sheet and new ones with the `sheet.defaultName` key, so in Italian it stays "Foglio1".

**QR code.** The encoder (`Assets/Qr/`) covers versions 1–40 and levels L, M, Q and H, with the
standard's Reed–Solomon block tables, choice of the smallest version and of the best
mask. The old one used for 4-M a single block of 78 codewords instead of two of 32: an error that
no lenient reader had revealed. The dialog (`IQrCodePrompt`) is shared by Ledger and Deck.
**Verified live**: the QR inserted in Ledger decodes with the macOS detector.

**Fill sheets** (`ISheetFillAcross`) now copies text, numbers, formulas (with the text unchanged, as
the reference suite does) and formats according to the reference suite's options, with "skip empty cells", in a single undo. The
default name of the pivot calculated field is translated.

### Bug audit, eleventh round: external data, themes, calculated fields, Fill sheets, QR (done)
**External data.** Links, streams and database ranges **follow the sheets** (insertion, moving,
deletion with restore on undo, `ExternalDataCatalog.Reindex`/`Attach`) and **rows and columns**
(`ExternalDataPart` in the structure, undoable). No more writing on protected sheets; a range name
already used by another range is not overwritten. Relative paths in ODF go through `OdfLinkSyntax`
(the reference suite writes them relative to the package, with one extra `../`: before, they were resolved in the wrong
folder). An HTML that makes regular expressions time out no longer brings down the app
(`InvalidDataException`), the table list of a huge flat XML is no longer quadratic, and an XPath that
yields no elements does not bring down reading.
**Automatic refresh**: `AreaLink.RefreshSeconds`, `table:refresh-delay` in ODS (verified with
the reference suite: "PT2M5S" comes back as 125 s even after one of its saves), declared loss in XLSX (`XLSX045`).
`ExternalLinkAutoRefresh` (UI timer, only documents not in read-only mode and unprotected sheets)
refreshes expired links; for safety it starts only after the user has created or refreshed the
links by hand in the session (`IExternalLinkSchedule.Trust`), as the reference suite asks before refreshing.
**Preview**: `TabularPreviewView` (shared in `PulseOffice.Data.UI`, with `DataPreviewControl` extracted
from the database import) shows the table list and a preview with column letters and count.
**Other.** Fill sheets skips protected sheets and no longer runs through a million cells on a whole column;
the sheet theme does not touch protected sheets and puts white text on accent styles; the pivot calculated
field distinguishes division by zero (`#DIV/0!`) from overflow (`#NUM!`); the forms' "Browse" does not
bring down the app if the picker fails; a translated diagnostic with wrong placeholders falls back on the
canonical message. QR verified by decoding it with CoreImage (versions 2–33, levels L/M/Q/H, UTF-8).

### Bug audit, eleventh round: engine functions compared with the real reference suite (done)
Six hundred formulas evaluated by us and by the reference suite (a macro run inside the reference suite
--headless`, which writes the results of `XCell`), and the differences verified one by one.
**Precedence**: `-2^2` gave −4 and `2^3^2` gave 512, while the reference suite and Excel give 4 and 64; now unary
minus binds tighter than power and power is left-associative. The printer rendered `-(A1+B1)`
as `-A1+B1` and `(A1+B1)%` as `A1+B1%`: now a binary operand of a unary operator goes in parentheses.
**SUMIFS, AVERAGEIFS, MAXIFS and MINIFS summed the criteria range** instead of the given one;
now they use their own and a range of different size gives `#VALUE!`. **TEXT used .NET
formatting**: `"yyyy-mm-dd"`, `"h:mm"`, `"@"` came out literally; now it goes through the format code
formatter (`IFormatCodeRenderer`). Finance: IPMT, PPMT, CUMIPMT and CUMPRINC had wrong sign or
interest; PRICE, YIELD, DURATION and MDURATION were an approximation without the coupon calendar,
now they follow the reference suite's (COUPDAYS per basis, end of month, fractional period). Statistics:
cumulative HYPGEOM.DIST, BETA.DIST (it took "cumulative" for the lower bound), PERCENTRANK with
interpolation and significant digits, CHITEST with the table's degrees of freedom, STEYX with fewer than
three points, gamma, chi-square and F densities at zero. Other: BESSELY and BESSELK (now the reference suite's
algorithm), two-argument ERF, POWER and `^` with odd roots of negatives, arithmetic overflow as
`#NUM!`, negative TIME, MINUTE and SECOND as in the reference suite, YEARFRAC with inverted dates and basis 1, TEXTJOIN
that skips empty texts, XLOOKUP "next smaller" that chose the first instead of the nearest, SORTBY
by columns and with several keys, stable sorts, TEXTBEFORE/TEXTAFTER with case and "end as
delimiter", COUNT of direct arguments, COUNTBLANK with `""`, TYPE of an array, VALUE of a
time, ROMAN with the simplified forms, complex numbers with fifteen digits and the `j` suffix.
Declared and left as they are: the differences due only to the reference suite's locale and to its deviations from Excel
(CEILING with negative step, MROUND, LEN of emoji, case-sensitive COUNTIF).

### Bug audit, eleventh round: Deck and shell (done)
**Deck.** When deleting a slide the *Slide show setup* range now shifts
(`ShowSetup.WithoutSlide`); when deleting an object its animations and click actions go with
it and come back with ⌘Z (`ElementBehaviours`); changing layout no longer erases free boxes and text
of placeholders without a counterpart; automatic advance does not get stuck on a running animation;
a `#name` link goes to the slide and in the slide show only http, https and mailto are opened;
the name proposed for export removes invalid characters.

**Shell and platform.** Recovery accepts only hexadecimal identifiers (a tampered manifest
could make files outside the folder be deleted) and no longer brings down start-up; autosave
interval bounded; non-finite window sizes are not saved; recents cleaned
on reading; errors in enabling conditions inside the executor; Esc closes the drop-down and not the
dialog; cancelling a macro is not shown as a timeout and Python keeps its output. External
processes (printing, scanner, Bluetooth) go through a single component (`ExternalProcess`) that
reads output and errors together and on cancellation kills the process tree; the WIA script escapes
values (an apostrophe in the path allowed command injection). Macro completion with
backslashes and Python triple-quoted strings.

**Verified live**: `=-2^2` gives 4, `=2^3^2` 64, `=POWER(-8;1/3)` −2 and
`=TEXT(45000;"yyyy-mm-dd")` 2023-03-15.

### Legacy 1.x office XML formats, damaged XLSX, ODF encrypted with OpenPGP (done)
**`.sxc`/`.stc` and `.sxi`/`.sti` files open**, the way the reference suite does with its transformer:
before the ODF readers an `ILegacyOdfUpgrader`
(`PulseOffice.Formats.Package/Legacy`) rewrites the package into ODF — MIME type and manifest, and every
XML part with the 2000 vocabulary translated by `LegacyXmlTranslator`, a chain of rules: namespaces
legacy 1.x namespaces → OASIS, `office:body` with its `office:spreadsheet`/
`office:presentation`, `style:properties` split into text, paragraph, cell, column,
row, page and graphic properties according to the family (underline and strikethrough with their new names), cell
values moved from `table:` to `office:`, text-only cells as strings, `draw:text-box`/`draw:image`/objects
inside a `draw:frame`, `form:control` merged with its control, typed form properties,
`#Pictures/…` without the `#`, lists, fonts, pages. **Verified against the reference suite**: five sample files from its test corpus (spreadsheets with
shapes, an image, four controls and a chart, and presentations) read the same as their conversion to ODS/ODP made by the reference suite's converter.
**Encryption** goes through the same decryptor (Blowfish CFB with SHA-1, or AES): the legacy 1.x
manifest is translated before reading the parameters; when `key-size` is missing the key is as long
as the algorithm requires (32 bytes for AES-256) — `passwordWrongSHA.ods` opens with «test». **Writing
stays ODF**: a document opened from a format without a writer is no longer saved in the native format with
the old extension; *Save* goes through *Save As* (Ledger and Deck). Charts and other
sub-documents get only the general translation: accepted loss.

**Damaged XLSX**: `forcepoint107.xlsx` (broken XML, wrong CRCs, parts that cannot be decompressed) is opened
by the reference suite only with *RepairPackage*, and Excel "repairs" it. Now we do too: `MalformedXmlRepair`
in the package repair (it applies to PPTX as well) reads whatever can be read of each part; a broken
sheet is rebuilt row by row and cell by cell (`WorksheetSalvage`), the other unreadable parts are
skipped and references to them dropped. Translated diagnostics `XLSX049`/`XLSX050`, `PPTX025`/`PPTX026`.

**ODF encrypted with OpenPGP: reading not supported, by choice.** Decrypting it needs the recipient's private
key, i.e. the user's GnuPG keyring (or a `gpg` binary): there is no managed path that does not touch it.
The manifest with `keyinfo`/`PGPKeyID` is recognized, no useless password is asked for,
and the reason is stated: `ODF030` in the readers, `UnlockOutcome.OpenPgp` when opening, text
`password.openPgp` in the five languages.

### Bug audit, fourteenth round: grid, pivot and analysis, math formulas, sheet objects (done)
**Ledger grid.** Lookup of the row and column under the pointer is now binary (it was quadratic with
many hidden rows); ⌘+arrows, ⌘+Home/End, End and PgUp/PgDn as in the reference suite (`CellNavigator`);
text overflow in a pure service (`CellOverflow`: centered on both sides, not stopped by empty
formatted cells, stopped by merges, also by cells out of view, drawn after backgrounds and grid);
**rotation, vertical alignment and wrapping finally drawn** (`CellTextPlacement`); negative and
"win/loss" sparklines (`SparklineBars`); autocompletion without formula results; conditional
rules: on equal attributes the highest priority wins.

**Pivot and analysis.** Aggregations and display modes that counted blanks as zero;
GETPIVOTDATA that matched filters by position and ignored column fields; subtotals, consolidation
and advanced filter as in the reference suite (case, numeric criteria in the locale); mode with several values.

**Math formulas and the reference suite.** The reference suite draws from the StarMath annotation, and ours was
not StarMath: matrices and symbols came out wrong. `StarMathSource` writes real StarMath; the parser reads
`%alpha`, `over`, `left … right`, matrices `#`/`##` and double operators. Verified with the reference suite.

**Sheet objects on files from the reference suite.** ODS chart style in the right namespace
(`style:chart-properties`: bar, stacked and percent were lost); `data-source-has-labels` read
backwards; axis titles, data labels and gridlines in both formats; position and `z-index` of
charts; primitive shapes and groups in ODS; **icon sets** in the model, the formats and the grid;
data bar and color scale thresholds preserved; full rule style in ODS. Declared losses
`XLSX046`–`048`.

**Limits closed.** **Legacy 1.x office XML** files (`.sxc`, `.sxi`, templates) translated into ODF before the
readers (`Legacy/`), encryption included, compared with the reference suite's conversion; XLSX and PPTX with
**broken XML** recovered part by part like the reference suite's repair (`MalformedXmlRepair`,
`WorksheetSalvage`, `XLSX049`/`050`, `PPTX025`/`026`); ODF encrypted with **OpenPGP** recognized and
declared (`ODF030`): decrypting it requires the private key from the GnuPG keyring, which we do not touch.

**Verified live**: wrapped text is drawn on several lines in the cell. This revealed that the row
did not grow by itself as in the reference suite: fixed, see the next section.

### Automatic row height (done)
As in the reference suite, a row that nobody has sized by hand **adapts to its content**: wrapped text, font size,
rotation, cells merged on a single row. `SheetLayout` distinguishes manual heights (`RowHeights`) from
automatic ones (`AutomaticRowHeights`); *Optimal Row Height* returns rows to automatic.
The measurement lives in `RowAutoHeight` (pure logic, with `ICellTextMeasure` as strategy) and the text is
laid out in **a single component**, `CellTextComposer`, used both by the measurement and by grid
drawing, so the two cannot diverge. Recalculation is **incremental**: `RowAutoHeightTracker`
listens to the touched cells and re-measures only those rows; it redoes the whole sheet only on opening or when
column widths, row and column styles, manual heights or merges change. A test on 100,000
rows watches the time of an edit. In the formats the distinction is native:
`style:use-optimal-row-height` in ODS, `customHeight` in XLSX, verified with the reference suite in both directions.
**Verified live**: long text in A1 with *Wrap Text*, row 1 grows to five lines.

### Bug audit, fifteenth round, and the limits closed (done)
**OpenPGP with BouncyCastle.** ODF documents encrypted for OpenPGP recipients open and save. The
library is `BouncyCastle.Cryptography` 2.7.0 (MIT, pure C#, no native binary), referenced only by
`PulseOffice.Formats.Package` and hidden behind an interface of ours (`IOpenPgp`, adapter
`BouncyCastleOpenPgp`), like Hunspell. The manifest follows the reference suite (`manifest:encrypted-key` with
`PGPKeyID`, `PGPKeyPacket`, `CipherValue`; also the `loext:` form). Two hierarchies: how it is protected
(`OdfProtection`: password or OpenPGP) and how it is opened (`OdfUnlockKey`). On opening, the user picks the secret
key file and the passphrase; *Protect with Password…* also offers "OpenPGP recipients…", in
Ledger and Deck; a reopened document is saved again for the same recipients, recovery copies included.
Tested with RSA, ECDH NIST P-256/384/521 and Curve25519, and with the reference suite's test files
(`encryptedGPG.odt`, ODF 1.3 format) decrypted with its test key. Not verified in the opposite
direction with the reference suite, which decrypts only through GnuPG.

**Encrypted saving verified with the real reference suite**: `tools/verify-encrypted/` has us write encrypted ODS and
ODP (AES-256-CBC, PBKDF2) and has the reference suite, headless, open them with a macro in a temporary
profile and the password; the text is there, and with the wrong password the reference suite rejects them.

**Exact object end.** `ISheetPlacement.End` computes the end cell and offset from the real layout
(automatic heights and hidden rows included): `table:end-cell-address`, `end-x`, `end-y` in ODS
(`OdfCellEnd`) and `xdr:twoCellAnchor editAs="oneCell"` with `xdr:to` in XLSX (`XlsxCellAnchors`).
Verified with the reference suite to a hundredth of a centimeter.

**Icon sets as in the reference suite**: its 22 families as shared vector geometry
(`PulseOffice.Drawing/ConditionalIcons`, one painter per shape), in grid, print and PDF —
conditional formatting previously did not print at all. "Strictly greater" threshold
(`calcext:greater_equal`, `gte`), reversal (`reverse`, in ODF `ODF040`), stars, triangles and boxes
in the x14 extension of XLSX, and **custom** sets (`calcext:custom-iconset`, `x14:cfIcon`);
the reference suite's ODS reader does not read custom icons (it only exports them).

**Sheet charts**: legend in every position, pie with the categories in the legend and one color per
slice, scatter with a numeric X axis, axis titles and data labels finally drawn,
ticks on round steps (`PlotScale.Divisions`), horizontal bars from the bottom as in the reference suite. When inserting a
chart the first row is a header only if it contains text, as in the reference suite: before, a leading number became
the series name (found live).

**Ledger**: automatic link updates always enter the history and mark the
document modified, like the reference suite's area link refresh; automatic heights and remembered sizes follow insertion and
deletion of rows; hidden rows keep their height in ODS and XLSX; a manual row as tall as
the default stays manual; **optimal column width** with the real measurement (`ColumnAutoWidth`,
same component as the height); sheet themes do not clear direct formatting; comparisons in
pivot calculated fields; numbers in the sheet's locale in external data; `PivotEngine` entirely from DI.
Incremental automatic height: `RowAutoHeightTracker` re-measures only the touched rows.

**Deck**: master graphics at full page in 4:3 and in custom formats (`ISlideResize.Stretch`),
missing layouts rebuilt at the presentation's size, previews and theme gallery in its
proportions, PPTX highlighting from theme, default and system colors, End on wrapped lines,
autocorrection that does not fire on the apostrophe, drag lost in the editor. Round trip of themes with
the reference suite in 16:9 and 4:3, in both directions and chained.

**Verified live**: column chart of 3, 8, −2 and 5 with four bars, the negative one below zero and round
ticks; the app starts with the container's new registrations.

### The chart picker (done)
"Insert chart" was a drop-down of fifty-five names. Now it is a real, shared picker
(`IChartPicker`, `ChartPickerView` in `PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Charts`), used by Ledger (*Insert ▸
Chart ▸ More Charts…*) and by Deck (*Insert ▸ Chart*, which used to place a fixed column chart), ready
for Folio. On the left the families with icons, derived from a single table (`ChartFamilyCatalog`, which rejects
a type without a family); at the top the variants as tiles with the **real thumbnail** (`ChartRenderMode.Thumbnail`
of the same `ChartRenderer`, without texts); below, the large preview with the selection's data; alongside,
title, legend and header. The **Recommended** ones are a chain of rules on the shape of the data
(`ChartRecommendations`): scatter only with a real numeric X column — `ChartData.OrdinalCategories`
distinguishes generated categories. Keyboard, double click, footer with Cancel and Insert.
**Verified live** in Ledger (3, 8, −2, 5: first recommended is the column chart, preview with the negative
bar) and in Deck with the sample data.
**Editing also goes through the picker**: "Edit chart" (double click, context menu, menu) opens
`ChartPickerView` in edit mode through `IChartEditor`, prefilled by `ChartSettingsMapper`
(type, title, axis titles, legend, values, gridlines, series in rows or columns, header,
validated range), with "Apply" and undo; in Deck the command `deck.chart.edit` did not exist.
The old field-based dialog is gone. Found live: in Deck double-clicking a chart placed over
a placeholder opened the text editor underneath; now the topmost object counts. **Verified live** in
Ledger and in Deck: column chart changed to stacked, applied, and ⌘Z brings it back.

### Keyboard shortcuts: a real editor (done)
*Customize* was a text box with "identifier = shortcut" lines: internal ids, Ctrl even on
macOS, all modules mixed together. Now it is *Tools ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…* (`ShortcutEditorView`,
shared): categories (all, modules, menus derived from the paths) with the active module preselected,
commands with icon, translated name and path, search by name, word or key (also by pressing it),
shortcuts in the system's symbols with **a single formatter** (`GestureNotation`, also used by menus,
palette and the F1 list). A shortcut is changed by **pressing** the combination (`KeyCaptureBox`; on macOS the native menu
forwards the gesture to the capture field through `TextEditingRouter`), with remove, restore
default and restore all; combinations reserved by the system are refused (`ReservedShortcuts`) and
conflicts are shown with the name of the other command and the choice to reassign (`ShortcutScope`, the same
rule as the startup check). Customizations go to `shortcuts.json` (canonical form, atomic
write, corrupt file ignored). The F1 help is now called "Shortcut list…".
**Verified live**: ⌘B pressed on "Paste formulas only" shows "⌘B is already used by Bold"
with *Reassign*.
**Three defects found afterwards, reported and tested live.** "Insert time" (`Ctrl+Shift+;`) made
the dialog blow up into a conflict warning with hundreds of commands: the semicolon was not a recognized
key, the shortcut came out as "none", and "none" was equal to every other absence. Now the
symbols (`; ' [ ] \ \` < > = *`) are real keys, an absence is never in conflict, and shortcut
parsing is **a single one**: `ShortcutGesture` (the one that executes them) went through a second parser,
which did not know `;` — so the "Insert time" shortcut had never worked. Then: **modal dialogs opened without focus**,
and whatever was typed ended up in the cell behind the dialog; now
`DialogHost` gives focus to the first field (or to the frame). Finally "Press a key" was a stock theme
button: now it is a keyboard icon inside the search field (`ui.keyboard`, class `keySearch`), with
a tooltip and an active state in the module's color.

### The Settings dialog redone (done)
It was a column with misaligned labels and descriptions, huge arrows, an untranslated category
("⟦settingCategory.devices⟧") and the default scanner as a raw id. Now (`PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Settings`)
it has on the left the categories with icons derived from the schema (first segment = page, the rest = section;
modules in a group of their own when they declare settings) and the search, on the right rows aligned in cards
with a control per type chosen by a factory (`ISettingEditorFactory`: `SwitchToggle` switch,
drop-down with descriptions, compact number with unit and range, color, path, text), a dot on
modified ones, ↺ on hover, "requires restart" and "set by the administrator" pills, "Restore
all". The default scanner is a drop-down of the real devices. The scanner settings moved up
into the shell (`ShellSettings`) because the command belongs to the shell. Pure logic in `PulseOffice.Settings/Navigation`;
a test checks the translations of every setting and category in the five languages. The command is now called
"Settings…" like the dialog (it was "Options…") and has **⌘,** — Ctrl+, elsewhere —, the shortcut
macOS expects. **Verified live**: ⌘, opens the dialog; General, Appearance and Devices.

### Autocorrection: a real dialog, and the reference suite's lists included (done)
It was a text box with "from → to" lines, and three commands for the same thing. Now it is **a shell
command**, *Tools ▸ AutoCorrect…* (`shell.tools.autocorrect`), with a shared dialog
(`PulseOffice.UI.Controls/AutoCorrection`) in the style of Settings and Shortcuts: **Options** with
switches and descriptions, **Replacements** as a real table (language, search with the filtered
count, inline addition with validation, edit by double click, deletion, origin of every entry,
"Import…" of an autocorrect `.dat` file, restore; only your own or modified entries carry a label — the provenance of the defaults does not matter to the writer, and the license is already declared in the files), **Exceptions** (abbreviations after which no capital follows,
words with two initial capitals allowed, also new in the engine). Customizations go to
`autocorrect.json`. Replacements follow the **language of the text** with a single resolver
(`TextLanguageResolver`, the same as spelling): cell, document, system.

**License decision (first exception to the rule of permissive-only data).** The default replacements
were a few dozen; the reference suite has thousands per language, under **MPL 2.0**. We include them
converted to JSON, one file per language (51 languages) in `PulseOffice.Text.Spelling/Data/autocorrect/`,
generated by `tools/import-autocorrect/` from the external reference clone, **versioned**, with
`LICENSE-MPL-2.0.txt` and `NOTICE` alongside. The MPL applies file by file: those JSON files stay MPL and readable (they are not
obfuscated or encrypted), the rest of PulseOffice does not. Only the language in use is loaded. Precedence: user
entries > JSON from the reference clone > our own JSON (`autocorrect-pulseoffice/`). We no longer look for
installations of the reference suite: it would be a duplicate.

Found while testing live: an **Esc pressed on the grid without an editor wrote the control character
into the cell**; now control characters do not start editing. **Verified live**: «qual'è»
becomes «qual è» when typing in a cell; the search «qua» finds the entries.

### "Developer tools" removed
They showed in a modal dialog a few model counts (sheets, styles, cells, history, number of commands):
stuff for developers, not users, and in the reference suite the entry is an inspector of its object model that makes no
sense here. Removed command, dialog, icon, ribbon and menu rules and texts, in Ledger and in Deck; in the maps the
entry is `escluso` (excluded). Coverage: spreadsheet 412/412, presentations 366/366.

It was our version of the reference suite's XML filter settings: XSLT stylesheets registered by the user to import or export other parties' XML formats, managed through a text box with "name | extension | path" lines. A niche feature: removed by choice the command, the dialog, the catalog (`XmlFilterCatalog`), the ribbon and menu rules, the icon and the texts. In the maps the entry is `escluso`. Coverage: spreadsheet 411/411, presentations 365/365.

### Events and macros: a shared view, with the editor at hand (done)
"Sheet events" was a column of identical drop-downs. Now it is a shared view
(`PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Macros`): one row per event with a description of when it fires, the chosen macro
(name, icon, language; "not found" if it was renamed or deleted), and the buttons *Edit*,

number of macros and "Open the macro editor", or an invitation if there are none. The editor opens over the

Events tab of form controls (Ledger and Deck) and Deck's *Interaction… ▸ Run macro*. Pure logic in
`PulseOffice.Document/Forms/MacroBindings.cs`. New test project `tests/PulseOffice.UI.Controls.Tests`

Two general fixes came out of it: drop-downs receive **data with a template** (`FuncDataTemplate`),
not already-built controls; and `Button.dialogPrimary:disabled` has a disabled state (before, a disabled
primary button stayed solid green). When a modal dialog opens, focus goes to the first text
field, otherwise to the frame without an indicator.

**A trap of live testing, written down because it wasted time**: the app window had
moved (99,167 instead of 92,137) and all clicks landed thirty pixels above the buttons, looking like
a dead interface. Before clicking, read the real position (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo`).
**Verified live**: *Create a macro* opens the editor, the saved macro appears in the dialog, it is
assigned to activation, *Apply* marks the document modified.
