### Pop-up notifications with severity (done)
Rejections ended up in small print in the status bar and it looked as if the button did nothing. Now
`IStatusBarService.Report` accepts a **severity** (`Info`, `Success`, `Warning`, `Error`) and an **action**
(`NotificationAction`: callback or registry command, executed as from the ribbon). Info stays discreet
in the status bar; the rest also appears as a **pop-up notification** at the bottom center
(`UI.Controls/Notifications`): stripe and icon in the severity's color, readable text, action, ✕; it expires
after 5 s (errors 7 s) but not with the pointer over it, at most three, and a duplicate shakes the visible
one instead of adding another (`NotificationQueue`, pure and tested logic). It sits above the modal
veil. The 380 calls were classified: 128 errors, 71 warnings, 40 confirmations, 119 information, 22
conditional; remedies "Remove protection…", "Edit mode" and "Save" where the command exists.
**Verified live**: in read-only mode, typing in a cell shows the red notification with "Edit mode".

**Message history.** Every message, information included, enters `INotificationHistory`
(in memory, 200 entries, consecutive duplicates counted as "×N"). In the status bar a bell carries
the number of unread warnings and errors and opens the panel: severity icon and color, text, time, action
and "Clear". A defect found while testing: the button without a background let clicks through, and only
the counter dot responded; now it has a transparent background and a headless test really clicks in the center.
"Undone: …" and "Redone: …" were written in Italian in the code: now they are keys in the five languages.

### Bug audit, seventeenth round — first point: large sheets in streaming (done)
Measured before changing, with [tools/format-bench](tools/format-bench) on a synthetic sheet of
500,000 rows by 10 columns (5 million cells; the model alone takes about 0.67 GB). Peak
memory from `/usr/bin/time -l`, because on macOS the .NET counter gives zero:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Save ODS | 3.3 GB, 12.7 s | 1.0 GB, 7.8 s |
| Open ODS | 2.9 GB, 14.0 s | 1.06 GB, 8.2 s |
| Save XLSX | 4.7 GB, 13.8 s | 1.67 GB, 4.6 s |
| Open XLSX | 4.8 GB, 24.6 s | 1.2 GB, 7.8 s |

**System.Xml.Linq stays**, but only where the tree is small. The body of the sheets goes through streaming:
- **ODS writing** (`OdsWriter`): automatic styles and font declarations are discovered only
  while the cells are written, but in `content.xml` they come *before* the body. So the body is written
  in streaming (`XmlWriter`, one row at a time as a small `XElement`) into a temporary file that
  deletes itself on close; then `content.xml` is assembled from header, styles and a streaming copy of the
  body. Row groups and header rows are opened and closed as the rows
  flow (`OdsRowGrouping`); external data links and alternative text are placed
  on the row instead of on the whole tree. The row index (`CellRowIndex` in `PulseOffice.Sheets`,
  shared with XLSX) replaces copying all cells into a dictionary.
- **ODS reading** (`OdsContentLoader`): `XmlReader` builds the tree of `content.xml`, but each
  `table:table-row` becomes an `XElement` of its own, whose cells are read into the sheet immediately
  (`OdsTableReader.ReadRow`). Then the row is compacted (`OdsRowCompactor`): cells that carried only
  value and style become bare cells with just the repetition. Everything the part readers use
  stays: merges, comments, frames, validations, external sources, row sizes and styles. **Equal rows are not
  merged**: the first version did it and changed the sizes read, because the height reader
  decides based on the repetitions per element.
- **XLSX writing**: the sections build the sheet with an empty `sheetData`; then the part is
  rewritten with `OpenXmlWriter`, and rows are generated and written one at a time (`UnloadRootElement`
  prevents the SDK from re-saving the DOM). The rest of the peak comes from the SDK: in a package opened for
  reading and writing `System.IO.Packaging` keeps the parts in memory until closing, and with a
  write-only stream the SDK refuses to create the document.
- **XLSX reading**: the sheet is read with `OpenXmlReader`, row by row. The part keeps a light
  DOM without cells, which the other readers use as before. The light DOM is rebuilt from its
  XML (`new Worksheet(outerXml)`), because elements loaded by `LoadCurrentElement` inside
  `mc:AlternateContent` remain unknown, and the form controls of `.xlsm` files disappeared. The
  document is opened without auto-save: before, on closing, the SDK re-saved every part
  into the in-memory copy. The attribute sanitizer no longer goes through reflection on every cell:
  it acts on a row only if reading it fails.

**Verified.** Old and new reader compared on 1,383 ODS and 578 XLSX/XLSM files of the external test
corpus, with a summary of the model read (cells, styles, merges, comments, objects, sizes,
groups, names): identical. The only difference is a randomly generated identifier, which also changes between
two reads with the old code. Forty-five ODS files re-saved by the new writer and exported to CSV by
the reference suite match those of the old writer, except for one cell with `NOW()`.
The reference suite opens our large ODS and XLSX files. **Live**: the 5-million-cell sheet opens,
saves and is read back whole.

### Bug audit, seventeenth round: the rest (done)
Four parallel searches, then merging and testing.

**The streaming just written.** A table inside a frame (in `table:shapes`) became a sheet and
reversed the order of the sheets: only a `table:table` child of `office:spreadsheet` is a sheet, as in
the reference suite. Overlapping row groups nested wrongly when writing, and grouping scanned
all groups at every row: now groups are sorted once and one that does not fit inside the open one
waits, as the previous code did.

**Re-saving compared with the reference suite on 135 ODS and 85 XLSX files**, in the four directions. Defects fixed:
- **dates turning back into numbers**: the number styles of `styles.xml` and of `content.xml` had the
  same names (`N100`…) and the reference suite took the wrong one (now the named ones have the prefix `NS`);
  a formula with the same style as the column repeated it on the cell;
- **"General" read as "0"** (`number:number` without decimals), and the **format sections** in the
  reference suite's form (main one last, maps `>=0`, `>0`, `<0`), with the format language `[$-407]`;
- the cached type of a formula no longer becomes a cell format; `boolean-value="8"` is TRUE;
- the cells of an array in error no longer become `=#VALUE!` formulas;
- cross-sheet references with two ends, whole rows and columns, vendor function prefixes, `[#REF!]`,
  the spill operator (`_xlfn.ANCHORARRAY`), XLSX inline arrays;
- **XLSX tables** (`Table1[Age]`, `[#This Row]`…) are read as database ranges and structured
  references are resolved: before, formulas broke on re-saving;
- an XLSX hyperlink without display text made **the reference suite hang** on opening.
New declared losses: `ODF041` (Basic macros), `XLSX051` (references to other documents).

**The grid showed custom formats as "General".** `CellPresenter` received from the container
a single number format catalog for the whole application, while formats from 164 up live in the
document's catalog: every date or custom format read from a file showed as a number, also in print,
in HTML and in the measurement of rows and columns. Now whoever presents receives the document's catalog; the
singleton was removed. Found only live, opening a corpus file.

**Shared components.** Thread-safe status bar (copy under lock, timer with generation,
empty messages ignored); notifications that stayed on screen after the host was detached; notification
actions that fired behind a modal dialog or crashed the app; messages marked read with the
history open; color picker without NaN and with the hexadecimal field returning to the color in use;
eyedropper only with the left button and tolerance with the shared `NumberBox`; "Select on sheet" in a
multi-range field replaces only the last one instead of clearing the others; accessibility names
translated.

**Commands.** The last visible sheet can be neither deleted nor hidden (`IWorksheetTabPolicy`), after
deletion the nearest visible sheet is selected, renaming by changing case is no longer
refused; query refresh goes through the history and respects protection
(`IQueryRefreshRunner`, one instead of two copies); fills, rows and columns respect protection;
"Show rows", heights and widths on whole rows or columns no longer scan a million entries
(`SheetLayout.ShowRows`, `SetRowHeights`…); "Right to left" enters the history; group and
edit shape respect read-only and protection. Ledger and Deck toggles now have the checked
state (`CheckedWhen`). **Ribbon and menus are refreshed after every executed command**
(`CommandExecutor.Executed`): before, checkmarks stayed frozen until something else changed the
context, and each module patched it case by case. In Deck re-announcing the context goes through
`IActiveDeckContext.Reannounce`, which does not steal the context for a presentation in the background.

**Verified live**: the dates of a corpus file show as dates; "Page breaks" turns on
and "Normal view" turns off on click; the 5-million-cell sheet opens and saves. Memory unchanged
after the fixes.

Inference of the format of formula results, left open here, is done: see the next section.

### The format of formula results is inferred as in the reference suite (done)
A formula with "General" format shows the result in the format the reference suite would give it: `=A1-B1` with A1 a
date shows as a date. The rules come from the reference suite's interpreter (its add/subtract rule and its
date/time difference rule; the range rules as well) and were **verified
against the real reference suite on 62 formulas**: a flat hand-written sheet, exported to CSV by the reference suite and
compared with what our engine shows (`present` mode of `tools/format-bench`).

- **Classification** (`PulseOffice.Sheets/Formatting/FormatHints.cs`): a format is date, time, date and time,
  duration, percentage, currency or none (`IFormatKindClassifier`); `IFormatHints` resolves a kind into its
  default format, registering it in the document's catalog (`dd/mm/yyyy`, `hh:mm:ss`,
  `dd/mm/yyyy hh:mm`, `[hh]:mm:ss`, `0.00%`).
- **Inference** (`PulseOffice.Sheets.Engine/Evaluation/Formats`): a visitor on the formula tree
  with the rules as strategies. A reference carries the **exact** format of the cell (or the inferred one,
  if it is itself a formula); a range carries that of the **last cell with a value**, as in the reference suite.
  Addition and subtraction: currency passes with its format; date minus date is a number, date plus number is
  a date, time plus time a duration, date plus time date and time, and percentage passes — always with the
  **default format of the kind**, not the cell's. Product and quotient carry only currency. Unary
  minus, `ROUND`, `ABS`, `EDATE`, `DATEVALUE` and `MEDIAN` carry nothing, as in the reference suite.
  Functions are a table (`FunctionFormatRules`): `TODAY`, `DATE`, `NOW`, `TIME`, `TIMEVALUE` give
  their kind; `SUM`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `MINA`, `MAXA` the format of the first argument; `AVERAGE` its kind;
  `IF`, `CHOOSE` and `INDEX` that of the argument **actually chosen**, evaluating condition and indexes in the
  cell's context.
- **Where it lives**: the engine writes the inferred format on the cell (`Cell.InferredFormatId`) together with the
  result, and `CellPresenter` uses it only if the cell has "General" format and contains a formula; a
  format chosen by the user always wins.
- **Formats**: in ODS nothing is written, because the reference suite infers it by itself on opening. In XLSX
  the inferred format is written on the cell, as the reference suite does when exporting: Excel does not infer it on opening.

**Verified live**: opening the test sheet the formula column shows the same formats as
the reference suite. Known limit, as in the reference suite: changing the format of a referenced cell does not redo the inference until
the formula is recalculated.

### Folio, F0: audit of the foundations Folio inherits (done)
First block of the [Folio plan](docs/folio-plan.md): a targeted round on the Deck and shared parts that
the new module will reuse. Eighteen defects fixed, each with its test where a test is possible.

**Rich text and lines.** Pasting hundreds of thousands of characters into a text box froze
the interface: `TextEditSplice` and the merging of runs had quadratic cost, now linear with
`StringBuilder`. End on a wrapped line put the caret in the middle of an emoji.

**Inline editor.** On Windows autocorrection did not fire with Enter, which inserts two
characters. A pending correction could touch an editor already closed. Esc and Enter during an
IME composition closed the box, and a click moved the caret under the composition: now the key
stays with the IME and the click is ignored (to be tested live with a Japanese or Chinese keyboard).

**Text in the formats.** In PPTX line breaks inside a paragraph (`a:br`) were lost on reading and
written as a bare character; in ODF a line break inside a run became a space in the reference suite
(now `text:line-break`), XML whitespace was not collapsed as ODF requires, and paragraphs
inside `text:h` and lists were not read. The text of ODP comments ended up in the box as an extra paragraph. In PPTX
first-line indent with zero margin was lost passing through the reference suite: now there too a margin
of one twip (`ParagraphMargins.Written`). In ODP bold inside a hyperlink (`text:a`) was
lost. The style chain of ODP frames looked for parents also among automatic styles:
now there are two scopes, as in ODF. **Verified with the real reference suite** in both directions: numbered and
bulleted lists on several levels, tabs, line breaks, multiple spaces, highlighting, fields, indents.

**Fonts.** Macintosh names were read as Latin-1 («Café» → «CafŽ»; now `MacRomanText`); symbol
fonts (platform 3/0) came out without a name; an inconsistent EOT returned garbage bytes;
the cache could return an error page as a font, downloaded the same family several times and
kept forever a list with a future date. The embedding permission is now checked on **all**
faces of a `.ttc`, and weights on the old 1–9 scale become hundreds. Robustness tests on the system's
real fonts, truncated and altered: no exception other than `InvalidDataException`.

**Spelling.** The tokenizer works on `Rune`: letters outside the basic plane split words.
`LanguageTag.Parse` took the script for a region («sr-Latn-RS» → «sr-LATN») and the POSIX suffix
(«de_DE.UTF-8»), so it did not find the dictionary. Hyphenation no longer splits a surrogate pair nor
breaks before a combining accent.

**Verified live in Deck**: typing «perchè» followed by a space becomes «perché»; Esc cancels the
edit; exiting with "Don't save" is clean. «teh» is not corrected in Italian because it is not in the Italian
list: replacements follow the language of the text.

**Left, to be decided in Folio**: a word longer than the line does not wrap in the two typesetters
(first line and justified), while the rest of the paragraph breaks it; the line typesetter costs
characters × lines, to be rewritten in F2; the first level (compound words) of libhyphen hyphenation
is not used; the hyperlink URL is not in the text model.

**To be moved into shared projects before F1**, because Folio must not depend on Deck:
- rich text model from `PulseOffice.Presentations` (`SlideText.cs` with `TextRun`, `TextParagraph`,
  fields; `TextFrame`, `ListLabels`, `TextEditSplice`, `TextOffsetMap`, `CaretWord`, `CaretRows`,
  `ParagraphLines`, `FirstLineBreaker`, `ParagraphMargins`, `DeckTextFormatter` and collaborators) to a
  rich text project without Avalonia, with neutral names;
- typesetters and text geometry from `PulseOffice.Presentations.UI/Rendering` (`TextBlockTypesetter`,
  `StyledParagraph`, `TextFrameComposer`, `TextFrameMeasure`, `TextCaretGeometry`, `SpellingWaves`…) and
  the inline editor (`InlineTextEditor`, `InlineImeClient`, the editor lifecycle of `DeckView`) to
  `PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Text`;
- `DeckSpelling` and `DeckTextInsertion` generalized over the paragraph;
- in the formats, readers and writers of paragraphs, runs, lists and fields currently under `Presentation`
  (ODF: `TextReading`, `ElementWriters`, `OdfFieldElements`, `OdfTextFrames`; OOXML/DrawingML:
  `TextReading`, `TextBuilders`, `PlaceholderInheritance`, `OoxmlFieldTypes`), with `OdfParagraphText`
  injected instead of instantiated.

### Folio, F1: the document model (done)
`PulseOffice.Documents` is no longer a placeholder: it is Folio's model, without Avalonia, with 41 tests in
`tests/PulseOffice.Documents.Tests`.
- **Blocks** (Composite, with Visitor `IBlockVisitor<T>`): `ParagraphBlock` (a `TextParagraph` plus the
  inline marks), `TableBlock` (cells with blocks, merges, header rows), `SectionBlock`
  (columns, protection, condition, link). `BlockTree` and `BlockPath` find a block and its
  path, also inside cells.
- **Inline marks** (`Marks/`): bookmarks, comments, revisions, notes, objects, index entries as
  zero-width marks in the paragraph, each with its own movement rule when typing there;
  a note or an object is deleted only if the mark is **strictly** inside the deletion.
- **Anchored objects** (`Objects/`): anchored to page, paragraph, character or as character,
  wrap, relative position; the content is an existing `EmbeddedObject` or a text box
  with its blocks (like `draw:frame` and `wp:anchor`).
- **Annotations**: comments with replies, footnotes and endnotes with block content,
  revisions in the ODF manner (insertions and formatting as ranges, deletions as a point
  with the removed text preserved), with recording and protection key.
- **Styles as document objects**: paragraph, character, list (ten levels), page
  (header and footer with first page and even), frame, table; nullable properties and a
  **resolver** (`StyleResolver`, chain with cycle protection: defaults → paragraph →
  character → direct) that returns full `TextRun` and `TextParagraph`, so layout reuses the
  typesetters. The initial styles have the reference suite's canonical names.
- **`TextDocument`**: implements the same interfaces as `Workbook` and `Presentation` (modules, fonts,
  macros, macro signature), with properties, language, versions; deep `Clone`; `TextDocumentFactory`.
- **Editing** (`Editing/`): positions (paragraph and offset) that follow edits with a
  `PositionTracker`; `DocumentEditor` to write over several lines, delete across paragraphs, split
  (with the next style, as the reference suite does), join, styles and direct formatting, tables, notes, comments,
  bookmarks, objects, fields, all on the `UndoStack` with transactions; `StoryCatalog` applies the
  same operation in body, notes, comments, text boxes, headers and footers.

**Shared rich text, additions only** (Deck unchanged): on the run, character style,
hyperlink, language, field argument; on the paragraph, style, list style, outline level,
right margin, "keep with next", "keep together", widows, orphans, break before,
tab stops; more field types. **Three-state direct formatting**: a true counts as direct, a
false only if declared in `Explicit` (`RunOverrides`, `ParagraphOverrides`), so bold can be removed
from one word inside a heading without changing Deck's types.

Open, to be decided in later blocks: service registration in the container (F3); deletion
that crosses different containers, refused today; copy and paste with new identifiers;
the exact sizes of the initial styles (F4, against a real `.odt`); changing the page style
on a paragraph.

### Folio, F1: the text codecs leave the presentations (done)
Structural refactoring, **identical XML output**: 150 PPTX and 150 ODP files from the external test corpus, rewritten in both
formats before and after, give 12,423 XML parts without differences (leaving out the parts that change at every round
even with the old code: relationship identifiers, field GUIDs, dates).
- **ODF** (`Formats.Odf/TextCodecs`): paragraphs, runs, lists, fields, text frames and the text style
  tables; stateless readers that receive the styles per call (`OdfTextStyles`);
  `OdfRichTextWriter` extracted from the slide writer; style builders on `ITextTheme`;
  `IOdfParagraphText` injected everywhere instead of instantiated. Common bases `OdfXml`, `OdfUnits`,
  `OdfValues`, `AutomaticStyleTable` at the root.
- **OOXML** (`Formats.OpenXml/DrawingML/Text`): the DrawingML text needed by slides, sheet
  shapes and DOCX text boxes — `DrawingRunReader`, `DrawingParagraphReader`, `DrawingFieldTypes`,
  per-level styles (`LevelStyles`), colors, frames (`BodyFrames`), run and paragraph builders.

### Folio, F1: the model's limits closed (done)
- **Deletion across containers** (`ContentTrails`, `RangeDeletion`), with the reference suite's rules: work starts
  from the innermost common container; a table crossed partially loses only the content of the touched
  cells, a table or section covered entirely disappears; a body paragraph never merges with
  a cell; notes and objects of deleted blocks go away with them; a single undo step.
- **Copy and paste** (`Clipboard/`): `DocumentFragment` with blocks, styles used (closure of the chain:
  parents, next, lists, pages), notes, comments with replies and objects; `FragmentRemapper` gives
  new identifiers and renames duplicate bookmarks; `StyleMerger` lets existing styles win;
  pasting several blocks splits the target as the reference suite does. Limit: a table crossed partially is
  copied whole.
- **Page style change on the paragraph** (`PageStyleName`, `PageNumberRestart`, also in paragraph
  styles as `master-page-name`), undoable; the formats arrive in F4.
- **Registration**: `AddDocumentsModel()`, tested with `ValidateOnBuild` resolving every service.
From 41 to 68 tests in the model.

### Folio, F2 first step: the layout engine (done)
`PulseOffice.Documents.Layout`, pure logic without Avalonia, 53 tests.
- **Measurement** as a Strategy (`ITextMeasurer`): a deterministic fake for tests and `OpenTypeMeasurer`,
  which reads the font's cmap, hmtx, hhea, OS/2 by itself. Line height uses ascender, descender and lineGap
  from **hhea**, as the reference suite does.
- **Lines**: `LineBreaker` (spaces, hyphens, soft hyphen, injected hyphenation points; a
  word that is too long is broken by characters as in the reference suite, without splitting surrogate pairs),
  `TabResolver` (left, right, center, decimal, fill, default interval 1.25 cm),
  `LineComposer` (alignments, justified as in the reference suite, baseline from the tallest font),
  line spacing as a `LineSpacingRule` hierarchy, list labels from list styles.
- **Pages** (`Paginator`): spacing, widows and orphans, "keep together", "keep with next" also
  chained, break before, page style change.
- **Tree** (Composite + Visitor): document → pages → lines → glyph runs with their origin;
  `ILayoutQueries` gives the position under a point and the caret box, tested round trip.
- **Incremental**: restarts one page before the edit and stops as soon as the pages
  coincide again; equal to complete re-layout; less than 50 ms for an edit on more than 500 pages.
- **Comparison with the real reference suite** on five `.fodt` files in Liberation Serif: same number of pages in
  all; lines 100% identical in three documents, 91–98% in the other two. The differences are lines at the
  width limit (482.11 pt against 481.89): kerning is missing.
Limits of this step: kerning and shaping, `.ttc` collections, exact and minimum line spacing, hyphenation
and contextual spacing as model properties, tables, columns, sections, headers, notes, objects,
borders and backgrounds, drop caps, right-to-left text.

### Folio, F2: kerning, model properties and second layout step (done)
**Precision.** Pair kerning from GPOS (formats 1 and 2, also through extension) with fallback on the
legacy `kern` table, as HarfBuzz does (`PairKerning` in `PulseOffice.Typography`, applied by the measurer
with `IKerningApplier`). Line breaks now coincide with the reference suite **100% in all test
documents** (before 91–98% in two), and the test requires it. There is a single metrics reader, in
Typography (`FontMetricsReader`), also for `.ttc` collections: the copy in the engine is gone.
In the model (additions, Deck unchanged): proportional, minimum, exact and added line spacing
(`ParagraphLineHeight`), hyphenation with ODF's options (`ParagraphHyphenation`), contextual
spacing; `StyleSheet.Version` triggers re-layout by itself after a style change.

**Second step.** Headers and footers (different first and even pages, "page N of M" resolved page by
page), page and section columns with balancing, footnotes with separator and
continuation, endnotes at the end, tables with columns, block cells, merges, split rows and
repeated header, paragraph borders and backgrounds (new in the model), objects as character and
anchored with all wrap modes. The page tree has areas, cells, objects and decorations;
point→position and caret also work in headers, cells and notes; incremental equal to complete.
**Comparison with the real reference suite**: headers (3/3 pages, 101/101 lines), two columns (2/2,
167/167), notes (2/2, 75/75), table over four pages (4/4, 153/153), image with text around it (1/1,
20/21: the missing line is the image placeholder in the PDF).

**Open limits**: in one test document the last two pages have 42 and 38 lines against 45 and 35 for
the reference suite (identical line breaks: it is the page division); paragraph borders and backgrounds are not yet in the
formats; edits to header and footer text do not trigger re-layout by themselves; page number in the
body not resolved; widows and orphans around objects, object-text distance, notes in columns and
in cells, numbering restart, vertically merged rows that do not split.

### Folio, F2: the layout limits closed — F2 complete (done)
- **Space above at the top of the page, as in the reference suite**: the space before the
  first paragraph of a page applies only on the first page or after an explicit break, not
  when one gets there by flow. It was the cause of the different lines per page: now **all
  test documents coincide with the reference suite 100%**, line breaks and line positions, and the tests
  require exact equality.
- **Page fields in the body** resolved page by page (`IPageFieldText`, shared with headers
  and footers), with the count iterated until stable; height of headers and footers with the final count.
- **Objects**: widows and orphans next to objects, object-text distance (`AnchoredObject.WrapSpacing`),
  text laid out inside frames (which grow if needed).
- **Notes**: under their own column with page columns, as the reference suite does; a note in
  a cell moves or splits the row; numbering per page and per chapter; page number
  restart, with even and odd following the displayed number.
- **Rows with vertically merged cells** split across pages, with vertical alignment per part.
- **Performance**: incremental re-layout on more than 500 pages in about 5 ms (median of five).
New test documents compared with the reference suite: notes in columns 126/126 lines, merged cells 102/102,
page fields 64/64, text in a frame 30/30.
Remaining: a merged cell that starts in the split row continues only there, Roman page numbers, notes
pending in the first column, inner padding of frames.

CSS, safe: no scripts or external resources, notes in the reference suite's `sdfootnote` form),
RTF (font and color tables, styles, lists, merged tables, images, fields, notes); a
common assembler (`TextDocumentAssembler`). External test corpus: 694 RTF and HTML files read and rewritten.

**F5**: 104 `folio.*` commands on a `FolioCommandSet` base with prototype: character, paragraph,
style gallery, insertions, page, search, tables, objects; context menus `foliotext`,
`foliocell`, `folioobject`; Home, Insert, Layout, References, Review, View tabs.
Survey with a former survey tool and a former command map: **125 out of 472 (26.5%)**.
Word count in a shared read-only view (`StatisticsView`); case changes on the selection's text
redistributed over the runs; rows and columns with merged cells as in the reference suite.

**Objects in Folio**: they can be selected, resized, rotated (`RotatedRect`, wrap on the rotated
box), moved re-anchoring as in the reference suite, copied and pasted (also images to and from the

edits to objects.

**Printing and PDF, common infrastructure**: images with alpha written with an `SMask`; shapes and paths in

Helvetica's widths.

**Verified live**: Folio with its ribbon, style "Intestazione 1" (Heading 1) from the gallery (the ribbon
follows: Liberation Sans 18, bold on), *Save As* with the nine formats, DOCX that the reference suite

### Galleries with the real look and translated formats in the file dialogs (done)
Gallery tiles with preview (`ChoiceSlot`, shared by the three modules) draw the sample
with the style's font, size fitted to the space (`SampleTypeScale`), decorations, color and alignment,
and the name on two lines. The font goes through `IDisplayFonts`, which uses the same metric
substitute as Folio's page (substitute table moved to `UI.Controls/Fonts`): without it, on a Mac

through a Decorator (`LocalizedFileDialogService`, keys `fileType.<extension>`).

### Dictionaries: a dialog of our own, no more dependence on another office suite (done)
"More dictionaries online…" opened the other office suite's extensions page, and the dictionary reader
also looked inside an installed copy of that suite: two dependencies on a third-party suite, removed by the user's
decision. System folders are now behind `ISystemDictionaryDirectories` in
`PulseOffice.Platform` (macOS `~/Library/Spelling`, Windows `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Spelling`, Linux
`/usr/share/hunspell` and similar); a test checks that no path names that suite or
its predecessors. Intended consequence: on this Mac the 30 dictionaries found before all came from
the third-party suite, and now they are installed from the dialog. The autocorrection lists, from the reference clone
origin and MPL, stay by the user's choice.

The command is now `shell.tools.dictionaries`, "Dictionaries…", with a shared dialog
(`UI.Controls/Dictionaries`): languages with their three parts — spelling, hyphenation, thesaurus — status,
license with its badge, source, install, update, remove, progress and cancel. Sources are
strategies (`IDictionarySource`) with a seven-day cache decorator and addresses in
`dictionaries.json` (https only): **spelling** from `wooorm/dictionaries` on GitHub, with the license of
each dictionary from its `package.json`; **hyphenation** from the TeX patterns of `hyph-utf8`, converted to
libhyphen format (`TexHyphenation`); **thesaurus**: no free and independent source, the dialog says
so and uses the system's. Dictionaries go into `dictionaries/<code>/` in the configuration
folder, with the license alongside, and become active immediately (`IDictionaryChanges`).
**Verified live**: real catalog from GitHub, Italian spelling (GPL-3.0, copyleft) and hyphenation
(MIT or LPPL) installed from the dialog, the registry goes from 0 to 1 dictionary without restart.

### Dictionaries: Mozilla, WordNet and OpenThesaurus sources (done)
More `IDictionarySource` strategies, merged per language with a ranking (`IDictionaryRanking`: first
license, then source priority) and a "Sources" drop-down in the dialog when there is more than one
candidate. **Spelling** also from Mozilla's dictionary extensions (API v5 of addons.mozilla.org,
`.aff`/`.dic` are extracted from the `.xpi` with `DictionaryArchive`, which rejects dangerous paths and caps
sizes). **Thesaurus** from Open English WordNet (CC BY 4.0, converted to MyThes format
by `WordNetThesaurusConverter` and `MyThesWriter`) and from OpenThesaurus (German and Swiss, copyleft, already in
MyThes format). Coverage measured on the real endpoints: spelling 189 languages, hyphenation 74, thesaurus
3. **Verified live**: English thesaurus installed from the dialog (`th_en_v2.dat`, 15.7 MB).
Limit: regional variants (`en-US`, `de-DE`) are rows separate from the base language.
**Regional variants grouped**: one row per base language, with the variants as pills in the detail;
codes are normalized (`en-US`, `de-DE`, `it-IT` → base language; `en-GB`, `de-CH`,
`pt-BR`, `pt-PT` stay distinct), and the base language's parts also apply to variants that do not have their own
("inherited"). 137 language rows instead of 206. **Verified live**: "English" with six variants,
spelling from two sources, hyphenation and WordNet thesaurus installed.
**Catalog cache with fingerprint** (source, catalog format, version of the code rules): a
catalog saved with old rules is discarded even within the seven days, and offline it is not shown. The
license of the English hyphenation from hyph-utf8 is the FSF All-Permissive notice (`FSFAP`), now recognized
as free.

### Digital signature inside the OOXML package (done)
Document signing now crosses **both formats**: `.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx` (and the macro-enabled
variants) are signed, verified and unsigned like `.odt`, `.ods`, `.odp`. Structure according to
ECMA-376 part 2 (§13), modeled on what Office and the reference suite write:
part `_xmlsignatures/origin.sigs` with the `digital-signature/origin` relationship from the package, one
`sigN.xml` part per signature with the `digital-signature/signature` relationship, the content types (`Default` for
`sigs`, `Override` for each signature). Each signature is XML-DSig with three `Object`s: `idPackageObject` (the
`Manifest` with one reference per part, URI `/part?ContentType=…`; `.rels` parts go through the
`RelationshipTransform` with one `RelationshipReference` per signed relationship, plus C14N),
`idOfficeObject` (`SignatureInfoV1`) and the XAdES `QualifyingProperties` (`SigningTime`,
`SigningCertificate` with SHA-256 fingerprint and issuer/serial). As the reference suite does, the following are not signed:
`[Content_Types].xml`, `docProps/core.xml`, `docProps/app.xml`, the signatures themselves, nor the relationships to the
properties and to the signature origin: this way a second signature does not break the first. RSA and ECDSA.

Structure: `OpcPackage` and `IOpcPackageStore` (the in-memory package and its atomic write),
`OoxmlSignatureScope` (what is signed), `IRelationshipTransform`, `IOoxmlSignatureBuilder`,
`OoxmlSignatureService`. `IDocumentSignatureService` is now a **composite**
(`DocumentSignatureService`) that chooses the strategy by extension among the `IPackageSignatureFormat`s
(ODF and OOXML): commands, signatures dialog and certificate selection are the same for the three
modules and the two formats. `IDocumentSignatureService.IsSigned` replaces the search for ODF entries inside
`SignedSaveGuard`, which now also warns for a signed OOXML before rewriting it (signatures are lost:
it is the declared invalidation, as in ODF). The signature tracker (`ISignedDocumentTracker`) moves
from Ledger to the **shell** and follows the workspace's active document; the status bar indicator
(`SignatureStatusIndicator`, segment `shell.signature`) applies to Folio, Ledger and Deck — before it existed
only in Ledger, fed by opening sheets.

**Verified**: tests on a hand-built `.docx` — signing and reading back, expected parts and relationships in the
package, signature broken by modifying a part, adding one or changing a signed relationship,
**not** broken by reformatting relationships or changing `docProps/core.xml`, two signatures that coexist and are
removed one at a time until origin and types are cleaned up, exact output of the `RelationshipTransform`, and the
XML signature checked again independently with `SignedXml.CheckSignature`. With the reference suite headless
(own profile) a `.docx` and an `.xlsx` produced by the reference suite and signed by us reopen without
errors. **Not verified**: that the reference suite *recognizes* the signature — `verifyDocumentContentSignatures`
in headless mode returns zero signatures even for a signed ODT, so the test is inconclusive either
way; it remains to be checked in the signatures panel with the interface, or in Word.

### "Open in design mode" closed in the three modules and the two formats (done)
Opening read-only was already largely done (`FormDocumentSettings.OpenInDesignMode`, command
`shell.form.openInDesignMode`, writing in ODF): three gaps remained, now closed.
- **Shared application on opening**: instead of the same line repeated in `LedgerView` and
  `DeckView`, and missing in Folio, `FormDesignModeOnOpen` (shell) listens to the workspace's `DocumentOpened`
  and turns on `IFormDesignMode` for any `IFormDocument` document that asks for it: Folio,
  Ledger and Deck alike. Ledger and Deck no longer give automatic focus to a control of a
  document opening in design mode. The command, belonging to the shell, was already in Folio's
  *Tools › Forms* menu (`TextDocument` is an `IFormDocument`).
- **ODF without controls**: ODS and ODP wrote `office:forms` (where `form:apply-design-mode` lives) only
  on sheets and slides with controls, so the setting of a document without controls
  was silently lost. Now `OdfFormControlMapper.SettingsOnly` writes an `office:forms` with an empty
  form on the first sheet or first slide, as ODT already does; with default settings nothing
  is written.
- **OOXML**: in DOCX opening in design mode is `w:formsDesign` in `settings.xml`, written and read back; the
  automatic focus and the data source have no equivalent and are declared (`DOCX013`). PPTX has
  nothing of the kind: declared loss (`PPTX027`). XLSX already declared it (`XLSX026`). Diagnostic texts
  in the five languages.

**Verified**: ODS, ODP and ODT round trips without controls that keep the settings, no
`office:forms` with default settings, DOCX round trip of `w:formsDesign`, the three declared losses,
and turning on at opening in all three modules (`FormDesignModeOnOpenTests`). The reference suite
headless (own profile) opens the ODS and the ODT and, rewriting them, keeps `form:apply-design-mode="true"`.

`TabbedDialogView` builds all tabs right away and stacks them in a grid: the unselected ones
are transparent, disabled and out of click reach, but they take part in measurement, so the dialog takes
the height of the tallest tab and no longer changes height when moving from one tab to another. It applies to
all tabbed dialogs of Folio, Ledger and Deck. Verified live in the Character and Page Setup dialogs: switching between tabs the height stays the same.

New Folio, one line, "Styles" in the ribbon, "Title" and "Apply": the paragraph becomes Title and the

### Folio, F6 — column break (done)
`ColumnBreakBefore` in the paragraph model (styles and direct formatting, like `PageBreakBefore`);
layout moves to the next column, or to the next page if the column is the last — as in
the reference suite, a single-column page breaks to a new page. Command *Insert › Breaks › Column
break* (`folio.insert.columnBreak`, Ctrl+Shift+Enter, also in the ribbon) and a checkbox in the
Text Flow tab of the paragraph dialog. ODT: `fo:break-before="column"`; reading `auto` no longer touches
the column break. DOCX: `w:br w:type="column"` at the start of the paragraph, also read back after the
text (it applies to the next paragraph) as already done for pages (`DocxPageBreaks.Place` takes the type).
Word has no column break in styles: declared loss `DOCX018`, five languages.
**Verified**: layout with and without columns, ODT and DOCX round trip and the four round trips through
the reference suite headless (`tools/formatting-fixtures.sh`, samples regenerated). The reference suite, exporting
to DOCX an ODT with the column break on a single-column page, removes it: it is its
exporter, the test excludes it for that round trip only.

### Folio, F6 — title page (done)
*Format › Page › Title Page…* (`folio.format.titlePage`, `FolioTitlePageCommands`), like
the reference suite's title page dialog: inserts N new pages at the start or converts the first N
existing ones, with the title page style of choice (default *First Page*) and numbering that
restarts, if requested, from the given number. The work lives in a core service, `ITitlePages`
(`TitlePages`), which composes the existing undoable operations into a single transaction: paragraph
split, `SetPageStyle` with numbering restart, `PageBreakBefore` on the title pages
after the first. For conversion the command picks the first paragraph that starts on
page N+1 of the current layout. No new attribute: page style, restart and break
already cross ODT and DOCX (Word sections). Texts in the five languages. **Verified**: `TitlePageTests`
(insertion of two pages with undo, conversion) and live: one line, *Title Page*, "OK"
→ an empty page with the *First Page* style and the text on the second.

### Folio, F6 — caret on the last line of a paragraph with a drop cap (done)
A paragraph shorter than the drop cap stretches its last line to cover all the drop cap's
lines, and caret, selection and wavy underline took that height: a caret three
lines tall. `ComposedLine` now carries `TextHeight` (the line's own height, only when the layout
height is greater) and `CaretHeight`; `LayoutQueries.Caret` and the drawing of the selection and
squiggles in `FolioCanvas` use `CaretHeight`. Tests in `CharacterEffectsTests`; live: «Breve
riga» (Short line) with a three-line drop cap, caret one line tall. Found during the test: in the **command
palette** clicking an entry only selected it (a double click was needed) and Enter after the click
did nothing, because focus had moved to the list. Now a click executes the entry and Enter works
from the list too (`CommandPaletteView`, shared by the three modules).

- **Drop cap and page break in DOCX**: the drop cap's framed paragraph was
  written *before* the paragraph carrying `pageBreakBefore`, so the break separated the
  drop cap from its text; the reference suite, reading back, left the frame's empty paragraph before
  the break **and** kept the break on the text: two breaks, one extra blank page.
  Now the break (page or column) goes on the frame's paragraph, the first in the flow, and the
  text does not repeat it. The test counts the breaks before the paragraph, also counting the empty
  paragraph the reference suite always leaves in place of the frame (tested with four variants of
  `w:framePr`: it leaves it in all of them, it is its importer), and wants exactly one.
- **Reference-suite round trips extended**: the sample of `tools/formatting-fixtures.sh` now also carries a

  page numbering from 3 (what the title page writes); both cross the six round trips

- **Consecutive checkboxes in form dialogs**: two checkboxes one below the other had the
  same spacing as two labeled fields (44-point step), and the dialog looked frayed.
  `FormPromptView` now brings consecutive checkboxes closer; it applies to all form and tabbed dialogs
  of the three modules. Seen live in the Character dialog.
- **Jumping command palette**: the dialog, centered, changed height at every letter
  typed according to how many results there were, and the search box moved under the caret (and
  under the click: a click aimed at one entry hit another). The list now has a fixed height, like

- **Side pane with a single page**: above the styles panel a single tab
  "Styles" appeared under the title "Styles". `SidePanelView` shows the tabs only when there is more than
  one page (applies to the three modules).
