### Folio F7 — Tables (done)
**Common parts** (`PulseOffice.Document.Tables`): `TableCellRange` (moved from Deck), `ITableSpans`
(algebra of merges and the rectangle enclosing merged cells), `IColumnWidths` (normalize, distribute,
resize a pair of columns, fit to content within a limit), `ITableSorter` (stable, up to
several keys, numeric or alphanumeric according to culture, empty cells last), formulas (`ITableFormulaParser`
with a node tree and a visitor; two writing dialects, `CanonicalFormulaSyntax` like Word —
`SUM(A1:A3)` — and `WriterFormulaSyntax` like ODF — `sum <A1:A3>`; the reader understands both, the prefixes
`ooow:`/`of:` and the list with `|`), `ITableStylePresets` (eleven styles with a canonical English name as in
the reference suite). Deck was restructured: `TableStructure` uses the common algebra, column sizes the
common normalization; it gained ascending and descending "Sort" and "Table styles".

**Why the model is not a single one.** Deck's cells are values of a `DataTableObject` (with
query, data snapshot, per-cell formats in coordinates); Folio's are containers of
blocks with paragraphs, lists and nested tables. Merging them would have given Deck rich text it cannot
display, or taken away Folio's rich cells; so everything that does not depend on the
cell content is shared.

**Model.** `TableCell` carries `Borders` (lines per side, `null` = the style's) and `Formula`
(canonical); `TableProperties` carries `HeaderColor` and `InnerLines`. `ITableAppearance` resolves the appearance of
a cell (own or style borders, own, header or band background, header ink and bold)
and is used by layout and by both writers. The `TableMemento` now captures everything
(spans, backgrounds, borders, formulas, heights, breaks, name, style, header).

**Layout.** Own borders are drawn side by side (`DecorationKind.CellEdge`, with dashed,
dotted and double); the style's header colors and bolds the text; bands start after
the header (before they counted from row zero). Tables cross pages, repeat
the header and respect rows that must not split (tests in `TableAppearanceLayoutTests`).
`ITableMeasure` measures the natural width and that of the longest word for "fit to content".

**Editing.** Separate services by responsibility: `ITableSelections`, `ITableCellEditing` (merge,
unmerge, split into rows or columns), `ITableGeometryEditing`, `ITableFormatting` (borders in six layouts,
background, alignment, header, break, name, default style created only once),
`ITableSorting`, `ITableFormulaEditing`, `ITableConversion` (text ↔ table with four separators,
split and join tables). In the editor: rectangle selection painted on the cells, widths draggable
on the right edge of cells (double-arrow cursor, preview line, nothing in read-only mode), Tab and
Shift+Tab between cells, formulas recalculated in the same transaction as typing (a single undo).

**Interface.** Forty-two table commands (thirty-five new) with titles in the five languages and icons; contextual "Table" ribbon
(rows and columns, merge, sizes, alignment, appearance, data) that appears only with the caret in a table
and now, as in Word, **after** the fixed tabs (applies to the three modules); Format › Table menu with
submenus; cell context menu extended. Dialogs: split cells, split table, rows and columns
to insert, height, width, three-key sort, formula, text to table, table to text,
three-tab properties. **Shared table style gallery** (`TableStyleGalleryView` in
`PulseOffice.UI.Controls.Tables`), with drawn previews and header and band options, wired into
Folio, Deck and Ledger (where it replaces the four fixed styles of before).

**Formats.** ODT: borders, fill and margins written resolved on each cell so that the reference suite sees them
(the table style stays in our attributes), with `pt:from-table-style` telling our reader
which values came from the style; header ink written on the texts and removed on
reading back; `table:formula` in the reference suite's dialect with `office:value`, and on reading also the field
`text:table-formula` that the reference suite produces when importing a DOCX. Columns written **without**
`style:rel-column-width`: with it the reference suite recalculated the widths wrongly (2000/3000/4000 twips
became 2000/2333/4667); `table:align` now `left`, because `margins` widened the table to the margins.
The `ooow` prefix is declared: without it, the reference suite read the formula as text (`ooow:ooow:sum …`). DOCX:
table style with `w:tblBorders`, margins, fill, first row (`firstRow`: fill, color,
bold) and bands (`band2Horz`), `w:tblLook`; own borders in `w:tcBorders` with the missing sides taken
from the style (as Word does); formulas as a `=…` field. Declared loss: `DOCX019` (Word always repeats
header rows). The six round trips (ODT, DOCX and four through the reference suite headless) are in
`TableRoundTripTests`, with the samples regenerated by `tools/table-fixtures.sh`.

**Final check of the areas touched.**
- *Undo and redo*: merge, widths, borders, style (in a transaction with the new style), sorting,
  formulas, conversions and splits are undone and redone in one step (tests in `TableFeatureTests` and
  `FolioTableCommandTests`).
- *Read-only*: table commands turn off, column dragging does not start, Tab does not
  add rows.
- *Dark theme*: gallery and dialogs seen live in dark; previews on white paper.
- *Translations*: five languages aligned; removed the seven `tableStyle.*` keys left orphaned in Ledger.
- *Performance*: a 3000-row table over 74 pages is laid out in about 320 ms and re-laid out after
  an edit in about 110 ms (`LargeTableTimingTests`); the table's layout key is now
  computed only once. A table is re-laid out in full: that is the point to improve if needed.
- *Found and fixed*: after insertion the caret stayed below the table (now in the first cell); the
  ribbon's style box showed an untranslated "Table Contents"; the contextual tabs sat
  among the fixed ones.

Word-processor survey: **199 out of 472 (42.2 %)**, with 26 new table commands. Still open: the
hand-drawn table (Word), cell protection , number format and recognition
in cells, "paste as nested table". **Next step**: F8 (objects and drawing).

### Folio F8 — Objects and drawing (done)
**Model.** `AnchoredObject` now carries the contour (`WrapContour` and `Contour`, polygon normalized on the
box), wrap of the first paragraph only (`WrapFirstParagraph`) and mirroring
(`FlipHorizontal`, `FlipVertical`, used for images; shapes and vector graphics are mirrored in the
content). `CopyAs`, `Assign` and `SameState` gather the copy of all properties: the objects'
memento saved only anchor, position, size and rotation (undoing a wrap or
order change did not go back), and paste lost the wrap distances. New services in the
model: `IFrameChains` (chain by name or identifier, head, tail, linkability: the target
frame must be empty and free, no cycles), `IObjectArrangement` (anchor with the marks in the
text, order), `ISequenceFields` (renumbers sequence fields in document order, frames
included, after deletions, paste, removal of objects), `ICaptions` (captions per category with
the same-named style child of "Caption", created on first use in a single transaction; for an anchored
object, as in the reference suite, a frame containing the object as character and the caption, with the object's position and
wrap), `IFrameLinking`.

**Layout.** `IObjectOutlines` derives the contour (from the model or, for ellipse, triangle and rhombus,
from the shape) rotated and mirrored; `WrapSegments` cuts the line on the polygon's extent in the line's
band, with the distances. First-paragraph-only acts as "no wrap" for the other paragraphs.
Linked frames: the head's content is composed with `ComposeFrom` frame by frame, with each one's
width and restarting from the line and offset where the previous one stopped (lines are
recomposed at the new width); only the last one grows. Images as character inside frames
were not drawn: now the frames' lines produce their object boxes. The drawing
and printing surfaces receive the transformation with the mirroring.

**Interface.** Contextual "Object" tab (anchoring, wrap, arrange, rotate and flip, text,
image, properties), Format › Object menu with Anchoring, Wrap and Frames, Arrange, Image and
Filters, object context menu. Three-tab properties dialog (position and size with
anchor and references, wrap with contour and distances, options with name and alternative text),
caption, name, link. Insertions: text frame, shapes with the shared gallery and six
families, line, chart, formula with the formula editor, Fontwork, QR, audio and video, object from
file, gallery, twenty-one form controls. Images: filters are applied to the pixels as in the reference suite
(so there is no loss in the formats; grayscale stays a color mode), crop, replace,
compress, save, color, color replacement, map, external edit, resolution check.
Typing with a frame selected types inside the frame (with another object it no longer types into the
body), double click enters the frame.

**Shared components** (rule 10), born or extracted here and used in the three modules: `IContentFlipping`
(Deck, Ledger, Folio), `IEmbeddedChartPrompt` (Deck, Folio), `IFormulaPrompt` with `FormulaEditorTexts`
moved to `PulseOffice.Formulas.Editor` (Ledger, Folio), `IPackagedFilePrompt` (Deck, Ledger, Folio),
`IRasterImageOperations` (Deck, Folio), `IImageContourTracer`.

**Formats.** ODT: `style:wrap-contour` with `draw:contour-polygon` (only for embedded objects and not as
character: with the contour on an image as character the reference suite did not draw it),
`style:number-wrapped-paragraphs`, `style:mirror`, `text:sequence` with the formula and the
`text:sequence-decls`; on reading also the frames' `draw:transform` and horizontal mirroring with
180° rotation brought back to vertical. **Found with the reference suite**: a frame without a parent style
is read as a drawing shape (and with the contour on a text frame the reference suite closes); now
every frame has a parent ("Graphics" if the style is implicit, marked with `pt:implied-style`). The reference suite's
text boxes imported from DOCX (custom shapes with text and chain in the style)
are read back as frames; the reference suite's shape names are no longer lost. DOCX: `wp:wrapTight` with
`wp:wrapPolygon`, `flipH`/`flipV`, title of `wp:docPr`, linked boxes with `wps:txbx id` and
`wps:linkedTxbx`, `SEQ … \* ARABIC` (without the format the reference suite lost the sequence name).
Declared `DOCX020` (Word has no first-paragraph-only wrap). Behaviors of
the reference suite, not ours: it does not keep the contour polygon coming from DOCX, it does not export the vertical
mirroring of an image to DOCX, it writes the sequence name in DOCX translated
(«Figura»), the chain of boxes imported from DOCX does not reach the ODT. The six round trips are in
`ObjectRoundTripTests` with the samples of `tools/object-fixtures.sh`.

**Verified live**: opening an ODT with contour, first paragraph only, caption and linked
frames; contextual "Object" tab; properties dialog (width and contour changed, a single
undo); context menu; caption on an anchored image (frame created, «Figura 1» (Figure 1), the next one
renumbered to 2), save read back by the reference suite with the same sequences; shape from the gallery with
text wrapping around; text typed in the frame flowing into the linked one; dark theme. Preferences and recent
documents restored to the initial state.

**Final check of the areas touched.**
- *Undo and redo*: anchor, wrap, contour, order, rotation, mirroring, properties (one
  transaction), caption, link are undone in one step (`ObjectEditingTests`,
  `FolioObjectCommandTests`). **Found**: Folio's undo and redo descriptions appeared as
  technical keys ("Undone: change-object"); now they are translated in the five languages.
- *Read-only*: object commands turn off.
- *Dark theme*: tab and dialogs seen live.
- *Translations*: five languages; caption style names translated too; the shape gallery
  text no longer says "in the sheet".
- *Performance*: five hundred objects with contour on 128 pages are laid out in about 120 ms and
  re-laid out after a text edit in about 13 ms (`ManyObjectsTimingTests`).

Word-processor survey: **285 out of 472 (60.4 %)**, 86 new commands. Still open: manual editing of the
contour, object grouping, freehand drawing, control and form properties (with
Folio's macros), "Insert frame interactively". **Next step**: F9 (fields, references and
indexes).

### Folio F9 — Fields, references and indexes (done)

**Fields.** `TextRun` carries a `FieldDetail` (format, value if true and if false, fixed, stored
value); new types: set variable, conditional text, hidden text, note reference,
citation, counts of tables, images and objects, custom property. Updating
(`IFieldUpdater`) walks the document in reading order (body with frames, then notes and
headers) and asks a strategy per type for the value (`IFieldValueSource`); variables are
set and read in order, conditions are evaluated by `FieldCondition` (comparisons with `==`, `EQ`,
`<>`…, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, `ooow:` prefixes), sequences are one of the strategies (`SequenceFields` was
rewritten on top of updating instead of having its own path). Rewriting the runs moves the
marks and records the text edits, so caret and positions follow a field that grows longer.
References find bookmarks and numbered captions (the reference name lives in the sequence, like
`text:ref-name` in ODF); references to headings place a `__RefHeading__…` bookmark. Pages
come from the layout (`IFieldLayoutFacts`, built by `FieldLayoutFactsFactory` with page,
list label and note citation), and "Update all" repeats up to three times until nothing
changes, in a single transaction.

**Indexes.** Sections with `IndexDefinition` (table of contents, alphabetical, figures, tables, bibliography,
user-defined), generated by `IIndexComposer` with one entry source per type and protected from writing
(`IGeneratedRegions`: no typing, deleting, line breaks or pasting inside an index). New styles:
index headings, "Contents 1–10", "Index 1–3" and separator, figures, tables, bibliography,
user-defined, "Index Link"; numbered names are translated with a `.level` key. Bibliographic database
in the document (`BibliographyCollection`), with the reference suite's twenty-nine fields and twenty-two types.

**Navigation.** `IDocumentNavigation` lists headings, tables, frames, images, objects,
bookmarks, sections, hyperlinks, references, indexes, comments, fields, footnotes and endnotes, and
resolves internal links (`#name`, `#text|outline`, `|table`, `|frame`, `|region`).
`IChapterMoving` moves a chapter with its subchapters (before another, up, down) and changes its
level. **Shared component**: `NavigatorPanel` in `PulseOffice.UI.Controls.Navigation`, with one source
per module gathered by `ModuleNavigatorSource` (like styles); sources for Folio (F5), Deck
(slides and named objects, Ctrl+Shift+F5) and Ledger (sheets, names, objects, comments, F5): the old
window navigators of Deck and Ledger were removed. Jump with double click or Enter, filter, context-sensitive
Up/Down/Promote/Demote buttons, dragging.

**Interface.** `FolioFieldCommands` (more fields Ctrl+F2 with per-type dialogs, edit field,
update fields F9, selected field, all Ctrl+Shift+F9, convert to text, cross-reference, special note,
edit note, two-tab note settings, open and remove hyperlink) and
`FolioIndexCommands` (table of contents, index with tabbed dialog, edit, update, delete, update
all, index entry with key, citation, bibliographic database, field shading Ctrl+F8, navigator).
"References" tab with the groups Table of Contents, Notes, Captions, Index, Citations, Update; menus
Insert › Table of Contents and Index, Edit › Fields and References, Tools › Update and References. Texts
in the five languages, icons.

**Formats.** ODT: field table rewritten on whole runs (`OdtFieldTable.Build(run, …)`),
`variable-decls` for set variables (no longer confused with user fields), `sequence-ref` to the
`ref-name` of captions, `note-ref` with the class, `bibliography-mark` with all fields, fixed date
with `date-value`; indexes with source, entry templates, title in `index-title`. DOCX: field
instructions with switches and quotes (`\@` also attached), `IF` with the condition translated (`=`/`<>`),
`SET` with the same-named bookmark and reading with `REF` (as Word does), `NOTEREF` to a bookmark
`_RefNote_…` placed on the note, `PAGEREF`, `REF \r`/`\p`, `STYLEREF`, `DOCPROPERTY`, `CITATION` with the sources
in `customXml` (`b:Sources`), locked fields (`fldLock`) read also from complex fields, fields with an
empty result no longer lost; indexes as `TOC`/`INDEX`/`BIBLIOGRAPHY` fields over several paragraphs, with the
title before the field and the `docPartObj` containers. Declared losses: `DOCX021` conditional hidden
text, `DOCX022` counts of paragraphs, tables, images, objects, `DOCX023` references by
chapter, caption or value, `DOCX024` bibliographic types and fields without a match, `DOCX025`
index settings without a switch. **Behaviors of the reference suite, not ours**, observed in the
round trips: it writes the sequence name in DOCX translated («Figura»); importing a Word `IF` it writes
`conto FORMULA 5`; it does not carry bibliographic sources from ODT to DOCX nor from DOCX to ODT; it does not import `NOTEREF`
(it leaves it as an unknown field); importing the bibliographic index from DOCX it loses the title; it exports the
read variable as `REF "conto"`; it rewrites the fixed date in its short format. The six round trips are in
`ReferenceRoundTripTests` with `tools/reference-fixtures.sh`.

**Verified live**: opening an ODT passed through the reference suite with table of contents, fields, notes, indexes and
bibliography; "References" tab; "Update all" (reference «sopra» (above) translated, letter «G»
in the alphabetical index); reference to a heading from the two-step dialog, undone and redone with
a single command; save read back by the reference suite headless (text and `bookmark-ref` present);
navigator in Folio and in Deck (new slides, Up, dragging), dark theme. Preferences and recent
documents restored to the initial state.

Word-processor survey: **301 out of 472 (63.8 %)**, sixteen new commands.

### Audit after F9 (done)

- **An edit to an object re-laid out the whole document**: the signature of the page frames
  contained every object, so moving one was enough to empty the caches and redo everything. Objects
  anchored to a body paragraph and not linked are already in the anchoring paragraph's key:
  now the signature keeps only page, header and footer, and chained ones. On 128 pages with 500
  objects editing an object goes from about 126 to 18 ms, with a result identical to complete
  layout (`ManyObjectsTimingTests`).
- **The navigator did not follow Deck's edits**: new slides did not appear. Now
  `ModuleNavigatorSource` follows the active document's history (with a 300 ms delay) for all
  three modules.
- **Navigator panel**: untranslated title (`panel.navigator.title`), fourteen category
  buttons that took up half the panel — now a drop-down list.
- **Shift key "stuck" with `uiprobe`**: it does not reproduce. A probe on the modifier state
  (`CGEventSource.flagsState`) shows that the warm-up of `keys` (Shift down and up) leaves nothing
  in the HID state; live, after `keys`, `click --mods shift` and `keys --mods shift`, arrows and clicks do not
  extend the selection. It is not the application's; if it happens again, the first suspect is a key with
  modifiers sent without the matching release.
- **Round trips with the reference suite**: formatting, table and object samples regenerated with today's code;
  all tests pass.
- **Undo, read-only, translations**: updates, indexes, references, chapters and notes in one undo
  entry each; in read-only mode nothing is updated or moved (`FolioReferenceTests`); every new text
  in the five languages (the catalog tests check it).
- **Performance**: 51 pages with 150 chapters, 450 fields, 150 notes, table of contents and alphabetical index: "Update
  all" in 180 ms, typing at 2 ms per key.
- **Test limit**: the headless scene (`FolioScene`) does not return with documents over about
  thirty pages: without a viewport the canvas draws all pages and the caret blink keeps
  the dispatcher busy. In the real application it does not happen (tested with a 50-page document); the
  tests on long documents use a `FolioEditor` without a view.

### Folio F10 — Review (done)

**Revisions.** The model existed since block F4 (`TrackedChangeLog`, `ChangeMark`, the formats), everything
else was missing. Folio's editor is now a **decorator**: `TrackingDocumentEditor` implements
`IDocumentEditor` on top of `IDirectDocumentEditor` (the old `DocumentEditor`) and, with recording
on, goes through `ITrackedEditing`. Choices:
- recorded deletion **removes** the text and keeps it in the `Deletion` (as in ODF): the caret
  does not stumble on deleted text, and rejecting means pasting the fragment again (`IFragmentPaster`);
- typing in one's own insertion does not create new ones (the end mark flows with the text); in
  another author's the end is pulled back and a new insertion is born; two insertions of the
  same author that touch become one (also across Enter);
- repeated Backspace and Delete merge into a single deletion; deleting inside an insertion
  really removes the text and, if the insertion becomes empty, removes it from the log;
- character formatting keeps the previous runs (`FormatChange`), paragraph formatting the previous
  paragraph (`ParagraphFormatChange`, with `PreviousKnown` false when it comes from ODT, which does not keep it);
- accept, reject and "reject while recording" (`RevisionVerdict.Reinstate`: a rejected insertion becomes
  a deletion by the current author, a deletion a reinsertion) work from the end towards
  the start, in a single transaction.
`IChangeRegions` gives the regions in reading order; `IDocumentComparison` compares by paragraphs and then
by words (common subsequence with prefix and suffix removed and a cap beyond which a stretch is
considered replaced as a block): **compare** marks the differences in the current document without
changing its text, **merge** applies the other document's differences as revisions by its author.
Revision signature from `IRevisionAuthor` (system user).

**On screen.** `ChangeMarkup` (layout) underlines insertions and bolds format
changes in the author's color; deletions are inline insets struck through, **one word per inset**
so they wrap (the line typesetter now breaks after a deletion inset). The per-paragraph regions
(`IChangeSpans`) are valid for one **document revision**: `TextDocument.Revision` grows at
every edit. Before they were invalidated on `Changed`, but the editor recomputes the layout in the same
event and, subscribed earlier, redid it with the old regions: live the last typed character stayed
without color. Margin bars (`IFolioChangeBars`) on screen and in print.

**Comments.** `ICommentEditing` (reply, edit, resolve the thread, delete with replies, bring a
reply to the top) and `ICommentAnchors`. Margin balloons (`FolioCommentMargin`): the desk reserves 190 points
to the right of the page when there are visible comments, balloons go down without overlapping, a
dashed line to the text (solid for the comment at the caret), commented text highlighted, resolved ones
faded and hideable. Balloons and ranges are computed once per revision and per page. Printing
comments **at the end of the document** (pages added by `FolioCommentSheet`), optionally from the File menu.

**Shared review panel** (`PulseOffice.UI.Controls.Review`, rule 10): two segmented tabs,
filter by author and by text, cards colored by author, accept, reject, all (according to the filter),
resolve, delete, delete by author, reply at the bottom (Ctrl+Enter). One source per module
(`ModuleReviewSource` in the shell, which in **read-only** mode blocks everything from a single point): Folio, Ledger
(cell changes and comments; accept and reject now go through `ILedgerChangeResolution`, which has
taken the code of the old "Manage changes" dialog, now replaced by the panel) and Deck
(slide comments, undoable deletion).

**Proofing.** `FolioProofing` checks **per run language** (`IFolioLanguages`, from the runs' effective
language, «zxx» = do not check) and adds **grammar**: our own rules in
`PulseOffice.Text.Spelling` (`RepeatedWordRule`, `DoubleSpaceRule`, `SpaceBeforePunctuationRule` which in
French leaves the space before `; : ! ?`, `SentenceStartRule`), blue squiggles. Shared check dialog
`ISpellingPrompt` (suggestions, free text, replace, always replace, ignore, always
ignore, add): Ledger and Deck now use it instead of their own forms. Language for selection,
paragraph and all text; thesaurus. Word count with selection already existed.

**Protection.** `IEditGuard` replaces the bare check of generated regions: protected sections, document
in read-only mode, comments only (one can comment but not write), tracked changes only (recording
cannot be turned off), forms only. Passwords with `IProtectionKeys`: for sections and
recording SHA-256 in UTF-8 as the reference suite writes, and on reading also SHA-1 in the three variants that
the reference suite accepts; for Word the salted and iterated hash of `w:documentProtection`.

**Formats.** ODT: an absent `text:track-changes` means **true** (ODF says so and it is what the reference suite does: we
read it as false), section key (`text:protection-key` with the algorithm), document protection
as settings (`LoadReadonly` and `ProtectForm` where the reference suite has them, `PulseDocumentRestriction` and the
key otherwise: `ODT005`). DOCX: an insertion crossing several paragraphs was written only in the
paragraphs with the marks (those in between and the paragraph end were lost); now it is carried from one paragraph
to the next and the **inserted paragraph end** is written and read in `w:pPr/w:rPr/w:ins`; `commentsIds`;
`w:documentProtection` in writing and reading. Declared losses: `DOCX026` (non-Word password),
`DOCX027` (comments on changes).

**Checks.** New tests: `RevisionTests` (16), `ChangeMarkupTests`, `GrammarTests`,
`ReviewParityTests` (ODT and DOCX equal; Word and section keys), `ReviewRoundTripTests` (four round trips with
a recent version of the reference suite headless, own profile, `tools/review-fixtures.sh`), `FolioReviewTests` (recording
while typing, panel, undo, thread and balloons, protected sections and read-only, language per run, printing
comments, performance). **Reference suite**: comments with replies and resolved, insertion, deletion and
format pass all four round trips; two limits of its own: from our DOCX it loses the inserted paragraph end
when the same paragraph also has a paragraph change (`w:pPrChange`), and in ODT it does not write
paragraph format changes. **Live**: recording with Ctrl+Shift+C, colored insertion with
bar, struck-through deletion, panel with reject, comment with balloon, reply and resolved from the panel,
spell check (replacement), dark theme (fixed the resolved balloon, unreadable on the dark
desk). Preferences restored to the initial state. **Performance**: 300 paragraphs with 600 revisions and 300
comments, 13 ms per key and about 11 ms more drawing per page.

Word-processor survey: **336 out of 472 (71.2 %)**, thirty-five new commands.

## F11 — Printing and export (2026-10-13)

**PDF with embedded fonts.** `PdfFontSet` replaces the fourteen standard fonts: for each font
it looks for the requested face (`IPdfFaceLocator`: in the app Folio's via Avalonia, then the index of installed
fonts `IndexedFontLocator`, which reads only the names and loads files on demand) and then a list of fallbacks
(`PdfFallbackFonts`). TrueType subset with renumbered glyphs and closed composites (`TrueTypeSubsetter`),
CIDFontType2 with Identity-H, `W` widths, `CIDToGIDMap /Identity` and `ToUnicode` CMap; whole OpenType CFF as
FontFile3/OpenType; fsType: embedding forbidden or bitmap only → `PDF010` and another font, no subsetting
→ whole font. Synthetic bold and italic when the family does not have them. Applies to Ledger and Deck (same
writer). `IFontFileLocator` moved from Documents.Layout to Typography. Options (`PdfExportOptions`, formerly
`PdfMetadata`): pages, bookmarks (from headings in Folio, from slide titles in Deck), hyperlinks,
notes from comments, keywords, language, PDF/A-2b with XMP, generated sRGB profile and `/ID`.
Checks: `PdfEmbeddedFontTests` with a test reader (Italian, German, Greek, Cyrillic, CJK with fallback to
Arial Unicode, extracted text equal to the original, subset less than a quarter of the font, 300 pages in
less than a second), PDFKit extracts and draws the text, the reference suite headless imports it with the right fonts.
Limits: no complex shaping (ligatures, Indic scripts, joined Arabic); color emoji without outlines
→ `?` declared; PDF/A not validated with veraPDF.

**Printing.** Shared preview (`PrintPagesView`, one/two/more pages, book, zoom, keyboard and wheel) with
Print button. New print dialog with a preview of the imposed sheet; `PrintImposition` (Printing,
shared by the three modules) does range, even/odd, reverse order, pages per sheet with orientation chosen
for the best scale, booklet, copies and collation when the service cannot do them, graphics filter and
black text. Print to PDF file. `IPrintService.Capabilities`; CUPS with `collate` and short/long edge; Windows with
`printto`, not tested. Live: Folio's print dialog and preview with mixed text (cancelled, no
job sent to the printer).

**Exports.** HTML restructured: `HtmlPageRenderer` with variant (HTML5 or XHTML) and image
destination; `XhtmlDocumentWriter`; `EpubDocumentWriter` (uncompressed mimetype first, OPF 3, nav and NCX from headings,
images as files, styles, metadata, fidelity entries `EPUB2xx`); export-only formats kept out of Save
As. Commands `shell.file.exportPdf(Direct)`, `folio.file.exportEpub(Direct)`, `folio.file.exportXhtml`; Ledger and
Deck use the same PDF options dialog. Folio now has `RenderHtml` (web preview, sending). EPUB not
validated with epubcheck (not installed).

**Mail merge.** `TextFieldKind.Database`; ODT `text:database-display` with database and table name,
source in the settings (`CurrentDatabase*` as the reference suite does, plus `PulseMergeConnection`); DOCX `MERGEFIELD`,
source declared lost (`DOCX028`). The reference suite reads the fields back from our ODT and DOCX and rewrites them with
the source. Engine `MailMergeEngine` (records and single document with page break), record preview,
commands in Tools → Mail Merge; results: single document, ODT/DOCX/PDF file per record, single PDF. Mail
is not sent (forbidden): document and files are prepared.

Word-processor survey: **347 out of 472 (73.5 %)**.

## F12 — Finishing touches and API (2026-10-13)

**Macros.** `FolioScripting` and `FolioMacros`: `doc` object for JavaScript and Python with paragraphs, styles,
tables, fields and controls; each run is a single undo step (`history.macro.run`). Properties and
events of form controls; clicks on controls outside design mode (`IFormDesignMode`, shared).

**Templates and master documents.** `.ott` and `.dotx` templates in the shared management (`OfficeTemplateExtension`);
`OdtFlavour` Text/Template/Master, `.odm` with `text:global`; `ISubdocuments` (insert, update, unlink)
with `IFragmentAdoption` extracted from `FragmentPaster`; package-relative links
(`LinkedFiles.ToPackageHref/FromPackageHref`). In DOCX subdocuments become normal sections: `DOCX029`.

**Autocorrection.** Rule-based `IParagraphAutoFormat` (bulleted and numbered lists, borders from `---`/`===`),
`IDocumentAutoFormat` (apply, also with tracked revisions), `IWordCompletion`, `IFolioTypingAssist`;
options in the profile, `shell.tools.autocorrectWhileTyping`. Enter on an empty list item ends the list.

**View.** `IFolioViewLayout`: Desk Single/Multiple/Book, web view (`IContinuousLayout`), draft, full screen
(`shell.view.fullScreen`, renamed from `ledger.view.fullScreen`), `RulerStrip` rulers in
`UI.Controls/Rulers` (draggable margins, indents, tab stops), formatting marks, boundaries, images,
grid with snapping, guides, baseline grid, space between pages, field names,
style and direct formatting highlighting, hidden paragraphs (`DOCX034`). Block selection
(ranges per line, copy/cut/delete in one step) and direct cursor (`IDirectCursor`: empty lines up to the
clicked point and indent, a single undo step).

**Remaining commands.** Paste special and unformatted, nested table, rows and columns pasted before,
breaks, go to page, HTML, data sources, citations, repaginate, calculate, outline to clipboard and
to Deck (`IOutlinePresentation`), auto-summary, horizontal line, scanner; Chinese and
Hangul conversion, redaction, manual hyphenation; area, line, fontwork, signature line (shared
`ISignatureLinePrompt`); protected table cells and cells with number format (`DOCX030`, `DOCX031`); line numbering
(`DOCX032`); protected fields and bookmarks (`DOCX033`); sorting; accessibility with monitor; glossary;
envelope; freehand drawing (`FreeformSketch` shared with Ledger); groups (`draw:g`); document theme (palettes
in `Document/Themes`, shared with Ledger); comment format; manual contour (`ContourEditorView` in
UI.Controls); index entry; page numbers; ruby (`text:ruby`, `w:ruby`). Round trips with the reference suite headless for
every format touched.

**Defect found.** `settings.xml` did not declare `xmlns:ooo`: the reference suite ignored all our
settings, including font embedding in Ledger and Deck. Fixed in `OdfFontFaces`; samples
regenerated. Also the reference suite omits `text:number-lines` when it is true: the reader now assumes it.

**Open points.** Deck's rulers still its own (to be moved onto `RulerStrip`); signature lines not written in
ODT (`ODT001`); `InsertContentControl` partial; the web view prints with the print layout and shows
headers and footers.

Word-processor survey: **470 out of 471 wanted entries (99.8 %)**, 1 partial, 22 excluded.

**Defect found live at the end of F12.** The app did not start: registering `IConnectorFramer` for Folio made
the constructors of `DeckConnectors` ambiguous (one with `IConnectorFramer`, one with `IConnectorRouter`). Restructured:
`DeckConnectors` has only the constructor with `IConnectorFramer`, registered once in the Desktop
composition. No test composes the whole Desktop container: that is why it slipped through, and it is an open point.
Live check with uiprobe: rulers, block selection (drag over two lines, deletion) and direct
cursor (click below the text, typing at that point) in a new document, closed without saving.
## Closing the open points of F12 (2026-10-13)

**Startup test.** `PulseOffice.Desktop.Tests` composes the app's entire container with the same
`ServiceConfiguration` (now split into `Register` and `Build`) and builds it with `ValidateOnBuild` and
`ValidateScopes`, in production too: an ambiguous constructor or a missing dependency stop both the startup and the tests.
The test resolves every registered service, composes commands, menus, ribbon and context menu (`ShellComposition`,
extracted from `App`), opens the window in headless Avalonia and creates one document per module. User data is
isolated with `PULSEOFFICE_DATA_HOME` (a new variable of `UserDataPaths`: configuration and cache under a given
folder); platform services are already lazy and touch neither keychain, mail nor network until they are used.
Verified that it fails when the second constructor of `DeckConnectors` is reintroduced (uncommitted change).
Found and fixed by the test: `shell.tools.autocorrectWhileTyping` without a menu rule, and two dead rules
(`folio.tools.updateLinks`, `folio.tools.updateCharts`) already covered by `folio.tools.update*`.

**Block selection.** The column is the horizontal band `[x1, x2]` in points: for each line we take the
characters whose horizontal interval intersects it (`ILineOffsets.SpanBetween`, `ILayoutQueries.Block`),
as the reference suite does. Before, we searched for the nearest character line by line, and with proportional glyphs the column
wobbled. Tested with a proportional measurer (narrow `i`, wide `W`).

**Signature line in ODT and ODS.** As the reference suite does:
a `draw:frame` with the unsigned image (SVG generated by `OdfSignatureLineCodec`) and `loext:signatureline` with
`loext:id`, suggested signer (name, title, email), instructions, `show-sign-date`, `can-add-comment`; the applied signature
(`signed-by`, `signed-on`) in our own namespace `urn:pulseoffice:signature`. In ODT the frame must have
an automatic graphic style **without a parent**: that is the signal by which the reference suite imports it as a shape; with the
parent «Graphics» it imported it as an image frame and lost the signature line (tested). `ODT001` is
removed. In ODS the signature line used to disappear **silently** (neither written nor declared): now it crosses the
format. The model gains `SignerEmail`. Round trip with the reference suite headless: ODT and ODS written by us, rewritten by
the reference suite with `loext:signatureline` intact, read back by us with all fields. Deck has no signature line
(the reference suite's presentation program has none). In DOCX and XLSX it remains lost and declared (`DOCX002`, which now names it, and `XLSX016`).

**Web view.** The reference suite's word processor in web mode does not create headers or footers,
fits the page to the window with a small border instead of the margins and,
for printing, preview and PDF export, **leaves web mode and paginates normally**
(#i38289). We aligned with it: `PageFrames` does not compose headers and footers
when the view is continuous (web and draft, like the reference suite with hidden whitespace), and printing goes through
`IPrintLayouts`, which paginates the document with the continuous view suspended. Before, printing in web view used the
screen layout, that is a single page one million points tall. The same service serves mail merge and
the comments sheet, which would otherwise have inherited the web view of the open document.

**Deck rulers.** Deck uses the shared `RulerStrip`, at the edges of the view as in the reference suite: with a text
box being edited it shows the box's internal margins (draggable, vertically too), left, first-line and right
indent and the paragraph's tab stops (click to add, drag to move, drag off the ruler
to remove); with an object selected it highlights its extent. Pressing on the ruler outside editing
creates a guide line, as before (`SlideView.BeginGuide`; new event `RulerStrip.BlankPressed`). The old
ruler drawing inside `SlideView` is removed. So that indents and tab stops would have an effect: right
indent and tab stops in Deck's text composer (`TabLayout` in Text.Rich, pure and tested; lines with
tabs are composed in pieces), in ODP (`fo:margin-right`, `style:tab-stops` with `OdfTabStops`, extracted from the
ODT codec and shared) and in PPTX (`marR`, `a:tabLst`). Ledger: **no rulers**, by choice — the reference suite's spreadsheet has none
(not even when editing shapes), and the grid already has its own headers.

Live verification: app started, Deck with rulers, title edited, indent dragged (the text
moves and editing resumes), tab stop added with a click, guide line dragged from the ruler; Folio and
Ledger opened; exit without saving, preferences unchanged.

Residual open points: signature line in DOCX and XLSX (VML `o:signatureline`), partial `InsertContentControl`.

### Signature line in DOCX and XLSX (2026-10-13)
**DOCX**: `w:pict` with `v:shape` (type 75), `v:imagedata` related to the unsigned image and
`o:signatureline` (signer, title, email, instructions, date, comments), inline or floating with position and
wrapping (`DocxSignatureLineCodec`). **XLSX**: the line lives in the sheet's `vmlDrawing` with
`x:ClientData ObjectType="Pict"` and a cell anchor; a single VML writer (`XlsxVmlDocuments`, `XlsxVmlShapes`)
serves notes and signatures, which would otherwise have written two conflicting VML drawings. There is only one unsigned image,
`SignatureLineImage` in `PulseOffice.Formats`, shared with ODF; `VmlStyle` and `VmlSignatureLineCodec` are common
to DOCX and XLSX. Losses: `DOCX002` no longer names signature lines; `XLSX016` becomes informational and applies only to
lines that are already signed; new `DOCX042` (born as DOCX035, renumbered at the merge because the code was already taken) for the same case in Word (signer and date come from the digital signature).
Reference suite headless: our DOCX and XLSX become ODT and ODS with a complete `loext:signatureline`, and read back by us
come back whole; an XLSX **saved by the reference suite** instead carries the line as a plain image (a limit of its
exporter). Tests: `SignatureLineOoxmlTests`, parity in `XlsxOdsParityTests`, sample `signature-line.lo.docx`.
In the same merge: a shared «Trova e sostituisci» (Find and Replace) (`UI.Controls.Search.FindReplaceView` on
`IFindReplaceTarget`) in place of the two duplicate windows of Ledger and Deck.

### Folio, content controls (complete InsertContentControl) (2026-10-13)
Model: a control is a pair of inline markers (`ContentControlMark`) with the properties on the start
marker — type (rich text, plain text, check box, drop-down list, combo box, date, picture),
title, tag, placeholder, lock of the control and/or the content, text/value items, check box symbols, date format
and language. Services in `Documents/Controls`: catalog, editing, lock guard, lock tokens,
marker order. Formats: DOCX `w:sdt` inline and at paragraph level (`w:sdtBlock`, also in the body with
sections); ODT `loext:content-control` as the reference suite writes it (checked against its source,
without copying code) plus `pt:` attributes for what the reference suite lacks. Editor: ten commands
`folio.contentControl.*` from the menu and the bar, properties dialog with a veil, a click that toggles the check box and
opens the list, date and picture pickers, grey placeholder replaced by typing, locks respected, read-only
mode. New shared components: `ChoiceItemsField` and `CalendarField` in `UI.Controls/Forms`.
Round trip with the reference suite headless in both directions, with the reference suite's files as evidence. Word-processor survey 471 of 471.
Losses: `DOCX043` (a control that starts or ends in the middle of different paragraphs), `DOCX044` (the placeholder of an
already filled control: Word keeps it in the glossary), `ODT006` (a control over several paragraphs becomes one per
paragraph), `DOCX108` on reading (controls around tables imported as content). At the merge these codes
had been born as `DOCX035`/`DOCX036`, already taken by the losses of the format audit: renumbered, and a test now forbids

written earlier read their form controls back as content controls (no migration).


### Final audit: closure (2026-10-13)
Merged into `main` the four work branches (formats and samples, code rules and theme, signature line,
content controls), with the diagnostic codes made unique and two new tests watching over that. Then the
typical path tested live in the three modules — new document, editing, formatting, saving in ODF and
in OOXML, reopening, PDF — with the reference suite headless re-reading every file and the app log free of exceptions.

**Defects found and fixed**
- *Folio*: a character without a glyph in the document's font (the ☐ box of a control) made the
  whole run draw with the fallback font and the widths of the right font: overlapping text. Now only the
  missing character falls back (`FaceGlyphMapping` in pieces).
- *Ledger*: formulas written in Italian gave `#NAME?` (`=SOMMA(A1:A2)`): the function vocabulary
  existed but was not connected to the cell. `IFormulaLocalization` converts between the interface language and canonical
  form on writing and on editing; the lexer accepts the decimal comma where it is used (`=SOMMA(1;2,5)` → 3,5).
- *Deck*: Esc in a box being edited **discarded** the typed text (lost, for example, the text typed after
  a tab stop added from the ruler). Now Esc keeps it, as in the reference suite and PowerPoint; Enter and F2 open
  editing of the selected box. Transition directions in the panel were in English: translated.
- *Deck, «Elimina oggetto» (Delete object) in the history*: the origin was the test tool `uiprobe/keys`, which before every
  text sent «a» and Backspace; with an object selected the Backspace deleted it. Now the warm-up is
  requested with `--prime`. In addition, editing keys without modifiers (Delete, Backspace, arrows, Enter…) reach the
  document's commands only from its surface (`IDocumentKeyScope`, `IDocumentSurface` on `SlideView`,
  `SheetGridView` and Folio's text surface): with focus on a panel or a field they no longer act on the
  selection, in the three modules.
- *Three modules*: the name proposed for PDF, sending and printing differed per module (Ledger the sheet name, Deck the
  title of the first slide or «Deck» in English): now the document name everywhere.
- *Ledger and Deck in read-only mode*: Ledger's object alignment, distribution and ordering were not disabled;
  a composition test now watches over the modifying commands in the three modules. Ctrl+Shift+V is «Incolla
  speciale» (Paste Special) in Ledger too, «Incolla solo valori» (Paste Values Only) moves to Ctrl+Alt+Shift+V.
- *Code*: static `UserDataPaths` became injected `IUserDataPaths`, the configuration stores receive the
  path from the composition; Deck on the shared zoom ladder `IZoomLadder`.
- *PPTX*: a slide without its own background wrote the resolved master color into `p:bg` and stopped
  following it; now it inherits. Master and layout Ids tested as unique and above 2^31.
- *Translations and appearance*: «OpenDocument Master Document» in English in the save dialog; calendar of the
  date controls with grey backgrounds from the default theme; «Aggiungi voce» (Add item) of the row lists larger than the
  other fields.
- *Tests*: two Folio performance measurements sensitive to load (median instead of mean).

**Verifications**: build without warnings, all tests green; live on macOS the three modules in light and dark theme, the
content controls (check box, list, date) inserted, toggled and chosen, Deck's tab aligned to the
tab stop added from the ruler, Delete with focus on the transitions panel having no effect on the slide;
preferences, recent documents and theme restored to the starting state.

**Observed, not reproduced**: once the app closed with ⌘Q without asking to save a modified sheet
(recovery then offered it at startup); later tests always showed the prompt.
**Evaluated and not done**: `ChoiceItemsField` (text/value pairs) for the form controls of Deck and Ledger — their
items are plain strings in the model (`FormControlProperties.Items`), and there `ListField` is the right component.

**Still open**: verifications on real Windows and Linux and in Word, Excel and PowerPoint (this machine is a Mac);
high PPTX allocations on writing; property audit of the shared codecs.


### Open points closable on a Mac (2026-10-13)
Six points, one per commit.

**⌘Q without a prompt on a modified sheet.** Reproduced live: you type in a cell, move to the formula
bar (or type directly there) and press ⌘Q: the app closed without asking. Cause: the pending text
in the formula bar is not a change until it is confirmed, and `LedgerView.CommitPendingEdits`
confirmed only the cell editor; when focus moves to the bar, `TakeOverEditor` moves the text there and
closes the editor, so the guard saw an untouched document. Now it confirms the bar too. In addition the exit
prompt is in `QuitCoordinator` (Shell), the same for closing the window and for the system's `ShutdownRequested`:
if the change check fails, the exit stops instead of going through. A headless test
(Desktop.Tests) repeats the case and fails without the fix; live the prompt appears in the three cases tested
(text in the bar, text in the cell, modified document). The recovery offered at startup on the reported occasion
is not explained by this defect (with a regular exit `Exit` discards the snapshots): in the logs that session
lacks the «Shutting down» line, so the process was terminated from outside.

**PPTX, allocations on writing.** Measured with `tools/format-bench`, which now counts the writing alone and with
`ALLOC=1` samples allocations by type (`GCAllocationTick`): 190 KB per slide before, 135 after (ODP 60).
The causes: a new `OoxmlObjectNameMapper` for every object, with its regular expression compiled each time
(5.5 MB of `RegexNode` over 400 slides); the slide list copied at every slide to know the
number (O(n²)); parts saved by hand and then again by the SDK on closing. The rest (about 40 KB per
slide in `byte[]`) are the buffers of the SDK's ZIP package, one part per slide and one for the notes.

**Audit of codec properties, by reflection.** `ModelPropertyProbe` (test) walks every public
property of a model, nested ones too, builds for each a variant with a different value (every value
of the enums), writes it and reads it back; `CodecPropertyAudit` demands the same value or a new code in
`CheckFidelity`. Watched: cell style (ODS and XLSX), default and sample number formats, character and
paragraph properties (ODT and DOCX), shape style (ODP and PPTX). A property added tomorrow enters the
audit by itself. Silent losses found and fixed: medium and thick borders read as thin in ODS; «fill»
alignment lost in ODS (`style:repeat-content`); XLSX border width always 1 pt on reading (now that of the
pen of that style); engineering notation (`##0.0E+0`) lost in ODS and ignored by the formatter
(`number:exponent-interval`); in ODP dashes other than the plain dash, hatch background, multi-color gradients
(`loext:gradient-stop`), arrow scale and bevel type (`urn:pulseoffice:shape`); in PPTX the bevelled
join (the SDK calls the outline's `a:bevel` `LineJoinBevel`) and the arrow size. Format losses,
now declared: DOCX109 (border-to-text distance in whole points), DOCX110-112, PPTX029-031, XLSX054-056 (ellipsoidal
and square gradients and gradient border, hatch angle and spacing, arrow scales outside small,
medium, large in DrawingML). Accepted equivalences, written into the test: proportional line spacing read from DOCX
as `LineHeight` instead of `LineSpacing` (same result in pagination), the page style of the first
paragraph which in DOCX becomes the document's initial style, hexadecimal colors in lowercase. The reference suite
headless reads back the ODS with engineering notation, «fill» and thick borders.

**Signature line, PNG beside the SVG.** `IVectorRasterizer` in the formats, with `NoVectorRasterizer` as a
fallback; `SkiaVectorRasterizer` (SkiaSharp 3.119.4, the same as Avalonia, and Svg.Skia 5.1.1) in the new
`PulseOffice.Formats.Rasterizing`, without Avalonia; the architecture test forbids SkiaSharp and Svg to the format
projects, which receive it only through `SignatureLineImage`. In the VML of DOCX and XLSX the displayed image is the
PNG (Office does not read SVG in VML) and the SVG stays in the package as a linked part; in ODT and ODS the frame has
the SVG and, after it, the fallback PNG, as the reference suite writes it. The PNG is at 192 dpi. Content tests: the PNG
decodes, has the expected width and drawn lines. The reference suite headless shows the DOCX signature.

**Avalonia 12 developer tools.** `Avalonia.Diagnostics` stops at 11; for 12 there is
`AvaloniaUI.DiagnosticsSupport` (2.2.3, free on NuGet, declares support for versions 11 and 12), which acts
as a bridge to the external application AvaloniaUI Developer Tools. Referenced only in Debug builds from the csproj;
the hook is `IDeveloperTools`, with two implementations of which the csproj compiles the one for the configuration
(no `#if`), called at startup in `Program` (not in `App`, which the headless tests create several times).
F12 opens the tools if the external application is present: it is not installed here and asks for an Avalonia account.

**CPython via pythonnet.** `CPythonScriptEngine` behind `IScriptEngine`; the «Motore Python» (Python engine) setting (already
present, with restart) chooses which of the two Python engines the composition registers. It looks for the app's standalone
Python, then the system one (`PythonDiscovery`); if there is none, it asks for consent with a modal (size,
origin, folder, and that CPython macros are not in the sandbox) and downloads from python-build-standalone the
`install_only` build for this machine, preferring 3.13, verified with `SHA256SUMS` and extracted into
`python-runtime` in the app's data folder; progress goes to the status bar. Sandbox: like IronPython,
CPython does not start without `AllowsUnsandboxedEngines` (only from the macro editor); the time cap is a
`sys.settrace` that every 512 events checks the cancellation token (pythonnet's `Interrupt` hung
on acquiring the GIL); it cannot stop code blocked in a native call nor limit memory; the
runtime starts once per process. Completion and keywords are now shared (`PythonLanguage`).
Tests: with the Homebrew Python 3.14 present on this machine (output, globals, errors with the line, syntax,
infinite loop stopped); refused consent does not download; choosing the build from a sample release
list. Real download tested once, from the app's code, into a temporary folder: 3.13.16, 25 MB,
checksum verified, macro executed; then deleted. Not yet: virtual environments and package installation.

**Still open**: verifications on real Windows and Linux and in Word, Excel and PowerPoint (the OOXML signature, the
signature line PNG, printing and mp4 on Windows); the OOXML signature in the reference suite's interface (forbidden here);
layouts of PPTX files exported by the reference suite (it is its exporter).

## PulseOffice signatures in the reference suite's interface (2026-10-13)

Live test in a recent version of the reference suite with its interface (throwaway profile), files signed by our
`DocumentSignatureService` with a self-signed certificate.

- ODT, ODS: «Almeno una firma ha problemi: non è stato possibile convalidare il certificato.» (At least one signature has problems: the certificate could not be validated.) — signature
  intact, certificate not trusted because self-signed (expected). Type XML-DSig.
- DOCX, XLSX, PPTX (after the fix): «Il certificato non può essere convalidato e il documento è
  firmato solo parzialmente.» (The certificate cannot be validated and the document is only partially signed.) — intact; the reference suite says «partially» of every OOXML signature, which by
  definition does not sign the metadata. Type XAdES. DOCX with two signatures: both listed and intact.
- DOCX altered after signing: «Questo documento possiede una firma non valida.» (This document has an invalid signature.) / «Le firme in questo
  documento non sono valide» (The signatures in this document are not valid) (expected).

**Defect found and fixed**: before the fix every signed DOCX showed as «invalid signature».
Digest and signature value were correct (recomputed by hand with xmllint and openssl), but the relationship
transform of xmlsec used by the reference suite keeps the whitespace-only nodes between the
`Relationship` elements, which the OPC specification and our transform discard: with an indented `.rels` the two
digests diverge. Now `OoxmlSignatureService`, on the first signature of a package, compacts the `.rels`
by removing the whitespace-only nodes (identical content); later signatures no longer touch them, so as not to
break existing ones. Tests: `LeRelazioniSiCompattanoPrimaDellaFirmaPerchéUnAltraSuiteContaGliSpazi`,
`LaSecondaFirmaNonRiscriveLeRelazioniGiàFirmate`. The signature in Word is still to be seen.

## Audit, cycle 1 — Ledger (2026-10-13)

Method: engine compared with the reference suite headless on its function corpus
(the external test corpus, converted and recalculated by `tools/calc-compare`), ODS/XLSX round trips on the
external test corpus's ods and xlsx files, performance measurements up to 1M cells. Every defect
fixed has a test that failed before (`LedgerAuditCycleOneTests` and format tests).

**Blocking (fixed)**: IF/CHOOSE propagated the error of the branch not taken; dynamic arrays
came back as #SPILL! after saving (now persisted in ODS and XLSX); a full recalculation
blocked spills; `A:A` and `1:1` gave #NAME?.

**Serious (fixed)**: OFFSET and INDIRECT (A1, R1C1, sheets, names); 1904 dates in XLSX; arity of
NORM.S.DIST and others; implicit intersection of legacy formulas; iterations (settings in the
document, command `ledger.calc.iterations`); wrong widening of references when deleting rows;
`transparent` background read as black; frozen panes not saved; CORREL and similar misaligned the
pairs; LINEST statistics; fake AMOR*, FOURIER, BAHTTEXT; empty results not rendered as 0;
the reference suite's tolerant equality; ROW/COLUMN created circular dependencies.

**Medium (fixed)**: text functions for wide characters and bytes, ASC/JIS, comparison rules
(case, wildcards, regex, whole cell), financial functions and rounding like the reference suite's math library,
EUROCONVERT, MULTINOMIAL, truncated degrees of freedom, localized error codes and `Err:` in ODS,
fractions in formats, children of shape groups lost, ODF042/043 and XLSX058/059 declared.

**Minor (fixed)**: TEXTBEFORE/TEXTAFTER, TEXTSPLIT, SEQUENCE, SHEETS, ERRORTYPE, HYPERLINK,
COLOR, CEILING.PRECISE and *.XCL, durations to 9 decimals.

**Open**: default capitalization in the reference suite's files; the `~` operator and 3D references;
CURRENT() sketched; FORECAST.ETS different from the reference suite; booleans in SUMPRODUCT; automatic
label recognition; reading in the document's language; ROW()/COLUMN() inside multi-cell array
formulas; INDEX over a range that contains itself seen as circular; REPLACEB at
half a character; CONCATENATE of a range; precision of the inverse distributions, of Bessel and
of complex numbers (IMCOT); GETPIVOTDATA on the reference suite's files; memory (~650 MB per 1M cells).
**Live editor not verified**: the PulseOffice window was not brought to the foreground,
so no click or key was sent; still to do (also with Avalonia.Headless tests).

Performance: 1M cells with 200k formulas, recalculation ~1.4 s; with 50 whole-column formulas ~6 s;
one edit ~1.6 s.

## Audit, cycle 2 — Deck (with the Ledger remainder)

**Method.** A run over the whole test corpus of the external test corpus (650 ODP, FODP,
PPTX, POTX, PPSX, PPTM files): reading, writing to ODP and PPTX, reading back and comparing slides,
objects, texts, notes, animations (class, preset, subtype, duration, delay, repetitions, path),
transitions, sections. No exceptions and no failed reads. Transitions and animations
also compared by counting the SMIL/OOXML nodes before and after, and by having the reference suite headless
(profile in /tmp) read back our PPTX of `AllTransitions.odp` next to the round trip made by the reference suite itself.
Performance: 600 slides with a 200 KB image each: ODP writes in 1.4 s and reads in 0.14 s,
PPTX in 1.7 s and 2.1 s (115 MB). Part 0 on Ledger with Avalonia.Headless tests in the composed desktop
(no live test: no keys sent to real windows).

**Serious (fixed)**
- Transitions: in ODP 41 of the reference suite's 76 transitions came back as fades on the first save.
  Now the transition carries the native identifier (`SlideTransition.Native`, valid as long as type and
  direction do not change) and a shared PowerPoint–reference suite table (`NativeTransitionTable`, derived from the
  reference suite's filter) translates them between the formats; declared losses ODP023 and PPTX033. On the round trip through
  PPTX we now match the reference suite on 58 transitions of 76, against 34 before.
- Animations: every effect was written as a fade (in the reference suite and PowerPoint a «fly in»
  entrance saved by us faded in). Now the effect's native node (`AnimationEffect.Native`)
  crosses its own format as long as the effect is not modified; the subtype (direction) is in the
  model and passes between formats with the reference suite's table (`AnimationSubtypeTable`).
- Presets: native names were lost between formats (the reference suite's preset names in PPTX, ooxml-N in ODP) and
  its newer vendor-prefixed ones in ODP too; table of the reference suite's 199 pairs (`NativeAnimationPresetTable`), PPTX032 for the newer vendor-prefixed ones only.
- PPTX: PowerPoint connectors (`p:cxnSp`) disappeared on opening; now they are connectors with the
  preset's path (straight, elbow, curved, flips).
- PPTX: an effect on a group disappeared (groups are flattened); now it animates every member.
- Ledger: after an internal copy, pasting text copied from another application pasted the old
  Ledger copy; without an internal copy pasting was disabled.

**Medium (fixed)**
- ODP: a movie's frame came back as an extra image at every reopening.
- ODP: animations on audio and video were lost (the media frame was not a target).
- ODP: wipe wrote non-existent SMIL subtypes (`rightToLeft`, `bottomToTop`); «uncover» was
  read back as «cover» because `smil:direction="reverse"` was not read.

**Minor (fixed)**: the headless desktop tests used two static Avalonia sessions and the
suite hung; now a single shared session (`HeadlessDesktopCollection`).

**Verifications on Ledger (part 0)**: typing in a cell and formulas, formulas in Italian saved in
canonical form (`SUM(A1,5)` in the XLSX), sorting, fill, undo and redo, merging, inserting
and deleting rows with shifted references, frozen panes, read-only, internal and tab-separated
copy/paste: all correct except the clipboard defect above.

**Open**
- Serious: an effect **created or modified** in Deck is still written as a fade (a library of
  behaviours per preset is missing); and across different formats the native node is not translated.
- Medium: the slide show shows as a fade the transitions that have no type of ours.
- Medium: in PPTX the left/right direction of cover and push is the opposite of what the reference suite
  reads back; we match the reference suite's export, which is not symmetric with its import:
  to be decided with a real PowerPoint.
- Not verified in this cycle: Deck editor (multiple selection, align, rulers, masters, dark
  theme), slide show and presenter view, PDF, image, mp4 and HTML exports, visual comparison of the
  rendering with the reference suite; in Ledger filters, find and replace, HTML paste, dark theme.
  **Resume**: these points open the next Deck round.

## Audit, cycle 2 bis — Deck (with the Ledger remainder)

**Method.** The open items of cycle 2, one by one. Animations: for every preset of the reference suite's effects definition
(302 preset–subtype pairs, entrance, emphasis, exit, paths) an effect created in Deck saved in
ODP and in PPTX, read back, and carried from one format to the other; the reference suite headless (profile in /tmp)
read back one ODP and one PPTX of ours with all the presets, comparing preset, subtype and behaviour nodes
slide by slide. Transitions: the reference suite's 89 transitions
(its transition definitions, including the OpenGL ones) measured frame by frame. Editor, slide show,
exports and Ledger with Avalonia.Headless tests in the composed desktop (no keys to real windows).
Rendering: twelve ODP files from the external test corpus exported to PNG by the reference suite and by us and compared.

**Serious (fixed)**
- Animations: an effect created or modified in Deck was saved as a fade. Now there is a
  library of behaviours per preset (`AnimationBehaviourLibrary`, data in
  `Resources/animation-behaviours.json` derived from the reference suite's effects definition with
  `tools/estrai-comportamenti-animazioni.py`), a neutral model of the behaviours
  (`AnimationBehaviour`: group, set, animate, color, transform, path, filter, command,
  physics; a visitor for the two formats) and two codecs: `OdfAnimationBehaviourCodec` (SMIL nodes as the
  reference suite writes them) and `PptxAnimationBehaviourCodec` (`p:set`, `p:anim`, `p:animEffect`, `p:animMotion`,
  `p:animRot`, `p:animScale`, `p:animClr`, `p:cmd`, `p:iterate` as PowerPoint writes them). The shared tables
  `AnimationAttributeTable` (x↔ppt_x, formulas `width`↔`#ppt_w`…) and `AnimationFilterTable` (PowerPoint's
  filters, derived from the reference suite's filter) translate the native behaviour read from one format into the
  other. An effect modified only in its duration keeps its own behaviour, scaled.
  The reference suite reads back our ODP with identical presets and nodes on 299 slides of 301 (the two
  remaining ones are «random», which the reference suite resolves at random), and our PPTX with identical presets and nodes
  except the presets without a PowerPoint number (declared, PPTX032) and the «to-*» subtypes of the exit, which
  its import does not know.
- Slide show: horizontal and vertical lines (zero height or width, like the reference suite's `draw:line`)
  were not drawn at all.
- Ledger: a single word typed in a cell got an initial capital («alfa» → «Alfa»); in the reference suite the
  correction fires only when the word is finished.

**Medium (fixed)**
- Slide show: all transitions without a type of ours were shown as a fade. Now the
  effects are computed in the model per family (`TransitionEffectFactory`: wipes, split,
  blinds, checkerboard, random bars, dissolve, iris and shapes, clock and wheel, wedge, strips,
  snake and spiral, cover and uncover, push, zoom) as clips, translations, scales and opacity, and the
  window applies them (`TransitionStage`). The reference suite's 3D is a flip: declared
  approximation (`ITransitionEffect.Approximate`). The SMIL map of transitions moved from
  `OdfTransitionMapper` to `SmilTransitionMapper` in `PulseOffice.Formats` to serve the UI too.
- PPTX, direction of cover and push: decided on ECMA-376 Part 1 (`ST_TransitionSideDirectionType` /
  `ST_TransitionEightDirectionType`, attribute `dir` of `p:push`, `p:cover`, `p:pull`): `dir` is the direction
  of the movement, as in PowerPoint («push from right» is `dir="l"`, «from bottom» is `dir="u"`). We keep
  this reading; the reference suite's import is inconsistent with itself (it reads `u`/`d` as the direction
  of the movement and `l`/`r` as the origin). Test on the eight combinations (`TransitionDirectionSpecTests`).
- Editor: «align» with several objects selected moved only the main object, and towards the edge
  of the slide; now it aligns the whole selection relative to its bounding box (with a single object,
  relative to the slide), as in the reference suite and PowerPoint. Ordering too (bring forward, send backward, bring to
  front, send to back) acts on the whole selection.
- Slide show: a key pressed during an animation or a transition was ignored; now it
  completes it.
- ODP: the fill inherited from named graphic styles (the reference suite's «standard», light blue
  `#729fcf`) was lost and shapes came back with the default blue (`OdfGraphicStyleInheritance`).
- ODP/PPTX: the master's explicit background color (not a theme color) was lost and the
  slides came back white; now it is `SlideMaster.BackgroundColor` and crosses the two formats.

**Minor (fixed)**: «to-*» exit subtypes and «downward» of «stretch» in PPTX;
`animateTransform` without `smil:attributeName="transform"`; effects iterated by letter
(`anim:iterate`) were not read in ODP.

**Verifications without defects**: Deck editor (text box and typing, group and ungroup,
compound undo and redo, read-only disabling the commands, zoom, rulers, guide lines, normal/master/notes/outline
views, dark theme); slide show (animation steps, transitions, back,
end, exit with Esc); PDF exports (slides, notes with embedded fonts, handouts), PNG,
HTML, mp4 on macOS; Ledger: autofilter, find and replace with undo, dark theme.

**Open**
- Medium: Deck's PDF is made of images of the slides: the text can be neither selected nor
  searched and the fonts are not embedded (only the notes are). A vector drawing
  of the slides on `IPageCanvas` is needed.
- Medium: bitmap fill of shapes and image background of the master do not exist in the model:
  they come back as solid color (seen on `fillbitmap2.odp`); `draw:background-size="border"` is ignored.
- Minor: ODF custom dashes (`draw:stroke-dash` with their own dots and dashes) are
  drawn with the nearest default dash (seen on `LineStylesOwn.odp`).
- Medium: pasting HTML into Ledger: the system clipboard gives only text and images; a table
  copied from a browser arrives as tab-separated text, without formatting.
- Still: «random» remains a fade (the reference suite resolves it at random); presets that exist only in the reference suite in
  PPTX come back as the class's default preset (PPTX032); physics has no PPTX counterpart.
- Live slide show and presenter view on a real screen, pen and laser pointer: not tested
  live (only headless keyboard navigation).

## Audit, cycle 3 — Folio (2026-10-13)

**Method.** Formats: a run over the whole word-processor test corpus present in the external test corpus (3,912
ODT, FODT and DOCX files; 3,873 read, the 39 rejected are the `fail/` files and the deliberately broken packages) to ODT and
to DOCX, with read-backs and counts of paragraphs, text (including deleted text), tables, objects,
notes, comments, fields, bookmarks, revisions and sections before and after; a decrease without a loss
declared in `CheckFidelity` is a defect. Pagination: the same documents (1,010 larger than 15 KB
in the layout, export and import folders) converted to PDF by the reference suite headless (its own
profile) and paginated by us with the same fonts (the reference suite's plus the system ones, with the
metric substitutions), comparing page count and first line of each page read with PDFKit; plus
ten generated documents (five fonts, running text and tables) and the worst cases looked at by hand.
Editor and printing: headless tests (Avalonia.Headless). Performance: a 505-page document.

**Pagination tolerance (written here and valid for later cycles).** Identical page count
up to 10 pages; beyond that, a maximum deviation of 5% rounded up. Breaks are compared
on the first line of each page. Outcome: generated documents 10 of 10 identical (5 of 10 before); on the
reference suite's corpus 765 of 890 within tolerance and 759 identical. The residual deviations are almost all
regression files of the reference suite built on one of its own defects (floating tables, a corpus case where the reference suite reaches
367 pages because of one of its loops, «bad» tables of contents, intra-paragraph line spacing of a corpus case): list at the
end of the «Open» items.

**Blocking (fixed)**
- Pagination: a paragraph with a side frame larger than the page sent the paginator
  into an infinite loop and the app hung when opening the document (a corpus case-1.docx). At the top of an empty
  column the paragraph is now written even if the object leaves no room.
- DOCX→ODT: a DrawingML path with zero height (a horizontal line) became `NaN` and the written ODT
  could no longer be read back (a corpus case); the SVG reader too no longer fails on a non-numeric
  coordinate.

**Serious (fixed)**
- DOCX: theme fonts (`asciiTheme="minorHAnsi"`, that is Calibri, Cambria, Aptos…) were not
  resolved: almost every Word document was paginated with the default font
  (`DocxThemeFonts`).
- DOCX: the paragraph spacing of the table style (Table Grid: after 0, single line spacing) did not
  apply in the cells, which took the document defaults (`DocxTableStyleParagraphs`,
  Word's rule: they apply where neither the paragraph nor its style sets them).
- Tables: cell padding was a single value for all four sides, while Word has none at top and
  bottom, and that of the reference suite's tables (even 0) was ignored: every row was 5–11 points taller.
  Now `TableProperties.VerticalCellPadding` is separate, the table has direct properties (`TableBlock.Direct`)
  read from ODT cells and from `tblCellMar`, written in both formats; a DOCX table without a style takes
  Word's default table style. a corpus case: 13 pages against 8, now 8.
- ODT: objects in headers and footers (charts, formulas, shapes) were lost when reading back,
  because pages were read before the context knew how to open the subdocuments.
- ODT: groups containing images were neither written nor read (the reference suite's too), and
  groups of form controls were lost on writing.
- ODT→DOCX: range deletions as the reference suite writes them (text between `change-start` and
  `change-end`) were lost silently and the deleted text became normal text; now they are `w:del`.
- DOCX: comments with only a `commentReference` were lost in ODT; notes and comments inside deleted
  text were lost in both formats.
- DOCX: hidden bookmarks referenced by a field (`REF`, `PAGEREF`, `NOTEREF`) and the reference suite's
  ones for references to headings (`__RefHeading`) were discarded: cross-references
  were left without a target after an ODT→DOCX round trip.
- A section or page change starting with a table lost its page style
  (orientation, headers) in DOCX and in ODT: now `TableBlock.PageStyleName` and `PageBreakBefore`
  cross the two formats and pagination opens the page.

**Medium (fixed)**
- Editor: arrows, Backspace and Delete split emoji with modifiers, ZWJ-joined families, flags and
  letters with combining accents: now they move by graphemes (`TextClusters`, in `Text.Rich`, shared).
  Alt+arrows stop at script changes (kanji, hiragana, katakana, hangul) and skip
  punctuation (`WordMotion`).
- DOCX: a continuous section read headers and footers back only to know the columns and left
  orphan objects anchored to non-existent paragraphs.
- Fonts: among faces with the same weight the narrow version too was chosen at random (DejaVu Sans
  Condensed for DejaVu Sans) in measuring and in PDF; now at equal weight the normal width wins
  (`OpenTypeFace.Width`).

**Minor (fixed, losses now declared)**: comments and notes without an anchor, which Word does not show,
are not imported (DOCX113); end-of-paragraph deletions and revisions on whole tables (DOCX114);
first-page or even headers that the style does not show (ODT007, DOCX045); the name of normal
sections in DOCX (DOCX003 widened). Translations in the five languages.

**Sentinels added**: `FolioCorpusParityTests` (no ODT/DOCX round trip of the corpus silently loses notes,
comments, objects, tables or text), `TextExportCorpusTests` (well-formed EPUB and HTML on the corpus),
`FolioPdfFontTests` (PDF with embedded fonts, `ToUnicode`, links, bookmarks, measured with the
real fonts: the text read back by PDFKit matches), editor tests (`FolioCaretClusterTests`,
`FolioEditingFlowTests`).

**Verifications without defects**: compound undo and redo, Enter and Delete at end of paragraph, backward
selection beyond the paragraph, typing over a selection of several paragraphs, Page Up and Down, Home and End
in Hebrew text, Tab in the last cell, read-only; performance on 505 pages (first pagination
580 ms, typing in the middle with repagination 2 ms median and 15 ms at most, ODT written in 160 ms and
read back in 110 ms, DOCX in 290 and 250 ms).

**Open**
- Medium: the system clipboard gives only text and images: copying from Word, another office suite or a browser
  into Folio (and from Folio outwards) loses formatting (RTF and HTML). Same cause as the Ledger
  remainder of cycle 2 bis; to be done once, shared, with each system's native formats behind
  an interface.
- Medium: pagination, residual deviations beyond tolerance: Word floating tables (`tblpPr`) paginated
  inline; Word tables of contents regenerated with our styles instead of the document's `TOC1…TOC9`
  (style-inheritance.docx, 17 pages against 15); line spacing within the paragraph (a corpus case); endnotes
  collected at the end of the section (inline-endnote-and-section).
- Minor: tracked insertions containing only a comment (a corpus case) and revisions inside Word's
  field instructions (a corpus case) do not reach DOCX; the `_GoBack` bookmark and the reference suite's
  `__DdeLink` ones are not preserved.
- Minor: a mouse click can still land inside a grapheme (the position from the point is not yet
  aligned to graphemes; arrows are).
- Not tested live: Folio's dark theme and five languages on the real interface (covered only by the catalog
  tests), mail merge to a printer.
