## Audit, eleventh round (2026-10-19) — first part

**Corpus tool: DECL tied to the feature.** Before, any code in the pass was enough for a drop to be
DECL. Now `DeclarationMatcher` (in `tools/corpus-audit`) compares the drop with the **message** of each collected
diagnostic: a feature is declared only if a message names its subject (frames: frame, text box, drawing,
object…; fields: field; lists: list, numbering, bullet…). The codes column of a DECL row carries only the
relevant codes. Immediate effect: 272 rows that were DECL because of unrelated codes (DOCX009 page styles, DOCX039
number style, DOCX040 frame styles, ODP010 theme, ODP022 layout…) went back to LOSS (from 186 to 458).

**Counting artefacts removed** (verified file by file, not losses):
- empty Word text boxes (`wps:txbx` without text but with `txBox="1"`) now count as frames: the empty
  `w:framePr` frames of a corpus file rewritten as boxes looked lost;
- `w:framePr` with `w:dropCap` is a drop cap, not a frame (a corpus file, written in ODT as `style:drop-cap`);
- the text of ODT shapes also counts in `text:h` (a corpus file, heading inside the box);
- `word/settings.xml` excluded (the `o:shapedefaults` carry `v:textbox`, `customxml.docx`);
- DOCX headers and footers not referenced by any `w:sectPr` (orphan parts, a corpus file,
  `floattable-from-bottom.docx`) are not counted.

**Declaration widened**: DOCX171 (unused page styles, not written in DOCX) said "text, links and
images" of headers; the 26 ODT→DOCX fields lost were all in `styles.xml`, in headers of unused page
styles (verified on 26 files). The message now also names fields and tables, in the five languages.

**Pass result**: LOSS 368, DECL 575 (before 186/850 with the loose classification). At the top remain frames and shapes
DOCX→DOCX/ODT (42+36+35), DOCX fields (17+14), DOCX images (15+14), PPTX→ODP links (15), XLSX shapes (13+11),
ODT→DOCX lists (9). **Not yet analysed one by one**: they are the resume point.

**Minor items fixed**:
- (minor) lines written in DOCX carried an empty `wps:txbx` box and a fill: now the empty story (only
  empty paragraphs, without anchored objects) is not written and the line has `a:noFill`. Test `DocxEleventhAuditLineTests`.
  The first version also removed the story of a corpus file (shape inside shape): objects anchored to the story
  make it non-empty, guarded by `FolioCorpusParityTests`.
- (minor) the bullet was drawn on empty paragraphs of boxes (Deck, Ledger): `TextBlockTypesetter` does not
  draw the label of a paragraph without text, as PowerPoint and the reference suite do outside editing.
- (medium, found live) Deck's Tools tab had only "Macro…" without an icon (log warning "Ribbon commands
  without an icon: deck.macro.editor") and a large button, different from Folio. Deck and Ledger now have the same three
  commands as Folio (edit, run, organise macros) with the same icons and the same labels in the five languages.

**Seen on screen** (own instance, throwaway `PULSEOFFICE_DATA_HOME`, foreground verified by pid before every
click and key with a script that refuses the action otherwise): date `19/10/2026` typed in Ledger with Italian
settings recognised as a date (right-aligned, formula bar `19/10/2026`), `1,5` as a number; Macro
group in Folio's Tools tab and, after the fix, in Deck's, identical to Folio, without warnings in the log.

## Audit, thirteenth round (2026-10-19)

Three branches worked in parallel and merged into main without conflicts; new loss codes verified unique, build without
warnings, full suite green, corpus pass rerun after the merge.

**Deck.** *Medium, fixed*: there were two group models — `SlideGroup` for groups reopened from file (only marked

## Fontwork: gallery with live preview (2026-10-20)

User request: "L'inserimento è orribile, e dovrebbe anche supportare l'anteprima" ("The insertion is horrible, and it should also support a preview"). The Fontwork dialog was a
flat `FormPromptView` (text, font, drop-down menus for shape and colours, shadow). Now it is `FontworkGalleryView`, in
`PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Shapes/Fontwork`, shown by `FontworkPrompt` (already shared, wired into Folio, Deck and Ledger):
- on the left text, the shared font picker with bold and italic, eight colour styles as clickable
  swatches (`IFontworkLooks`, three new: purple, teal, ink), fill and outline customisable with
  the shared colour picker (`ColorFieldControl`), shadow;
- on the right the gallery of the eight shapes with thumbnails that draw the typed word in the shape, with the current style and
  shadow, and below it the large preview, updated on every change;
- thumbnails, swatches and preview (`FontworkPreview`) use `IFontworkRenderer`, the same engine as the document;
- keyboard: arrows, Home and End in the gallery, Enter confirms (also from the text field), Esc cancels; double click on a
  thumbnail confirms. "Forma del Fontwork" ("Fontwork shape", `ChooseWarpAsync`) uses the same gallery in shape-only mode.
- The view model is `FontworkDesigner` (without Avalonia): it composes the `FontworkObject`, rejects empty text, falls back to the
  sample in the preview.
- **Engine defect fixed**: `FontworkPath` measured lengths and angles in the unit square ignoring the
  frame's proportions, and the inset computed after sizing shrank the area without reducing the font size:
  in wide frames (wave, arch) the letters overlapped. Now `Length`/`Place`/`At` receive the
  height/width ratio (default 1, so the ODF geometry does not change) and the font size readapts to the inset area.
- New texts in the five languages. Headless tests in `PulseOffice.Desktop.Tests/FontworkGalleryTests.cs` (view model,
  gallery with keyboard and Enter, thumbnails painted with Skia identical to the engine's direct drawing).
- **Live** (own instances, throwaway `PULSEOFFICE_DATA_HOME`, foreground checked by pid before every
  click or key, captures with `windowshot --pid`): Folio, Ledger and Deck in light and dark theme; dialog opened from the
  palette, text typed with preview and thumbnails updated, red style and shape changed by mouse and arrows,
  insertion with Enter: the object in the document matches the preview.

## Table insertion with grid and preview; real tabs across the app (2026-10-20)

User requests: "Anche l'inserimento della tabella non mi piace… miglioralo" ("I don't like the table insertion either… improve it") and "In tutta l'app i tab non sembrano
tab, sembrano dei pulsanti con sotto una linea" ("Throughout the app the tabs don't look like tabs, they look like buttons with a line underneath").

**Table insertion.** The dialog was a `FormPromptView` with two numeric fields. Now it is `TableInsertView`, in
`PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Tables/Insert`, shown by `ITableInsertPrompt` (shared, wired into Folio, Deck and Ledger):
- on the left the `TableSizeGrid` grid: one hovers or drags to choose columns × rows, the arrows move it
  from the keyboard, below appears "4 × 3" (columns × rows); the grid starts at 10 × 8 and grows by one row or
  column when the pointer touches the edge, up to 20 × 16; for larger values there are the two numeric fields,
  synchronised with the grid; then header row and banded rows;
- on the right the gallery of the existing table styles (`ITableStylePresets`, the same `TableLookPreview` thumbnails
  as the "Stile tabella" ("Table style") gallery) and below the live preview with the chosen rows and columns (beyond 12 × 10 the preview
  stops and says so);
- Enter confirms (also from the numeric fields, which first commit the value), Esc cancels, double click on a style
  confirms, arrows/Home/End in the gallery.
- Model without Avalonia: `TableSizeModel` (chosen size, size under the pointer, grid extension, limits
  per module) and `TableInsertDesigner` (size, style, header, bands, preview).
- **Quick grid on the ribbon**, as in Word: the insert command carries `TableGridSpec`; `TableGridSlot` opens a
  popup with the grid ("Tabella 4 × 3" ("Table 4 × 3") while hovering) that inserts immediately with the default style, and
  "Altre opzioni…" ("More options…") which opens the dialog. `RibbonControlSpec.FollowsDisplay` lets a control keep the
  large/small form of the item instead of becoming a strip.
- **Folio**: table inserted, style applied and cursor in the first cell in a single transaction (one Undo removes it).
  Applying the style is now `IFolioTableLooks`, used also by "Stile tabella".
- **Deck**: the table is born with cell-by-cell styling (`IDeckTableLooks`: fills, ink and bold
  of the header, borders, `OwnLook`), so it matches the preview; with the header the chosen rows include
  the column names row. Deck's "Stile tabella" also goes through here: before it changed only the accent colour.
  `OwnLook` and the cell looks already cross ODP and PPTX.
- **Ledger** had no table insertion: new command `ledger.insert.table` (⌘T, ribbon "Inserisci › Tabelle" ("Insert › Tables"),
  menu Insert › Table). It starts from the active cell or covers the data area around it (or the selection), applies the style to the
  cells (`ILedgerTableLooks`, the same code as "Stili di tabella" ("Table styles")), writes "Colonna 1…" ("Column 1…") in empty headers and
  defines a data area "Tabella1…" ("Table1…") with header: a single undo step. Data area and cell formats
  already cross ODS and XLSX.
- New texts in the five languages; keys of the old dialog removed.

**Tabs.** `TabbedDialogView` drew buttons with top corners and a line underneath. Now there is a single component,
`PageTabStrip` (in `PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Tabs`, a child of `TabStrip<T>` like the ribbon tabs): secondary
text, discreet hover, active tab in the module's accent colour with the underline indicator,
baseline under the whole strip, arrows/Home/End, visible keyboard focus, light and dark theme from tokens. Moved
onto the component all the places that had tabs: tabbed dialogs (`TabbedDialogView`, hence Table Properties,
Format Cells, Validity, Character, Paragraph, Page, form controls…), shape style (formerly a Fluent `TabControl`),
side panel, Review panel (formerly a segmented selector), Palette/Spectrum of the colour picker,
categories of the symbol picker (in a scrolling strip; dialog widened to 900). The focus frame of
tabs (ribbon included) appears only if focus comes from the keyboard, not after a click. The `Button.segment` style has
no more users and was removed from `PulseTheme`.

Headless tests: `PulseOffice.Desktop.Tests/TableInsertTests.cs` (grid model, designer, dialog with arrows,
mouse, gallery and Enter, tabs with arrows and click, Deck cell-by-cell style), Folio (insertion with style and
quick insertion undone in one step) and Ledger (data area, headers, style, undo).

**Live** (own instances, throwaway `PULSEOFFICE_DATA_HOME`, foreground checked by pid before every click or
key, captures with `windowshot --pid`): Folio, Ledger and Deck in light and dark theme; quick grid from the ribbon
("Tabella 5 × 4" on hover, insertion on click), dialog from "Altre opzioni…" and from ⌘T in Ledger, size chosen with
mouse and arrows, style from the gallery, Enter: in all three modules the inserted table matches the preview. Seen the
tabs of Table Properties, Format Cells and Insert Symbol in both themes. *Defects found and fixed live*: the
quick grid popup errored ("Altre opzioni…" reassigned a text already a child of the button); the grid
showed the default black focus frame; initial focus landed on the Columns field instead of the grid;
the tabs' focus frame appeared even after a click; the symbol categories did not fit at 720.

## Side panel: styles, navigator and review in the same language (2026-10-22)

User request: the "Stili" ("Styles") tab of Folio's panel was ugly (four big family buttons that
wrapped, a flat list, five action buttons on two rows). Redone, and with it Navigator and Review, which
had the same defect; the panel is shared by Folio, Deck and Ledger, so the change applies to all three modules.

**Shared components** (`PulseOffice.UI.Controls/Panels`): `PanelActionBar` (bar of icon buttons with tooltip and
accessible name, groups with a separator that hides when the group is empty, right-aligned actions, disabled
state from tokens), `PanelChoiceBox` (compact drop-down with icon and title, on data and model, not on controls),
`PanelSearchBox` (field with magnifier, cross to clear, Esc clears, down arrow moves to the list, Enter confirms),
`PanelListFrame` (list frame; rows with soft corners, discreet hover, selection in the module's soft
accent, keyboard focus with an accent border: `ListBox.panelList` style in `PulseTheme`). New icons in
`PanelIcons` (`PulseOffice.UI.Icons`): style families, actions, moves, review, navigator categories.

**Styles.** `StylesPanelModel` (without Avalonia, tested without interface) holds family, filter, search, rows,
selection, style in use and deletion confirmation; `IStyleRecents` remembers the styles applied from the panel. The view:
- family in a drop-down with icon (Folio: Paragraph, Character, Frame, Page, List, Table — Frame and Table
  are new: they apply to the selected object and to the table the cursor is in; Ledger: Cells; Deck: Objects), the
  filter behind a funnel icon (All / Recently used / Custom / Applied in the document; the last only where the
  source knows usage: Folio and Ledger), search below;
- list with a preview of the name in the style itself (font, size bounded between 11 and 17, bold, italic,
  underline, colour if readable on the theme; in Ledger also the cell background, like Excel's gallery; in Deck and
  for frames and tables a fill swatch), inherited hierarchy indented with guide lines, style in use marked
  by an accent bar; filters and search flatten;
- double click or Enter applies; context menu Apply / Edit… / New from this… / Update from selection /
  Delete; Delete asks for confirmation in a strip inside the panel (Enter confirms, Esc cancels), F2 edits;
- at the bottom an icon bar: New, Update from selection, Edit and, on the right, Delete.
`IStylesPanelSource.CanApply` becomes per family; `StylePanelAction.Derive` ("New from this") creates in Folio a child
style (paragraph, character, frame, table) or a copy (list, page), in Ledger a cell style with a parent.
Deletion from the panel no longer goes through Folio's modal confirmation (the panel asks, the same in the three modules).
`IStyleUsage` (`PulseOffice.Documents`) collects the styles used in the document, with a per-revision cache in the source.

**Navigator and Review**: category and authors in the same drop-down with icon, search with magnifier, actions in the icon bar
(Go | Up, Down | Promote, Demote; moves disappear where the category cannot be reordered. Accept, Reject | Accept
all, Reject all; Resolve, Delete | Delete by author, Delete all). Enter and Delete in the three lists are listened to in
tunnel: a `ListBoxItem` consumed Enter before the handler, and live Enter did not apply the style (tests that raised
the event directly on the list did not see it; now the test goes through the window).

Tests: `PulseOffice.UI.Controls.Tests/StylesPanelTests.cs` (model: follows the style in use, hierarchy, filters, recents,
search, deletion confirmation, actions; view: previews, bar, Enter from the window, Delete and Esc, context menu;
action bar: enabling, visibility, separators; navigator with the bar), `PulseOffice.Documents.UI.Tests/
FolioStylesPanelTests.cs` (families with icons, previews, usage in the document, application, frame and table, deletion
of the custom style). New texts in the five languages.

**Live** (own instances, throwaway `PULSEOFFICE_DATA_HOME`, foreground verified by pid, captures with
`windowshot --pid`): Folio in light theme (paragraph with previews and hierarchy, family drop-down, character, filter
"Applicati nel documento" ("Applied in the document"), context menu, double click that applies) and dark; Ledger dark (cell styles with background);
Deck light (object styles with swatch, icon navigator, deletion confirmation). *Defects found live*:
orphan separators in the navigator bar when moves are hidden; Enter that did not apply; the drop-down with
a single item looked broken because disabled (now it stays active); the confirmation text was Folio-specific.

## AI agent: MCP server (2026-10-24)

Implemented [docs/agent-plan.md](agent-plan.md) in five steps. Two new projects: `PulseOffice.Agent` (protocol,
transport, tools, security; without Avalonia) and `PulseOffice.Agent.UI` (adapters to workspace, commands,
macros, rendering, modal, status bar and settings). Protocol written by us (JSON-RPC 2.0 + MCP 2025-06-18, with
negotiation down to 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05) because the official SDK is not in the local cache.

- **Tools**: 7 for documents, 2 for commands, 129 content tools generated from `ScriptApiCatalog` (Ledger 93, Folio 25,
  Deck 11, counting property reads), 1 view tool: 139 in all at the highest level.
- **Same API and same checks as macros**: content tools compose `object.Member(...)` with literal JSON
  arguments and run it in the sandboxed JavaScript engine, with the same globals (`IModuleScriptGlobals`, now
  implemented by the Ledger, Folio and Deck globals) and the `ReadOnlyGuardedDispatcher`.
- **Structures touched**: `IDocumentFileService.SaveToAsync` (saves to a path without a window, with the usual
  signature confirmation and fidelity report); `IDocumentOperations.BuildRange` and `ISheetPrintDocumentBuilder.BuildRange`
  (a range of the active sheet as a printable document); `SettingField.IsWide` (a full-width setting editor
  below the title, used by the connection card); `AvaloniaPageCanvas` accepts `IDisplayFonts`, without which
  uninstalled families (Liberation Serif) fell back to a fallback font with the wrong widths.
- **Security**: off by default, only 127.0.0.1, foreign `Origin` values refused, access code in a
  0600 file in the data folder, levels read / edit / files and network, forbidden commands (options, macros, security,
  passwords, signatures), confirmation in a modal with backdrop for overwrites and destructive commands, every edit an
  "Agente: …" ("Agent: …") step of ⌘Z, indicator in the status bar, log `config/agent/operations.jsonl` and log messages in English.

**Tests**: `PulseOffice.Agent.Tests`, 40 cases: JSON-RPC encoding, negotiation, sessions and expiry, MCP endpoint,
generation and levels of tools from the catalogue, arguments that do not become code (a string with `"); sheet.Write(...)`
written verbatim), real execution in the JavaScript engine, refusal by level, confirmation accepted and refused,
command policy, access code (0600 permissions, regeneration), operations log, and integration: the
HTTP server actually started and a client doing `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`
(including an image), `DELETE`; 401 without a code or with a wrong code, 403 with a foreign `Origin`, 405 on `GET`, the
controller that turns the server on and off according to the settings.

turned on from the new section, level "Modifica, file e rete" ("Edit, files and network"), client `tools/mcp-client`.

`IDisplayFonts` for the family for measuring and drawing, and the measured width is that of the resolved font), constructors updated in

### Fourteenth round, Folio minor items: revisions in ODT headers, default tab distance (done)

- **Revisions inside a DOCX→ODT content control** (`SdtContent.docx`, LOSS in the corpus pass) — *medium*. The cause was not
  the content control but the header: `OdtChangeWriter` wrote all the `text:changed-region` elements in the body's
  `text:tracked-changes` (`content.xml`), while the header's `text:change*` marks live in `styles.xml`;
  the ODF schema wants a `text:tracked-changes` of its own at the top of `style:header`/`style:footer` (`header-footer-content`).
  The file was inconsistent (references between two package parts) and the corpus pass counted it as a loss. Now
  revisions cited only by a header or footer are written inside them (deletion styles in
  `styles.xml`) and `OdtStylesReader` rereads them; old files with everything in the body read as before. A recent version of the reference suite
  opens the file (it discards header revisions even from the original DOCX: its own limit). Corpus: `SdtContent.docx`
  from LOSS to OK.
- **Default tab distance not modelled** — *medium*. `StyleSheet.DefaultTabInterval` (points, default
  1.25 cm) replaces the `LayoutOptions` constant; ODT reads and writes it in `style:default-style` as
  `style:tab-stop-distance`, DOCX as `w:defaultTabStop` in `settings.xml` (absent → 720 twips, Word's default;
  `w:documentProtection` moved after `w:trackRevisions` as the schema requires). Before, it was not written: the reference suite, without
  the attribute, pushed the text of `listformat.odt` rewritten by us 18.6 pt further right.
- **List label wider than its space** — *medium*. `LineBreaker` attached the text at the end of the label; as
  other word processors do, it now jumps to the next tab (explicit or default, relative to the indent). Note labels
  (`FollowedByTab = false`) stay attached to the text.
- **Interface**: in the paragraph window, "Tabulazioni" ("Tabs") tab, the field "Tabulazioni predefinite del documento" ("Document default tabs") (cm,
  five languages, undoable); the "nessuna tabulazione" ("no tabs") text no longer says "every 1.25 cm" but refers to the document's.
  In the styles window the field does not appear (it belongs to the document, not to the style).

**Verifications.** Tests that failed before: `OdtHeaderChangesTests`, `OdtDefaultTabStopTests`, `DocxDefaultTabStopTests`,
`TabTests` (distance from the document, wide label), `FolioFormattingDialogTests`. Headless reference suite and `tools/pdfprobe`:
`listformat.odt` rewritten by us now gives in PDF the same x character by character as the original (before 18.6 pt to the right
at the second level); our live layout puts the text of the three levels where the reference suite puts it. Live
(own instances, throwaway `PULSEOFFICE_DATA_HOME`, foreground and coordinates checked by pid before every click or key):
in light `listformat.odt`, paragraph window, distance raised to 2.5 cm and text moved; in dark the ODT of

`scratchpad/live15/c` (`light-1…5.png`, `dark-1…2.png`).

Open: the model treats tabs as relative to the indent (ODT semantics of other word processors); Word in DOCX measures them from the
margin (the reference suite's `TabsRelativeToIndent` setting is not modelled), so an indented paragraph with tabs carried into
DOCX may shift — pre-existing, minor.
### Fourteenth round, geometry minor items: shading, handles, adjustments of shapes with their own type (2026-10-24)

**Path shading.** *Cause*: the preset catalogue read only `none` from `fill`, and the ODF commands H–K
were accepted and ignored; the figure (`ShapeFigure`) had nowhere to keep the shading. *Fix*: `ShapeShade`
(Normal, Darken, DarkenLess, Lighten, LightenLess) on the figure; the catalogue reads `fill="darken|darkenLess|lighten|lightenLess"`,
the ODF interpreter translates H/I/J/K, the preset→ODF translator writes them, `ShapeRenderer` (the single painter of the three modules) lays
a black or white veil at 40 % / 20 % over the fill. In OOXML the freeform geometry (`custGeom`, PPTX190) now carries `fill`
and `stroke` of each path. **Silent defect found along the way (medium)**: `ArcFlattener` rebuilt the figures
losing `Filled`/`Stroked`, so every freeform geometry exported to OOXML lost its paths without fill or without
outline; now it keeps them.

**`draw:handle` handles.** *Cause*: the translator wrote no handles. *Fix*: the catalogue reads `ahLst`
(`ahXY`, `ahPolar`) into `PresetHandle`; the translator writes for each handle `draw:handle-position` (translated guides) and the
ranges (`handle-range-x/y-*`, for polar ones `handle-radius-range-*`), in the order of `ahLst`: for `ooxml-*` types the reference suite
rebuilds the handle→adjustment link from there, because ODF cannot write `RefX`.

**Adjustment handles in the editor (shared component).** `IShapeAdjustHandles` (core, `Drawing`) exposes the handles
of a shape (preset with `ahLst`, ODF geometry with handles bound to `$n`, and also shapes with their own `ShapeKind` that have
an OOXML preset with handles, e.g. rounded rectangle) and resolves dragging: the handle position is a
function of the adjustments, so `AdjustHandleSolver` inverts it numerically (sampling over the range and golden section,
coordinate descent on both axes, rounding to integer for OOXML). `IAdjustHandleChrome` (`UI.Controls`) draws the yellow
diamonds, grabs them even on rotated shapes and draws the dashed preview; it is wired into Deck (`SlideView` →
`DeckActions.AdjustShape`, "Regola la forma" ("Adjust shape")), Folio (`FolioCanvas` → `IFolioObjectEditing.Replace`) and Ledger
(`SheetGridView.ShapeAdjusted` → `LedgerView`, history entry "Regola la forma"), with undo. New keys translated into the five
languages: `deck.action.adjustShape`, `history.draw.adjustShape`.

**`avLst` of shapes with their own type.** *Cause*: `DrawingPresetGeometry.Shaped` for a preset known as a `ShapeKind`
(roundRect, can, wedgeRectCallout…) kept the type and discarded `avLst` (except arcs); in ODF a `draw:type="ooxml-roundRect"`
was recognised as a known type and the `draw:modifiers` ignored. *Fix*: if the adjustments differ from the default
values (`IPresetGeometryEngine.Adjusted`), the shape keeps its `ShapeKind` and receives a `PresetGeometry` with the
adjustments, which PPTX/DOCX/XLSX rewrite in `avLst` and ODF in `ooxml-*` with `draw:modifiers`; on ODF reading a known type with
modifiers different from the defaults comes back with the type and the adjusted geometry. With the default values nothing changes.

**Classification.** Medium: paths without fill/outline lost in OOXML freeform geometry (`ArcFlattener`).
Minor closed: shading not drawn; `draw:handle` not written; adjustment handles missing in the three editors; radius
of the rounded rectangle (and any `avLst` of a shape with its own type) lost on OOXML and ODF reading. No new loss
code: nothing remains lost.

**Verifications.** Tests: `GeometryShadesAndHandlesTests` (Drawing), `AdjustedPresetTests` (PPTX, XLSX, DOCX, ODP, ODS, ODT,
freeform geometry), `AdjustHandleChromeTests` (UI.Controls, also with a rotated shape), `DeckShapeAdjustmentTests` (undo and
redo). A recent version of the reference suite in headless mode (own profile) on an ODP written by us (roundRect at 45000, cube, can,
wedgeRectCallout): converted to PPTX it has `avLst` `adj=45000` and those of the presets; resaved as ODP it keeps the four
`draw:handle`; in PNG the cube and the cylinder have darkened and lightened faces. Reread by us the reference suite's PPTX and ODP:
rounded rectangle with `adj=45000`. Not tested live: dragging handles in the three editors is covered only by
tests.

**Open (minor).** Shapes with their own `ShapeKind` without adjustments (cylinder, cube as a type) are drawn by our
geometry and have no shading; vector printing (`ObjectPathBuilder`) ignores fill, outline and shading
per figure; horizontal/vertical flipping is not considered in the handle positions; polar handles of
native ODF geometries (`draw:handle-polar`) are not draggable; the `draw:modifiers` of the reference suite's native ODF shapes
(`round-rectangle` without the `ooxml-` prefix) are not read.
## Audit, fifteenth round, Ledger and Deck: minor items of the fourteenth (2026-10-24)

**Fixed** (cause and remedy at the root):
- **Formula bar with `TRUE`/`FALSE`** (minor): `LedgerView` showed `CellValue.ToString()`. Now `ICellEditText.Value`
  writes booleans with `CultureBooleanNames` in the cell's language (VERO, WAHR, VRAI, VERDADERO), the same that
  `CellInputRecognizer` reads back; it also applies to the data form. Decision 17 respected (the canonical form does not change).
- **Cell linked to another sheet that did not follow rows and columns** (medium, it wrote into the wrong cell):
  `FormControlRelinker` saw only the controls of the modified sheet and only unqualified references. Now it visits all
  sheets (`FormLinksPart` in `SheetStructure`, and cell moves) and moves references, qualified or not, that
  point to the modified sheet, keeping the sheet name; the same for the source range.
- **Sound on click discarded by the reference suite** (medium): `script:event-name="dom:click"` used the `dom` prefix without
  declaring it; the reference suite resolves the name with the namespace map and discarded the event. Now `OdfPackage.Namespaces.Dom`
  and `script` are declared in ODP, ODS and ODT (same latent defect for control and sheet events).
  Verified headless: the event survives ODP→ODP. The reference suite, however, does not re-embed the sound file (its limit).
- **Linked text in shapes without link appearance** (minor): shared `IHyperlinkAppearance`
  (`PulseOffice.UI.Controls`), used by `RunStyler` (Deck) and `ShapeRenderer` (Ledger, Folio): the theme's link colour
  and underline, as in PowerPoint, even if the run carries an explicit colour (ODP always writes it).
- **Text frames in Ledger's `table:shapes`** (minor, corpus LOSS): new `SheetTextFrameReader` (rectangle with
  text; black, top left if the style says nothing else); the `draw:a` link stays `PlacedObject.Hyperlink`

## Audit, sixteenth round, shape geometries: open minor items of the fifteenth (2026-10-24)

**Fixed** (cause and remedy at the root):
- **Shading of shapes with their own type** (minor): cylinder, bevel, folded corner and smiley, without
  adjustment, were drawn by their own geometry (`ShapeGeometry`) without darkened or lightened faces; after moving
  the handle they became a shaded preset, so the shape changed appearance at the first drag. New service
  `IImplicitPresetGeometry` (core, `Drawing`): for a `ShapeKind` whose OOXML preset has shaded paths
  `ShapeGeometry.Outline(shape, w, h)` uses the preset with the default adjustments; the same service gives
  `ShapeAdjustHandles` the implicit preset with handles (before it was a private copy).
- **Handles and flips** (minor): handles ignored the shape's `FlipHorizontal`/`FlipVertical` and the flip
  of the Folio object (`AnchoredObject.FlipHorizontal`). The shared component `IAdjustHandleChrome` now receives an
  `AdjustFrame` (frame, rotation, flips) and a single placement matrix (`Placement`: unit → frame → shape mirror
  XOR frame mirror → rotation) to draw, grab, drag (inverse) and trace the preview. Wired
  into Deck (`SlideView.AdjustFrameOf`), Folio (`FolioCanvas`, with the object's flips) and Ledger
  (`SheetGridView.AdjustFrameOf`).
- **ODF polar handles** (minor): `FormulaAdjustableGeometry` discarded handles with `draw:handle-polar`. Handles are
  now strategies (`CartesianEnhancedHandle`, `PolarEnhancedHandle`, created by `EnhancedHandleFactory`); the polar one computes the
  position as the reference suite does (centre + radius · (cos θ, sin θ) in viewBox
  units), the radius is in `handle-radius-range-*`, the angle in ]-180°, 180°] as in the reference suite's dragging; the
  existing numerical solver inverts them.
- **`draw:modifiers` of native ODF shapes** (minor): `round-rectangle`, `can`, `cube`, `quad-bevel`, `isosceles-triangle`,
  `parallelogram`, `hexagon`, `ring`, `plaque`, `paper` written by the reference suite lost the adjustment (known type: modifiers
  ignored) or stayed freeform geometry (the cube, then exported as `custGeom`). New `INativeShapeModifiers` with the data table
  `NativeShapeMappingTable` (native type → OOXML preset, linear rule per modifier with the reference extents):
  the conversions follow those of the reference suite's OOXML exporter (rounded
  rectangle, bevel, triangle proportional; parallelogram and hexagon on the width relative to the short side;
  cylinder and cube proportional). On ODP/ODS/ODT reading the shape becomes the preset with the adjustment (with the default
  values a known type stays without geometry); on writing it goes out as `avLst` in PPTX/XLSX/DOCX and as `ooxml-*` with
  `draw:modifiers` in ODF, which the reference suite rereads. A mapped type is no longer treated as an unknown literal path.
- **Vector printing per figure** (minor): `ObjectPathBuilder` printed the whole outline with a single fill and a single
  stroke. Now, if a figure is without fill, without stroke or shaded, it emits a fill path per shading
  group with the black/white veil at 40 %/20 % over it (the same values as `ShapeRenderer`), then a single stroke
  path for figures with an outline; the shadow stays on the first path. Applies to PDF and printing in the three modules.

**New tests**: `ShapeGeometryParityTests` (Drawing: shading before and after the handle, polar handle, native table,
per-figure printing), `AdjustHandleChromeTests` (flips of shape and frame), `AdjustedPresetTests` (native ODP
→ PPTX `avLst`, flipped cube, cylinder, ODS and ODT), `FolioShapeAdjustTests` (dragging with the pointer and undo, flipped
shape), `LedgerEditorTests.La_maniglia_di_regolazione_di_una_forma_segue_il_puntatore_e_si_annulla` (pointer and
undo in Ledger).

**Verifications.** A recent version of the reference suite in headless mode (own profile) on FODP/FODS/FODT written by hand with `round-rectangle` 5400, `can`
4320 (ODP only), flipped `cube` 2700: converted by the reference suite into ODP/ODS/ODT and PPTX/XLSX/DOCX, read by us they give the
same values the reference suite writes in its OOXML (roundRect 25000, can 20000, cube 12500 with `flipH`); our
PPTX/ODP/XLSX/ODS/DOCX/ODT rewritten from those files, reconverted by the reference suite both ways, keep `avLst`,
`ooxml-*` + `draw:modifiers` and the flip. **Tests only**, no on-screen test: flipped and polar handles in the three
editors, per-figure printing.

**Open (minor).** The native table covers ten types; the other native types with modifiers (the reference suite's arrows, stars,
callouts) remain geometry read from the reference suite's path, faithful on screen but exported to OOXML as `custGeom`.
Native types are rewritten as `ooxml-*` and not with the native name (the reference suite reads them anyway).
## Audit, sixteenth round, text, links and tabs (2026-10-24)

Open minor items of the fifteenth round. No new loss code (reserved and unused: ODF205-209, DOCX203-206,
XLSX203-206, ODT200-203); `ODF194` and `XLSX182` narrowed to what is really lost.

- **Black shape text on the dark grid** (minor). *Cause*: the model did not distinguish explicit colour from
  automatic; Ledger frames without colour received a fixed `#000000`. *Remedy* (restructured): `ShapeTextStyle.AutomaticColor`;
  `IShapeTextInk` in the core (`PulseOffice.Drawing`) picks black or white from the fill's luminance (with its opacity) or,
  without fill, from the document background, as Word and the reference suite do. The background passes as `ShapeBackdrop` through
  `IShapeRenderer`, `IDrawingObjectRenderer` and `IContentPainter`: Ledger gives the grid colour, Deck the slide
  background (or the first colour of its fill), Folio the paper or the page background (`IPageSurface.Backdrop`); printing
  uses the paper. ODF: `style:use-window-font-color="true"` (with `fo:color` as the last explicit colour), read also
  when `fo:color` is missing; OOXML: run without `a:solidFill`. In the shape style window the checkbox "Colore
  automatico (secondo lo sfondo)" ("Automatic colour (according to the background)"), five languages; choosing a colour makes it explicit. ODS text frames without
  style are now without fill or border, as in the reference suite.
- **Links in the text of Ledger shapes** (minor, formerly `ODF194`/`XLSX182`). *Remedy*: `OdpShapeTextLinks`
  becomes `OdfShapeTextLinks`, shared between Deck and Ledger (shapes, rectangles, ellipses, lines, `draw:text-box` frames);
  `DrawingShapeTextLinks` shared between PPTX and XLSX with `XlsxDrawingRunLinks` on the drawing's relationships; the
  `a:hlinkClick` runs of `xdr:txBody` are read and written. `ODF194` remains only for paths, polygons, connectors;
  `XLSX182` only for freeform shapes and WordArt.
- **Tabs relative to the indent towards DOCX** (minor). *Cause*: the model always measured them from the indent; Word from the
  margin. *Remedy*: `StyleSheet.TabsRelativeToIndent` (default true, as in the reference suite); layout uses
  `ParagraphFrame.TabOrigin` (also for default tabs), and so does Folio's ruler. ODT: `TabsRelativeToIndent`
  in `settings.xml` both ways. DOCX on reading: absolute positions and flag false; on writing, if relative,
  `DocxTabPositions` adds the indent (the style's for styles, the effective one for the paragraph) and, if the paragraph inherits
  tabs from a style with a different indent, writes them shifted, clearing the style's (`w:tab w:val="clear"`).
  Limit: the indent added by lists does not enter the computation, and paragraph format revisions stay raw.
- **Tests of Deck's action window**: the logic moves out of `DeckObjectCommands` into `DeckInteractionForm`
  (injected, no more `static`): "Riproduci un suono" appears and stays selected, the sound stays on confirming and
  changing action, "Nessuna azione" removes the interaction, the entries exist in the five languages.
**Verifications** (tests and a recent version of the reference suite in headless mode only, nothing on screen): shape with a link in its text written by us in
XLSX and ODS, converted by the reference suite into the other format and reread: text and link intact, no declared loss.
Tabs: relative ODT (indent 72 pt, tab 72 pt), our DOCX and the round trip ODT→DOCX by the reference suite→our absolute ODT
give in PDF (`tools/pdfprobe`) the same x for the text after the tab (201.02 pt); the default ones differ
by 0.5 pt as in the reference suite's own conversion. Build `--no-incremental` without warnings; tests green for Architecture,
Documents, Documents.Layout, Documents.UI, Drawing, Formats.Odf, Formats.OpenXml, Presentations, Presentations.UI,
Printing, Sheets.Printing, Sheets.UI, UI.Controls.

**Open (minor)**: automatic colour not seen on screen in the dark theme; image fill does not take part in the
ink choice (the background counts); list indentation outside the tab computation towards DOCX.

## Audit, sixteenth round, live test: handles, links, booleans, budget (2026-10-24)

On-screen test with an own instance (throwaway `PULSEOFFICE_DATA_HOME`, captures with `windowshot --pid`) and comparison
with a recent version of the reference suite in headless mode.

**Seen on screen and working**: adjustment handle in Deck (rounded rectangle) and in Folio (arrow):
dragging, limit at the maximum, undo ("Annullato: Regola la forma" ("Undone: Adjust shape")), flipped shape with the handle mirrored and
draggable; saving ODP/PPTX and ODT/DOCX with `flipH`/`mirror-horizontal` and modifiers; PPTX and ODT reopened with the
handle in the right place. Budget in Ledger (sums, histogram, pivot table on a new sheet), saved as ODS and XLSX;
boolean formulas in German and formula bar in French (`=ET(VRAI();FAUX())`); dark theme.

**Defects fixed**
- **Folio's adjusted shapes shrunk in the reference suite** (severe). *Cause*: `OdfComputedGeometry` writes the frame
  of formula geometries (`logwidth`/`logheight`) in hundredths of a millimetre, which is the logical unit of the presentation and spreadsheet applications but
  not of the word processor, where it is the twip: the reference suite drew the arrow at 57 % inside its frame, with the text outside.
  *Remedy*: `OdtLogicalViewBox`, a step of the ODT writer (also for group members) that converts the frame to twips
  when it matches the object's frame. Seen in the reference suite before and after (`v2/folio-forma2.png`).
- **Folio links without appearance** (medium). *Cause*: the command puts `Hyperlink` on the run without a style, and
  resolution did not apply the "Internet link" style, which the reference suite's word processor applies automatically to every `text:a` without a style.
  *Remedy*: `StyleResolver.EffectiveRun` uses "Internet link" for linked runs without a style of their own (not for fields):
  blue and underlined in the body and in shape text, as in the reference suite. Seen on screen after the fix.
- **Ledger chart categories with the raw value** (medium). *Cause*: `ChartDataExtractor` used `Value.ToString()`:
  booleans as `TRUE`/`FALSE`, unformatted numbers. *Remedy*: strategy `IChartCellText` (`RawChartCellText` for the
  formats, `PresentedChartCellText` with `ICellPresenter` in the grid and in the container): the chart shows "VERO"/"FALSO"
  like the cell. Seen on screen.
- **Pivot preview with "Totale generale" as the values header** (minor): without column fields it now shows
  the field name, like the created table.
- **"Excel Template" and "PowerPoint Template" not translated** in the save window (minor): `fileType.xltx` and
  `fileType.potx` in the five languages.

**Tests**: `StyleTests` (implicit link), `OdtShapeStoryTests` (frame in twips and modifiers round trip),
`ChartDataTests` (shown categories), `PivotPreviewHeaderTests`, `FileTypeNamesTests`.

**Open**
- **Text inside shapes cannot be typed in Deck and Ledger** (severe): double click, Enter or typing on a selected shape
  do not open the editor (Deck opens only `TextElement`s, Ledger only charts; in Ledger typing ends up
  in the active cell). Text arrives only from files. A shared inline editor is needed in `PulseOffice.UI.Controls`
  wired into both modules (Folio already has one). For this reason the automatic colour in the dark theme could not be seen on a
  shape created on screen.
- Not tested live in this round: moving a control's linked cell by inserting rows, letter with
  mail merge in Folio, slide show with animations and notes in Deck.
- Pivot XLSX: the reference suite recalculates and titles it "Sum of Gen"; in ODS it shows "Gen" as we do.

## Audit, seventeenth round (2026-10-24)

**Severe item of the sixteenth, closed: text in Deck and Ledger shapes.** Folio's editor writes into shapes through its
stories (one `BlockContainer` per shape, modified by the document editor): it cannot be extracted, because it is Folio's
editor itself. The shared component is therefore new and serves `ShapeObject` shapes (text and runs), which Deck and Ledger
use; Folio stays on stories, which are richer (paragraphs, styles).
- Core (`PulseOffice.Drawing`): `IShapeTextEditing` — plain text, replacement that keeps runs (common prefix and
  suffix; inserted text takes the formatting on its left), formatting of a range (empty = all),
  normalisation against the shape's style (`WithRuns`, `Formatted`).
- Component (`UI.Controls/Shapes/ShapeTextEditor`): transparent `TextBox` over the shape with caret and selection; the
  live shape (`Live`) is drawn by the module, so bold and size are visible while typing. Esc or ⌘↩ close,
  leaving focus saves (except for the editor's companions, such as the ribbon, via `ITextEditingFocus`); caret in the
  ink colour, automatic included.
- **Deck**: double click, Enter/F2 or typing on a selected shape enter the text; the character ribbon goes
  through `IShapeRichText` (runs ↔ `RichText`), so all character commands work; `SlideView.LiveText` now accepts
  any element. **Ledger**: double click or typing with a shape selected (typing with an object
  selected no longer ends up in the cell); the character ribbon goes to the shape's text with `ISheetShapeText` and
  `IShapeTextCellStyle` (synthetic cell style from the run and back). One undo step for typing ("Testo
  della forma" ("Shape text")) and one per formatting, in the five languages.
- **Formats**: formatted runs of shapes were not saved at all (only links). `DrawingShapeTextRuns`
  (PPTX, XLSX) and `OdfShapeTextRuns` (ODP, ODS) write and read bold, italic, underline, size, colour and
  font (`a:rPr`; `text:span` with an automatic style of family `text`); shape paragraphs carry a paragraph
  style with the alignment, because the reference suite ignores the `paragraph-properties` of the graphic style (centred text
  came out left-aligned). In XLSX multi-line text lost its line breaks on reading (`InnerText`): now one paragraph per line.

**Minor items of the sixteenth, closed.** Folio's "+ Intestazione" does not appear with an object selected (it covered the top
handles, seen on screen); pivot preview at fixed height (the window recentred as it grew); Deck's inspector
keeps its scroll position when rebuilt (it went back to the top, on "Transizione"); image fill in the ink
choice (`IShapeBrushes.Average`, pixel average blended with opacity); list indentation
(`Indent + Hanging` of the level) in tabs written in DOCX. **Native ODF types with modifiers outside the table**
(medium: they were read as presets with the default proportions, a silent loss): new data table
`NativeShapeDefaults`, generated by `tools/native-shape-defaults.py` from the reference suite's sources (76 types); with modifiers
different from the defaults the shape is read from the reference suite's formula path, faithful on screen, and in OOXML goes out as
`custGeom` declared by `PPTX190` (and by the XLSX/DOCX equivalents). With the defaults the preset remains.

**Classification.** Severe: text in shapes (closed), including the loss of formatted runs in the four formats.
Medium: line breaks of XLSX shapes on reading; native ODF arrows with their own modifiers. Minor: alignment of shape
text in the reference suite and the six of the sixteenth, all closed.

  scroll through slides and focus stays on the new thumbnail, Enter returns to the canvas; on the canvas with nothing selected
  Page Up and Down, Home and End change slide (`ISlideKeyNavigation`).
- **Ledger** (medium): the grid said nothing to a screen reader. Now its accessible name is sheet, cell and
  displayed value ("Data, cella B2: 1234,5" ("Data, cell B2: 1234,5"), "vuota" ("empty")), with the formula as help text, and the cell editor is called
  "Modifica della cella B2" ("Editing cell B2"). New commands **Ctrl+Shift+F5** (name box) and **Ctrl+Shift+F2** (formula bar),
  as in other spreadsheets.
- **Live language switch** with the settings dialog open: dialog, ribbon, command bar and status switch
  immediately to English and back to Italian (seen on screen). With other dialogs open the language cannot be changed
  from the interface; the dialog title follows the language anyway (`DialogHost.OnLanguageChanged`).

**Large documents** (Release, times from app launch to the title with the document, app start ~1.4 s included).
| Document | Before | After | Scrolling and saving |
|---|---|---|---|
| ODS sheet, 100,000 rows × 10 columns | 9.2 s, interface frozen ~7 s | 5.6 s, reading in background | end of sheet immediate; saving 3.1 s |
| ODT text, 6000 paragraphs (353 pages) | 2.4 s | — | end of document immediate; saving 1.3 s |
| ODP presentation, 150 slides | 1.8 s | — | smooth slide change |
Severe bottleneck found (medium): on opening `RowAutoHeightTracker` measured the text of **every cell** with the
font engine (4.7 s on a million cells). Now a single-line cell, without wrap or rotation and with Latin
characters, takes its font's row height, measured once per font; text is measured only for wrap,
rotation, multi-line text or characters outside Latin. In addition the file reading moves to `Task.Run`: the status bar
shows the activity and the interface does not freeze. The format alone: 2.3 s (ODS and XLSX), peak memory 270–340 MB.

**Classification.** Medium: invisible main button in the data dialogs; Deck not usable from the keyboard in the slide
panel; Ledger grid mute for screen readers; opening the 100,000-row sheet slow and with
the interface frozen. Minor: the three of the seventeenth, the tool, the "Dati" tab, provider names, keywords,
icon, title of the mail merge source, mail merge dialog that restarted from the first record even with
the preview on the last (now it starts from the preview's record; only compiled, not retested on screen). All fixed.

**Open (minor).** Default names and labels of form controls are English identifiers ("CheckBox1");
no F6 cycle between the window's areas; saving large files stays on the UI thread (3 s for a
million cells); with the caret without
a selection, bold and similar apply to the whole shape text (as in Deck's text boxes, a consistent choice
but different from the reference suite's presentation application).

**Tests only**: `La_ribbon_mostra_il_grassetto_del_testo_della_forma_in_modifica`,
`Con_il_testo_di_una_forma_in_modifica_restano_attivi_solo_i_comandi_del_carattere`,
`IlTestoAutomaticoDiUnaFormaScuraDiventaChiaroEQuelloConColoreProprioResta`,
`Salva_in_formato_Office_propone_il_nome_e_il_filtro_OOXML`, `Le_miniature_si_scorrono_da_tastiera_e_hanno_un_nome_accessibile`,
`La_griglia_annuncia_la_cella_attiva_ai_lettori_di_schermo` (including the two focus commands). The rest above was seen on
screen, except where stated.

**Corpus** (whole pass rerun): **LOSS 0, DECL 478**, 9948 copies, 28 READFAIL, unchanged. **Status: the eighteenth round
did NOT find only minor items**: no blocking or severe ones, but four medium, all fixed; only minor items remain open.

Goal of the round: only minor defects. Captures in scratchpad `live19`, own instance with throwaway `PULSEOFFICE_DATA_HOME`,

  gives "Casella di controllo 1", "Pulsante 2", "Markierfeld 1"… from the `form.defaultName.*` texts in the five languages, skipping
  names already taken regardless of case; wired into Folio, Deck and Ledger (before "CheckBox1", "checkBox"). The default
  label is the name, as in the reference suite.
- **F6 / Shift+F6 cycle between the window's areas** (minor): `IWindowRegionCycle` cycles between ribbon, document areas,
  the shell's side panel and status bar, skipping hidden areas; the document exposes its own areas with

  frame when focus comes from the keyboard (`KeyboardFocusFrame`). Seen on screen in Deck (canvas → inspector → status → ribbon →
  thumbnail → canvas, and Shift+F6 backwards) and in Ledger (grid → "Data" tab → … → name box).

  caret inside a word the format goes to the word, outside a word it stays pending and applies to the text being typed
  (`ShapeTextEditor.FormatRange`/`Pend`, shared by Deck and Ledger; the word comes from `ICaretWord`). Moving the caret without
  typing cancels the pending format. A shape selected without the editor receives the format on all its text, as before. Seen on
  screen: "Ciao " + ⌘B + "mondo" in a rectangle, "mondo" in bold and "B" lit while typing.

  End goes to 150 and the canvas shows it.
- **Ledger grid with the new keys**: ⌘⇧F2 moves focus to the formula bar (on macOS the shortcuts' Ctrl is ⌘).

**New exploration.**

  cells' CSS `border` property give the borders (`CellShape.Borders`).
- **Print preview** in the three modules (without printing): Ledger with header, footer and cells; Deck with the
  slide (empty placeholders are not printed, as in other presentation applications); Folio with the text. All with backdrop and a "Stampa…" ("Print…") button.
- **Recovery after a forced close**: autosave at one minute, `kill -9`, on restart "Ripristino dei documenti" ("Document recovery") with
  Folio1 "mai salvato su file" ("never saved to file"), "Ripristina" ("Restore") reopens the text, status "Documenti ripristinati: 1" ("Documents restored: 1").

## Two minors and Folio accessibility (2026-10-25)

Closed the two minors left open by the nineteenth round and went through Folio using only the keyboard and with screen readers.
Captures in the scratchpad `live20a`, own instance with a throwaway `PULSEOFFICE_DATA_HOME`, every key sent after checking the
foreground pid; no clicks.

**Minors of the nineteenth.**
- **Borders of HTML tables pasted into Ledger** (minor): reading borders is now a single service, `IHtmlCellBorders`
  (`PulseOffice.Formats.Interchange.Text.Html`), used both by `HtmlDocumentReader` (Folio) and by `HtmlTableReader` (Ledger):
  table `border`, cell `border` and `border-top/right/bottom/left` with width and colour, `none`/`hidden`/`0`
  remove the side. Ledger maps the width to thin/medium/thick (`CellBorders`). Seen on screen: a table with
  `border="1"` and a cell with `border:2pt solid #FF0000`, pasted with ⌘V from the clipboard (`osascript`), arrives with the grid
  and the red cell.
- **Ribbon "B" lit immediately for pending formatting** (minor), Deck and Ledger: `ShapeTextEditor.PendingProbe()` applies
  the pending format to a probe character at the caret, and the format reading of Deck (`ShapeText`/`ShapeRange`) and of
  Ledger (`CurrentShapeTextStyle`) reads that probe; the `PendingChanged` event updates the ribbon. Applies to bold,
  italic and underline. Seen on screen in Deck: rectangle, "Ciao ", ⌘B, ⌘I: "B" and "I" lit before typing, then
  "mondo" in bold italic. In Ledger proven by tests (in Ledger pending bold is now a single undo step,
  as in Deck).

**Folio by keyboard and with screen readers** (compared with the reference suite's word processor and Word).
- **No keyboard context menu** (serious, in all three modules): Shift+F10 and the menu key did nothing
  (the reference suite and Word open it at the caret). Now `IContextMenuKey` (shared, `PulseOffice.UI.Controls.Services`) and
  `IContextMenuFactory.OpenAt` open the menu at the given anchor with focus on the first item: Folio at the caret, Ledger on the
  active cell and on the sheet tabs, Deck on the editor, on the selected object or on the thumbnail. Seen on screen in
  Folio and in Ledger.
- **Position and format not announced** (medium): the document field was always called "Testo del documento" (document text). Now
  `IFolioCaretSpeech` gives the name "Testo del documento, pagina 1 di 2, riga 3, colonna 5" (document text, page 1 of 2, line 3, column 5) (plus "tabella, riga r, colonna c" (table, row r, column c) in
  a cell, or "oggetto selezionato: cornice" (selected object: frame) with an object) and as help text style, font, size and bold,
  italic, underline, including the pending format. The reference suite announces page and position from the status bar, Word line and
  column: here the field itself says them. In the five languages.
- **Objects not selectable by keyboard** (medium): "Seleziona l'oggetto successivo" (Select next object) (⌘⌥⇧O, menu Edit › Select) and,
  with an object selected, Tab / Shift+Tab cycle through the objects as in the reference suite; Esc returns to the text (`IFolioObjectCycle`).
- **Ribbon tabs without a name** (minor): the tab strip (and every `TabStrip`) now has the name of the current
  tab; it was the only unnamed element in the F6 cycle.
- **Rulers without a name** (minor), Folio and Deck: "Righello orizzontale" / "Righello verticale" (Horizontal ruler / Vertical ruler).
- **Numeric fields without a name in dialogs** (minor): `NumberBox` passes name, label and help to the inner field (rows and
  columns of Insert table, numeric fields of Modify style); the Insert table dialog has its own name.
- Verified without defects: F6 cycle (ribbon → document → status bar), Character, Paragraph, Table, Fields,
  Hyperlink, Style dialogs (initial focus inside, Tab staying in the dialog, Esc returning to the document), text navigation and
  Tab between cells.

**Classification.** No blockers. One serious (keyboard context menu), two medium (position and format announcement,
object selection), five minor (the two from the nineteenth, tabs, rulers, numeric fields). All fixed.

**Tests only**: `FolioAccessibilityTests` (names of all reachable controls in Folio and in the seven dialogs, rulers,
page/line/column/cell/format announcement, Shift+F10 with focus on the first item, objects with ⌘⌥⇧O and Tab, F6),
`Maiusc_F10_sulla_griglia_apre_il_menu_della_cella_da_tastiera`, `Maiusc_F10_apre_il_menu_della_forma_selezionata_da_tastiera`,
`Una_tabella_html_con_bordo_incollata_porta_i_bordi_nelle_celle`, `La_lettura_dei_bordi_e_la_stessa_per_le_celle_di_Ledger`;
extended `La_ribbon_mostra_il_grassetto_del_testo_della_forma_in_modifica` and
`Scrivere_con_una_forma_selezionata_entra_nel_testo_della_forma_e_non_nella_cella`. Seen on screen: borders in Ledger, pending "B" and
"I" in Deck, menu from Shift+F10 in Folio and Ledger. Not tried with VoiceOver on (system settings are not
